# === AI assistants ===

## Liberty Next — AI assistant
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/ai-assistant/

The Liberty Next AI assistant: the drawer opened from the Assistant button, the page context it receives, files attached to a question, saved conversations and notes, starter questions and follow-ups, the model picker, what it can do (read the connectors' queries, search the catalogue, describe the installation, follow playbooks, call the applications' tools, read the jobs and the server log, call API endpoints, propose configuration), how it is restricted (ai:chat, the permissions of each tool, allowed connectors, read-only queries, data scope), and its settings.

**Assistant**, at the right of the top bar (its icon alone on a narrow screen), opens a drawer on the right of the page where users ask questions about their data in plain language. The assistant answers by running the connectors' queries, with the user's rights.

---

## At a glance

---

## Using it \{#use\}

Type a question and press Enter (Shift+Enter for a new line), or click one of the **starter questions** shown on an empty conversation. The answer arrives as it is written; **Stop** interrupts it and keeps what was received.

- **Tool calls** are folded into one muted line — *3 tool call(s)* — that opens to show them; a failed call keeps its message visible.
- A table in an answer scrolls sideways, each figure on one line.
- Each answer ends with two or three **follow-up questions** as chips; a click sends one.
- The conversation stays when the drawer is closed and after a reload, and it is saved for the user — see [Conversations and notes](#history). **+** (*new conversation*) starts another one.
- The **paperclip** in the message box gives the assistant a file to read — see [Attach a file](#attach).
- When several models are allowed, a **Model** picker in the drawer's header chooses the one that answers. The choice is kept on this device.

The assistant knows today's date: *last month* or *this quarter* need no explanation.

Examples: *How many open orders per company this month?* — *Which users have not signed in since June?* — *Where do I close a period?*

---

## Attach a file \{#attach\}

The paperclip (*attach a file for the assistant to read*) adds a file to the question: a screenshot of an error, a procedure in PDF, a list to compare with what the installation holds, a log.

| File | Sent to the assistant |
|---|---|
| Image — `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.webp` | As it is; 5 MB at most. |
| PDF | As it is. |
| Spreadsheet — `.xlsx`, `.xlsm` | As text: the first sheet. |
| Delimited file — `.csv`, `.tsv` | As text, the delimiter detected. |
| Text — `.txt`, `.log`, `.md`, `.json`, `.xml`, `.sql`, `.toml`, `.yaml`, `.ini`, `.html`… | As text. |

A sheet or a text longer than 60,000 characters is cut: the file's chip then ends with `*`, and its tooltip says what was attached. The assistant only reads the file: nothing is loaded into a table, nothing is stored on the server. The file stays with the conversation while it is open; a saved conversation keeps its name only, and the assistant is told the file is gone when the conversation is resumed.

The largest file is set by **File attached to a question: megabytes at most** in Liberty Next → Administer → App → AI Assistant — 10 by default, `0` removes the paperclip. A file counts as input tokens at every question of its conversation.

---

## Conversations and notes \{#history\}

The history button of the drawer's header (*conversations and notes*) opens a panel with two lists.

**Conversations** — each conversation is saved on the server for the user and follows them from one device to another. A click on a row (*Resume this conversation*) reopens it; the bin deletes it. What is kept is what the user saw — the questions and the answers; a resumed conversation reads its data again. The 30 latest conversations are kept.

**Notes — what the assistant remembers for you** — ask the assistant to remember something for later conversations: a convention, a preference, how a figure is defined. It proposes the note on a card: **Apply** saves it, **Skip** drops it, and nothing is saved without that click. A note is 300 characters at most; it belongs to the application of the page, or to *every application*, and then travels with the user's questions. Notes are private to the user; the bin deletes one.

---

## What the page tells it \{#context\}

While a data screen is the active tab, every message carries what the user is looking at: the application, the screen and its read query, the active filters, the number of rows loaded and their columns, and the row last clicked (or whose row menu was opened). *This screen*, *these rows* or *the selected row* need no further explanation, and the assistant runs the screen's own query when it needs more data.

On the **Data Explorer** page, the context is the model and the analysis on the canvas (entity, rows, measures, period) or the saved analysis open: *Save this as an analysis* or *Make a dashboard of these* need no further explanation.

On a page an application ships (see [Pages an application ships](./apps/plugins.md#pages)), the page itself says what the user is looking at: a title and a few facts — the object open, the tab, a filter, never rows. A question about *this* then needs no name there either.

A line under the drawer's header shows what is sent — *Page: orders · filters: 2 · the clicked row*, with the screen's identifier. Its **×** stops sending the page for as long as the user stays on it. The context is limited to 4,000 characters.

---

## Starter questions \{#starters\}

On an empty conversation, the drawer offers questions suited to where the user is: those of the current screen (or of the Data Explorer page, or of the page an application ships), else those of the application, else those set for everywhere — the most specific place that has questions wins. An application can group them under headings, shown as pills above the questions; after an answer, the follow-ups take their place. When an application ships its questions in several languages, the drawer shows them in the user's language.

Questions come from two sources:

- **Liberty Next → Logic → AI**: the questions an application ships, per application, by heading and per screen, in each language — see [below](#settings-ai);
- **Liberty Next → Administer → App → AI Assistant → Starter questions**: the operator's own, for everywhere, an application or an *application/screen*. They win over the application's questions for the same place.

---

## What it can do \{#tools\}

| Tool | Does | Setting |
|---|---|---|
| `list_connectors` | Lists the connectors with the **read** queries and the endpoints the user may run (descriptions, no SQL, no credentials). On a large installation it answers with an overview, then narrows to one connector or to keywords. | **Connector tools** (on by default). |
| `sql_query` | Runs a **read** query of a SQL connector the way its screen does: column labels and formats, the screen's filters, the environment of the page. It filters by column — a value or a range — and a filter that matches no column is refused. Write queries are always refused. | **Connector tools**; **Rows per query, at most** (200). |
| `explorer_models`, `explorer_fields`, `explorer_query` | List the [Data Explorer](./explorer/overview.md) models and their fields, then compute a total, a ranking, a trend or a comparison on a model — rows, measures, filters, period, sort, Top N (100 rows by default, 10,000 at most) — under the user's data scope. | On by default. |
| `explorer_saved`, `explorer_save_analysis`, `explorer_save_dashboard` | List the user's saved analyses and dashboards, and save what the user asks for: an analysis is run once before it is stored, so a wrong field is refused; a dashboard gathers saved analyses as tiles. Both are **private** unless the user asks to share them. | On by default. |
| `describe_instance` | Summarises what the installation holds, or one application: menus, screens with their read query, dashboards, Data Explorer models, jobs, playbooks. *Where do I find…* is answered from the real configuration. | Always. |
| `search_catalog` | Finds a screen, a menu entry, a dashboard, a Data Explorer model, a job or a playbook by keyword, without reading the whole configuration. | Always. |
| Application tools | Functions an application ships for its own subject, named `<app>_<id>`. Read-only. See [Liberty Next → Logic → AI](#settings-ai). | **The applications' tools** (on by default). |
| `remember_note` | Proposes a note for later conversations — see [Conversations and notes](#history). | Always. |
| `screen_form`, `screen_write`, `screen_write_many`, `screen_action`, `job_form`, `job_run` | Read what a screen lets its user do, then add, change or delete a record — or up to 50 records on one card —, or run an action of the screen, through the screen's own queries and rules; read a job as its page shows it, then run it — see [Write through a screen](#write). | **Write tools** (off by default), with the `ai:write` permission. |
| Playbooks | Lists the applications' procedures and loads the one that fits — see [Playbooks](#playbooks). | Always. |
| `jobs_status`, `server_log`, `integrity_checks` | The Nomaflow jobs with their schedule, last run and next start, and one job's recent runs with the failing step; the recent server log lines, by level and text; the configuration cross-checks. | **Operations tools** (off by default); superusers only. |
| `api_call` | Calls an endpoint of an API connector. | **API tool** (off by default — an endpoint may change data). |
| `api_run` | Calls an endpoint marked **Changes data** — a report submitted, an orchestration run. `api_call` refuses such an endpoint. In the chat it proposes a card; nothing is sent until the user applies it. See [API endpoints](./build/api-endpoints.md#writable). | **API tool** and **Write tools**, for a user holding `ai:write` and the endpoint's permission; over MCP, **Allow changes over MCP** as well. |
| Scaffold tools | Propose a query, a dictionary entry, a screen or a menu item; the user reviews the proposal and applies it. | **Scaffold tools** (off by default); superusers only. |
| Web fetch | Reads pages of the allowed domains. | **Allowed domains** (none by default). |

The assistant only uses existing named queries: it does not write SQL against the database. Beyond **Rows per query, at most**, a result is marked as truncated and the assistant is told not to count or add up the rows it received: it narrows its filters, or computes the figure with the Data Explorer tools. A tool result above 60,000 characters is cut, and the assistant is asked to narrow its call. A question that uses all its tool rounds (**Max tool iterations**, 15 by default) ends on a closing answer: what was done, what was found, what is left — and the user can ask to continue.

The **Operations tools** let the assistant read the running server rather than guess when a job failed, is late or is missing. They are meant for installations whose chat users are administrators: the server log can hold anything the server wrote.

---

## Write through a screen \{#write\}

With the **Write tools** on, the assistant can do what a user does in a screen or on a job's page — nothing by another path:

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `screen_form` | Reads what the screen lets this user add, change, delete and run: the key, each column with its label, whether it is required or locked, its default and the values it accepts, the columns a picked value fills, and the screen's actions. |
| `screen_write` | Adds, changes or deletes **one** record. |
| `screen_write_many` | Adds, changes or deletes **several** records of one screen — the same operation for all, 50 at most — on one card. |
| `screen_action` | Runs **one** action of the screen — a row menu's *Validate* or *Close*, a button of the toolbar or of a form tab. |
| `job_form` | Reads a job as its page shows it: what it does, the parameters a user may set with their choices, its presets, whether it is running, its last runs with their state and error. |
| `job_run` | Runs the job — the page's **Run now** — with its declared parameters and presets only. |

The record is read through the screen's read query, and the form's rules apply: a missing required column, a value outside its list, a column or a record the screen holds read-only are refused with the reason. The save then runs as from the form — dictionary rules, sequences, related tables, audit, data scope, change package, notification rules — and so do the screen's save hooks and the steps of its actions, each under its own permission. A value picked in a list fills its sibling columns, as in the form; a sibling the request gives is kept.

**Three locks, all needed:** the **Write tools** setting, the `ai:write` permission of the role, and the permission of each query, endpoint or plugin that runs, as in the screen — `job:<id>` for a job.

**Who confirms.** In the drawer the tools only propose: the user gets a card — *Change sales/orders — … — STATUS: 'OPEN' → 'CLOSED'*, or the action with the screen's confirmation and what it runs — and nothing happens until **Apply**; **Skip** drops the step. Over [MCP](./mcp.md#changes), these tools exist only where **Allow changes over MCP** is on, and the client asks its user before calling one.

**Several records.** Every record of the list is checked before the first is written: if the screen refuses one, nothing is written and the answer names each refused record with its reason. One **Apply** then writes them in order, each as `screen_write` writes one. Should a save still fail midway, it stops there: the records before it stay written, and the answer says how many. Beyond 50 records, the grid's Excel import is the way.

**Jobs.** A run is queued and goes on in the background; the assistant follows it with `job_form`, and the user sees it in the Nomaflow [run history](../nomaflow/runs/history.md). A job that is already running is refused. A job that loads a file the user brings asks for it **on the card** — one picker per file step, with the kinds of file the job's upload takes: **Apply** sends the file through the job's own upload and runs the job with it. The file never goes through the model. From Claude Desktop, the file comes from the [extension's folder](./mcp.md#files).

| Refused | Reason given |
|---|---|
| A record open in its form | The form holds the record: it cannot be changed or deleted until the form is closed — by another user, or by the user's own open form. |
| A screen that cannot be written | The screen is read-only, has no query for the operation, runs actions when its form opens, or reads its data from a connector left out of **Allowed connectors**. |
| An action made only of what a browser does | Opening a page or an address is noted, not run. |

As in the screen, a save, its related tables and its hooks are separate statements: when a hook or a step fails, what ran before stays, and the answer says so.

**What is kept.** Each applied card and each saving tool called over MCP is in the usage record — who, the screen, the operation or the action, the key of the record, the job, and the reason of a refusal; never the values. [Monitoring → AI usage](../monitoring/ai-usage.md#changes) lists them, and on a change-tracked screen the change package names these entries *AI assistant*.

---

## Playbooks \{#playbooks\}

A **playbook** is a step-by-step procedure an application ships for the assistant: *Close a period*, *Add a user to a role*. When a user asks how to do something in an application, the assistant looks for a playbook that fits, loads it and follows its steps in order, saying which one it follows. Without a suitable playbook, it says so and answers from what it can read.

---

## Liberty Next → Logic → AI \{#settings-ai\}

**Liberty Next → Logic → AI** edits what each application ships for the assistant; **Discard** and **Save** are in the page header. The **App** row lists the applications that already have some, plus `*` for everywhere; **Add scope** picks another one. For each:

| Part | Content |
|---|---|
| **Language** | The language whose questions are shown and edited: **As written** (the questions as the application ships them), or another language — then the lists below are the questions shown to the users of that language. A list left empty in a language shows the one as written. Shown when the interface has another language than the one the configuration is written in. |
| **Starter questions anywhere in** *app* | The questions offered everywhere in the application. |
| **Starter questions by heading** | **Add a heading**: a **Heading** and its questions. The chat shows the headings first, then the questions of the heading picked; when headings are set, they are shown instead of the list above. *No heading: the chat shows the list above.* |
| **Starter questions per screen** | **+ a screen…** adds a screen — or a page the application ships, by its name — and its own questions. **Add a heading for this screen** groups them under headings, as for the application: a **Heading** and its questions; when a screen has headings, they are shown instead of its plain questions. A screen taken out leaves every language with it. |
| **Playbooks** | **Add playbook**: an **Id** (letters, digits, `_` and `-`, unique in the application), a **Title** — what the procedure achieves, the assistant picks a playbook by it —, **When it applies** (one line, optional) and **The procedure** in Markdown. |
| **Tools** | **Add tool**: an **Id** (lowercase letters, digits and `_`, unique in the application — the assistant sees the tool as `<app>_<id>`), the **Function (module:function)** — one of the entry points of the application's [plugins](./build/plugins/overview.md), whose parameters become the tool's arguments —, the **Description** (what it answers and when to use it: the assistant picks a tool by it) and the **Permission the user needs** (blank: the function's own). A tool must not change anything. Tools belong to an application: none on the `*` scope. |

**Save** writes and reloads at once. This material travels with the application: it is installed and upgraded with it, versioned like the rest of the configuration. The questions set under **Liberty Next → Administer → App → AI Assistant** win over the application's, place by place.

---

## Who can use it, and on what \{#access\}

- The user needs the `ai:chat` permission (a role's *AI assistant* rule, in **Beyond the menus**).
- `ai:chat` opens the drawer; each tool then checks what the screens check, for the signed-in user:

  | Tool | The user needs |
  |---|---|
  | `sql_query` | `sql:<connector>:<query>`. |
  | `api_call` | `api:<connector>:<endpoint>`. |
  | Data Explorer tools | `explorer:<app>:<model>`. |
  | `list_connectors`, `describe_instance`, `search_catalog`, playbooks | Nothing more, and they show only what the user can open: a screen by its read query, a menu entry by the [menu's rule](./build/menus/permissions-and-roles.md#gating), a job by `job:<id>`. An application with nothing for the user is not named. |
  | Application tools | The tool's permission. |
  | `screen_form`, `screen_write`, `screen_write_many`, `screen_action` | `ai:write`, and the permission of each query, endpoint or plugin the screen runs. |
  | `job_form`, `job_run` | `ai:write` and `job:<id>`. |
  | Operations and scaffold tools | Superuser. |

  A user holding `ai:chat` without the `sql:` or `explorer:` permissions of an application gets no figure from it: grant them, as for the screens. A refusal reads the same for a query that exists and for one that does not.
- **Allowed connectors** in Liberty Next → Administer → App limits the connectors the assistant may reach, and the applications `describe_instance` and the playbooks cover; empty means all. The write tools follow it too: a screen whose data is on another connector does not exist for them.
- Every query it runs goes through the same server checks as a screen: the user's [data scope](./build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md#data-scope) filters the rows.
- **Model** in the drawer only offers the models allowed in the settings; the server refuses any other.

---

## From Claude, and what is recorded \{#beyond\}

- The same tools answer an external client — Claude Desktop, claude.ai, Claude Code — through the server's MCP endpoint, each user with a personal access token and their own rights. See [Connect Claude (MCP)](./mcp.md).
- An installation can flag its sensitive columns and keep them from the assistant, and [Data sent to Anthropic](./ai-data-sent.md) lists what a question sends and what it never does.
- Every question is recorded: who asked, the model, the tokens, the tools called — never the question, the answer or a row. Superusers read it in [Monitoring → AI usage](../monitoring/ai-usage.md).

---

## Settings \{#settings\}

In **Liberty Next → Administer → App → AI Assistant**: **Enabled**, **Anthropic API key** (encrypted), **Model**, **Effort**, **Max tokens**, **Max tool iterations** (15), **Request timeout (s)**, **Adaptive thinking**, **System prompt**, the tools above, **Allowed connectors**, **Rows per query, at most**, **File attached to a question**, **Usage record kept**, **Write tools**, **Hide sensitive data from the assistant**, the **MCP endpoint**, and for the chat drawer the **Models users may pick** and the **Starter questions**. See [App settings](./build/settings-app.md#ai). Without a key, the drawer says the assistant is not configured.

---

## Tips \{#tips\}

- Give queries a clear label and description (Liberty Next → Data → Connectors): the assistant chooses its queries from them.
- Write dedicated read queries for the questions users ask often (totals per company, per month), rather than expecting the assistant to aggregate thousands of rows.
- Write a playbook for each procedure users ask about more than once: the answer is then the application's procedure, not a guess.
- Keep **API tool** and **Operations tools** off unless the endpoints are read-only and the chat users are administrators.

---

## Liberty Next — Connect Claude (MCP)
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/mcp/

Use the Liberty Next assistant's tools from Claude Desktop, claude.ai or Claude Code: the MCP endpoint of the server, the mcp:use permission, the sign-in from the client, the Claude Desktop extension for a server that is not on the internet, personal access tokens, sending a file for a job, changes over MCP behind their own switch, and how an access is ended.

The tools of the [AI assistant](./ai-assistant.md) can answer an external client — Claude Desktop, claude.ai, Claude Code — through the server's **MCP endpoint**, `/mcp`. The client acts as a Liberty Next user: it is offered what that user is offered in the chat drawer, each call goes through the same permission checks and the same data scope, and each call is recorded.

Three things are needed: the endpoint turned on, the `mcp:use` permission, and a way to connect — a sign-in from the client, the Claude Desktop extension, or a pasted **personal access token**.

What goes to Anthropic in that case, and what does not, is described on [Data sent to Anthropic](./ai-data-sent.md).

---

## At a glance

---

## Turn the endpoint on \{#enable\}

In **Liberty Next → Administer → App → AI Assistant**:

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **MCP endpoint (/mcp)** | Off | The server answers on `/mcp`. Applied on save, without a restart. |
| **Allow changes over MCP** | Off | Off: an external client reads only. On: the tools that save something are offered to it — see [Changes](#changes). Read at each request. |
| **Personal access token: longest life (days)** | 366 | The longest validity a user may ask for a token, and how long a sign-in from a client lasts before the user allows it again. |

Behind a reverse proxy, also set **Public address** (same page, *Server*) to the address users reach the server at: the addresses the sign-in publishes are built on it.

The endpoint needs the `mcp` extra of the package (`pip install "liberty-next[mcp]"`); `liberty-next[all]` and the Docker image include it.

---

## Grant the permission \{#permission\}

In **Liberty Next → Administer → Access**, give the role the rule **AI assistant → AI tools from an external client (MCP) — create a personal access token** (`mcp:use`), in **Beyond the menus**. The user then sees the **Access tokens** tab in their profile; a superuser always does.

`mcp:use` only opens the endpoint: what the client reaches still depends on the user's other permissions — see [Who can use it, and on what](./ai-assistant.md#access).

---

## Connect the client \{#connect\}

| Way | For | Steps |
|---|---|---|
| **Sign-in from the client** | A custom connector in Claude Desktop or claude.ai. The connector is called from Anthropic's servers: the Liberty server must be reachable from the internet. | Give the connector the address of `/mcp` only. The browser opens Liberty: the user signs in the usual way (password or SSO), then, on the **Allow access** page — *the client asks to use the application as the user* — clicks **Allow** (or **Refuse**). The page says whether the server lets the client make changes, and how many days the access lasts. Nothing to create, nothing to paste. |
| **Claude Desktop extension** | A server that is not on the internet: an internal address, a VPN. | In the profile's **Access tokens** tab, **Claude Desktop extension** downloads a `.mcpb` file named after the server. Open the file with Claude Desktop and paste a token created in the same tab — see [below](#extension). |
| **Pasted token** | Claude Code, a script. | [Create a token](#token) and give it to the client as the request header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, with the **Connector URL** of the tab — `https://<server>/mcp`. |

| Answer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `404` | The endpoint is off. |
| `401` | No token, or a token that is invalid or ended. |

---

## Create a token \{#token\}

The user opens their profile — their name in the top bar — then **Access tokens**:

1. **Valid for (days)**: 90 by default. A longer validity than the server allows is shortened to the server's maximum; the expiry date shown with the token is the one that applies.
2. **Create a token**.
3. The token takes the place of the validity field, with its expiry date: copy it (**Copy**) — *it is shown once and not stored*. **Close** leaves the tab; the next visit offers a new token.

The tab also gives the **Connector URL**, the address of the server followed by `/mcp`.

---

## The Claude Desktop extension \{#extension\}

The extension runs a small relay on the user's own computer: it passes Claude's messages to `/mcp` with the user's personal access token, so the server only has to be reachable from that computer. The file is built at download with the server's address filled in and carries no secret. Nothing to install: Claude Desktop brings what the relay needs.

| Setting in Claude Desktop | Content |
|---|---|
| **Liberty address** | The address of the server, ending with `/mcp` — already filled in. |
| **Personal access token** | A token created in the profile's **Access tokens** tab. |
| **Files folder** | Optional. The folder Claude may send a file from, for a job that loads one — see [below](#files). |
| **Accept an internal certificate** | To turn on only when the server uses a self-signed or company certificate. |

The settings are in French when the extension is downloaded from a French interface.

**Several servers in one Claude Desktop.** The extension is named after its instance — the installation's **Environment** (Administer → App → Server) and the host of its address: *Liberty Next – Test · liberty-test.example.com*. The extensions of a production and a test server, or of two customers, install side by side, each with its own token. The server also tells Claude which instance it is, so an answer or a change names the instance it concerns.

### Send a file for a job \{#files\}

With a **Files folder**, the extension offers two tools that run on the user's computer: one lists the spreadsheets and delimited files of that folder — `.xlsx`, `.xlsm`, `.csv`, `.txt`, `.tsv` —, the other sends one of them to Liberty for a job. The file lands in the job's own upload area, as from the job's page, with the same size limit; nothing runs on the upload, and `job_run` then names the file.

Sending a file needs what running the job needs: the **Write tools** and **Allow changes over MCP** settings, `ai:write` and `job:<id>`. A connector by sign-in has no access to the user's disk: the file is then loaded from the job's page.

---

## What the client can do \{#tools\}

- The client is offered the tools the user is offered in the chat drawer, with the same descriptions; a tool the user cannot use is not listed.
- Every call checks the user's permissions and applies their [data scope](./build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md#data-scope), as in the drawer; the columns the installation [marks as sensitive](./ai-data-sent.md#sensitive) are left out in the same way.
- The tools whose result is a card of the chat drawer are not offered: the scaffold proposals and the notes.
- A personal access token opens the MCP endpoint only: the rest of the API refuses it.

---

## Changes over MCP \{#changes\}

In the drawer a change is a card the user applies. Over MCP the only gate is the client's own approval, which its user can set to *always allow*: an administrator therefore decides whether changes are made from an external client at all.

| **Allow changes over MCP** | The client |
|---|---|
| Off (default) | Reads only. The tools that save are not listed; called anyway, they answer that changes over MCP are off on this server. |
| On | Is also offered the tools that save: a Data Explorer analysis or dashboard, [a record, an action or a job through the write tools](./ai-assistant.md#write). Each still needs its own switch and the user's permissions, and tells the client it changes something — the client asks its user before calling it. |

Every change made this way is listed in [Monitoring → AI usage](../monitoring/ai-usage.md#changes).

---

## When an access ends \{#end\}

The account is read again at every call, so an access carries the user's rights of the moment, never more.

| Access | Ends |
|---|---|
| **A sign-in from a client** | When its user ends it: the profile's **Access tokens** tab lists the clients under **Connected by sign-in** — the client's name and its last use — and **End access** stops one from its next call, the others kept. Otherwise after the **longest life** set above; the user then allows the client again. |
| **A pasted token** | At its expiry date. It is not stored, so it is not listed. |
| **Both** | When the account is deactivated or loses `mcp:use`, and when the account's password changes. |

**Changing the password ends every access of the account** — tokens and sign-ins alike. That is what to do when a token has leaked.

A superuser reads every user's clients with `GET /oauth/grants?everyone=1`.

---

## What is recorded \{#usage\}

Each call is in the usage record, under the channel *External client (MCP)*: the user, the tool, what it was called on, whether it failed, its size and its time — never a row it returned nor a value it wrote. See [Monitoring → AI usage](../monitoring/ai-usage.md).

---

## Tips \{#tips\}

- Prefer the sign-in for a server on the internet, the extension for an internal one: neither asks the user to handle a secret by hand more than once.
- Grant `mcp:use` to the roles that already use the assistant in the application; the answers depend on the same `sql:` and `explorer:` permissions.
- Serve the endpoint over HTTPS only: the token travels in a request header.

---

## Liberty Next — Data sent to Anthropic
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/ai-data-sent/

What Liberty Next sends to Anthropic and what it never sends: the AI assistant (instructions, page context, notes, conversation, tool results, attached files, with the installation's API key) and Claude connected through MCP (Liberty only answers tool calls). The Sensitive flag and the switch that keeps flagged columns from the assistant, what stays on the server, and the settings that decide.

Liberty Next uses Anthropic's models in two ways, and the path of the data is not the same:

- the **[AI assistant](./ai-assistant.md)** — the server calls Anthropic's API with the API key of the installation;
- **[Claude connected through MCP](./mcp.md)** — Liberty calls nobody: it answers the tool calls of the user's Claude client, and that client talks to Anthropic under the user's own Claude account.

Nothing is sent while nobody asks a question: no background send, no telemetry, no other AI provider. An installation can also name its [sensitive data](#sensitive) and keep it from the assistant.

---

## At a glance

---

## The AI assistant \{#assistant\}

Each question is sent to Anthropic's API with the **Anthropic API key** of **Liberty Next → Administer → App → AI Assistant**. A request holds:

| Sent | Content |
|---|---|
| **Instructions** | The built-in instructions, or the installation's **System prompt** in their place, and today's date. |
| **Tool list** | The name and the description of each tool offered to this user. |
| **Page context** | What the user is looking at: the application, the screen and its read query, the active filters, the number of rows loaded and their columns, the row last clicked. 4,000 characters at most; the **×** of its chip stops sending it. |
| **Notes** | The user's notes for the application, 2,000 characters at most. |
| **Conversation** | The questions and the answers of the conversation in progress — the last 40 messages. |
| **Tool results** | What each tool read to answer: the rows of a read query (200 by default), Data Explorer figures, the description of the installation (ids and labels — no data, no SQL), a playbook, the form of a screen, the record before and after a write. With the tools an installation turns on: the jobs, the server log lines and the integrity checks (operations tools, superusers only), the answer of an API endpoint (API tool), what an application's own tool returns. A result is cut at 60,000 characters. |
| **Attached files** | An image or a PDF as it is; a spreadsheet (its first sheet), a CSV or a text file as text, cut at 60,000 characters. A file stays with its conversation while the page is open, and is sent again with each question of it. A file chosen on the card of a job is not one of them: it goes to the job's own upload, never to the model. |

When domains are listed under **Allowed domains**, Anthropic reads those web pages itself; Liberty sends nothing more.

Within one question, each tool round sends the earlier rounds again; Anthropic reads the repeated part from its prompt cache for a few minutes, at a lower price. It is not a storage kept by Liberty.

---

## Claude through MCP \{#mcp\}

| Step | Who talks to whom |
|---|---|
| The user asks Claude a question. | The Claude client ↔ Anthropic, under the user's Claude account. |
| Claude calls a Liberty tool. | The client → the server, with the user's access. |
| Liberty answers. | The server → the client: the result of that tool, 60,000 characters at most. |
| Claude writes its answer. | The client → Anthropic: the conversation, with the results it received. |

**Liberty makes no call to Anthropic here, and the API key of the installation is not used.** What a tool returned leaves the server towards the user's Claude client, and from there to Anthropic on the terms of the user's Claude plan. There is no page context and there are no notes over MCP. A file the Claude Desktop extension sends for a job goes from the user's computer to the server, not to Anthropic.

| Client | The server is called from |
|---|---|
| A custom connector in Claude Desktop or claude.ai | Anthropic's servers: the server must be reachable from the internet. |
| The Claude Desktop extension, Claude Code | The user's computer: an internal address or a VPN is enough. |

---

## Sensitive data \{#sensitive\}

An installation decides what is sensitive, and Liberty keeps it from the assistant — in the chat and through MCP alike. Nothing is flagged in what the applications ship: the flags are the installation's to set and to maintain.

| Step | Where | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Flag an item** | Liberty Next → Data → Dictionary → an entry → *Rule* → **Sensitive** | Covers every column carrying the item, on every screen, query and Data Explorer model. A column is matched by its dictionary item, by its name, or by its name without the connector's prefix (`ABALPH` → `ALPH`) — as the [data scope](./build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md#data-scope) finds its columns. |
| **Flag a column** | Liberty Next → Screens → Screens → a column → *General* → **Sensitive** | Three choices: *(default)* follows the column's item, *yes* covers a column that carries no item, *no* exempts a column whose item is flagged. |
| **Turn the hiding on** | Liberty Next → Administer → App → AI Assistant → **Hide sensitive data from the assistant** | Off by default. Applied at the next call, without a restart. |

With the hiding on, the flagged columns are left out of:

| Place | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Rows a read query returns** | The flagged columns are removed from the rows. The assistant is told which columns are hidden, so it can say so and point the user to the screen. |
| **Write and action cards** | The values of the record are shown as *(hidden: sensitive)*: the record before a change, the record of a delete, the screen's confirmation of an action, and the messages of the actions the screen runs after a save. The value the user asked to write is theirs, and is shown. |
| **Page context** | The flagged columns leave the column list and the clicked row, and a filter typed on one of them is not sent. |
| **Data Explorer** | A flagged field cannot be a row heading nor be read by a measure other than a count — no sum, average, minimum or maximum. It can be counted, and filtered on a whole value the user gives (*equals*) only: a range, a *contains* or a period on it is refused, as it would let the values be found out count by count. |
| **Filters of a read query** | The same rule: a flagged column is filtered on a whole value, not on a range. |

The screens themselves do not change: the users who may open them see the values as before.

**What the hiding does not cover:**

- what a user types in a question, or attaches;
- a free-text column that is not flagged;
- what an API endpoint (API tool), an application's own tool or the operations tools return — Liberty does not know their columns;
- the key of a record on a write card.

---

## What is never sent \{#never\}

| Never sent | How |
|---|---|
| Pool passwords, API keys, encrypted secrets | The tools give descriptions only — never credentials. A password field of a form is shown as `••••••`. |
| The SQL text of a query | The assistant sees the name, the label and the description of a query. |
| Rows the user may not read | Each tool checks the permission the screens check, and the user's [data scope](./build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md#data-scope) filters the rows. |
| Connectors left out of **Allowed connectors** | The assistant is told they are not available. |
| What a switched-off tool would read | A tool that is off is not offered at all. |

---

## What stays on the server \{#stays\}

| Kept | Content, how long |
|---|---|
| **Conversations** | What the user saw — questions, answers, the names of the attached files — for the 30 latest conversations of each user. |
| **Notes** | The user's own, until they delete them. |
| **Usage record** | Who asked, the model, the tokens, the time, and for each tool its name and a short summary of what it was called on; for a change made through the assistant, the screen, the operation, the key of the record or the job — never the question, the answer, a row, a value written or the text of a note. 90 days by default; see [AI usage](../monitoring/ai-usage.md). |
| **Clients connected by sign-in** | The client's name, when it connected, its last use and the day its access ends — never a token. An ended access is dropped after 30 days. |
| **Attached files** | Not stored. |

The [licence usage report](./build/secure/license-key.md#usage-report) goes to the licence management tool, not to Anthropic, and carries nothing of the assistant.

---

## What decides \{#controls\}

| Setting | Where | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Enabled**, **Anthropic API key** | Administer → App → AI Assistant | Off, or no key: no assistant, nothing sent. |
| The tool switches | Same section | **Connector tools**, **Data Explorer tools**, **The applications' tools**: on by default. **API tool**, **Operations tools**, **Scaffold tools**, **Write tools**: off by default. |
| **Allowed connectors** | Same section | The connectors the assistant may read; empty means all. |
| **Hide sensitive data from the assistant** | Same section | Off by default — see [above](#sensitive). |
| **File attached to a question** | Same section | `0`: no attachment. |
| **MCP endpoint (/mcp)** | Same section | Off by default: no Claude client can connect. |
| **Allow changes over MCP** | Same section | Off by default: a Claude client reads only — see [Changes over MCP](./mcp.md#changes). |
| `ai:chat`, `ai:write`, `mcp:use` | Administer → Access → a role → Beyond the menus | Who uses the assistant, who writes through it, who connects Claude. |
| `sql:`, `explorer:`, `api:` permissions and the data scope | The role | What the assistant reads for that user. |

---

## To know before opening it widely \{#limits\}

- **The tools read what the screens show.** Without the hiding, a name, an e-mail address or an amount goes to the model when a query returns it.
- **Flag before turning the hiding on.** The switch hides what is flagged, nothing else: review the dictionary entries of the personal and banking data first.
- **Keep the API tool and the operations tools for installations that need them.** Their answers are not covered by the hiding.
- **The use Anthropic makes of what it receives** depends on the contract of the installation's API key for the assistant, and on the user's Claude plan for MCP.

---

## Liberty Next — AI usage
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/monitoring/ai-usage/

Monitoring → AI usage in Liberty Next: who uses the AI assistant, the estimated cost, the tokens with the share read from the cache, the tools called and their failures — by user, day, model, channel and tool —, the changes made through the assistant, and the latest activity with its tool calls. What is recorded, what never is, and how long it is kept.

**Monitoring → AI usage** shows how the [AI assistant](../framework/ai-assistant.md) is used: who asks, what it costs, which tools it calls and which fail, and what was changed through it. It is for superusers, from **Liberty Next → Operate → Monitoring**.

---

## At a glance

---

## What is recorded \{#record\}

Each question to the assistant leaves one record: who asked, from which application's page, the model, the tokens (in, out, read from and written to the cache), the time it took and how it ended. Each tool call of the question is kept with its name, what it was called on (the connector and the query, the model, the keywords, the screen and the key of the record), whether it failed and why, its size and its time.

**The question, the answer, the rows a tool returned and the values written are never recorded.** A question the user abandons half-way is recorded with what had happened until then.

Three **channels** feed the record:

| Channel | One entry is |
|---|---|
| **Liberty chat** | A question asked in the assistant's drawer, with its model and its tokens. |
| **External client (MCP)** | A tool called by a Claude client — see [Connect Claude (MCP)](../framework/mcp.md). No model and no tokens: they are the client's. |
| **Card applied** | A card the user applied in the drawer: a record written, an action or a job run — see [Write through a screen](../framework/ai-assistant.md#write). |

---

## The period in figures \{#figures\}

The period is **Last 7 days**, **Last 30 days** (default) or **Last 90 days**, picked at the top left; beside it, a line recalls what is recorded and how long it is kept, and **Reload** reads the figures again.

| Tile | Shows |
|---|---|
| **Questions** | Entries over the period. |
| **Users** | Users with at least one. |
| **Estimated cost, at list price** | What the tokens of the chat's questions cost at Anthropic's list price, in US dollars written in the reader's language (*$38.20*). A model without a listed price is left out and named (*without … (no listed price)*). |
| **Tokens in** | Input tokens, with the share read from the cache (*71 % from cache*): the part of a conversation sent again at each tool round is read from the cache, at a lower price. |
| **Tokens out** | Output tokens. |
| **Tool calls** | Tools called, with the number that failed. |
| **Changes made through the assistant** | Their number over the period — see [below](#changes). |

The cost is an estimate: the prices are the list prices known to the installed release, and the contract of the installation's API key may differ. A call over MCP costs the installation nothing: it has no tokens here.

---

## Breakdowns \{#breakdowns\}

Six panels, two a row:

| Panel | Columns |
|---|---|
| **By user**, **By day** | Questions, Tokens in, From cache, Tokens out, Cost. |
| **By model** — *the questions of the chat* | The same columns, one row per model that answered a question. |
| **By channel** | Entries, Tool calls, Failed, Cost — the cost for the *Liberty chat* only. |
| **By tool** | Calls, Failed, Average time, Average size. |
| **Changes made through the assistant** | When, User, Channel, What. |

A click on a user narrows the questions below to theirs (*Questions of …*); a click on a channel narrows them to that channel.

---

## Changes made through the assistant \{#changes\}

The panel lists what was changed through the assistant over the period, newest first, 200 at most — *cards applied, and saving tools called over MCP*:

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| **When**, **User** | Who made the change, and when. |
| **Channel** | *Card applied* for a card of the drawer, *External client (MCP)* for a tool a Claude client called. |
| **What** | The tool, then the screen and the operation or the action with the key of the record, or the job; in red with its reason when the change was refused. |

The values written are not kept. On a screen under [change tracking](../nomaflow/change-packages.md), the change package names these entries *AI assistant*.

---

## Latest activity \{#recent\}

One row per entry: When, User, Application, Model, Tokens in, From cache, Tokens out, Tool calls, Time and **Outcome**.

| Entry | Model column | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| A question of the chat | The model. | *Answered*, *Failed*, *Abandoned* or *Round limit* (the question used all its tool rounds and ended on a closing answer). |
| A card applied | *Card applied*. | *Applied* or *Refused*. |
| A run of MCP calls | *External client (MCP)*. The calls of one user less than two minutes apart are one row. | *Answered*, or the number of calls that failed. |

A row opens on its tool calls, each with what it was called on, its size in characters and its time. Above the list, **Every channel** narrows it to one channel and **Failures only** to the entries with a failure.

---

## How long it is kept \{#retention\}

**Usage record kept (days; 0 = without limit)**, in Liberty Next → Administer → App → AI Assistant, is 90 by default. Older entries are deleted with the notifications' clean-up, and the store appears as **AI usage** on the [Retention](./retention.md) view, with its number of entries, **Preview** and **Run now**.

---

## Tips \{#tips\}

- A tool that fails often points at a missing permission or at a query whose description misleads the assistant: open the question's tool calls to read the reason.
- A user with many questions and few tool calls is probably asking for what the assistant cannot reach: check the role's `sql:` and `explorer:` permissions.
- Read the **Changes** panel after turning the write tools on: it says who uses them, on which screens, and what is refused.
- The same figures are served by `GET /admin/ai-usage` for an external report.
