## Liberty Next — Expose data to the AI assistant
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/expose-to-ai/

Recipe — choose what the AI assistant reaches and help it pick the right query: the ai:chat permission, the allowed connectors, read queries only, the user's data scope, and query labels and descriptions written for the model.

## The problem

The [AI assistant](../ai-assistant.md) answers questions by running the connectors' named queries. It must reach the right data — and only that — and pick the right query for each question.

## The pattern

| Layer | Setting | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Who** | The `ai:chat` permission, through a role. | Without it, the user has no assistant. |
| **Which connectors** | **Allowed connectors**, Liberty Next → Administer → App → AI Assistant. | Empty: every connector; otherwise only those listed. |
| **Which queries** | Read queries the user holds the `sql:` permission of. | The assistant runs a query only for a user who could open it from a screen. Write queries are always refused; the assistant never writes SQL of its own. |
| **Which rows** | The user's rights and [data scope](../build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md#data-scope). | A query run by the assistant is checked like a screen's: the user sees the same rows. |
| **Which query to pick** | The queries' **label** and **description**. | The assistant reads them to choose. |

## The recipe

### 1. Grant the assistant

In **Liberty Next → Administer → Access → Roles**, give the users' role the *AI assistant* rule (`ai:chat`), in **Beyond the menus**. See [Roles & permissions](../build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md).

### 2. Limit the connectors

In **Liberty Next → Administer → App → AI Assistant**, fill **Allowed connectors** with the connectors whose data the assistant may read — for example the CRM's, without the HR one. Keep **API tool** off unless the endpoints only read.

### 3. Describe the queries

In **Liberty Next → Data → Connectors**, give each query the assistant should use a **label** and a **description** (Advanced tab). The assistant lists the connectors with their queries and descriptions, then picks one:

| Good | Weak |
|---|---|
| `Invoices of a period with customer, amount and status. For questions about invoicing volume, recent invoices, status breakdown.` | `Get invoices` |
| `Number of deals per pipeline stage. For pipeline breakdown questions.` | `Aggregate deals` |
| `Customer activities (calls, meetings, e-mails), most recent first. Parameter CUSTOMER_ID.` | `Activities` |

Two sentences are enough: **what the rows are**, and **which questions it answers**. Mention the parameters and their format.

### 4. Add dedicated queries

For the questions asked often — totals per company, per month — write a read query that computes them, rather than letting the assistant go through thousands of rows. Name its parameters clearly (`PERIOD_FROM`, `COMPANY`) and declare their labels.

### 5. Check

Sign in as a user of the role and ask a question the role should answer, then one it should not: the assistant shows the tools it used and the queries it ran.

## Common mistakes

| Mistake | Symptom |
|---|---|
| Queries without description | The assistant hesitates between similar queries, or picks the wrong one. |
| Several queries with the same description | Same. Make each description specific. |
| A sensitive connector left in an empty **Allowed connectors** list | The assistant may read it for any user who has rights on its queries. List the connectors explicitly. |
| Expecting the assistant to update data | Write queries are refused; changes go through screens and actions. |

## What's next

- [AI assistant](../ai-assistant.md) — the drawer, the tools, the settings.
- [Roles & permissions](../build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md) — `ai:chat` and the data scope.
- [App settings → AI Assistant](../build/settings-app.md#ai) — every setting.

---

## NomaUBL — AI Capabilities
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/ai-capabilities/

The NomaUBL AI assistant — a chat panel that knows the page and the invoice you are on, answers from the NomaUBL documentation, from the generated documentation of the instance and from its data (invoice dossier, period figures, backlog, lifecycle, validation errors, server log, integrity checks, e-directory), follows diagnostic playbooks, proposes follow-ups, and only reads.

The **AI Assistant** is a chat panel embedded in NomaUBL. It answers three kinds of questions:

- *How does the product work?* — from the NomaUBL documentation, indexed by the server, with the title and the link of the page it used.
- *How is this instance set up?* — from the [implementation report](reports/implementation-report.md) generated from the configuration of the instance: documents, mappings, rules, jobs, roles.
- *What is the state of my data?* — from the database, in **read-only** mode: one invoice in full, the figures of a period, the backlog, the errors, the server log, the integrity checks.

The assistant knows **the page you are on and the invoice you have open**, so *"why is this invoice refused?"* needs no number typed by hand. Replies stream as the model writes them; every tool call appears as a pill with the filters used; each reply ends with **follow-up buttons**. The assistant works in French or English and follows the language of the question.

---

## Opening the assistant

- Click **✦ AI Assistant** at the right end of the top bar. The panel opens as a drawer beside the page; it stays usable while an invoice window is open.
- Press **Enter** to send, **Shift+Enter** for a new line, **■** to stop a reply in progress.
- The **paperclip** (*Attach an XML or PDF file*) attaches one or several files to the question: the assistant reads them with the message. A file is kept with the user's [sample files](./claude-mcp.md#samples) for 7 days: it is listed, and deleted, in the **Sample files** tab of the profile window.
- **The conversation is kept** when the panel is closed or the page reloaded (the last 40 messages, in the browser). **+ New chat** starts a fresh one.
- **Opening another invoice starts a new conversation**: the previous exchange was about another invoice and would mislead the model.

---

## At a glance

| Element | Role |
|---|---|
| **Model picker** | *Default* uses the model set by the administrator; the list offers Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Haiku 4.5. The choice is remembered in the browser. |
| **+ New chat** | Clears the conversation. |
| **Context bar** | The page you are on and, when an invoice window is open, a chip with the invoice number and status. **×** on the chip leaves the invoice out of the current chat. |
| **Tool pills** | Each tool called, with the filters it received. |
| **📋 Copy** | Copies the reply as Markdown, without the follow-up line. |
| **Domains and questions** | Above the input: the follow-ups of the last reply, or the four questions of a domain — see [Context and starter questions](#context-and-starter-questions). |

---

## Context and starter questions

With every question the panel sends the **current page**, its **navigation filter** and the **open invoice** (document, type, company, number, status, customer). The assistant assumes the question is about them unless told otherwise.

Above the input, a **domain picker** offers four questions per domain. A question ending with *…* only fills the input, to be completed (an invoice number, a customer).

| Domain | Questions |
|---|---|
| **This invoice** *(when an invoice is open)* | *Why is this invoice in this status?* · *Summarise its lifecycle* · *What should I fix to resubmit it?* · *What are its validation errors?* |
| **Period** | *Give me this month's invoice summary* · *Last month's summary, compared to the month before* · *Deposit rate and error rate this month* · *Net amounts deposited this month, per company* |
| **Backlog** | *Which invoices await an action and what to do?* · *Which refused invoices still await an action?* · *Any invoices pending at the platform for more than 2 days?* · *Which invoices are deposited but not transmitted?* |
| **Invoices** | *Which invoices failed this week and why?* · *Find invoice number …* · *Invoices of customer …* · *Any duplicates this month?* |
| **Statuses & errors** | *What does status 9906 mean?* · *What to do with an invoice refused by the customer?* · *What to do with an invoice rejected by the platform?* · *What does rule BR-FR-…* |
| **Configuration** | *Which documents are sent to the platform?* · *Which notification rules are active?* · *Who has access to what (roles and users)?* · *How is the platform connection configured?* |
| **Documentation** | *How do watched folders work?* · *How does e-reporting work?* · *How do I resend or reprocess an invoice?* · *What changed in the last release?* |
| **Technical** | *Any errors in the server log today?* · *Is the instance healthy?* · *Did all scheduled jobs run?* · *Run this month's integrity checks* |

The page chooses the starting domain: **This invoice** when an invoice is open; **Technical** on the IT dashboard, Diagnostics and Scheduled jobs; **Configuration** on Settings, Roles, Users, Developer, Documents, Notification rules, Actions and Watched folders; **Documentation** on the reference pages and the release notes; **Period** everywhere else — accounting and sales land on the period, IT on the instance.

Every reply ends with **one to three follow-ups** — the natural answer to a question the assistant asked, the next check, or a deeper question. They show in place of the domain's questions; a click on a domain brings its questions back.

---

## What the assistant uses

### Documentation

| Tool | Pill | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **`search_docs`** | 📚 | Searches the NomaUBL documentation, indexed by the server from the site's full-text export (`llms-full.txt`); returns the best pages with title, URL and passage. Called first for any product question. |
| **`read_doc_page`** | 📖 | Reads one page found by `search_docs`, in windows of 12,000 characters for long pages. |
| **`list_doc_pages`** | 📑 | The table of contents of the documentation, when the search finds nothing relevant. |
| **`instance_docs`** | 📘 | The [implementation report](reports/implementation-report.md) of this instance: table of contents, one section, or a search across sections. Called first for any question about how *this* instance is configured. |

The documentation is indexed per language: a French interface searches the French pages, an English interface the English ones. The index is refreshed every six hours; when the site cannot be reached, the assistant uses the copy of the documentation bundled with the application and says so in its answer.

The assistant quotes the page it used and gives its link. It never invents a setting, a status code or a URL: when the documentation does not cover a point, it says so.

### Data of the instance

| Tool | Pill | What it returns |
|---|---|---|
| **`invoice_dossier`** | 🧾 | Everything about one invoice in one call: header (status, customer, amounts, dates, PA identifier), lines, VAT breakdown, validation errors and the full lifecycle with the PA reasons. |
| **`list_invoices`** | 🧾 | Up to 50 invoices filtered on status, company, transaction type (B2B / B2BINT / B2C / B2G / OUTOFSCOPE), customer, invoice number (BT-1) and issue dates. |
| **`lifecycle_history`** | 🕘 | Every status event of an invoice, with the PA rejection reason, expected action and status note. |
| **`validation_errors`** | ⚠️ | The validation errors of an invoice (level, source, rule, message), as in [Integration errors](./diagnostics/integration-errors.md). |
| **`period_figures`** | 🗓️ | The summary of a period from the [audit report](reports/audit-report.md): indicators with the previous period and the variation, the breakdown of processed invoices, the findings, and the backlog across all periods (by status, company and age). Default: the current month to date. |
| **`billing_overview`** | 💶 | The figures of the [Billing overview](./billing-overview.md) for a period, sales or purchases: revenue excl. VAT with invoices and credit notes apart, VAT, counts, transmission or acceptance rate, compared with the previous period; twelve months by outcome; what needs a decision, all dates, in amounts; the split per company and per transaction type. Options: date basis (document date by default) and whether to count the reviewed errors. |
| **`status_statistics`** | 📈 | The data of the [Statistics](./statistics.md) dashboard for a period, sales or purchases: invoices by stage, status, activity code, reason and transaction type (count and amount), the same for the previous period, the trend per day, and the open invoices by waiting time. Same options. |
| **`dashboard_overview`** | 📊 | The counters of the [Operations](./dashboard.md) dashboard for a date range. |
| **`tech_dashboard`** | 🩺 | The health of the instance, as on the [IT dashboard](./tech-dashboard.md): JVM, scheduled jobs and their last runs, send failures, waiting invoices, configuration issues, table sizes. |
| **`server_log`** | 📜 | The end of the [server log](./diagnostics/server-log.md), newest first, filtered on level, module and text. |
| **`integrity_checks`** | 🔎 | The configured [integrity checks](../configuration/system/integrity-reports.md) and, for one check, its result on a date range. |
| **`list_ereports`** | 🔍 | Up to 50 e-reporting runs filtered on direction (inbound / outbound — each run carries both flows 10.1 and 10.3), company and status. |
| **`explain_status_code`** | 🏷️ | The tag and the FR / EN labels of an invoice or e-reporting status code. |
| **`reason_codes`** | 📋 | The PA rejection reasons and expected actions with their labels. |
| **`edirectory_lookup`** | 🏢 | A company in the [e-directory](./edirectory.md) by SIREN, SIRET or name: legal data and routing lines. |
| **`template_settings`** | ⚙️ | The settings of one template, secrets masked. Requires the *Settings access* feature. |

The assistant knows every page of the application — among them the [Billing overview](./billing-overview.md), [Statistics](./statistics.md), the [Explorer](./explorer.md) and the [invoice stages](./invoices.md#status-by-stage) — and answers a question on revenue, credit notes, transmission rate or decisions with `billing_overview`, a question on stages, waiting time or reasons with `status_statistics`. Through the implementation report (`instance_docs`) it also knows the default periods and the dashboard rules of the instance. The two tools answer only when the user's role grants the page (Billing overview, Statistics).

The assistant also receives the live **status catalogue**, so *"en litige"*, *"refused"* or *"awaiting deposit"* map to the right code.

The data tools follow the rights of the signed-in user: the company visibility of the role applies to the invoices, figures and backlog the assistant reads.

### Sample files and mapping

With a file attached, or one of the user's [sample files](./claude-mcp.md#samples), the assistant works as the [XSL editor](../ubl-tools/xsl-editor.md) does:

| Tools | Use |
|---|---|
| **`samples`**, **`sample_structure`**, **`sample_text`** | The user's samples; the structure of an XML sample; its text, in windows. |
| **`pdf_to_xml`** | Converts a PDF sample to the XML NomaUBL builds from it, with a document's settings. |
| **`document_fields`**, **`ubl_variables`**, **`mapping_brief`**, **`read_mapping`** | A document's settings, the variables its rule set requires, the brief of an auto-mapping, the saved mapping. |
| **`check_mapping`**, **`test_transform`** | Checks a mapping on a sample and shows the UBL it gives. |

Nothing is saved: the assistant gives the values to enter in the mapping editor.

### Playbooks

For a diagnosis, the assistant first loads the matching **playbook** (🧭 `load_playbook`), then follows its steps. The built-in playbooks are:

| Playbook | Diagnosis |
|---|---|
| `refused-invoice` | An invoice awaiting an action (213, 9905, 9907, 9904, 207, 208, 210, 221, 206): what was refused, what to correct, how to resubmit — or, for a refusal, the internal credit note to issue. |
| `backlog` | What still awaits an action, for one company or all: to fix and resend, answer to the buyer expected, pending at the platform, deposited but not transmitted. |
| `missing-invoice` | An invoice or a JDE print job that did not reach NomaUBL: which step failed and what to run. |
| `ereporting-error` | A failed e-reporting run (9956 to 9959): the offending data and the correction. |
| `status-not-updated` | An invoice that keeps an old status although the platform moved on. |

The administrator can add playbooks or replace a built-in one under the same name, from the *Custom playbooks* field of the [global settings](../configuration/system/global.md) (*AI* tab).

At most **10 tool calls** are chained for one question. When a tool fails, the assistant gives the tool, the input and the error.

---

## Conversation examples

### Diagnosing the open invoice

> **User** — *(invoice F2026-1203 open)* Why is this invoice in this status?
>
> 🧭 `load_playbook · refused-invoice` &nbsp; 🧾 `invoice_dossier · 1203 RI 00001`
>
> **AI Assistant** — Invoice **F2026-1203** was **refused by the buyer** (status 210) on 2026-10-22 with the reason `PU_ERR` — incorrect unit prices. A refusal requires an internal credit note: cancel the invoice with a credit note, then issue a corrected invoice.
>
> *Follow-ups:* `Show its lifecycle` · `Other refusals this month?`

### Summary of the month

> **User** — Give me this month's invoice summary
>
> 🔍 `period_figures · 2026-10-01 → 2026-10-24`
>
> **AI Assistant** — 1,240 invoices processed (+6 % on September), 1,180 deposited — deposit rate 95 %. 38 await an action: 22 to fix and resend, 16 awaiting an answer to the buyer. First-pass validation: 97 %.
>
> | Awaiting | Count | Oldest |
> |---|---|---|
> | 9905 — Validation failed | 14 | 6 days |
> | 213 — Rejected | 8 | 3 days |
> | 210 — Refused | 16 | 9 days |
>
> *Follow-ups:* `Detail the 9905 errors` · `Which companies are behind?`

### How the product works

> **User** — How do watched folders work?
>
> 📚 `search_docs · watched folders` &nbsp; 📖 `read_doc_page · …/management/watched-folders`
>
> **AI Assistant** — A watched folder is scanned on a schedule; each new file is processed with the document it is bound to… *(Source: Watched Folders — link)*

---

## What the assistant cannot do

- **Change anything.** It only reads. Asked to resend, reprocess or change a setting, it says where in the application to do it.
- **Go beyond your rights.** Invoices and e-reporting runs are those of the companies and row filters of your role; the server log and the IT dashboard need their page; the implementation report and the settings need the *Settings access* feature.
- **Read a file other than XML or PDF.** The paperclip takes `.xml` and `.pdf` files: a PDF up to 10 MB, the first 150,000 characters of an XML.

The administrator sets the API key, the default model, the documentation source, the custom playbooks, the system prompt and the tools from the *AI* tab of the [global settings](../configuration/system/global.md).

The same tools answer **Claude Desktop** and **Claude Code** when the instance opens its MCP endpoint — see [Claude (MCP)](./claude-mcp.md).

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Open the invoice, then ask.** The context chip gives the assistant the invoice; there is nothing to type. Use **×** on the chip to ask a general question without leaving the window.
- **Ask for a period summary in plain words.** *"This month"*, *"last quarter"*, *"our deposit rate"* — the assistant reads the figures of the audit report.
- **Click the follow-ups.** They carry on the diagnosis with the right next check.
- **Start a new chat for a new subject.** A long thread on another topic weighs on the answers.
- **Pick a heavier model for a long diagnosis**, the default for everyday questions.
- **Treat the panel as an external service.** Questions, tool results and attached files are sent to Anthropic — [Data sent to Anthropic](./ai-data-sent.md) lists what goes and what never does; avoid pasting personal data that the screens do not already show.
- **For exhaustive lists, use the dedicated pages.** The assistant characterises a problem; the [E-Invoicing](./invoices.md) list, [Diagnostics](./diagnostics/overview.md) and [Reports](reports/overview.md) give the full picture.

---

## NomaUBL — Claude (MCP)
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/claude-mcp/

NomaUBL in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and claude.ai through the MCP endpoint of the instance: turning it on, the MCP access role feature, the Claude Desktop extension, the sign-in from the client, personal tokens, what Claude can read, sample files, mapping work, changes when allowed, and the usage per user. For JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP alike.

The **MCP endpoint** lets a user question their NomaUBL instance from **Claude Desktop**, **Claude Code** or a **claude.ai connector**, under their own account: invoices and their history, validation errors, e-reporting, dashboards and period figures, the server log, the settings, the documentation. Invoices and e-reporting runs are those of the user's companies and data scope, as in the lists of the application. It is read-only unless the instance allows changes, off by default, and it needs a valid licence.

What goes to Anthropic in that case, and what does not, is described on [Data sent to Anthropic](./ai-data-sent.md).

---

## At a glance

---

## Turn it on \{#enable\}

In **Settings → Global → AI**, group **MCP server** (this editor is in English in the application):

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **MCP endpoint** | `N` | The instance answers at `/mcp`, for the users whose role has *MCP access*. |
| **Allow changes over MCP** | `N` | Claude may save analyses, mappings and documents when the user asks — see [Changes](#changes). Off: read only. |

Sign-in must be enabled on the instance: Claude always acts as a named user.

Behind a reverse proxy, fill in **Public address** in **Settings → Global → Authentication**: the sign-in from Claude uses it, as the password reset links do.

---

## Who may connect \{#access\}

Only the roles that have the **MCP access** feature ([Roles](../configuration/security/roles.md), tab *Access*) can connect Claude; no role has it by default. The other grants of the role then decide what Claude reaches:

| Tools | The role needs |
|---|---|
| Invoices, errors, lifecycle, e-reporting, dashboards, period figures, documentation | *MCP access*. Invoices and e-reporting runs are limited to the companies and the row filters of the role. |
| Server log | The **Server log** page. |
| IT dashboard | The **IT dashboard** page. |
| Data Explorer — model, fields, aggregations, saved analyses | The **Explorer** page. |
| PDF to XML conversion of a sample | The **Process Document** page, or **Settings access**. |
| Implementation report; setup review — configuration objects, configuration check, scheduled jobs, rule sets, licence state, system —; mapping work | **Settings access**. |

A role without a list of allowed pages reaches every page. An invoice outside the user's scope is answered as not found.

---

## Connect Claude \{#connect\}

The server address, the tokens and the extension are in the **Claude (MCP)** tab of the profile window (the user button of the top bar).

| Way | For | Steps |
|---|---|---|
| **Claude Desktop extension** | Claude Desktop, including for an instance that is not reachable from the internet. | **Extension** downloads a `.mcpb` file. Open it with Claude Desktop: the server address is already filled in, and the extension asks for the personal token. Nothing else to install. |
| **Sign-in from the client** | Claude Code; a claude.ai connector when the instance is reachable from the internet. | Give the client the **Server address** only. The browser opens NomaUBL: sign in as usual (password or SSO), then on *Connect Claude to NomaUBL* choose 30, 90 or 365 days and click **Allow** (or **Refuse**). |
| **Pasted token** | Claude Code, a script. | **Create a token**, copy it — *shown once, copy it now* — and give it to the client as the request header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. |

The extension has four settings in Claude Desktop: **NomaUBL address**, **Personal token**, **Samples folder** (optional — the only folder Claude may send files from) and **Accept an internal certificate** (for a self-signed or company certificate). They are in the language of the interface the extension was downloaded from.

The extension carries the environment and the address of its instance in its name — *NomaUBL – prod · nomaubl.example.com* — so the extensions of several instances install side by side, each with its own token. Claude is told which instance it is talking to and says which one an answer concerns.

| Answer of the endpoint | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `404` | The MCP endpoint is off. |
| `401` | No token, or a token that is unknown, expired or revoked. |
| `403` | The role has no *MCP access*, or the instance has no valid licence. |

---

## Tokens \{#tokens\}

**Your tokens** lists the user's tokens and the accesses opened by a sign-in from Claude. Each line gives its origin — the name of the client the access was allowed for, or *created here* for a token created in this tab — and its creation and expiry dates; **Revoke** ends one at once. A token is valid 30, 90 or 365 days.

A password change — by the user or by an administrator — and the deactivation of the account remove the user's tokens: an account enabled again starts without any. A token also stops working when the role loses *MCP access*.

The server keeps a fingerprint of the token, never the token itself.

---

## What Claude can do \{#tools\}

| Subject | Claude can |
|---|---|
| **Invoices** | List invoices, read one in full (header, lines, VAT, validation errors, lifecycle with the platform's reasons), list the e-reporting runs. |
| **Figures** | Read the [Billing overview](./billing-overview.md), [Statistics](./statistics.md), [Operations](./dashboard.md) and [IT dashboard](./tech-dashboard.md) figures and the summary of a period. |
| **Data Explorer** | Run any aggregation of the [Explorer](./explorer.md) — grouping, measures, filters, period, Top N — and the saved analyses. |
| **Diagnosis** | Read the server log, the integrity checks, the status and reason codes, the e-directory, and follow the diagnostic playbooks. |
| **Setup review** | Read the configuration objects, the configuration check, the scheduled jobs, the rule sets, the licence state and the settings — secrets are never shown. |
| **Documentation** | Search and read the NomaUBL documentation and the implementation report of the instance. |
| **Samples and mapping** | Read the structure of an XML sample, convert a PDF sample with a document's settings, propose and check a mapping — see below. |

A result longer than 60,000 characters is cut, and Claude is asked to narrow its request.

---

## Sample files \{#samples\}

A customer's XML or PDF can be given to Claude to work on:

- from the profile window: **Sample files** tab, button **Add**;
- from Claude Desktop, which sends a file of the **Samples folder** chosen in the extension's settings, and of no other folder, when the user asks it to work on one.

Samples are `.xml` or `.pdf` files of 20 MB at most, 50 per user, kept 7 days and then removed by the server. They are working copies of one user: they are never processed as invoices nor sent to the platform.

The **Sample files** tab is shown to every user, with or without *MCP access*: a file attached in the [AI assistant](./ai-capabilities.md) is listed there too, and deleted there.

With a sample, Claude reads the structure of an XML, or converts a PDF with a document's settings and tries table anchors without saving. With **Settings access** it also does the mapping work of the [XSL editor](../ubl-tools/xsl-editor.md): it proposes the mapping of a sample (and, for a text PDF, the extraction rules), reads a document's saved mapping and the variables its rule set requires, checks a mapping on a sample and shows the UBL it gives. The sample follows the steps of a real run: a PDF converted as a text PDF or a JD Edwards PDF according to the document, the pre-processing stylesheet, the split into invoices, the sign inversion. Nothing is saved: Claude gives the values to enter in the mapping editor.

---

## Changes \{#changes\}

With **Allow changes over MCP**, Claude can, when the user asks:

| Change | The role needs |
|---|---|
| Save an Explorer analysis. | The **Explorer** page. |
| Save mapping values in a document's stylesheet. | **Settings access**. |
| Save a document's PDF to XML settings. | **Settings access**. |
| Create a document — by source: XML, PDF, UBL or connector, with its own blank stylesheet or from an existing one — or update its settings. | **Settings access**. |

Each source keeps its own rules: text PDF settings are refused on a JD Edwards document and the reverse, and a UBL document has no mapping. Passwords, tokens and keys cannot be set this way. The previous version stays in the [file history](../management/file-versions.md) or the configuration history, and every change is written to the server log with the user's name. Claude asks the user before a call that changes something.

---

## Usage \{#usage\}

The [AI usage](./diagnostics/ai-usage.md) view of Diagnostics lists the calls made from Claude under the channel *Claude (MCP)* — by user, by day and by tool, with those that failed and those that saved a change. The [server log](./diagnostics/server-log.md) holds one line per failed call and one per change; a successful read leaves no line.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Grant *MCP access* to a dedicated role first.** The grants of the role are what Claude reaches: the Explorer page and Settings access open the corresponding tools.
- **Keep *Allow changes over MCP* off on production** until the mapping work is finished on a test instance; [Promotion](../management/promotion.md) then carries the result.
- **Prefer the extension for an internal server.** A claude.ai connector is called from the internet; the extension calls the instance from the user's computer.
- **Revoke rather than wait.** A token no longer used is ended from the profile in one click.

---

## NomaUBL — Data sent to Anthropic
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/ai-data-sent/

What NomaUBL sends to Anthropic and what it never sends: the AI assistant of the application (the question, the page context, the tool results, the attached file, with the API key of the instance) and Claude connected through MCP (NomaUBL only answers tool calls; the user's Claude client talks to Anthropic). What stays on the server, what is never exposed, and the switches that decide.

NomaUBL uses Anthropic's models in two ways, and the path of the data is not the same:

- the **[AI assistant](./ai-capabilities.md)** of the application — the server calls Anthropic's API with the API key of the instance;
- **[Claude connected through MCP](./claude-mcp.md)** — NomaUBL calls nobody: it answers the tool calls of the user's Claude client, and that client talks to Anthropic under the user's own Claude account.

Nothing is sent while nobody asks a question: no background send, no telemetry, no other AI provider.

---

## At a glance

---

## The AI assistant \{#assistant\}

Each question is sent to `api.anthropic.com` with the **API Key** of **Settings → Global → AI**. A request holds:

| Sent | Content |
|---|---|
| **Instructions** | The built-in NomaUBL prompt, or the *System Prompt* of the instance in its place; the status catalogue; the names of the playbooks. |
| **Page context** | The current page and its filter, the language, and the open invoice: document, type, company, number, status, customer. 4,000 characters at most. |
| **Conversation** | The questions and the answers of the conversation in progress — the last 40 messages, kept in the user's browser. |
| **Tool results** | What each tool read to answer, as it read it: invoices (customer name, amounts, VAT, status, messages), lines, lifecycle, validation errors, period figures, dashboards, e-reporting runs, e-directory data, lines of the server log, sections of the implementation report, settings with secrets masked. A result is cut at 60,000 characters; a list holds 50 invoices at most, the server log 300 lines. |
| **Attached file** | An XML as text, up to 150,000 characters; a PDF as it is, up to 10 MB. The file is sent again with each later question of the same conversation. |

Two other screens call the same API:

| Screen | Sent |
|---|---|
| **AI mapping** of the [XSL editor](../ubl-tools/xsl-editor.md) | The paths of the sample with the first value of each (120 characters at most), the text rows of a PDF, the list of variables — and the PDF itself when the sample is one. |
| Documentation in *Sitemap* mode | Nothing more from NomaUBL: Anthropic fetches the pages of the allowed documentation domains itself. |

Business data is sent as the tools read it: no customer name, amount or e-mail address is replaced or hidden. Only the secrets are masked — see [below](#never).

---

## Claude through MCP \{#mcp\}

| Step | Who talks to whom |
|---|---|
| The user asks Claude a question. | The Claude client ↔ Anthropic, under the user's Claude account. |
| Claude calls a NomaUBL tool. | The client → the instance, with the user's personal token. |
| NomaUBL answers. | The instance → the client: the result of that tool, 60,000 characters at most. |
| Claude writes its answer. | The client → Anthropic: the conversation, with the results it received. |

**NomaUBL makes no call to Anthropic here, and the API key of the instance is not used.** What a tool returned leaves the instance towards the user's Claude client, and from there to Anthropic on the terms of the user's Claude plan — not on those of the instance's API key.

Where the call comes from depends on the client:

| Client | The instance is called from |
|---|---|
| Claude Desktop with the extension, Claude Code | The user's computer: an internal address or a VPN is enough. |
| A claude.ai connector | Anthropic's servers: the instance must be reachable from the internet. |

The Claude Desktop extension runs a small relay on the user's computer. It reads one folder only — the **Samples folder** chosen in its settings — and sends NomaUBL a file of that folder only when the user asks Claude to work on it.

---

## What is never sent \{#never\}

| Never sent | How |
|---|---|
| Passwords, tokens, API keys, client secrets, the licence key | A setting whose name marks it as a secret is given as `***`; the licence is described by its state, never by its key. |
| The personal tokens | The server keeps their fingerprint only. |
| A file nobody attached or asked for | The assistant reads the attached file; over MCP, Claude reads the user's own samples. |
| Anything a switched-off tool would read | *Custom Tools* at `N`: the assistant keeps the documentation only. *MCP endpoint* at `N`: no client can connect. |
| Changes | The assistant only reads. Over MCP, a change needs *Allow changes over MCP*, and secrets cannot be set that way. |

---

## What stays on the server \{#stays\}

| Kept | Where, how long |
|---|---|
| The conversation of the assistant | In the user's browser (the last 40 messages); not on the server. |
| Sample files and files attached in the assistant | On the server, per user, 7 days. |
| AI usage | For each turn of the assistant, of the auto-map and of Claude (MCP): who, when, the model, the tokens, and each tool's name and input summary — for 90 days by default; never the question, the answer or what a tool returned. See [AI usage](./diagnostics/ai-usage.md). |
| MCP calls in the server log | One line per failed call and one per change, with the user, the tool and the beginning of its arguments and of its result. A successful read leaves no line. |

---

## What decides \{#controls\}

| Switch | Where | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **API Key** | Settings → Global → AI | No key: no assistant, nothing sent. |
| **Custom Tools** | Settings → Global → AI | `N`: the assistant answers from the documentation, without reading the data of the instance. |
| **MCP endpoint** | Settings → Global → AI → MCP server | `N` (default): no Claude client can connect. |
| **Allow changes over MCP** | Same group | `N` (default): read only. |
| **MCP access** | [Roles](../configuration/security/roles.md) → Access → Features | Which users may connect Claude; no role by default. |
| **Explorer** page, **Settings access** | Roles | Which tool groups a user's Claude reaches. |
| **Server log** and **IT dashboard** pages, **Settings access** | Roles | Who may have the server log, the IT dashboard and the implementation report read, in the assistant and from Claude. |
| Companies and row filters | Roles → Data scope | The invoices and e-reporting runs a question can reach. |

---

## To know before opening it widely \{#limits\}

- **The tools read what the screens show.** A customer name, an amount, an e-mail address of the users list in the implementation report go to the model when a tool reads them.
- **Invoices and e-reporting runs follow the role.** The assistant and Claude read those of the user's companies and row filters, as the lists of the application do.
- **The server log, the IT dashboard and the implementation report are those of the whole instance.** A tool gives them only to a role that has the matching page — *Server log*, *IT dashboard* — or, for the implementation report, *Settings access*.
- **What the user types or attaches is theirs to check.** A file attached in the assistant is sent as it is.
- **The use Anthropic makes of what it receives** depends on the contract of the instance's API key for the assistant, and on the user's Claude plan for MCP.

---

## NomaUBL — AI usage
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/diagnostics/ai-usage/

The AI usage view of NomaUBL Diagnostics shows what the in-app assistant, the mapping auto-map and Claude (MCP) were used for: turns, users, tokens with the share read from the cache, tool calls and failures — by user, day, channel, model and tool — and each turn with its tools. What is kept, what never is, and for how long.

The **AI usage** view of [Diagnostics](./overview.md) shows what the AI was used for on the instance, by whom, and what it cost in tokens. It covers the three ways the AI is reached: the [in-app assistant](../ai-capabilities.md), the auto-map of the [mapping editor](../../ubl-tools/xsl-editor.md) and [Claude connected through MCP](../claude-mcp.md).

Open it from **Diagnostics → AI usage**. The view is granted per role, as **AI usage view** ([Roles](../../configuration/security/roles.md)).

---

## At a glance

---

## What is kept \{#record\}

Each turn leaves one record: who, when, the channel, the page the question was asked from, the model, the tokens (read, written, read from and written to the cache), the time it took and how it ended. Each tool called during the turn is kept with its name, a summary of its input, its time, the size of its answer, whether it failed and why, and whether it saved a change.

**The question, the answer and what a tool returned are never kept.**

| Channel | One turn is |
|---|---|
| **In-app assistant** | A question asked in the assistant of the application. |
| **Mapping auto-map** | An auto-map run from the mapping editor. |
| **Claude (MCP)** | A tool called by a user's Claude client. No model and no tokens: they are those of the user's Claude plan. |

---

## The period in figures \{#figures\}

The period is **7 days**, **30 days** (default) or **90 days**.

| Tile | Shows |
|---|---|
| **Turns** | Turns over the period. |
| **Users** | Users with at least one turn. |
| **Tokens in** | Everything the model read, with the share read from the cache (*68 % cached*), billed at a fraction of the price. |
| **Tokens out** | What the model wrote. |
| **Tool calls** | Tools called, with the number that failed. |
| **Average turn** | Average time of a turn. |

Below the tiles, a bar chart gives the turns per day.

---

## Breakdowns \{#breakdowns\}

**Breakdown** switches the list:

| Choice | Rows and columns |
|---|---|
| **Turns** | The latest turns: When, User, Channel, Page, Model, Tokens in, Cached %, Tokens out, Tool calls, Tool failures, Time (s), Outcome, Tools. |
| **By user**, **By day**, **By channel**, **By model** | Turns, Tokens in, Cached %, Tokens out, Tool calls, Tool failures, Failed turns. |
| **By tool** | Calls, Failed, Changes, Average time (ms), Average answer (characters). |

The list sorts, filters and exports like the other lists of the application.

---

## One turn \{#turn\}

A click on a turn opens it: its outcome — *Answered*, *Failed*, *Stopped by the user* or *Cut short* (the answer reached its length limit) —, its time, its model and tokens, the page it was asked from, then one line per tool with the summary of its input, its time and the size of its answer. A tool that saved something is marked *saved a change*; a failed one shows its reason in red.

---

## How long it is kept \{#retention\}

90 days by default. **AI usage kept (days)**, in **Settings → Global → AI**, sets another duration.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Read *By tool* after opening MCP.** The **Changes** column says which tools saved something, and **Failed** points at a missing grant or a question the tools cannot answer.
- **A low cached share on long conversations** means a prompt that changes at every turn: check the *System Prompt* and the custom playbooks.
- **Grant the view to those who follow the cost**, not only to administrators: it shows no question and no data of the instance.

---

---

# === Liberty Next — framework ===

## Liberty Next — The sales demo
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/demo-app/

The Sales demo application shipped with Liberty Next: invoice lines loaded from Excel by period, period validation and closing, a home dashboard, the Data Explorer with ready-made analyses, the AI assistant's starter questions, a monthly digest e-mailed by Nomaflow, and three demo users who see different rows — every feature built in the Liberty Next pages, without code.

**Sales demo** is a small application shipped with Liberty Next to show, on one coherent subject, what the framework does without code: monthly invoice lines loaded from Excel, periods validated then closed, a home dashboard, free analysis in the Data Explorer, the AI assistant, a digest e-mailed every month, and users who see only their own company. Everything in it is configuration — connector, dictionary, screens, menus, dashboards, model, jobs — readable and editable in the Liberty Next pages — the [Studio](./studio.md) shows it as a map.

It is a showcase, not a product: open it to see a feature at work, copy what fits into an application of your own.

---

## At a glance

---

## The data \{#data\}

| Table | Holds |
|---|---|
| **Items** | The items, with their family and sub-family. |
| **Companies** | The companies, with their business unit, region and currency. |
| **Customers** | The customers met in the sales; the codes are added by each load, the names completed by hand. |
| **Sales lines** | One row per invoice line: period, company, item, customer, destination country, quantity, weight, revenue in the company's currency. |
| **Periods** | One row per loaded period: status (*open*, *validated*, *closed*), number of companies and lines, quantity, who changed the status and when, a comment. |

The revenue is in each company's own currency: it is never summed across currencies, so the analyses give it per currency or per company.

---

## The screens \{#screens\}

- **Sales → Sales lines**: the invoice lines, read-only, up to 5,000 rows. The grid opens empty: pick a period, a business unit, a family… first. The filters cascade — the companies follow the business unit, the sub-families the family, the items both.
- **Sales → Periods**: the loaded periods. The row menu offers **Validate**, **Close** and **Reopen**, each after a confirmation. A **closed** period is read-only in the grid — see [Conditional fields](./build/screens/conditional-fields.md) — and a new load of that period is refused.
- **Reference data → Items, Companies, Customers**: the reference tables, editable.

---

## Loading the files \{#loads\}

The **Import** folder of the menu holds the loads, each a [job page](../nomaflow/jobs/run-from-menu.md) where the user picks the file, runs it and follows its log:

| Entry | Job | Does |
|---|---|---|
| **Items file** | `nomademo-load-items` | Loads the item file (sheet *Items*: code, name, family, sub-family), replacing the table. |
| **Companies file** | `nomademo-load-companies` | Loads the company file (sheet *Companies*: code, name, business unit, region, currency), replacing the table. |
| **Sales file (one month)** | `nomademo-load-sales` | Loads one month of invoice lines (sheet *Sales*). |
| **Refresh periods** | `nomademo-refresh-periods` | Rebuilds the period rows from the loaded lines, keeping their status. |
| **Load the sample files** | `nomademo-load-samples` | Loads the sample files shipped with the demo — every file at once, no upload. Run it again any time to reset the demo. |

The **sample files** ship with the application: about 320 items in six families, 14 companies in six business units, and six months of invoice lines (October to March). The data is synthetic and anonymous; a reload gives the same figures.

The sales load shows the [`file_load` step](../nomaflow/steps.md#file-load) at work:

- it **replaces** the partitions the file carries — year, month and company — in one transaction: reloading a corrected month replaces that month only, and a failed load leaves the previous data in place;
- a **guard** refuses the file when one of its periods is closed, with the reason in the log;
- rejected rows are offered for download under the log;
- the following steps add the new customers and refresh the period rows.

Two more jobs are run from **Nomaflow → Jobs**: `nomademo-init-db` creates the tables, `nomademo-demo-accounts` creates the demo users ([below](#accounts)). The jobs are delivered without a schedule.

---

## The home dashboard \{#dashboard\}

**Overview** is the application's home page: the [dashboard](./dashboards.md) *Sales overview*, built on the synthesis widgets.

| Widget | Shows |
|---|---|
| **Invoice lines**, **Latest period**, **Periods**, **Items sold** | The figures, with a detail line: units, companies and customers; the latest period and its quantity; the periods still open; the families. |
| **Monthly quantity by business unit** | One series per business unit, per period. |
| **What needs attention** | The open periods to close, the companies without sales in the latest period. |
| **Revenue by currency**, **Quantity by family** | Proportion bars — the totals first, then per business unit. The revenue is never added across currencies. |
| **Periods** | Each period's status, who changed it and when. |
| **Top items**, **Quantity by business unit** | The largest quantities. |

The bar carries a **period** (all dates when the page opens) and a **Business unit** filter that narrows every widget whose query returns the business unit — no screen needed behind the widgets.

---

## The Data Explorer \{#explorer\}

**Data Explorer**, right under **Overview**, opens the [Data Explorer](./explorer/overview.md) on the *Sales* model: the invoice lines at the centre, with the item (family, sub-family), the company (business unit, currency) and the customer around them.

The model ships ten shared analyses — quantity by business unit, by company, by family; revenue by currency, by business unit, by company; the monthly quantity, alone and by business unit as a pivot; the top items; the number of invoice lines — and the *Sales overview* dashboard that gathers them. They are a starting point: open one, change it, save it under another name.

---

## The AI assistant \{#ai\}

The application ships its [starter questions](./ai-assistant.md#starters) under four headings — *Sales*, *Periods*, *Loads*, *Reference data* — with *Which business unit sold the most last month?* or *How do I reload a month that was wrong?*. The *Sales lines* screen has its own, which use the page context: *Sum the quantities of the rows I see, by business unit*.

Three [playbooks](./ai-assistant.md#playbooks) — *Load a month of sales*, *Validate or close a period*, *Analyse quantities and revenue* — let the assistant walk a user through the application's procedures. All of it is visible and editable in **Liberty Next → Logic → AI**.

---

## The monthly digest \{#digest\}

`nomademo-monthly-digest` is a scheduled digest without code:

1. two [`report` steps](../nomaflow/steps.md#report) render the analyses *Revenue by business unit* and *Quantity by company* to Excel, over the previous month;
2. a [`notify` step](../nomaflow/steps.md#notify) sends them to the holders of the group role, the two files attached.

Schedule it on the first of the month once the e-mail account is set in [Notifications](../nomaflow/notifications.md#smtp).

---

## Three users, three views \{#accounts\}

`nomademo-demo-accounts` creates two roles and three users, password `demo`:

| User | Role | Sees |
|---|---|---|
| `demo_group` | `nomademo_group` | Everything. |
| `demo_bu` | `nomademo_scoped` | The companies of one business unit. |
| `demo_company` | `nomademo_scoped` | One company. |

Both roles grant the same things: the application's queries, its Data Explorer models and the assistant. The scoped role adds a [data scope](./build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md#data-scope) on the company, whose values come from each user's *companies* attribute. Sign in as each user in turn: the same screens, dashboard, analyses and exports show other rows, the totals included.

Load the companies (or the sample files) before running this job: it reads them to fill the users' attributes.

---

## Setting it up \{#setup\}

1. In **Liberty Next → Administer → Pools**, a pool named `nomademo` pointing at an empty database.
2. In Nomaflow, run `nomademo-init-db`.
3. Open **Sales demo** from the application switcher, then **Import → Load the sample files**.
4. Run `nomademo-demo-accounts` in Nomaflow to create the demo users.

---

## What's next

- [Dashboards](./dashboards.md) — the widgets and the export.
- [Data Explorer](./explorer/overview.md) — models, analyses, dashboards.
- [Steps](../nomaflow/steps.md) — file loads, reports and notifications.
- [Roles and permissions](./build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md) — the data scope.

## Liberty Next — First app walkthrough
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/getting-started/first-app/

Build a working Liberty Next app end to end: a pool, a SQL connector with its queries generated from a table, a screen with a grid and an edit dialog, and a menu entry — all from Settings, applied without a restart.

This page goes from an empty install to a working app — a sidebar entry that opens a grid on a table, with an edit dialog. Everything is done from **Settings** (superuser), nothing is edited by hand.

Four elements, in order — **pool → connector → screen → menu** — each saved and applied at once.

---

## At a glance

The example uses the `default` pool and a small `tasks` table.

---

## Step 1 — The pool \{#pool\}

Open **Liberty Next → Administer → Pools**. The installation created the `default` pool: on a Docker install it points at the bundled PostgreSQL database, on a Python install without PostgreSQL at a local SQLite file. It is enough for this walkthrough. To work on another database, add a pool with its URL — see [Connectors](../connectors.md#pools).

Create the example table with any SQL client connected to that database:

```sql
CREATE TABLE tasks (
  id        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  title     VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
  status    VARCHAR(10)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',
  due_date  DATE
);
INSERT INTO tasks (id, title, status, due_date) VALUES
  (1, 'Draft sprint plan',      'open', '2026-06-10'),
  (2, 'Review pull request 42', 'done', '2026-06-05'),
  (3, 'Customer follow-up',     'open', '2026-06-12');
```

---

## Step 2 — The connector and its queries \{#connector\}

1. **Liberty Next → Data → Connectors → ＋ Connector**: name `tasks`, type **SQL**, pool `default`. Save.
2. With `tasks` selected, pick the **Tables** stage card, then **＋ Add queries → Generate from DB**.
3. In the CRUD wizard, pick the `tasks` table, keep every column, tick **key** on `ID`, and keep the four statements (SELECT, UPDATE, INSERT, DELETE).
4. Save. The connector now holds `tasks_get`, `tasks_put`, `tasks_post` and `tasks_delete`:

```sql
SELECT ID, TITLE, STATUS, DUE_DATE FROM tasks
UPDATE tasks SET TITLE = :TITLE, STATUS = :STATUS, DUE_DATE = :DUE_DATE WHERE ID = :ID_ORIGINAL
```

The columns are read from the database when the query runs; nothing else needs declaring. See [Create from a database table](../build/queries/create-from-database.md).

---

## Step 3 — The screen \{#screen\}

1. **Liberty Next → Screens → Screens → ＋ Add scope**, pick `tasks`: the `tasks` chip appears.
2. **＋ Add screen**, id `tasks`. Click the new card: the [Screen Designer](../build/screens/overview.md) opens on its stages — *What it is*, *Data*, *Grid*, *Record form*, *Actions*, *Output*.
3. **What it is**: label `Tasks`.
4. **Data**: **Fill from table** `tasks` sets the four queries at once — read `tasks_get`, update `tasks_put`, insert `tasks_post`, delete `tasks_delete`.
5. **Record form**: place the columns on the form.
6. **Save**.

The grid columns come from the read query; their labels and formats from the [dictionary](../dictionary.md) when entries exist (its **Scan a table** button proposes them). The [Screen Creation Assistant](../build/screen-assistant.md) does steps 2 and 3 in one pass for a table.

---

## Step 4 — The menu entry \{#menu\}

1. **Liberty Next → Screens → Menus → + Add scope**, pick `tasks`: the empty tree of the app appears.
2. **＋ Item**, then in the inspector: label `Tasks`, icon `table`, type `screen`, target `tasks` (the screen of step 3).
3. Save.

With a menu, and **Show in switcher** on in the connector's settings, `tasks` is an app: it appears in the app picker, and its sidebar shows **Tasks**. A click opens the grid: a row opens the edit dialog, **＋ Add** an empty one. See [Build the tree](../build/menus/build-the-tree.md) and [Make a connector an app](../build/menus/make-connector-an-app.md).

---

## What you have now

- **A pool** — the database connection.
- **A connector** — the four queries on the table.
- **A screen** — the grid and the dialog on these queries.
- **A menu** — the entry that opens the screen; with **Show in switcher** on, it makes the connector an app.

Every save was applied without a restart. The pool and the connector are stored in `connectors.toml`, the screen in `screens.toml`, the menu in `menus.toml`.

## Liberty Next — Project layout
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/getting-started/project-layout/

File map of the two repositories — liberty-next (framework binary) and liberty-apps (per-installation configuration). What lives where, what is committed, what is per-installation, and how LIBERTY_APPS_DIR routes the framework to the apps repo.

The Liberty Framework is split between **two repositories** that work together at runtime: the framework binary (`liberty-next`) reads its per-section configuration from the apps repo (`liberty-apps`). This page is the file map — where each piece lives, what is committed, what is per-installation.

---

## At a glance

The framework is told where the apps repo lives via the `LIBERTY_APPS_DIR` environment variable. Out of the box, with `LIBERTY_APPS_DIR` unset, the framework reads its per-section TOML from `liberty-next/config/` — convenient for local experimentation but not the production layout.

---

## `liberty-next` — the framework binary

```text
liberty-next/
├── start.sh                  ← run/dev helper (build, init-db, init-config, …)
├── pyproject.toml            ← Python deps + CLI entry points
├── liberty/                  ← FastAPI backend (Python 3.12)
│   ├── main.py               ← app factory, lifespan, routers
│   ├── config.py             ← TOML loading + env expansion
│   ├── connectors/           ← SQL / API connector engine, dictionary (dictionary.py)
│   ├── auth/                 ← local users, OIDC, JWT, permissions
│   ├── screens/              ← screen engine (grid + dialog runtime)
│   ├── dashboards/           ← dashboard layout + widget rendering
│   ├── charts/               ← chart definitions
│   ├── menus/                ← menu tree + permission pruning
│   ├── jobs/                 ← Nomaflow (jobs, steps, scheduler)
│   ├── actions/              ← services
│   ├── notify/               ← notifications
│   ├── ai/                   ← Anthropic tool-use assistant
│   ├── licensing/            ← RS256 license-key verification
│   ├── web/                  ← HTTP routes (one module per area)
│   └── *_cli.py              ← CLI entry points (admin, connectors, crypto, license)
│
├── frontend/                 ← React 19 + Vite SPA (built to frontend/dist/)
│   └── src/
│       ├── pages/            ← pages, including Settings/ (one editor per configuration type)
│       ├── common/           ← shared UI parts (fields, lists, dialogs, SQL editor…)
│       ├── components/       ← layout (sidebar, app picker, tabs)
│       ├── locales/          ← interface texts, en and fr
│       └── api/              ← REST client
│
├── config/                   ← bundled templates + per-installation files
│   ├── app.toml              ← application settings — edited in Liberty Next → Administer → App
│   ├── auth.toml             ← local users — created by init-db, gitignored
│   ├── *.toml.example        ← templates for connectors / dictionary / menus / screens / charts / dashboards
│   └── *.toml                ← real per-section files (only when LIBERTY_APPS_DIR is unset)
│
├── tests/                    ← pytest suite
└── docs/                     ← framework-internal planning notes (not the public docs)
```

| File | Status | Edited by |
|---|---|---|
| `liberty/`, `frontend/`, `pyproject.toml`, `start.sh` | Committed | Framework maintainers — *don't* edit per-installation. |
| `config/app.toml` | Per-installation | Liberty Next → Administer → App. |
| `config/auth.toml` | Per-installation, gitignored | `liberty-admin` CLI / the Liberty Next pages. |
| `config/*.toml.example` | Committed | Framework maintainers — bundled templates. |
| `config/*.toml` (without `.example`) | Per-installation, gitignored | Editable from the Liberty Next pages when `LIBERTY_APPS_DIR` is unset. |

---

## `liberty-apps` — your configuration

```text
liberty-apps/
├── README.md
├── config/                   ← per-section TOML — read by liberty-next at runtime
│   ├── connectors.toml       ← pools, connectors and their queries / endpoints
│   ├── dictionary.toml       ← data items, enums, lookups, sequences
│   ├── menus.toml            ← one menu per app
│   ├── screens.toml          ← grids and dialogs
│   ├── charts.toml           ← saved charts
│   ├── dashboards.toml       ← dashboards
│   ├── actions.toml          ← services
│   ├── explorer.toml         ← Data Explorer models shipped with the apps
│   ├── ai.toml               ← starter questions and playbooks for the AI assistant
│   ├── theme.toml            ← colours and branding
│   └── tests/                ← test suites, one file per suite
│
├── plugins/                  ← Python packages (functions called by steps and actions)
│   ├── <package>/            ← one folder per package, with __init__.py
│   └── nomaflow/
│       └── jobs.toml         ← the Nomaflow job catalogue
│
└── docs/                     ← deployment & operations notes (per-installation)
```

| File | Edited by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `config/connectors.toml` | *Data → Connectors* | Owns the pool registry plus every connector. |
| `config/dictionary.toml` | *Data → Dictionary* | Per-column metadata reused by screens and charts. |
| `config/menus.toml` | *Screens → Menus* | One root per app, optional folder/leaf hierarchy. |
| `config/screens.toml` | *Screens → Screens* | Grids + dialogs + per-field conditions. |
| `config/dashboards.toml` | *Insight → Dashboards* | KPI, chart and table widgets. |
| `config/charts.toml` | *Insight → Charts* | Chart definitions referenced by dashboards. |
| `config/actions.toml` | *Logic → Services* | Services called by screens, jobs and endpoints. |
| `config/explorer.toml` | *Insight → Explorer* | Explorer models and their bundled analyses. |
| `config/ai.toml` | *Logic → AI* | Starter questions and playbooks the apps ship. |
| `config/tests/<suite>.toml` | *Logic → Tests* | Test cases, packaged and delivered with the app. |
| `config/theme.toml` | *Administer → Theme* | Colours and branding. |
| `plugins/nomaflow/jobs.toml` | Nomaflow → *Jobs* | The job catalogue. |
| `plugins/*/*.py` | Developer | Custom step callables — exposed to the framework via `sys.path`. |

Every file is plain TOML you can read with `cat`, diff with `git`, edit in `vim`. The Liberty Next pages uses the same on-disk format — what you save in the browser is what `git status` reports.

---

## How the framework finds your config

The wiring is one environment variable:

```bash
export LIBERTY_APPS_DIR="$HOME/work/liberty-apps/config"
```

When `LIBERTY_APPS_DIR` is **set**:

| Config | Read from |
|---|---|
| `connectors.toml`, `dictionary.toml`, `menus.toml`, `screens.toml`, `charts.toml`, `dashboards.toml` | `${LIBERTY_APPS_DIR}/<name>.toml` |
| `app.toml` | `liberty-next/config/app.toml` *(stays per-host)* |
| `auth.toml` | `liberty-next/config/auth.toml` *(stays per-host)* |
| `plugins/` packages | `${LIBERTY_APPS_DIR}/../plugins/` added to `sys.path` |

When `LIBERTY_APPS_DIR` is **unset**, every file is read from `liberty-next/config/`. Convenient for a single-host dev install; in production keep them separate.

The full env-var contract is documented under [Configuration → Environment variables](../configuration/environment-variables.md).

---

## Naming conventions

- **App identifier** — every screen, menu and job carries an `app` field (e.g. `nomajde`, `nomasx1`, `tutorial`). It's the namespace for screen ids and the prefix of the sidebar entry.
- **Connector name** — short, kebab-case (`jdedwards`, `tasks`, `crm-sql`). The same name surfaces in the catalog page, the AI assistant tool list and the URL of a query.
- **Pool name** — short, lowercase. `default` is reserved for the framework's own pool.
- **Permission code** — `sql:<connector>:<query>` for SQL queries and `api:<connector>:<endpoint>` for HTTP/API endpoints. The Liberty Next pages builds them automatically; no manual code is needed.

---

## Version control conventions

- `liberty-next` is upgraded by **switching git tags** — the framework binary is treated as an external dependency, not modified in place. The `liberty-apps` repo stays untouched across framework upgrades.
- `liberty-apps` is committed normally — every TOML edit done in the Liberty Next pages ends up as a diff in the repo. Commits made by the operator are reviewable like any other code change.
- Secrets — JWT signing key, master key, license key, AI key — live in the **environment**, not in either repo. See [Encryption & secrets](../configuration/encryption-secrets.md).

---

## What's next

- [The Liberty Next workspace](../configuration/settings-ui.md) — the in-browser editor for everything under `liberty-apps/config/`.
- [Apps & Plugins → Apps](../apps/overview.md) — how to organise multiple apps inside `liberty-apps`.

## Liberty Next — Installation — overview
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/overview/

How to install Liberty Next: pick Docker (light or full layout) or a Python install, run one command, sign in, add the licence and the licensed apps, switch on HTTPS. Every step afterwards — status, backup, upgrade, rollback — goes through the same command.

Liberty Next is one server — a web application, its API and its job scheduler in a single process — plus a database and a folder of configuration files. Installing it means choosing where that server runs; everything after that is done with **one command**: `./liberty` on a Docker host, `liberty-ops` on a Python install.

---

## At a glance

---

## Which installation? \{#choose\}

| You want… | Install | Page |
|---|---|---|
| A production or test server for several users | **Docker — full layout**: Liberty Next, PostgreSQL, Traefik (HTTPS), pgAdmin, Portainer on one host | [Docker](./docker.md#full) |
| A quick trial or a demo on a laptop | **Docker — light layout**: one container, SQLite | [Docker](./docker.md#light) |
| A host where Docker is not allowed | **Python install** with pipx, run by systemd, PostgreSQL of your own | [Python server](./python-server.md) |
| Several nodes in a Docker Swarm | **Swarm**: the full layout adapted to `docker stack deploy` | [Docker](./docker.md#swarm) |

The licensed applications (Nomasx-1, Nomajde) and the bundled Nomaflow jobs need PostgreSQL: choose the full layout or a Python install with your own PostgreSQL.

---

## Install in three commands \{#quickstart\}

On a Linux host with Docker and the Compose plugin:

```bash
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/fblettner/liberty-next.git
cd liberty-next && git sparse-checkout set release && cd release
./liberty install full          # or: ./liberty install light
```

The command generates the secrets, starts the stack, waits until it answers and prints the sign-in details. Open `http://<host>/` (port `8000` on the light layout), sign in as **`admin`** with the printed password, and the server is ready.

Then, in this order and only if you need them:

1. **Licence** — *Liberty Next → Administer → App → License*: paste the key you were delivered.
2. **Licensed apps** — `./liberty apps liberty_apps-<version>-py3-none-any.whl` ([Licensed apps](./deploy-prebuilt-apps.md)).
3. **HTTPS** — `./liberty ssl letsencrypt --domain liberty.example.com --email ops@example.com` ([HTTPS and Traefik](./traefik.md)).

---

## The one command \{#one-command\}

Every operation on a Docker install goes through `release/liberty`, run from the `release/` folder:

| Command | Use it to |
|---|---|
| `./liberty install [light\|full]` | Install (once). |
| `./liberty status` | See versions, health, pending migrations, last upgrade. |
| `./liberty doctor` | List what is wrong and how to fix it. |
| `./liberty apps <wheel>` | Add or refresh the licensed apps. |
| `./liberty ssl letsencrypt\|provided\|off` | Switch HTTPS on, change mode or switch it off. |
| `./liberty backup` / `restore <dir>` | Save and restore everything the install holds. |
| `./liberty upgrade` / `rollback` | Upgrade with a backup first; undo the last upgrade. |

A Python install has the same verbs in `liberty-ops`. The full reference is on [Operations](./operations.md).

:::warning[Never run `docker compose -f …` by hand]
The install records which compose files it uses (layout, HTTPS, licensed apps) in `release/.env`. A `docker compose -f docker-compose.full.yml up -d` names only the first file: the container comes back without the licensed apps and without HTTPS, and the install looks empty. Use `./liberty start`, `./liberty upgrade`… which always reuse the recorded files.
:::
