## Liberty Next — Columns
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/columns/

The columns of a Liberty Next screen, in the Screen Designer (Grid → Columns) — set each column's label, format, dictionary item, kind of field, default and filtering once; a list read from a table made in one step; both the grid and the dialog use them.

**Grid → Columns**, in the [Screen Designer](./overview.md#designer), is where you set each column's settings: how the column renders in the grid, how it appears in the dialog form, whether it filters, whether it's required, whether it's part of the row's primary key. Set each column once — both surfaces (grid and dialog) use the same configuration.

---

## The columns at a glance

The list shows one line per column with its marks — key, filter, its kind of field, read only…; a click on a line opens its settings beside the list, in six tabs. Each field carries one short sentence of help; **more** opens the longer explanation.

| Tab | Holds |
|---|---|
| **General** | **Column**, **Dictionary item**, **Key**, **Sensitive data**, **Related table** (the related one-to-one table the column is written to). |
| **Display** | **Label**, **Hidden**, **Format**, **Alignment**, **Width**, **Wrap long text**, **Parameters of the service in**, **On a phone**, **Width in the form**, **Link that runs**. |
| **Filter** | **Filter**, **Period shown at first**, **Narrowed by**, **Shown only when**. |
| **Rules** | **Kind of field**, the field that kind needs, **Another kind when** — and, for a list read from a table, **Code only**, **Values given to the list**, **Fills other fields**. |
| **Edit** | **Required**, **Required only when**, **Read only**, **Read only when**, **Read only when adding**, **Read only when changing**, **Align when saving**, **Align as the item in**. |
| **Defaults** | **Default value**, **Forced value when**, **Saved only when**. |

A list setting (a condition, a cascading filter) opens in the same panel; the breadcrumb at the top leads back to the column.

---

## Field by field

Every column carries the same settings. They are described below by purpose.

### Identity

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Column** | The result column these settings apply to. Case-insensitive match against the read query's columns. Normalised to UPPERCASE on save. |
| **Dictionary item** | The dictionary entry that gives the column its label, format and list. *(default)* uses the column's name as the key. |
| **Sensitive data** | Whether the column holds sensitive data, for the AI assistant: left out of what the assistant is given when the installation hides sensitive data. Three choices: *(default)* follows the column's dictionary entry, *yes* flags the column, *no* exempts it even when its entry is flagged. See [Sensitive data](../../ai-data-sent.md#sensitive). |

The dictionary is Liberty's shared vocabulary — one entry defines a field's label, format, kind of field and list once; every screen that has a column with that name inherits it. See [Concepts → Dictionary](../../dictionary.md).

### Display in the grid

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Label** | The title of the grid header and the label of the form field. Falls back to the dictionary's label, then to the column name. |
| **Hidden** | The column is hidden at first. The operator can show it from the grid's *Columns* menu. |
| **Wrap long text** | Long text wraps over several lines in the grid instead of being cut. |
| **Width** | Fixed column width in pixels. Blank fits the content. |
| **Alignment** | Left, right or centred. Blank follows the kind of value (numbers right, text left). |
| **Format** | How to render the value — date, number, yes / no, currency… Overrides the dictionary format. Drives both the grid cell and the form field. |
| **Long Text**, **Name = value list** | Two formats worth knowing. *Long Text* is typed in a multi-line box, in the record form and in the grid's edit mode, and keeps its line breaks. *Name = value list* shows a text of `name = value` lines as rows of fields in the record form (add, remove, **As text** / **As fields**); with **Parameters of the service in** — the column of the screen that names an endpoint — it becomes that endpoint's own form, one labelled field per parameter. |
| **On a phone** | Where the column goes on a card, when the grid is a list of cards: `title` puts it in the card's heading, `show` always gives it a line, `hide` never shows it. Blank: the grid decides. See [Phone and tablet](../../mobile.md#card-setting). |

### Kind of field \{#kind\}

**Kind of field** (Rules tab) says what the field is, in plain words, with its code beside it. *(default)* uses the dictionary's — the line under the field says which (*What the dictionary says for this item: ENUM (PERIOD_STATUS)*).

| Kind of field | Code | In the form | The field it needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| *A yes / no box* | `BOOLEAN` | A check box. | **Value that means yes** (`Y`, `1`, `true`…), and **Value for no**. |
| *A fixed list of values* | `ENUM` | A dropdown of the list's values. | **List of values** — an enum of the dictionary. |
| *A list read from a table* | `LOOKUP` | A searchable list of the table's rows. | **List from a table** — a lookup of the dictionary, or a new one made from here: see [below](#list-from-table). |
| *A number given automatically* | `SEQUENCE` | Filled by the server on insert. | **Numbering rule** — a sequence of the dictionary. |
| *The signed-in user* | `LOGIN` | Filled with the user's name. | — |
| *Today's date* | `SYSDATE` | Filled with today's date. | — |
| *A password (hidden, stored encrypted)* | `PASSWORD` | Encrypted on write. | — |
| *A database of this installation* | `POOL` | A dropdown of the pools. | **Only the databases of** — blank offers every pool. |
| *Free text; left empty, it takes its default value* | `DEFAULT` | Free text. | — (the **Default value** of the Defaults tab). |
| *Free text, whatever the dictionary says* | `DISABLED` | Free text: cancels the kind the dictionary gives, for this screen. | — |

Only the field the chosen kind needs is shown, under the name of what it is for that kind. The effect of each kind on writes is described in [Dictionary → Kinds of field](../../dictionary.md#rules).

A list read from a table adds three settings:

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Code only** | Shows the code alone in the grid, without its description. |
| **Values given to the list** | Values of the record that narrow the list's query — for instance the application of the row, to offer only that application's roles. See [Parameter binding](../queries/parameter-binding.md). |
| **Fills other fields** | When a line is picked, copies columns of that line into other fields of the record. |

**Another kind when** gives the field another kind — another list, another enum, a yes / no box — while another column has a given value. See [Form conditions](../../form-conditions.md).

### A list read from a table, in one step \{#list-from-table\}

When the list does not exist yet, **New list from a table…**, under **List from a table**, makes it without leaving the column. The *New lookup* window asks for:

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Table** | A table of the screen's database. |
| **Value column** | The code stored on the row. |
| **Label column** | The description shown to the user. |
| **Optional WHERE clause** | Written without the keyword. |
| **Query name**, **Id**, **Description** | Filled from the table; they can be changed. |
| **Generated SQL — editable** | The query, as it will be saved. |

**Save** adds the query to the application's list queries and the list to its dictionary — two new objects, nothing existing is changed —, reloads the configuration and picks the new list in the column.

### Edit

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Required** | The field is marked with an asterisk and **Save** stays blocked while it is empty. |
| **Read only** | The operator sees the value but cannot change it. |
| **Read only when adding** / **Read only when changing** | Read only only when a record is added, or only once it exists — the second one for keys that must not change. |
| **Required only when** / **Read only when** | Required or read only only while conditions on other fields hold. A required field blocks **Save** only while it is visible. |
| **Align when saving** | How the written value is padded, for codes stored right-aligned. Blank does as the dictionary says. |
| **Align as the item in** | The column naming the dictionary item whose alignment and width this value follows. |

### Defaults

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Default value** | The value a new record starts with. |
| **Forced value when** | A value set (and locked, unless **Locked** is unticked) while another column has a given value. |
| **Saved only when** | The column is saved only while the condition holds; otherwise it is saved empty. |

### Key

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Key** | This column identifies the record, alone or with the other key columns. Drives:– Excel-import update-vs-insert matching.– In add mode, a key column shows a plain input instead of its list (a new key is typed, not picked).– The `_put` query's `:NAME_ORIGINAL` binding (the CRUD Wizard's convention). |

A key is not locked automatically when a record is edited: tick **Read only when changing** (Edit tab) on the key columns that must not change once the record exists. Mark every column that uniquely identifies a record. Multi-column keys are supported — tick **Key** on each. When the screen's **Key columns** is empty (the usual case), the columns marked **Key** are used.

### Filtering

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Filter** | The column appears in the filters above the grid. The user picks a value to narrow the grid; on a column with a fixed list of values, several values at once, and a code typed beyond the list is accepted. A list read from a table keeps a single choice. A date column (`date`, `datetime`, `timestamp` format, or a date type in the database) filters by a [period](#period). |
| **Period shown at first** | On a date column with **Filter**, the period the screen opens on: today, yesterday, last 7 or 30 days, this or last month, this quarter, this or last year, last 12 months. Blank or *all*: no period, every row. The screen's first automatic run already applies it. |
| **Narrowed by** | Cascading filter — narrows this column's choices with another filter's value: **Filter** (the other filter) and **Matched on** (the column of this list compared with that filter's value). |
| **Shown only when** | In the grid, hides the column when a filter is set to a value outside the condition; in the form, shows the field only while the form's values match. |

The conditions are described on [Form conditions](../../form-conditions.md), with examples on [Conditional fields](./conditional-fields.md).

### A typical column

For a `STATUS` column on a customers screen, the settings usually are:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Column** | `STATUS` |
| **Dictionary item** | *(default)* — uses `STATUS` as the key |
| **Label**, **Format** | blank — inherited from the dictionary |
| **Kind of field** | *A fixed list of values* |
| **List of values** | `STATUS_CODES` (an enum of the dictionary) |
| **Default value** | `OPEN` |
| **Required** | ✓ |
| **Filter** | ✓ |

That renders a dropdown in the form (sourced from the `STATUS_CODES` enum), pre-fills new records with `OPEN`, requires a value, and adds a filter to the grid.

---

## Inheriting from the dictionary

The default behaviour — when most fields are blank — is to **inherit from the dictionary**. The chain:

| Column setting | Blank → taken from |
|---|---|
| **Label** | the entry's label, then the column name |
| **Format** | the entry's format, then the type of the value |
| **Kind of field** and its list | the entry's kind of field and its list |

This means a column named `USR_ID` on a screen automatically reads its label, format, kind of field and list from the dictionary entry `USR_ID` (or the one picked in **Dictionary item**). The screen overrides only when **this** screen needs different behaviour from the rest.

The column list is therefore mostly **empty** for well-dictionary'd installs — entries only appear when there's something to override.

---

## Filtering and cascading filters

When a column has **Filter** ticked, a chip for it appears in the grid's filter panel. The user picks a value, the grid re-runs the read query with that value bound to the matching `:placeholder` param. The query is responsible for accepting the bind.

### A period on a date column \{#period\}

On a date column, the filter panel shows a period instead of a single date: the same picker as the dashboards, with its presets (*Today*, *Yesterday*, *Last 7 days*, *Last 30 days*, *This month*, *Last month*, *This quarter*, *This year*, *Last year*, *Last 12 months*, *All dates*) and a two-month calendar for a custom range. The run sends the two bounds as `<COL>_from` and `<COL>_to`, and the server bounds the column itself — the read query needs no placeholder for them. A period ending on a day keeps all of that day's rows, times included.

A drill or a link that passes a date to a date column opens the screen on that one day.

**Cascading filters** narrow one filter's options based on another. The classic case: a *Role* dropdown that shows only roles for the currently-picked *Application*:

| Field | Value on `ROLE_ID` |
|---|---|
| **Kind of field** | *A list read from a table* |
| **List from a table** | `get_roles` |
| **Filter** | ✓ |
| **Narrowed by → Filter** | `APPS_ID` (the parent filter) |
| **Narrowed by → Matched on** | `APP_ID` (the column of the list's query that matches the parent filter's value) |

When the user picks an application, the role lookup re-runs with the application id bound — the user only sees that application's roles.

---

## Order of columns

The order of the column list = the display order in the grid. Columns the read query returns but that aren't listed here keep their discovery order and follow the hinted ones.

To reorder:

| Goal | Action |
|---|---|
| Move a column up / down. | Drag its row in the list (the drag handle is the left edge of the row). |
| Hide a column entirely. | Tick **Hidden**. The operator can still un-hide it from the grid's *Columns* menu. |
| Drop a column from both grid and dialog. | Remove it from the list (✕) AND make sure it's not on any dialog tab's fields. (Or alter the read query to not return it.) |

---

## Common pitfalls

| Mistake | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **Dictionary item** `USR_ID` but no dictionary entry named `USR_ID`. | Label and format fall back to the column name verbatim. | Add the dictionary entry, or set **Label** and **Format** on the column. |
| *A list read from a table* but **List from a table** blank. | The dropdown is empty. | Pick a list, or make one with **New list from a table…**. |
| **Narrowed by** set but **Filter** not ticked. | The cascade does nothing — the source filter never fires. | Tick **Filter** AND set **Narrowed by**. |
| **Required** on a column the read query doesn't return. | The dialog saves with NULL; if the DB has a NOT NULL constraint, the write fails. | Add the column to the read query, or untick **Required**. |
| **Key** on a non-unique column. | Excel import treats duplicate values as updates of the same row. | Verify the key columns genuinely identify a row uniquely. |
| **Format** *currency* but the value is in cents (integer). | The grid renders `1,234.00` for `123456`. | Format expects the value in the unit you want displayed — divide by 100 in the query, or use a Python step before display. |

---

## Liberty Next — Dialog builder
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/dialog-builder/

The record form of a Liberty Next screen, built in the Screen Designer — three panels (Add a field / Dialog / Inspector) where you add fields to tabs, set their column settings, choose the tab types and add per-tab actions.

The **Record form** stage of the Screen Designer opens the **visual builder** — a WYSIWYG editor for the add/edit form. The data model is the same `ScreenDialog` shape stored in `screens.toml`, but instead of editing TOML you add fields to tabs and tune them in a side inspector.

A screen without a dialog still works as a read-only / grid-edit table. Build a dialog when the user needs a full form to add or edit rows.

---

## Three-column layout

| Region | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Add a field** *(left)* | Source of new fields. Two sub-tabs: **Dictionary** (every entry available on the current connector scope) and **Columns** (every column the read query returns). A filter narrows the list; a click on an entry adds a field card to the current tab. The panel folds away with its arrow. |
| **Dialog** *(center)* | The tabs strip across the top — each tab with its field count, **＋ Add tab** at the end — then **Tab settings** (folded: tab label, tab type, columns, the title in the other languages, the two *Left out* boxes, tab actions) and the field cards. Each card shows the label, a preview of the input (a number, a date, a lookup and its query…), the column name and its *key* mark; the picked card has a blue border. The header counts the grid's columns and the tab's fields. A **Hidden fields** group at the bottom collects the fields with `hidden = true`. |
| **Inspector** *(right)* | The picked field and its **Column configuration** — see Step 3 —, or, with no field picked, the dialog's title and its events. It folds away with its arrow. |

**Delete dialog**, above the panels, removes the whole form: the screen becomes a read-only or grid-edit table again.

---

## Building from scratch

### Step 1 — Open the Record form stage

The first time, the canvas is empty with a *Create dialog* button. Click it to seed `dialog.tabs = [{id: 'general', label: 'General', fields: []}]` and reveal the three-column layout.

### Step 2 — Add the first tab's fields

Two ways:

| Method | When |
|---|---|
| **Click a Dictionary entry or a column in Add a field** | Adds a field card at the end of the current tab. A dictionary entry pre-fills `dd`, so the field picks up the entry's rule; a column adds a plain field bound to the read query. |
| **Click + Add field at the end of the tab** | Asks for the field name (a column of the read query) and adds it. |

The added field becomes the selected card; the Inspector switches to it. Drag a card to put it elsewhere in the grid. Set `colspan` to widen it (the grid is by default 2 columns; a `colspan = 2` field fills the row).

### Step 3 — Tune the field properties

A dialog field displays a screen column, and the column carries every behaviour. The Inspector shows:

| Section | What it holds |
|---|---|
| **Breadcrumb** | *Dialog title › FIELD* — a click on *Dialog title* goes back to the dialog's own settings. |
| **Field** | The field's name and, with several form tabs, the **Tab** it sits on. |
| **Column configuration** | The column's full editor — the same as in Grid → Columns: label, format, dictionary entry (`dd`), rule and lookup binds, required / read-only flags, conditions, defaults, and the field's span on the dialog grid (**Display ▸ Colspan**). A change applies to the grid as well. |
| **Events** | The hooks wired on the screen, by event, for information — they are edited on the **Actions** stage. |
| **Delete field** | Removes the field from the tab; the column stays on the screen. |

See [Columns](./columns.md) for each setting and [Conditional fields](./conditional-fields.md) for the conditions.

### Step 4 — Add tabs

Click **＋ Add tab** at the end of the tab strip; it asks for the tab's id. The new tab is empty; add fields from **Add a field**. Common tab patterns:

| Tab name | What's on it |
|---|---|
| **General** | Identity + most-used fields. |
| **Audit** | Created at, created by, updated at, updated by — often `hide_on_add` to hide the tab when inserting. |
| **Notes** | Free-text fields. |
| **Address** | A group of related fields (street, city, postcode, country). |

### Tab settings \{#tab-settings\}

**Tab settings**, above the field cards, sets the picked tab: its label, its type, its columns — and how it reads in other languages and when it is shown.

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Tab label** | The tab's title, as written. |
| **Tab type** | *Form* (a grid of editable fields), a nested table or another screen's form — see [Nested tabs](./nested-tabs.md). |
| **Columns** | The number of columns of the tab's grid. |
| **Title in the other languages** | The title for the users of another language: a language picked in the list, then its text; **+ add** for another. A language with no line shows the tab label as written. |
| **Left out when a record is added** (`hide_on_add`) | The tab is not shown when a new record is added. |
| **Left out when a record is edited** (`hide_on_edit`) | The tab is not shown when an existing record is edited. |
| **Tab actions** | Buttons shown inside the tab — see [Tab actions](#tab-actions). |

### Step 5 — Reorder fields

Drag a field card within the same tab to reorder. Drag across to a different tab to move it between tabs. The drag is HTML5 native — the drop target highlights while you hover. When dragging is awkward, select the field and use the **Tab** picker in the Inspector to move it to another form tab — the field lands at the end of the target tab and stays selected.

### Step 6 — Hide a field

Two ways:

| Method | Effect |
|---|---|
| Tick **hidden** in the column configuration (Display). | The card moves to the **Hidden fields** group at the bottom of the Dialog panel. The field still binds at save time. |
| Delete the field from the tab. | The field is removed from the dialog entirely. The column is still on the screen; it just doesn't surface in the form. |

The "hide but keep" pattern is useful for technical columns the dialog must submit (e.g. an audit timestamp) but the user shouldn't see.

---

## The three tab kinds

Tabs aren't all the same. Three types live under `dialog.tabs`, discriminated on the `type` field:

| Type | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **`form`** *(default)* | A grid of editable fields — the case described above. |
| **`nested_form`** | The form of another existing screen (`form_screen`), shown in the tab; `param_binds` pass the parent's values (usually its key) to that form's queries, and it is saved with the parent's **Save**. See [Nested tabs](./nested-tabs.md). |
| **`nested_table`** | A related-rows TableView embedded in the tab. Renders another screen's grid scoped to the parent's PK. See [Nested tabs](./nested-tabs.md). |

The visual builder shows the same tab strip for all three — switching to a `nested_form` or `nested_table` tab shows the target-screen picker and its `param_binds`.

---

## Per-tab actions \{#tab-actions\}

Each tab can carry its own action list — buttons shown inside the tab, set under **Tab settings → Tab actions** (**Add action**). Common patterns:

| Pattern | Why per-tab |
|---|---|
| A *Recompute* button on a calculations tab. | Triggers a stored procedure only when the user is looking at those fields. |
| A *Test webhook* button on a notification tab. | Only meaningful in that context. |
| A *Refresh from source* button on a sync tab. | Re-pulls data the tab displays. |

The action editor opens in the **Inspector** when you click an action's row — the Inspector shows one thing at a time (a field OR an action). Selecting a field clears the action selection and vice versa.

See [Actions and lifecycle](./actions-and-lifecycle.md) for the full action types.

---

## Dialog title

The dialog's title sits at the top of the modal when it opens. Set it in the Inspector when no field is picked, under **Dialog title**; blank falls back to the screen's `label` (*Falls back to the screen label*), then to `id`. Below it, **Events** lists the hooks wired on the screen, for information.

---

## Common pitfalls

| Mistake | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Field on a tab references a column that doesn't exist in the read query. | The dialog shows the field but the value is always blank, and saving sends no value for it. | Either add the column to the read query or remove the field from the tab. |
| `lookup_param_binds` references a field that's not on the same tab. | The bind resolves to NULL at submit. | Either move the source field onto the same tab or use a cross-tab binding (the engine reads the whole form state, but the inspector's Param dropdown only lists fields visible on the current tab). |
| `colspan = 3` on a 2-column grid. | The field overflows; layout breaks. | Cap `colspan` at the tab's `cols`. |
| Two fields with the same `name` on the same tab. | The save sends two values for the same column; the second wins. | Each field's `name` must be unique within the dialog. |
| `hide_on_add = true` AND `hide_on_edit = true`. | The tab never appears. | Either flip one off or drop the tab. |

---

## Liberty Next — Conditional fields
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/conditional-fields/

Make a dialog field appear, become required, lock itself or take a forced value only when another field has a given value — set on the column in the Liberty Next Screen Designer, with worked examples.

A static dialog asks the same questions every time. A conditional dialog adapts to what the user has already chosen: show **IBAN** only for a bank transfer, mark **Cancellation reason** as required only for a cancelled order, lock the **Invoice number** once the invoice exists.

The settings and their exact behaviour are listed on [Form conditions](../../form-conditions.md). This page shows how to set them up.

---

## At a glance

---

## Where to set them

A dialog field displays a screen column, and the column carries every behaviour — the same settings drive the dialog and the grid. In the Screen Designer:

1. On the **Record form** stage, click the field in the [Dialog builder](./dialog-builder.md) — or, on the **Grid** stage, pick the column in **Columns**.
2. The column's settings show, split into tabs (**Column configuration** in the Inspector): the conditions sit in **Filter** (`visible_when`), **Edit** (`required_when`, `disabled_when`, `disable_on_add`, `disable_on_edit`), **Defaults** (`default_when`, `write_when`) and **Rules** (`rules_when`).
3. Under the setting, **+ add** opens a new condition in the same panel — its breadcrumb reads *Required When: (new)*, for example: pick the **Field** among the screen's columns and give the **Value**, or several values (**+ add** under Value). The breadcrumb leads back to the column.

All the lines of one setting must match together (AND). For an OR on the same field, list the values in one condition.

---

## Worked examples

### Show fields for one choice

A *Payment* dialog where `PAYMENT_METHOD` is a list (`CASH`, `TRANSFER`, `DIRECT_DEBIT`, `CARD`):

| Column | `visible_when` |
|---|---|
| `IBAN` | `PAYMENT_METHOD` = `TRANSFER`, `DIRECT_DEBIT` |
| `BIC` | `PAYMENT_METHOD` = `TRANSFER`, `DIRECT_DEBIT` |
| `CARD_LAST4` | `PAYMENT_METHOD` = `CARD` |

With `CASH`, none of the three fields shows. With `TRANSFER`, `IBAN` and `BIC` appear.

### Mark a reason as required on cancellation

| Column | `required_when` |
|---|---|
| `CANCELLATION_REASON` | `STATUS` = `CANCELLED` |

The field always shows; it gets the required asterisk as soon as the status is `CANCELLED`.

### Lock a key once the row exists

| Column | Setting |
|---|---|
| `INVOICE_NUMBER` | `disable_on_edit` ticked |

The number is typed when the invoice is added, then read-only — in the dialog and in grid editing. `disable_on_add` does the reverse, for a value assigned on creation.

### Force a value for one kind of row

| Column | `default_when` |
|---|---|
| `CREDIT_LIMIT` | `STATUS` = `CANCELLED` → default `0`, lock on |

As soon as the status becomes `CANCELLED`, the limit switches to `0` and locks. With **lock** off, `0` is only proposed and the user can change it.

### Make closed periods read-only

On the screen's **What it is** stage:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| `editable_when` | `PERIOD_STATUS` = `OPEN`, `VALIDATED` |

A row of a closed period opens in view-only mode, and the server refuses changes to it.

---

## Things to know

| Situation | What happens | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| The deciding field is not on the dialog. | Its value is unknown to the form: the condition never matches, and the dependent field stays hidden. | Add the deciding field to the dialog, hidden or not. |
| `visible_when` on a key column. | A user adding a row may not see the key. | Lock a key (`disable_on_edit`); do not hide it. |
| `required_when` matches while `visible_when` does not. | A hidden field is never demanded: **Save** goes through with it empty. | Keep the two conditions in line. |
| A value with different spelling. | The condition never matches: values are compared exactly (only the surrounding spaces are ignored). | Copy the stored codes, not their labels. |
| A threshold (`AMOUNT > 1000`). | Conditions only test equality. | Return a flag from the read query (`HIGH_VALUE = 'Y'`) and test that flag. |

---

## Liberty Next — Form conditions
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/form-conditions/

Every conditional setting of a screen column — show, require, lock, force a default, change the rule or skip the write depending on another field's value — and the screen's row-level editable_when rule. One condition shape: a field and a value, ANDed.

A screen column can react to the value of another field of the same row: appear only for one kind of record, become required, lock itself, take a forced value, change its list of values, or not be written at all. The screen itself can make whole rows read-only. All these settings use the same condition shape.

For a step-by-step use in the Screen Designer, see [Screens → Conditional fields](./build/screens/conditional-fields.md).

---

## At a glance

---

## The condition \{#condition\}

A condition names a **field** of the same row and the **value** it must have — or a list of values, any of which matches:

```toml
{ field = "STATUS", value = "CANCELLED" }
{ field = "PAYMENT_METHOD", value = ["TRANSFER", "DIRECT_DEBIT"] }
```

A setting holds a list of conditions: **all of them** must match (AND). Values are compared as text, without their leading and trailing spaces, so a code padded with spaces still matches. Field names are matched regardless of case.

In the Screen Designer, each setting is a list in the column's settings: **+ add** opens a condition, with the **Field** picked from the screen's columns and one or several **Value** entries.

---

## Settings on a column \{#column-settings\}

| Setting | Inspector tab | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `visible_when` | Filter | **Dialog**: the field shows only while the conditions match the form's values. **Grid**: the column hides when a filter of the screen is set to a value outside the condition; with that filter empty, the column stays. |
| `required` / `required_when` | Edit | The field is marked required (asterisk), always or only while the conditions match. |
| `disabled` / `disabled_when` | Edit | The field is read-only, always or only while the conditions match. |
| `disable_on_add` | Edit | Read-only when a row is added, editable afterwards — for a value assigned on creation. |
| `disable_on_edit` | Edit | Read-only once the row exists — for a key that must not change. Applies to the dialog and to grid editing. |
| `default` | Defaults | The value proposed when a row is added. |
| `default_when` | Defaults | While its condition matches, the column takes the given **default** and is locked. With **lock** off, the value is only proposed and stays editable. With several rules, the first that matches wins. Re-applied when the deciding field changes, in the dialog and the grid. |
| `rules_when` | Rules | While its condition matches, the column uses another rule — another lookup, enum or Boolean, with its own lookup parameters and returned values — or none (plain input). The first match wins; otherwise the column's own rule applies. |
| `write_when` | Defaults | The column is written only while the conditions match. Otherwise the server writes a neutral value (blank or 0) and the dictionary default or rule is not applied — for a field that means nothing for this kind of row. |

A static setting and its conditional version combine simply: when the `_when` list is empty, the static flag decides; when it is filled, the conditions decide.

---

## Setting on the screen — `editable_when` \{#editable-when\}

Set on the **What it is** stage of the Screen Designer, `editable_when` says when an **existing** row may be changed or deleted:

```toml
editable_when = [{ field = "PERIOD_STATUS", value = ["OPEN", "VALIDATED"] }]
```

A row that does not match is read-only: plain cells in the grid, a view-only dialog without **Save** or **Delete**. The server refuses a change to such a row as well. Adding rows is not affected.

---

## What happens on save \{#save\}

- **Hidden fields** — on an update, a field hidden by `visible_when` is not sent: the column keeps its stored value. On an insert, a hidden field is sent only when it holds a value.
- **Locked fields** — their value is sent as it is.
- **Where it is checked** — `visible_when`, `required_when`, `disabled_when`, `default_when` and `rules_when` act in the browser, as the user types. `editable_when` and `write_when` are applied by the server too, whatever the client sends.

---

## Action prompts \{#prompts\}

The fields of an action's prompt dialog accept `visible_when`, `required_when` and `disabled_when` with the same shape, evaluated against the prompt's own fields. See [Actions and lifecycle](./build/screens/actions-and-lifecycle.md).

---

- [Screens → Columns](./build/screens/columns.md) — every other column setting.
- [Dictionary](./dictionary.md) — the rules a column inherits.

## Liberty Next — Actions and lifecycle
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/actions-and-lifecycle/

The Actions tab — dialog hooks (on_load / on_save / on_cancel), toolbar buttons, row hooks (on_insert / on_update / on_delete / on_duplicate), the row menu, the action types with their param_binds, prompts, chains, translations and services.

A screen with a grid and a dialog covers the standard read and write flow. **Actions** and **lifecycle hooks** add everything else: run a query from a button, open another view from a row, call an API or a plugin after a save, refresh the grid after a delete.

They are set on the **Actions** stage of the [Screen Designer](./overview.md#designer), in its two sections **Actions** and **Row menu**, with the same action shapes everywhere. **Actions** lists the hooks and toolbar buttons as folded groups, each with its count; a group opens on its actions, one per line (id, type, label, number of steps), with **Add action** below. **Row menu** lists the entries of the row's context menu the same way.

---

## Where actions fire \{#groups\}

| Group | Lists | When they fire | `source` reads from |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Dialog hooks** | `on_load` | Once the dialog has loaded the row (edit) or seeded the defaults (add). | The form. |
| | `on_save` | After the dialog's main insert or update succeeds. | The form at save time. |
| | `on_cancel` | When the dialog is closed without saving, before it closes; an error keeps it open. | The form. |
| **Toolbar** | `actions` | Each entry is a button above the grid. | No row context; prompt values under `INPUT.<name>`. |
| **Row hooks** | `on_insert`, `on_update`, `on_delete` | After the write succeeds — from the dialog or from grid editing. | The new row, or the deleted row. |
| | `on_duplicate` | When a row duplicated with the dialog's **Duplicate** is saved, instead of `on_insert`. | The new row, and the source row under `SOURCE_<column>`. |
| **Row menu** *(own section)* | `row_menu` | Each entry is a menu item on a row: right-click, or the ⋯ handle at the start of the row. | The clicked row. |

Hooks run their list in order and stop at the first error, unless an action has **stop_on_error** off. A toolbar or row-menu entry runs as one action: to run several steps from one button, use a `chain`.

For a left click on a row, use the **row-click** settings of the *What it is* stage (`row_click_screen` with `row_click_binds`, or `row_click_route`).

---

## Action types \{#types\}

Every action has an **id** (unique in its list, also its key in a chain's context), a **label** (button caption), its label in the other languages ([Translations](#translations)) and **stop_on_error**.

| Type | What it does | Main fields |
|---|---|---|
| **`run_query`** | Runs a query of a connector, read or write. | `connector`, `query`, `param_binds`, `bind_result` |
| **`call_api`** | Calls an endpoint of an API connector. | `connector`, `endpoint`, `param_binds`, `bind_result` |
| **`call_plugin`** | Calls a server-side Python function (`module:function`), the same entry points Nomaflow runs as steps. | `callable`, `param_binds`, `bind_result` |
| **`call_action`** | Runs a [service](#shared) by its id. | `ref`, `param_binds` |
| **`navigate`** | Opens another view: a screen (`screen`) or a query (`to`), with `param_binds` passed as its parameters. | `connector`, `screen` or `to`, `param_binds` |
| **`open_url`** | Opens an external address — another application on the row's record. | `url`, `new_tab` |
| **`set_field`** | Writes a value into a form field. | `target`, `value` or `source` |
| **`confirm`** | Asks for confirmation; **Cancel** stops the chain. The message is filled like an `open_url` template (`{COLUMN}`, `{INPUT.x}`, built-ins), not encoded: `Reset the password of {INPUT.user} on #POOL#?`. | `message`, `confirm_label`, `cancel_label` |
| **`notify`** | Shows a message, filled the same way. | `message`, `tone` (`info` / `ok` / `warn` / `error`) |
| **`send_notification`** | Fires a notification rule of type *action* (e-mail, portal…). | `rule`, `param_binds` |
| **`refresh`** | Reloads the grid. | — |

`bind_result` keeps the rows (or the response) of the step in the chain's context, so that a later step reads them with `source = "<id>.first_row.<COLUMN>"`.

### Open an external address \{#open-url\}

An **`open_url`** action opens another application on the record at hand — the JD Edwards form of an address book entry, a ticket in a help desk. It can sit in a row menu, on the toolbar, in a dialog tab, behind a drill column or in a chain, and can ask for values first.

- **`url`** is a template: `{COLUMN}` takes the value of a column of the row, a field of the form, a value asked for, or a step of the chain — `{step.first_row.X}` —, encoded for an address; `#LOGIN_USER#` and the other built-ins are filled too. `https://helpdesk.example.com/tickets?customer={CUSTOMER_ID}`.
- An address that differs from one install to the next is written `#URL.NAME#` at the start: `#URL.JDE_WEB#/ShortcutLauncher?OID=P01012_W01012A&…`. Each install sets the address once, in [App → External addresses](../settings-app.md#external-urls); without it, the action opens nothing.
- **`new_tab`**: on by default; off, the address replaces the page.

Only `http://`, `https://` addresses and paths of this server are opened; anything else is refused when the configuration loads, and checked again on the filled address. A row menu whose only action is an `open_url` fires it from the row handle.

### The row handle and drill-downs \{#drill\}

A screen with row-menu actions shows a small handle at the start of every row, so the actions stay in reach on a wide table:

- with several actions, the handle (**⋯**, *Row actions*) opens the same menu as the right-click;
- with a single `navigate` action, the handle (a return arrow) fires it at once — its tooltip is the action's label.

**Link cells.** A column's **drill** setting (Liberty Next → Screens → Screens, stage *Grid*, column, tab *Display*) names a `navigate` action of the row menu: the value shows as a link that fires it for the row — the customer code opens the customer, with no menu to open. A screen whose row menu holds a single `navigate` action does it by itself on its first key column. A wrong action name is refused when the configuration loads.

**Where the target opens.** By default, a `navigate` action opens its target in a new tab. With **Drill-downs open inside the current tab** in [Liberty Next → Administer → App](../settings-app.md#display), it opens as a panel inside the current tab, over the grid: a breadcrumb names each level, **Back** returns to the one before, and the grid behind keeps its rows and filters. A drill from the panel nests the same way. An action decides for itself with `inline = true` (panel) or `inline = false` (new tab), set in `screens.toml`.

### Composite types

| Type | What it does |
|---|---|
| **`chain`** | A list of steps run in order, sharing one context. |
| **`if`** | Runs `then_steps` or `else_steps` depending on a condition: a `source`, an operator (`equals`, `not_equals`, `has_rows`, `no_rows`, `truthy`, `falsy`, `greater_than`, `less_than`) and a `value`. |
| **`loop`** | Runs `steps` once per item of a list taken from the context (typically the rows of an earlier step). |
| **`return`** | Copies values of the context back into the form's fields — at the end of a chain, to show computed values. |

**Wrap in chain** puts an existing action inside a `chain`, to add steps around it.

---

## Values passed to an action \{#binds\}

`run_query`, `call_api`, `call_plugin`, `call_action`, `navigate` and `send_notification` take a list of `param_binds`: for each parameter of the target, a fixed **value**, or a **source** read at call time — a column of the row, a form field, `INPUT.<name>`, `<step>.first_row.<COLUMN>`, or a built-in such as `#LOGIN_USER#` / `#SYSDATE#` — with an optional **default**. See [Parameter binding](../queries/parameter-binding.md).

In the action editor, the list reads **Values passed**. Each line names the parameter, then **Fixed** — a value written there — or **Taken from** — picked among the record's columns, what the service received, what an earlier step returned, or the signed-in user / today —, with **a value to use when that one is empty**. Without any line: *Nothing is passed: it runs without any value.*

### Prompt before running \{#prompt\}

`run_query`, `call_api`, `call_plugin`, `call_action`, `navigate` and `chain` can open a small form **before** they run:

| Field | Role |
|---|---|
| **prompt_fields** | The inputs to ask for — each with its name, label, dictionary entry, default, required / hidden / read-only flags and conditions. |
| **prompt_title** (and its translations) | The window's title; defaults to the action's label. |
| **prompt_cols** | Number of columns of the form (2 by default). |

The values entered are available as `INPUT.<name>` to the action and to every later step of the same chain. **Cancel** stops the chain without an error.

### The label in other languages \{#translations\}

The action's editor has three tabs under its target: **General** (id, label, stop on error), **Translations** and **Prompt**. **Translations** gives the label in each other language — a language picked in the list (`fr Français`), then its text; **+ add** for another. The label read by the user follows his language wherever the action shows: a row-menu entry, a toolbar or tab button, a step of a chain. A language with no line shows the label as written.

---

## Services \{#shared\}

An action used by several screens is defined once as a **service**, in **Liberty Next → Logic → Services**: an id, a label, a description, declared inputs and its steps (the same action types), drawn as a flow in the service designer — see [Services](../services.md).

A screen runs it with `call_action`: `ref` names the service (the field reads *Shared action*), and its `param_binds` fill the service's `INPUT.<param>` values.

---

## Examples

### Recompute, then reload the grid

```toml
[[screens.crm.customers.actions]]
type  = "chain"
id    = "recompute"
label = "Recompute balances"
steps = [
  { type = "run_query", id = "compute", connector = "crm", query = "compute_balances" },
  { type = "refresh",   id = "reload" },
  { type = "notify",    id = "done", message = "Balances recomputed.", tone = "ok" },
]
```

### Confirm before deleting

```toml
[[screens.crm.customers.row_menu]]
type  = "chain"
id    = "delete_customer"
label = "Delete customer"
steps = [
  { type = "confirm", id = "ask", message = "Delete this customer and its deals?", confirm_label = "Delete" },
  { type = "run_query", id = "delete", connector = "crm", query = "customers_delete",
    param_binds = [{ param = "CUSTOMER_ID", source = "CUSTOMER_ID" }] },
  { type = "refresh", id = "reload" },
]
```

**Cancel** on the confirmation stops the chain: nothing is deleted.

### Open the deals of a customer

```toml
[[screens.crm.customers.row_menu]]
type        = "navigate"
id          = "view_deals"
label       = "View deals"
connector   = "crm"
screen      = "deals"
param_binds = [{ param = "CUSTOMER_ID", source = "CUSTOMER_ID" }]
```

The **deals** screen opens with its filters seeded from the binds.

### Stamp audit columns

For `CREATED_BY` / `CREATED_AT` columns, no hook is needed: the dictionary rules `LOGIN` and `SYSDATE`, or the `{{LOGIN}}` / `{{SYSTIMESTAMP}}` tokens in the insert query, fill them on the server — see [Dictionary → Rules](../../dictionary.md#rules). To log every write in a history table, set `audit_table` on the *What it is* stage.

---

## Saving

The Actions and Row menu sections edit the screen's lists; the Screen Designer's **Save** writes them with the rest of the screen and reloads the configuration — the next click runs the new version.

---

## Common pitfalls

| Mistake | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Two toolbar entries meant to run one after the other. | They are two separate buttons. | Put the steps in one `chain`. |
| A toolbar action reading `source = "CUSTOMER_ID"`. | The toolbar has no row: the value is empty. | Move the action to the row menu, or ask for the value with a prompt (`INPUT.CUSTOMER_ID`). |
| `confirm` placed after the delete. | The question comes once the row is gone. | `confirm` first in the chain. |
| A step reads `<id>.first_row.X` from a step without `bind_result`. | The value is empty. | Turn on `bind_result` on the step that produces the rows. |
| `value = "#LOGIN_USER#"`. | The text is written as it is. | Use `source`. |

## Liberty Next — Nested tabs
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/nested-tabs/

Embed a child-record form (nested_form) or a related-rows grid (nested_table) in a dialog tab — same dialog, multiple data sources.

A dialog with all its fields on one form covers the *single-row* case. When a row has **related data** — a customer with several addresses, a user with per-application settings, an order with line items — you embed that related data right inside the dialog as a nested tab.

Two variants:

| Tab type | What it shows | When |
|---|---|---|
| **`nested_form`** | The form of another screen, for zero or one related row, saved with the parent. | When the related table has **at most one** row per parent (one-to-one or zero-to-one). |
| **`nested_table`** | A full TableView of related rows, embedded inline — renders another screen's grid scoped to the parent's key. | When the related table has **many** rows per parent (one-to-many). |

Both attach to the dialog like any other tab; the user clicks between them without leaving the form.

---

## When to reach for each

| Pattern | Choose |
|---|---|
| One customer → at most one billing address. | `nested_form`. |
| One customer → many orders. | `nested_table`. |
| One application → its JD Edwards-specific settings (zero-or-one row). | `nested_form`. |
| One project → its line items. | `nested_table`. |
| One employee → their current job assignment (one row). | `nested_form`. |
| One employee → their job assignment history. | `nested_table`. |

The schema's `_check` validator enforces tab id uniqueness; otherwise both types can coexist in the same dialog — a *Customer* dialog with a `nested_form` on *Billing* and a `nested_table` on *Orders* is a natural shape.

---

## nested_form — a child-record form

A `nested_form` tab shows, inside the dialog, the **form of another existing screen**. That screen owns the read, update and insert queries and the fields; the tab only says which screen to reuse and how to pass the parent's values to it.

### Fields

| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| **`form_screen`** *(required)* | The id of the screen whose form is reused. |
| **`connector`** | The connector of that screen. Blank = the parent screen's connector. |
| **`param_binds`** | Bind the parent's values into the reused screen's queries — typically `CUSTOMER_ID ← CUSTOMER_ID`. |
| **`label`**, **`l`**, **`hide_on_add`**, **`hide_on_edit`**, **`actions`** | As on any tab — see [Tab settings](./dialog-builder.md#tab-settings). |

### Behaviour

1. **Editing a parent row** — the reused screen's read query runs with the bound values. A row found is shown for editing; otherwise the form starts empty.
2. **Adding a parent row** — the form starts empty (the parent has no key yet).
3. **Saving** — the nested form is saved by the **parent's Save**: an update when a row was loaded, an insert otherwise — only if the user typed something. On an insert, the binds take the parent's new key, including one assigned by a sequence.
4. **Duplicating the parent** — the nested row is inserted again for the copy.

Fields hidden by their conditions are not written, and the bound key columns always take the parent's values.

### Use case — billing address

A *Customer* dialog with a *Billing* tab that reuses the `billing_address` screen (its read, update and insert queries keyed on `CUSTOMER_ID`):

```toml
[[screens.crm.customers.dialog.tabs]]
id          = "billing"
label       = "Billing"
type        = "nested_form"
form_screen = "billing_address"
param_binds = [{ param = "CUSTOMER_ID", source = "CUSTOMER_ID" }]
```

To change the billing fields, edit the `billing_address` screen: every dialog that reuses it follows.

---

## nested_table — a related-rows grid

A `nested_table` tab embeds another screen's TableView inline. No new fields — the entire grid + dialog of the target screen renders inside the tab, scoped to the parent's key.

In the Screen Designer, stage **Record form**: **＋ Add tab**, then open **Tab settings** and choose **Tab type** = *Nested table*. The panel then asks for the **Target screen**, its **Connector** and the **Parameter bindings — parent column → nested query param** (**Add binding** for each); **Tab actions** add buttons inside the tab.

### Fields

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| **`connector`** | Connector hosting the target screen. Blank = parent's connector. |
| **`screen`** *(required)* | The target screen's id. The picker is fed from the same connector's screens list. |
| **`param_binds`** | Bind parent columns into the target screen's `read_query` `:placeholder` params. |

### Behaviour

The tab renders the target screen — its grid, its filters, its add / edit dialog, its row menu — exactly as it would on its own page, but **narrowed** by the bound parameters. The user can:

- Browse the related rows in the embedded grid.
- Open the *＋ Add* button to create a new related row — the bound parent columns pre-fill matching columns on the add dialog.
- Right-click for the target screen's row menu.
- Click the inline edit button to open the target screen's dialog and edit a related row.

### Use case — customer + deals

A *Customer* dialog with a *Deals* tab showing every deal for this customer:

```toml
[[screens.crm.customers.dialog.tabs]]
id = "deals"
label = "Deals"
type = "nested_table"
screen = "deals"

[[screens.crm.customers.dialog.tabs.param_binds]]
param = "CUSTOMER_ID"
source = "CUSTOMER_ID"
```

The *Deals* tab embeds the `deals` screen's TableView, filtered to the current customer. When the user clicks *＋ Add deal* in the embedded grid, the new deal's `CUSTOMER_ID` is pre-filled with the parent's value.

### What renders inside

The embedded TableView carries everything the target screen has:

| Element | Inherited |
|---|---|
| Columns + their hints | ✓ |
| Filters | ✓ — the user can narrow further within the parent's scope. |
| Dialog (add / edit) | ✓ |
| Actions (toolbar / row menu / hooks) | ✓ |
| Export config | ✓ |

The target screen exists independently — you can navigate to it as a standalone page, AND embed it as a nested tab. The same configuration drives both surfaces.

---

## When to nest vs. when to navigate

A common decision: should the related data be **embedded** in the parent's dialog, or open as a **separate screen** on row-click?

| Choose embedding | Choose row-click navigation |
|---|---|
| The user always wants to see the related data alongside the parent (single-screen flow). | The related data is occasionally relevant; opening it on demand keeps the parent dialog focused. |
| The related table is small (a few columns, few rows). | The related table is large; embedding clutters the dialog. |
| Users edit both at the same time. | Users typically edit one then the other in separate steps. |
| | Multiple sibling screens drill into the same target — defining it once as a standalone screen is cleaner. |

Embedding is the high-affinity choice for **mandatory relationships** (a customer with at least one address); row-click is the right choice for **broad data** (a customer with hundreds of historical orders).

---

## Permissions on nested data

Nested tabs honour the **same permission model** as standalone screens — the underlying query's `sql:<connector>:<query>` permission is checked. A user who can see the parent dialog but lacks permission on the nested read query sees the nested tab as empty / read-only / hidden depending on the missing permission:

| Missing permission | Effect on the nested tab |
|---|---|
| `sql:<connector>:<nested_read>` | The tab is hidden entirely. |
| `sql:<connector>:<nested_update>` | The form is read-only. |
| `sql:<connector>:<nested_insert>` | The *＋ Add* button is hidden. |
| `sql:<connector>:<nested_delete>` | The row delete is disabled. |

This means you can build dialogs that progressively reveal data based on the user's role — same screen definition, different surfaces per user.

---

## Common pitfalls

| Mistake | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| The reused screen's read returns more than one row. | The form shows the first one only. | Tighten the binds so the read returns 0 or 1 row; use `nested_table` for a one-to-many relation. |
| `nested_table` without `param_binds`. | The embedded grid shows **every** row of the target — including unrelated ones. | Always bind at least the parent's foreign-key columns. |
| The reused screen has no insert query and no row exists yet. | Nothing is created on save. | Set the insert query on the reused screen. |
| `nested_table` pointing at a screen on a different connector + missing `connector` override. | The runtime tries to resolve the target screen on the parent's connector and fails. | Set `connector` explicitly to the target screen's connector. |
| Two nested tabs with the same id. | Save validation fails ("duplicate dialog tab id"). | Pick unique ids per dialog. |

---

- [Actions and lifecycle](./actions-and-lifecycle.md) — wire the parent's `on_save` to fire writes on the nested data.
- [Parameter binding](../queries/parameter-binding.md) — the full ParamBind reference, including `#LOGIN_USER#` / `#SYSDATE#`.

## Liberty Next — Saved grid views
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/saved-views/

Save a data grid's columns, sort, filters and grouping as a named view — your own views follow you across devices, and an admin can publish shared views with one set as the default. Also covers the screen's Summary view — parent rows counted by the database, detail rows loaded on demand — and day-grain filtering on timestamp columns.

Any data grid — a screen's table or an ad-hoc Table View — can remember how you set it up. A **view** captures the grid's full presentation and lets you switch back to it in one click:

- which **columns** are visible, and their **order**;
- the **sort**;
- the per-column **filters**;
- the **grouping**;
- the **page size**.

---

## At a glance

---

## Your views vs shared views

The **Views** menu on the grid toolbar lists two groups:

- **Shared** — published, read-only views available to everyone on that screen. An admin authors them in the [Screen Designer](build/screens/overview.md) (*Grid* stage, *Views* section), and may mark one as the **default** — the layout the grid opens with.
- **My views** — the views you save yourself. They are stored per user on the server, so they **follow you across devices and sessions**. You can have as many as you like per grid.

A regular user reads shared views and manages their own; publishing a view for everyone is an admin action in the Designer. The menu's header carries **Save** (on one of your views), **Save as…** and **Reset to shipped**; the default shared view reads *Standard · default*, a tick marks the view in use, and the button takes the name of the active view.

---

## Working with views

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Save as…** | Names the current columns, sort, filters and grouping as a new personal view. Reusing a name overwrites that view. |
| **Save** | Overwrites the active personal view in place (shown only when the active view is one of yours). |
| Select a view | Applies a shared or personal view. |
| **Delete view** | Removes one of your own views (the trash icon). |
| **Reset to shipped** | In the Views menu: back to the layout the screen ships with — its default shared view, else its base layout. |
| **Reset** | Reverts to the screen's default shared view, or to its base column layout if there is none. Handy when an older saved state conflicts with a column that is now conditionally hidden. *Reset* lives in the Columns menu. |

The grid also remembers, **per device**, the last view you opened on each table — so you land back where you left off — while the views themselves live on the server.

---

## Summary view \{#summary\}

The **Summary** view is set on the screen, not saved by the user: when the **Summary** section of the Screen Designer's *Grid* stage lists grouping columns, the grid gains a **Summary** button next to **Table** and **Chart**.

In that mode the grid shows one parent row per combination of the grouping columns, with the number of rows behind it (the count column's header is set in the same tab). The count is computed by the database over the whole result, so it stays exact even when the grid caps the rows it loads. A chevron on each parent row loads its detail rows — the screen's own query, narrowed to that group — only when it is opened.

A date or timestamp grouping column can be bucketed by **day**, **month** or **year**: the parent row then shows the period, and the detail rows are the records that fall into it.

---

## Day-grain filter on timestamp columns

Filtering a timestamp column doesn't force you to type a full `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` bound. The column-header filter lets you pick a **day** and matches every row whose timestamp falls on that day (server-side lower / upper bound).

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Save the layouts you reuse.** A "month-end" view with the right columns, filter and sort is one click away every time.
- **Publish the team's standard as a shared default.** Author it once in the Designer (*Grid → Views*) and mark it default, so everyone opens the grid on the agreed layout.
- **Reach for *Reset* when a grid looks wrong after an upgrade.** If a column became conditionally hidden, an old saved state can fight the new rule — *Reset* clears it back to the screen's default.

---

## Liberty Next — Bulk edit
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/bulk-edit/

Edit a screen's rows directly in the grid — change cells, add, clone, copy, paste and delete rows, paste from Excel or import a file — then write every change with one Save, the row hooks included.

**Bulk edit** turns a screen's grid into an editor: cells are changed in place, rows are added, cloned, copied, pasted or marked for deletion, and a single **Save** writes everything — through the same queries as the dialog, with the same row hooks.

---

## At a glance

---

## Opening bulk edit \{#open\}

The grid's toolbar shows **Bulk edit** when the screen has an update or an insert query — **Edit** when the screen has no dialog. The button is hidden on a screen that is [read-only](./build/screens/overview.md) or whose `editable` setting is off; the server's permissions still apply on top.

In bulk edit, the toolbar becomes:

| Button | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Save (n)** | Writes the pending changes; *n* counts the edited, new and deleted rows. |
| **Cancel** | Drops every pending change and leaves bulk edit. |
| **Add row** | Adds an empty row at the top of the grid, filled with the columns' default values. |
| **Import** | Reads an Excel or CSV file into the grid — see [Import a file](#import). Shown when the screen allows imports. |
| **Copy (n)** | Copies the ticked rows. |
| **Paste (n)** | Adds the copied rows as new rows. |
| **Delete selected (n)** | Marks the ticked rows for deletion; a ticked new row is simply removed. |

**Add row**, **Paste**, **Clone row** and **Import** need an insert query and are hidden when the screen disables adding. A refresh of the grid ends bulk edit without saving; the copied rows stay available.

## Rows and cells \{#rows\}

Each row starts with a check box, a marker and two buttons:

| Element | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **+** | A new row, not written yet. |
| **●** | An existing row with edited cells. |
| **−** | A row marked for deletion. |
| **Clone row** | Adds a copy of the row at the top — see [Clone, copy and paste](#clone). |
| **×** | Marks the row for deletion (a second click undoes it); on a new row, removes it. |
| Padlock | The row is read-only: the screen's `editable_when` rule excludes it, so its cells stay plain and it cannot be deleted. |

A cell stays read-only when its column is disabled — `disabled`, or `disabled_when` for the row's values —, or locked for that kind of row: `disable_on_add` on a new row, `disable_on_edit` on an existing one. See [Conditional fields](./build/screens/conditional-fields.md).

## Clone, copy and paste \{#clone\}

**Clone row**, and **Paste** of copied rows, add new rows that keep every value of the source, keys included — copy a row, then change the one value that differs. The only exception is a column filled by a `SEQUENCE` rule: it is left empty, and the insert takes a new number from the sequence; the related one-to-one tables of the screen follow that new key.

A row born from a clone or a paste is a duplicate: on Save it fires the screen's `on_duplicate` hook, with the source row's values under `SOURCE_<column>`, exactly as the dialog's **Duplicate** does — see [Actions and lifecycle](./build/screens/actions-and-lifecycle.md).

## Paste from Excel \{#paste-excel\}

Cells copied from Excel (or any tab-separated text) and pasted into the grid — with no cell being edited — become new rows:

- when the first pasted line matches at least two column headers, it is read as a header line and each value goes to the column of that name, whatever the order;
- otherwise the values follow the order of the visible columns, as an export of the grid lays them out.

A column with a lookup fills its dependent columns from the pasted code, as when the code is picked in the list.

## Import a file \{#import\}

**Import** in bulk edit reads an Excel or CSV file whose first line holds the column headers. A line whose key columns match a row already in the grid becomes an edit of that row; the other lines become new rows. Nothing is written until **Save**, so the result can be reviewed and corrected first.

Outside bulk edit, the toolbar's **Import** opens the Import dialog instead, which checks every line against the screen's rules before saving — see [Bulk import](./cookbook/bulk-import.md).

## Save \{#save\}

**Save** writes the rows in one pass:

- each edited row through the update query, each new row through the insert query, each row marked for deletion through the delete query — together with the columns stored in the screen's related one-to-one tables;
- a column whose default is forced by a condition (`default_when`) is written with that value even when its cell was not edited;
- then, row by row, the hooks: `on_update`, `on_insert` (or `on_duplicate` for a cloned or pasted row) and `on_delete`.

When a write or a hook fails, its message shows and bulk edit stays open. After a successful save, bulk edit closes and the grid reloads.

---

## Liberty Next — Phone and tablet
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/mobile/

Liberty Next applications on a phone and a tablet: the menu as a drawer or an icon rail, a grid shown as a list of cards with a heading, full-screen dialogs, a record form in one column, the period picker and filters fitted to a narrow screen, the Card setting of a column — and the resizable menu on a desktop.

An application built with Liberty Next is used as it is on a phone and a tablet: nothing is designed twice. The layout follows the width of the screen; on a desktop nothing changes for a mouse.

The Studio stacks its columns one under the other, its panel below them; the designers and the authoring of an Explorer analysis remain desktop layouts.

---

## At a glance

---

## On a phone \{#phone\}

Below 768 px:

| Element | Becomes |
|---|---|
| **Menu** | A drawer, opened by the **Menu** button at the top left. |
| **Header** | Its buttons sit in a row of their own above the tabs, which scroll sideways. |
| **Dialogs** | Full screen. |
| **Grid** | A list: each row a card. |
| **Record form** | Its fields in one column; its tabs scroll. |
| **Filters, period** | Each filter takes the whole width; the period picker shows its presets as a row above one month. |

### A row as a card \{#card\}

A card has a **heading** — the first two columns, side by side and larger — then four lines *label · value*; **+N** opens the rest. A blank value gives no line, and a field shown as a code and its label is one line.

The search, the pager, the row menu (**Row actions**) and **Bulk edit** are there; the views, grouping, columns and export controls keep only their icon. Sorting and the header's filter row are wide-screen gestures: the filters set on a wider window still apply, and **Clear filters** stays to remove them.

### Choosing what a card shows \{#card-setting\}

A column decides for itself with its **Card** setting, in the [column settings](./build/screens/columns.md):

| Value | Effect |
|---|---|
| `title` | The column is in the card's heading. |
| `show` | The column always has a line. |
| `hide` | The column is never shown on a card. |
| blank | The grid decides: the first two columns are the heading, the next four are lines, the others open with **+N**. |

---

## On a tablet \{#tablet\}

From 768 to 1100 px — a tablet in portrait — the menu is the **icon rail**, whatever the mode saved on a desktop: its button opens it over the page, a tap elsewhere folds it back. The header's buttons take their short form so that the tabs keep their room. Grids and forms keep their desktop layout.

---

## On a desktop: a menu as wide as needed \{#menu\}

The menu's right edge is dragged to resize it, from 180 to 460 px; the width is remembered on the browser, and a double click gives the default back. A menu entry's label takes two lines instead of being cut; its full text stays in the tooltip.

---

## Tips & best practices \{#tips\}

- Put the two columns that identify a row first — a number and a name — or set them to `title`: they are the heading of every card.
- Set to `hide` the technical columns a phone user never reads.
- Give long labels a short form in the dictionary: a card line is *label · value*.
- Check the screens meant for the field on a real phone before delivering.

---

## Related

- [Columns](./build/screens/columns.md) · [Bulk edit](./bulk-edit.md) · [Saved views](./saved-views.md)

## Liberty Next — Apps
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/apps/overview/

What an app is in Liberty Next — a connector with a menu, shown in the app picker — what belongs to it (queries, dictionary scope, screens, menu, charts), how users switch between apps, and how an app is copied, moved between environments or installed ready-made.

In Liberty Next, an **app** is a **connector that has a menu and is shown in the app switcher** (**Show in switcher**, on by default): its name appears in the app picker at the top of the sidebar, and picking it shows its menu. There is no separate app object to create — the connector is the app. The [Overview](../studio.md#overview) page lists the apps of the installation, and the [Studio](../studio.md#studio) shows each one as a map of its menu, screens, data and services.

---

## At a glance

---

## What belongs to an app \{#scope\}

Everything an app shows is filed under its connector's name:

| Element | Where it is set | Stored under |
|---|---|---|
| Queries (tables, queries, sequences, lookups) | Liberty Next → Data → Connectors | The connector itself. |
| Dictionary entries, enums, lookups, sequences | Liberty Next → Data → Dictionary, the connector's **scope** | `[connectors.<app>.*]` — on top of the shared entries. |
| Screens | Liberty Next → Screens → Screens, the app's chip | `[screens.<app>.<id>]` |
| Menu | Liberty Next → Screens → Menus, the app's chip | `[menus.<app>]` |
| Charts | Liberty Next → Insight → Charts, the connector's scope | `[charts.<app>.<id>]` |
| Dashboards | Liberty Next → Insight → Dashboards, the app | `[dashboards.<app>.<id>]` — a menu item opens it with the target `<app>.<id>`. |

Services have a single namespace. Nomaflow jobs are not tied to an app.

---

## The app picker \{#picker\}

The picker sits at the top of the sidebar:

- it lists the apps whose menu the user can see, and appears only when there are at least two;
- picking an app switches the sidebar menu and the workspace tabs to that app — it is a switch, not a filter;
- the choice is remembered in the browser;
- when the app's connector has several pools, a **Pool** picker next to it chooses the database instance every screen runs against — see [Connectors → Multi-pool](../connectors.md#multi-pool).

A connector's **show_in_switcher** (on by default) and **home** settings decide whether it is offered in the picker and which menu item opens first. See [Make a connector an app](../build/menus/make-connector-an-app.md).

---

## Creating an app \{#create\}

1. **Liberty Next → Data → Connectors** — create the SQL connector and its pool, then its queries (the CRUD wizard writes them from a table).
2. **Liberty Next → Screens → Screens** — build the screens on these queries.
3. **Liberty Next → Screens → Menus** — **+ Add scope**, pick the connector, add the items that open the screens.
4. Back on the connector, check **show_in_switcher** and, optionally, set **home**.

The [Screen Creation Assistant](../build/screen-assistant.md) chains steps 1 to 3 for one table. The [CRM tutorial](../tutorial-crm/01-setup.md) builds a complete app.

---

## Copying and moving an app \{#copy\}

| Need | Tool |
|---|---|
| A second app built on an existing one (another database, a test copy). | **Clone** on the connector: copies the queries with the dictionary scope, screens, menu, charts and dashboards under the new name. See [Clone a query or a connector](../build/queries/clone.md). |
| Move an app, or part of it, to another environment (development → production). | **Packages**: pick the screens, menus, dashboards… to ship, download the ZIP with everything they depend on, import it on the target. See [Packages](../build/packages.md). |
| Rename a connector, a screen or a query. | **Rename** in its editor — every reference is rewritten. |

---

## Ready-made apps \{#ready-made\}

**Nomasx-1** and **Nomajde** are delivered as ready-made apps with their Nomaflow jobs. They are installed and upgraded as described in [Deploy the licensed apps](../../installation/deploy-prebuilt-apps.md). Their screens, menus and dictionary are visible and editable in Liberty Next like any app; an entry marked **override** keeps local changes through upgrades.

---

## Who sees an app \{#access\}

An app appears for a user when it is shown in the switcher and its menu has items that user may open. Roles decide which menu items, screens and queries each user reaches — see [Roles & permissions](../build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md) and [Menus → Permissions and roles](../build/menus/permissions-and-roles.md).

---

- [Make a connector an app](../build/menus/make-connector-an-app.md) — the two settings that put a connector in the picker.
- [Plugins](./plugins.md) — Python functions called from jobs and screen actions.
- [Translations](./i18n.md) — labels per language.
