## Liberty Next — Dashboards
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/dashboards/

Liberty Next dashboards: KPIs, figures, decision lists, proportion bars, charts and tables over connector queries on a 12-column grid, Excel and PDF export, a period with presets and comparison with the previous period, dictionary filters, a cache with Refresh — built in Liberty Next → Insight → Dashboards and opened from the menu.

A dashboard puts several **widgets** — figures, decision lists, proportion bars, charts, tables — side by side, each fed by a query of a connector. It opens from the menu like a screen, and it is built in **Liberty Next → Insight → Dashboards**.

---

## At a glance

---

## Widgets \{#widgets\}

Widgets sit on a 12-column grid, in the order they are declared. Each one takes a width of 1 to 12 columns and a height of 1 to 8 rows, and carries a title and an optional **subtitle** — one line under the title that says what the widget covers.

| Widget | Shows | Settings |
|---|---|---|
| **KPI** | One figure computed over every row of a query. | Connector, query, column, aggregation (`count`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, or `none` for the first row's value), format, and **compare with the previous period**. |
| **Figure** | A figure card read from the query's **first row**, with a line of detail under it. | **Value column**, **Format**, **Unit**, **Sub line**. |
| **List** | A decision or ranked list: one line per row, with a coloured dot, a title, a subtitle, a figure and a tag. | **Title column** (required), **Subtitle column**, **Value column**, format, unit, **Count column** and **Count wording**, **Tone column**, **Tag column**, **Rows shown**. |
| **Bars** | A ranked list with a proportion bar under each row. | **Label column** and **Value column** (required), **Sub label column**, format, unit, **Bar as a share of**, **Note under the bars**, **Rows shown**. |
| **Chart** | A bar, line, area or pie chart. | A chart saved in **Liberty Next → Insight → Charts**, or a connector, a query and a chart definition written in the widget — see [Charts](./charts.md). |
| **Table** | The rows of a query. | Connector, query, the columns to show (all when empty), a row limit. |
| **Text** | A block of Markdown: what the page is for, how to read it. Headings, lists and links are allowed. | **Text (Markdown)**. |
| **Jobs** | The Nomaflow jobs with their next run, their schedule in words and their last state, and **Run now** / **Pause** / **Resume**. Superusers only. | **Jobs (ids, in order)** — empty = every scheduled job —, **Only these tags**, **Max rows** (12 when blank). |
| **Links** | A card of entry points: menu items of the dashboard's application, or web addresses. | **Links per row** (1 to 4); per link a **Menu item** or a **URL**, an **Icon**, a **Label** (blank: the menu item's) and a **Description**. |

A widget whose query the user may not run is hidden; the rest of the dashboard still shows. Every card carries its title and subtitle inside it, and the page grows with its widgets: it scrolls to the last one.

### Figure, List and Bars \{#synthesis\}

These three widgets turn a dashboard into a **synthesis page**: the figures that matter, what needs a decision, and the proportions, each read from a query written for it.

- **Format**: *Number*, *Integer*, *Currency* (euros, no decimals for a whole amount) or *Percent* — a ratio between 0 and 1, shown as a percentage. The **Unit** follows the figure (`users`, `lines`); a currency carries its own symbol.
- **Sub line** (Figure): a sentence with placeholders filled from the first row, `{COLUMN}` or `{COLUMN:format}` — `{ENABLED:integer} enabled · {DISABLED:integer} disabled` gives *380 enabled · 32 disabled*. A placeholder naming an unknown column stays as written.
- **Tone column** (List): a column holding `ok`, `warn`, `error` or `info` colours the dot green, orange, red or blue; any other value gives a grey dot. The query decides the tone — a period that is closed, an amount above a threshold.
- **Count wording** (List): the text around the count column, `{n} conflict lines`. The **Tag column** shows its value as a pill next to the title, in the line's tone.
- **Bar as a share of** (Bars): **The total of the rows** — the bars add up to 100 % — or **The largest row**, which gets the full bar.

The editor shows a live preview of the widget as soon as the connector, the query and the required columns are chosen.

### Jobs \{#jobs\}

A **Jobs** card puts the scheduler on a dashboard. Each line shows the job — a click opens it in Nomaflow —, its next run or *Paused*, its schedule in words (*every day at 03:00*), the state of its last run, and three buttons: **Run now** with the job's saved values, **Pause the schedule**, **Resume the schedule** — applied at once. Without ids, the card lists the scheduled jobs, the next to run first, optionally narrowed to some tags (`main`, `nomasx1`). The card refreshes itself while a run is going.

The card is for superusers only: for anyone else, it does not show on the dashboard.

### Text and Links \{#text-links\}

These two widgets turn a dashboard into the **home page of an application**: a few lines on what it does, the figures, then where to go.

- A **Text** or **Links** widget the full width of the grid (12 columns) takes the height of its content, with no scroll bar; a narrower one scrolls within its tile.
- A **Links** widget only shows the menu items the user may open: an entry their roles do not grant disappears from the card. A URL opens in a new browser tab. A URL link needs a label.
- In an export, a text keeps its Markdown and a links card becomes a table (*Link*, *Description*).

---

## The period \{#period\}

A dashboard can carry a **period**: a date range control in its bar that applies to every widget.

- **Presets**: Today, Yesterday, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month, Last month, This quarter, This year, Last year, Last 12 months, All dates. The *Yesterday* preset covers yesterday and today.
- **A free range**: pick a start date, then an end date, in the two-month calendar, then **Apply**.
- **Date basis**: when the dashboard offers several dates (*Document date*, *Paid on*), a **Date** choice at the bottom of the panel picks the one the range applies to.

The dashboard opens on its own default preset, otherwise on the application's default (**Liberty Next → Administer → App → Default period (dashboards)**, *This month* by default). A choice lasts as long as the dashboard tab stays open.

### What the queries receive

| Bind | Value |
|---|---|
| `:PERIOD_FROM`, `:PERIOD_TO` | The chosen range, as dates. *All dates* binds `0001-01-01` to `9999-12-31`. |
| `:PREV_FROM`, `:PREV_TO` | The period before (see below). |
| `:PERIOD_BASIS` | The chosen date basis, when the dashboard offers several. |

A query that does not mention them is not affected. When the period names its date column — directly or through a dictionary item found in the widget's screen — the widget is also filtered on the server on that column, **without any change to its SQL**.

### The previous period

| Range | Compared with |
|---|---|
| Starting on 1 January (*This year*, *Last year*) | The same dates one year earlier. |
| Starting on the 1st of a month | The same number of months just before — *Last month* with the month before, a whole quarter with the quarter before; *This month* on the 27th with the 1st–27th of the previous month. |
| Anything else | The same number of days just before. |

### Comparing a KPI

With **Compare with the previous period** ticked, a KPI runs its query a second time on the previous period and shows, under the figure, the change — in percent, in points for a percent KPI — in green or red, and the previous value. Nothing is compared on *All dates*.

---

## Filters \{#filters\}

A dashboard can also carry **filters**, shown as dropdowns in its bar. Each filter has a label, a dictionary item and a query that provides its choices (value column and label column), and an optional value at opening — the value the dashboard opens on. Choosing a value reloads every widget whose query returns a column carrying that dictionary item — through the widget's screen, or directly from the query's result columns: a column with the item's name, or with the connector's column prefix in front of it. The other widgets are left as they are. A period whose date column is given as a dictionary item finds its column the same way.

In the editor, each filter says which widgets it reaches — *Reaches: …*, with *not: …* for the others — or *Reaches no widget* when no column carries the dictionary item.

With **All**, nothing is filtered: a query that returns one total row first, then one row per value, shows the totals in its Figure and List widgets.

---

## Refresh and cache \{#cache\}

When a dashboard is opened again, each widget reuses its last result for **Liberty Next → Administer → App → Dashboard cache (seconds, 0 = none)** — 60 seconds by default. The **↻** button in the bar reloads everything, and *Updated at 14:05* says when the data was fetched. The cache is kept in the browser, per user, until the page is reloaded.

---

## Export to Excel and PDF \{#export\}

The **Excel** and **PDF** buttons, next to **↻**, export what the bar holds: the filter picks, the period and its date basis, under the user's data scope. The server runs every widget again; nothing is taken from the screen.

| | Excel | PDF |
|---|---|---|
| Layout | One sheet per widget; the KPIs together on a *Key figures* sheet. | A cover with the dashboard, the period and the filters, then the widgets one after the other. |
| KPI, Figure | A row of values. | A card, with the sub line in small type under the figure. |
| List, Bars, Table | Its rows. | A table. |
| Text, Links | The text; the links as rows. | The text; a table of the links. |
| Chart | Its data table. | The chart drawn, with a legend and the values on the bars. |

A widget whose query fails becomes an error section; the rest of the export still renders. Numbers follow the reader's language (`1 234,5` / `1,234.5`). PDF branding is set in [Liberty Next → Administer → App](./build/settings-app.md#branding).

---

## Building a dashboard \{#builder\}

**Liberty Next → Insight → Dashboards** lists the dashboards of one application: the **Connector** chips at the top pick it, **Add scope** adds another, and **Filter…** narrows the list. Each line gives the id, the title, the number of widgets and filters, and the description. **Add dashboard** and **Reload config** are in the page header, and each line has:

| Button | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Find dependencies** | Lists what the dashboard relies on (queries, charts, connector…) and downloads it with the ticked items as a package. |
| **Rename** | Changes the dashboard's id. |
| **Clone** | Copies the dashboard under a new id. |
| **Delete** | Removes the dashboard. |

### Opening the editor \{#open-editor\}

**Add dashboard** first asks for the new dashboard's name (*Its name:*, e.g. *Sales overview*) and makes its id from it (`sales_overview`), shown while it is typed. A click on a line, or the name given, opens the editor over the whole window. Its title bar names the dashboard by its title, followed by its application and its id (*Sales overview* `sales · overview`). A refused save keeps the editor open and lists what to correct — see [A refused save](./configuration/settings-ui.md#refused).

| Part | Content |
|---|---|
| **Title**, **Description** | Shown at the top of the dashboard; the *In the other languages* block under them gives both in the other languages — see [Texts in other languages](#languages). |
| **Keep this one as it is on upgrade (an upgrade of the application then leaves it as saved here)** | Ticked, an upgrade of the application that ships the dashboard leaves it as saved here. |
| **Add widget** | Chart, KPI, Table, **Figure**, **List**, **Bars**, **Text**, **Links** or **Jobs**: the widget's dialog opens on that kind, and **Cancel** leaves nothing behind. |
| The grid | The real widgets, drawn with live data as the dashboard shows them, each under its label. Hovering a card shows its tools: the **grip**, its size (`4 × 1`, columns × rows), **✎** to edit it and the bin to remove it. A card is moved by **drag and drop** — its grip dragged onto another card, a bar showing on which side it will land — and sized by its **bottom-right corner**, in whole columns (1 to 12) and rows (1 to 8). The grip takes the keyboard too: arrows move the card, Shift + arrows size it. |
| **Period** | **Add a period** / **Remove the period**: **Opens on** (a preset, or *App default (Liberty Next → Administer → App)*), **Date column** or **or dictionary item**, and optional **Date bases** (key, label, date column or dictionary item). |
| **Filters** | **Add filter**: **Id**, **Label**, **Dictionary key**, then the **Connector**, the **Query**, the **Value column** and the **Label column** that fill the dropdown, and **Value at opening** — the value the dashboard opens on (blank: *none: every value*). Under each filter, *Reaches: …* names the widgets it filters — see [Filters](#filters) —, and an *In the other languages* block gives its label in the other languages. A filter left without an id or a label stops the save: *A filter has no id or no label yet: complete it or remove it.* |

The footer counts the widgets and holds **Cancel** and **Save**. Closing the editor with unsaved changes asks whether to save them, discard them or keep editing.

### The widget dialog \{#widget-dialog\}

The **✎** of a card opens the **Widget** dialog: the nine kinds as tabs at the top — a widget can change kind —, then **Label**, **Width (1–12)**, **Height (rows)**, **Subtitle**, the connector and the query, and the fields of the kind (see [Widgets](#widgets)). Below the fields, a preview draws the widget with live data as soon as the required fields are set. The footer shows the widget's kind (`stat`, `list`…) on the left, **Cancel** and **Save** on the right.

### Texts in other languages \{#languages\}

A dashboard reads in the user's language. Every text it shows is given in the other languages in the editor itself, in an **In the other languages** block under the field: one line per language, one box per text. A box left blank shows the text as written (*Left blank, the text above is shown.*).

| Where | The block gives |
|---|---|
| The dashboard | Its **Title** and its **Description**. |
| A widget (its dialog) | Its **Label** and **Subtitle**, and by kind: the **Sub line** and **Unit** of a Figure; the **Count wording**, **Unit**, and the **Title column**, **Subtitle column** and **Tag column (a pill)** of a List; the **Note under the bars**, **Unit**, **Label column** and **Sub label column** of Bars; the **Text (Markdown)** of a Text. |
| A link of a Links widget | Its **Label** and its **Description**. |
| A filter | Its **Label**. |

A column given in another language names the column to read for the users of that language — for a query that returns one column per language (`TITLE`, `TITLE_FR`).

To make the dashboard reachable, add a **dashboard** entry to a menu ([Menus](./build/menus/item-types.md)); its permission is `dashboard:<app>.<id>`.

### In TOML

```toml title="dashboards.toml"
[dashboards.sales.overview]
label = "Sales overview"
period = { column = "DOC_DATE", default = "thisMonth" }

  [[dashboards.sales.overview.widgets]]
  type = "kpi"
  label = "Revenue"
  connector = "sales"
  query = "revenue_by_company_get"
  column = "REVENUE"
  aggregation = "sum"
  compare_previous = true
  col_span = 4

  [[dashboards.sales.overview.widgets]]
  type = "chart"
  chart = "revenue_by_month"
  col_span = 8
  row_span = 2
```

---

## Tips \{#tips\}

- Give the dashboard a period rather than date filters in each query: one control, and the comparison comes for free.
- For a synthesis page, write one small query per Figure or List and let the query compute the tone: the dashboard only shows it.
- A KPI with `none` shows the first row's value: let the query compute the figure when the aggregation is complex.
- Keep the cache on for dashboards opened often; **↻** always gives fresh figures.

---

## Liberty Next — Charts
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/charts/

A saved chart draws the result of a connector query as bars, lines, areas or a pie: an X column, one or more series with their colour and axis, and an aggregation. Built in Liberty Next → Insight → Charts or saved from a screen's Chart view, then reused in dashboards.

A **chart** draws the result of a connector's query: an X column, one or more series, and an aggregation for the rows that share the same X value. It is saved under a name and reused in [dashboards](./dashboards.md); the same chart settings are available on the fly in a screen's **Chart** view.

Four types are available: **bar**, **line**, **area** and **pie**.

---

## At a glance

---

## Liberty Next → Insight → Charts \{#list\}

Charts are grouped by connector: the **Connector** chips at the top pick one, **Add scope** adds a connector that has no chart yet, and **Filter…** narrows the list. Each line shows the chart's id, its label, then its query, its type and its X column (`sales.revenue_get · line · x: MONTH`), with an *override* badge when it is marked as a local customisation. **Add chart** and **Reload config** are in the page header. Each line has:

| Button | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Find usages** | The dashboards that show the chart. |
| **Find dependencies** | Lists what the chart depends on (query, connector…) and downloads the chart with the ticked items as a package. |
| **Rename** | Changes the chart's id. |
| **Clone** | Copies the chart under a new id. |
| **Delete** | Removes the chart. |

**Add chart** opens the editor for a new chart in the current scope; clicking a line opens it for editing.

---

## The editor \{#editor\}

The editor opens in a window titled by the chart's label, followed by its connector and its id (*Revenue by month* `sales · revenue_by_month`), and has two tabs, **General** and **Chart**. **Cancel** and **Save** are in its footer; closing it with unsaved changes asks whether to save them, discard them or keep editing.

### General \{#general\}

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Id** | The chart's identifier: letters, digits, underscores and hyphens. Dashboards refer to the chart by this id. |
| **Label** | The chart's title in lists and dashboards. |
| **Description** | Optional. |
| **Keep this one as it is on upgrade (an upgrade of the application then leaves it as saved here)** | Ticked, an upgrade of the application that ships the chart leaves it as saved here — see [Upgrades](#override). |
| **Connector** | The connector of the scope — fixed; to move a chart to another connector, recreate it in that scope. |
| **Query** | The read query whose result the chart draws. The buttons next to it edit the query, clone it or create a new one without leaving the editor. |

### Chart \{#chart\}

The tab loads a sample of the query's rows and draws the chart as it is set:

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Chart** | The type: bar, line, area or pie. |
| **X axis** | The column along the X axis — the slice labels on a pie. |
| **Series** | One block per Y column: the column, a colour swatch, **L** / **R** to put the series on the left or the right Y axis, and **✕** to remove it. **+** adds a series. A pie uses the first series only. |
| **Pivot by** | Optional, not on a pie. A column whose distinct values become the series: one series per value (a process, a status), each the aggregate of the first Y column. A query returning *refresh date · process · lines* gives one bar per refresh, stacked by process, without pivoting in SQL. |
| **Options** | How the chart is drawn, each box showing what the chart does now: **Stacked** (bar and area only), **Legend**, **Grid lines** (not on a pie) and **Sort the X axis**. |
| **Aggregate** | How rows sharing the same X value are combined: **Sum**, **Average**, **Count** (counts rows, ignores the Y value), **Min**, **Max**, or **None (per row)** to keep each row — for a time series whose X is already unique. |

The Y axis shows compact ticks (1.2k, 27.5M); the tooltip gives the full figure. As soon as one series is on the right axis, the chart gets a second Y axis — useful for two scales, such as an amount and a count. Unless **Legend** says otherwise, the legend shows when there is more than one series. Without a colour, a series takes the next colour of the palette.

An X column and at least one series are required to save.

---

## From a screen's Chart view \{#from-a-screen\}

The **Chart** button of a screen switches the grid to a chart of the rows on display, with the same settings (type, X axis, series, aggregation). Two extras appear there:

- **Load saved** — applies a saved chart built on the same connector and query;
- **Save…** — saves the current chart under an id, a label and a description, ready for dashboards. Only a superuser sees this button.

---

## In a dashboard \{#in-a-dashboard\}

A dashboard's **Chart** widget shows a saved chart by its id, or holds its own chart definition. A change to the saved chart shows on every dashboard that uses it. See [Dashboards](./dashboards.md).

---

## Upgrades \{#override\}

The *override* badge flags a chart marked as a local customisation — the **Keep this one as it is on upgrade** box of its editor: an upgrade package does not overwrite it. See [Packages](./build/packages.md).

---

## What's next

- [Dashboards](./dashboards.md) — put charts, figures and tables side by side.
- [Connectors](./connectors.md) — the queries a chart reads.
- [Saved views](./saved-views.md) — what a user can keep from a screen.

## Liberty Next — Data Explorer
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/explorer/overview/

The Liberty Next Data Explorer: free analysis of an app's data without writing SQL — fields pane, rows, measures and filters, a period, table, pivot, charts and KPI views, detail rows and drill, calculated fields, saved analyses, dashboards and Excel / PDF export, over a model built in Liberty Next → Insight → Explorer.

The Data Explorer lets users analyse an app's data on their own: they pick fields, group, filter, choose a period, then read the result as a table, a pivot, a chart or KPI cards — without writing a query. It works on any connected application whose data is reached through a SQL connector, or through the endpoints of an API connector.

An operator first describes the data once, as a **model**, in **Liberty Next → Insight → Explorer**. Users then open the explorer from the **compass** in the header, which appears when at least one model is available to them, or from a menu entry that opens it on a model, a saved analysis or a dashboard.

---

## At a glance

---

## The pieces \{#pieces\}

| Piece | What it is | Page |
|---|---|---|
| **Model** | One data mart of an app: a central entity (the **hub**, such as deals or invoice lines) and the entities around it (customers, activities…), each read by a query or a table of a SQL connector (or an endpoint of an API connector), joined by relations. An app can have several models. | [Build a model](./model.md) |
| **Analysis** | What the user puts together on the page: rows, measures, filters, a period, a view. | [Analyse data](./analysis.md) |
| **Calculated field** | A field computed from the others (`AMOUNT * 0.6`, `year(CLOSE_DATE)`), typed and checked on the server. | [Calculated fields](./calculated-fields.md) |
| **Saved analysis, dashboard** | An analysis kept under a name, private or shared; a dashboard is a grid of saved analyses. Both export to Excel and PDF. | [Saved analyses and dashboards](./saved-and-dashboards.md) |

---

## Who sees what \{#access\}

- A model is offered to the holders of a role that grants it: in **Liberty Next → Administer → Access → Roles**, **Beyond the menus**, type **Data Explorer**, then a model, or every model of an app. Superusers see every model. See [Roles & permissions](../build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md#access).
- The role's **data scope** applies inside every query the explorer runs: a user who sees one company's rows in the screens sees the same rows in the explorer, the totals included. See [Data scope](../build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md#data-scope).
- A menu entry can open the explorer on one model (`/explorer/<app>/<model>`), so each functional folder of an app reaches its own data; the model picker still lets the user switch. See [Menu item types](../build/menus/item-types.md#explorer).
- A shared analysis or dashboard can become a menu entry of its own: a superuser uses **Add to a menu**, and one click on the entry opens the explorer on it, its result at once. See [Add to a menu](./saved-and-dashboards.md#menu).
- Only a superuser edits **Liberty Next → Insight → Explorer**, and sees the SQL of an analysis and the model's warnings (a column that disappeared, a measure that is not numeric).

---

## What it is not \{#limits\}

- **Not a SQL editor.** Users never type SQL: the explorer builds one statement from the model, the same on Oracle, PostgreSQL and SQLite. A calculated field is a small expression language, compiled by the server.
- **Not unlimited.** An aggregate reads at most 50,000 grouped rows (beyond that, a note says the figures are partial) and shows the **Top** N groups (up to 10,000). The detail view pages through the rows; an export holds up to 3,000 rows per section.
- **Not a replacement for dashboards.** [Dashboards](../dashboards.md) are designed by an operator over chosen queries; the explorer lets users build their own views over a model.

---

## What's next

- [Build a model](./model.md) — Liberty Next → Insight → Explorer, from scratch or from a Screen Assistant preset.
- [Analyse data](./analysis.md) — the page, step by step.

---

## Liberty Next — Build a model
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/explorer/model/

Liberty Next → Insight → Explorer in Liberty Next: an explorer model per data mart — the hub, the entities (a query with its cardinality, key, measures, hidden columns and default date), the relations on column pairs, and a model filled from a Screen Assistant preset.

A model tells the explorer what a user may analyse and how the tables relate. It is built in **Liberty Next → Insight → Explorer** by a superuser, with no SQL: every entity reads an existing query of a connector, and the columns are discovered from that query's result.

---

## At a glance

---

## The app and the model \{#app-model\}

1. **App** — the chips at the top list the apps that already have a model; **Add scope** opens *Add an app*, which offers the SQL connectors that have none.
2. **Model** — pick a model of the app, or **Add model** and give its id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`). An app can hold several models: tables that do not relate to one another belong in different models. **Delete model** removes it with its entities and relations.
3. The header of the model:

| Field | Use |
|---|---|
| **Label** | The name users see in the explorer's model picker. |
| **Hub** | The entity every analysis starts from: a fact table, a document header, the lines of a document. |
| **Description** | Shown under the explorer's title. |
| **Preset (Screen Assistant)** | Fills the model from a preset — see [below](#preset). |
| **Listed under** | The heading the model sits under in the explorer's list of models (*Finance*). Blank: its preset's, else the application. |
| **Keep this model as it is on upgrade** | An upgrade of the application then leaves the model as saved here. |
| **Delivered analyses**, **Delivered dashboards** | What the model delivers: analyses and dashboards installed for everyone, picked among those saved and shared in the explorer — see [What a model delivers](#delivers). |

### What a model delivers \{#delivers\}

Under the model's settings, two lists name the analyses and the dashboards the application ships with the model. **Deliver a saved analysis…** / **Deliver a saved dashboard…** offers the model's analyses and dashboards that are saved and shared in the explorer; the one picked is copied into the model, with its version (*version 1*). Each delivered line has:

- **↻** — *Refresh from the saved one*: its version goes up, and the installed copies nobody changed follow;
- the bin — *No longer deliver it*: the installed copies stay.

Picking again one already delivered (*delivered — pick to refresh*) refreshes it too. A delivered dashboard that shows analyses not delivered says so: *shows analyses that are not delivered: …*.

**Save** writes the model and reloads it: the explorer sees it at once. A model without any entity is refused, by name — *Not saved: these models have no entity yet — crm · deals. Add an entity (or apply a preset), or delete the model.* — unless it names a preset: it is then kept, filled from the preset at first use, and the page draws it with the offer to fill it.

---

## The model as a diagram \{#diagram\}

In **Insight → Explorer**, a model is drawn: the **hub**, the entities it reaches placed by how far they are from it — the details (several rows per hub row) on its left, what a hub row has one of on its right —, and each relation as a line carrying the columns it joins on. Above the canvas, **Add entity** and **Add relation**, and a count: *N entity(ies) · N relation(s)*, with the entities not linked to the hub and the relations without columns when there are any. The canvas zooms with **−** / **+**. Set apart in orange: the entities **not linked to the hub** — an analysis cannot use them — and the relations with *no column pair yet*. The layout is computed from the model; nothing is placed by hand.

| Click | The side panel shows |
|---|---|
| Nothing | The model's own settings: **Label**, **Hub**, **Description**, **Preset (Screen Assistant)**, **Listed under**, **Keep this model as it is on upgrade**, and what it delivers. |
| An entity | What it is — its query or table, key, measures, default date — and its relations, with **Edit**, **Make it the hub**, **Delete**, and **Add relation** from it. A relation of the list opens it; the button at the top goes back. |
| A line | The relation: its two entities, its column pairs (**Joined on**) and **Delete this relation**. |

An empty model starts **From a prebuilt model** — a preset — or **By hand**. **Add model**, **Delete model** and **Save** are in the page header.

---

## Entities \{#entities\}

**Add entity** (or a click on an entity) opens its form:

| Field | Use |
|---|---|
| **Id** | The entity's identifier, fixed once created (`deals`, `customers`). |
| **Label** | The name of the group in the fields pane. |
| **Rows per hub row** | **1..1 · one** — at most one row per hub row (the customer of a deal); **1..n · many** — several rows (the activities of a deal). The hub itself is always 1..1. |
| **Description** | Free text. |
| **Connector** | The connector of the query; the app's own by default. The list holds the SQL connectors and the API connectors that have an endpoint with rows, shown as `name (API)` — see [below](#api-entity). |
| **Reads** | *a query* or *a table* — on an API connector, *a service*. The fields below follow the choice. |
| **Query** | With *a query*: a SELECT query of that connector — or, on an API connector, one of its endpoints with rows (**a service**). Its columns are discovered by running it for one row. |
| **Schema**, **Table** | With *a table*: the table is read as it is, without writing a query — the schema, then the table, picked from the database (or typed). An entity filled from a preset reads its table this way. |
| **Screen (column hints)** | A screen whose column settings give the labels, formats and lists of values. The screens that read the same query come first. The entity opens a row in that screen's dialog, so **Deploy → Integrity** counts the screen as reached even when no menu entry leads to it. |
| **Default date** | The date field the period applies to first. |
| **Fixed values of the query's parameters** | Shown when the query asks for parameters — those it declares and the binds of its statement —, one field each: the value given there is used for every analysis. A parameter left blank is not sent. |
| **Keep this entity as it is on upgrade** | An upgrade of the application then leaves the entity as saved here. |

The **Columns** table lists the discovered columns, with the label and the type taken from the screen. For each one:

- **Key** — the columns that identify a row. A new entity takes the screen's key columns. The key opens a row in its screen's dialog from the detail view.
- **Measure** — a numeric column that users sum, average, count…: pick its default aggregate (`sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`, `count_distinct`). Left on *— dimension —*, the column groups and filters.
- **Hidden** — left out of the fields pane. A column hidden by the screen stays hidden.

A column that the query no longer returns is flagged with **?** so it can be unticked.

### What users get from a column \{#fields\}

Each column becomes a **field** of the pane, labelled and formatted through the dictionary and the screen, and typed as text, number, date, date-time or yes/no. A column with a list of values (an enum or a lookup in the screen) shows its labels and offers its values in the filters. A column declared as a measure but not numeric stays a dimension, and the model reports it to superusers.

### An entity read from an API endpoint \{#api-entity\}

An entity can also read an endpoint of an API connector — one that returns rows, as a screen reads it. It is picked in the entity form: the API connector in **Connector** — listed as `name (API)` when it has an endpoint with rows —, the endpoint in **Query**; it then shows on the diagram like the others. Its fields are discovered from the endpoint's columns and labelled by the dictionary; the explorer reads the rows under the user's data scope and filters, groups, measures, sorts and pages them itself, so analyses, dashboards, exports and the assistant work on it unchanged. An `=` filter on a field that is a parameter of the endpoint is also sent to the endpoint.

Such an entity is never joined with another one and takes no calculated field: both are refused with the reason. Every request calls the endpoint, up to 50,000 rows.

---

## Relations \{#relations\}

A relation joins two entities on one or more **column pairs**: `customers` → `deals` on `ID = CUSTOMER_ID`. **Add relation** — above the canvas, or in an entity's panel — adds one and opens it in the side panel: pick both entities, then the columns under **Joined on** (the lists show each entity's columns; a name can also be typed); **+** adds a pair for a composite key. **Delete this relation** removes it.

Every entity must reach the hub, directly or through other entities. The explorer then picks the joins an analysis needs, and never multiplies rows twice: an analysis groups by at most one 1..n entity, and the others are reached without duplicating the hub's rows.

---

## A model from a preset \{#preset\}

A Screen Assistant preset already declares a set of tables and their joins. Picking it in **Preset (Screen Assistant)** fills the model:

- every table of the preset becomes an entity (all its columns, or the preset's own column list), the base table the hub;
- the joins become relations, matched on the real columns — the column of that name, the one carrying that dictionary item, or, on a connector with a table prefix (JD Edwards EnterpriseOne: `ABAN8`, `WWAN8`), the one whose name without the prefix is the item.

Entities already declared are kept and completed; a key, measures, a default date or a cardinality set by hand stay as they are. Then adjust what is needed and **Save**. Picking the preset again fills the model once more.

Applying the preset also creates the dictionary entries its tables lack — on a JD Edwards source, from its data dictionary: *Preset applied: 6 entities · 42 dictionary entries created*.

### Models shipped by a preset \{#shipped\}

A preset can also give the explorer a model **by itself**: the *full* presets of the JD Edwards catalogs (Address Book, A/P ledger, sales order, work order…) appear in the model picker without anything in Liberty Next → Insight → Explorer. In the model picker, the models are grouped by area — *JDE · Accounts Payable*, *JDE · Sales* —, the others by application. The model is built from the preset when it is first opened; the page header says *shipped by the preset “…”*. In such a preset, a table's label becomes the entity label, and a lookup table joined to a transaction hub has the cardinality *one*.

To change such a model, add a model in Liberty Next → Insight → Explorer from the same preset: the declared model replaces the shipped one.

---

## Things to know

| Situation | What happens | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| An entity is not linked to the hub. | **Save** is refused and names the entities left out. | Add the missing relation. |
| The entity's query expects parameters. | The explorer sends the fixed values given in the entity form; a parameter left blank is not sent. | Fill **Fixed values of the query's parameters**, or point the entity at a query without parameters. |
| **Save** says a model has no entity yet. | A model with neither an entity nor a preset cannot be read by anybody. | Add an entity, apply a preset, or delete the model. |
| No column is discovered. | The query failed or returned nothing. | Check the query in Liberty Next → Data → Connectors. |
| A field is missing in the pane. | It is hidden, or the query does not return it. | Untick **Hidden**, or add the column to the query. |
| Fields show their raw column name. | The columns have no dictionary entry. | On the explorer page, a superuser sees *N column(s) have no dictionary entry and show their column name* and **Create the entries from the data dictionary** creates them in one click. |

## What's next

- [Analyse data](./analysis.md) — what users do with the model.
- [Roles & permissions](../build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md#access) — give access to a model.

## Liberty Next — Analyse data
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/explorer/analysis/

Using the Liberty Next Data Explorer: the fields pane, the Rows, Measures and Filters shelves, the period, Top N, the table, pivot, bar, line, pie and KPI views, the detail view, the drill to the rows behind a figure and the record dialog.

The explorer opens from the **compass** in the header. The model picker at the top right switches between the models available; picking an app in the left navigation opens that app's model.

The analysis runs on its own a moment after each change; **Run** runs it again on demand.

---

## Fields pane \{#fields\}

The left pane lists the model's entities — the analysed one opened, the others folded — with their **1..1** or **1..n** badge. In each entity, the dimensions come first, then the **Σ Measures**. The search box filters the fields of every entity.

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Click a field | A dimension goes to **Rows**, a measure to **Measures**. |
| Funnel on a field | The field goes to **Filters**. |
| Drag a field | Drops it on the shelf of choice. |
| Double-click an entity | Makes it the **analysed entity** — the one the analysis starts from (the hub by default). The selector at the left of the toolbar does the same. |

Fields already in use are highlighted. **New calculated field**, at the bottom of the pane, opens the [calculated-field editor](./calculated-fields.md).

---

## Shelves \{#shelves\}

| Shelf | Content |
|---|---|
| **Rows** | The dimensions to group by. A date gets a grouping: *Exact value*, *Day*, *Week*, *Month* (the default), *Quarter*, *Year*. In the detail view, this shelf lists the columns shown. |
| **Measures** | One aggregate per chip: *Sum*, *Average*, *Min*, *Max*, *Count*, *Distinct count* for a number; *Count* or *Distinct count* otherwise. **+** adds a row count. A dimension dropped here counts its distinct values. |
| **Filters** | A field, an operator, a value. Text: *contains*, `=`, `≠`, *starts with*, *ends with*, *in*, *is empty*, *is not empty*. Numbers and dates: `=`, `≠`, *between*, `<`, `≤`, `>`, `≥`, *in*, *is empty*, *is not empty*. A field with a list of values offers its values; *in* takes a comma-separated list. On a date or date-time field, a day stands for the whole day: `≤` and the end of *between* keep that day's rows whatever their time, `=` and `≠` mean within or outside that day; the date is picked with the application's date picker. |

Chips move by drag within a shelf; the cross removes one. A filter value applies on **Enter** or when leaving the field.

---

## Period and Top N \{#period\}

The **Period** bar appears when the analysed entity has a date field: pick the date field (the entity's default date first), then a preset — *Today*, *Yesterday*, *Last 7 days*, *Last 30 days*, *This month*, *Last month*, *This quarter*, *This year*, *Last year*, *Last 12 months* — or a custom range on the calendar. *All dates* removes the period.

**Top** keeps the first N groups (up to 10,000). The note in the toolbar reads *N group(s) from M row(s)*, and says when the list was cut or when the figures are partial.

---

## Views \{#views\}

The buttons of the toolbar switch the view without running the query again.

| View | Shows |
|---|---|
| **Table** | One row per group, sortable by header. A click on a row drills to its rows. |
| **Pivot** | The rows as a collapsible hierarchy with subtotals, one dimension spread as **Columns** (*Automatic*: the last one), a grand total, and a **Share** — *of parent* or *of total* — beside each value. Subtotals appear only for a sum or a count: a sum of averages means nothing. Toolbar: expand all, collapse all, Excel export. A click on a value drills. |
| **Bars**, **Lines** | The first dimension on the x axis, the second one (or the measures) as **Series**; the top 10 series, the rest folded into *Others*; dates in order, other categories by value; **Stacked** option. |
| **Pie** | The first dimension as slices, top 10 plus *Others*. |
| **KPI** | One card per measure with its total. |
| **Detail** | The rows themselves, 50 per page, with the **Rows** shelf as columns (the analysed entity's fields when empty). |

**Measure** picks the measure of the pivot or the chart (the first one by default).

---

## Drill and record \{#drill\}

A click on a group of the table or on a value of the pivot lists the **rows behind that figure**: the key, the dimensions and the measures' fields of each row. The values of the cell show above the list (*Country: France*, *Stage: Negotiation*); **Back to the analysis** returns to the figures.

In the detail view, and after a drill, a row of an entity linked to a screen opens that screen's **dialog**: the record shows as it does in the screen, and can be edited with the same rights. The analysis refreshes after a save.

---

## The page \{#page\}

What an analysis is made of reads as cards, each with its icon and its colour: **View**, **Period**, **Rows** (**Columns** in the Detail view), **Measures**, **Filters** — and **Options** for a pivot or a chart. Fields are still clicked or dragged onto a shelf, and chips reorder by drag. The result is a panel whose head says the view and what the run answered — *N group(s) from N row(s)*, *first N shown*. **Save**, **Save as**, **Delete**, **Add to a menu** (a superuser's, see [Add to a menu](./saved-and-dashboards.md#menu)), **Excel** and **PDF** are in the page header, beside the model picker.

- **Definition**, beside the analysis picker, hides the fields and the shelves: **the result takes the page**, with the view, the period, the Top and **Run** on one line. A saved analysis opens that way, a new one on its definition.
- **The table is the grid of the data screens**: search, a filter per column, sort on several columns, grouping, the column chooser and its own CSV / Excel export of what is shown. A row still drills; a detail row still opens its record; the detail stays paged by the server.
- **A coded field shows its label, its code, or both** — the chip of a field read through an enum or a lookup offers **Label**, **Code + label**, **Code**. In the table, *Code + label* gives two columns — `Company (ID)` then `Company` —, each sorted, filtered and exported by itself; a pivot writes `101 · Alpine Foods SA` in its label cell. The choice is saved with the analysis and followed by the dashboard tiles.
- An export cut by the analysis's own Top says so: *first 20 of 44 groups*.

---

## Things to know

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| A measure of a 1..n entity next to hub dimensions. | Summed per hub row, without duplicating the hub's rows. |
| Two 1..n entities in the rows. | Refused, with a message: one many-side entity at a time. |
| The note says the figures are partial. | More than 50,000 grouped rows were read: narrow the period or add a filter. |
| A superuser wants to see the query. | The `</>` button, in the head of the result, shows the statement and its values. |

## What's next

- [Calculated fields](./calculated-fields.md) — fields of your own.
- [Saved analyses and dashboards](./saved-and-dashboards.md) — keep, share, export.

---

## Liberty Next — Calculated fields
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/explorer/calculated-fields/

Calculated fields in the Liberty Next Data Explorer: the editor (name, label, expression, field and function pickers, Test), the expression language — arithmetic, comparisons, conditions, in, is empty, date, text and number functions — and how the result type makes a measure or a dimension.

A calculated field computes a value from the other fields: a margin, a weighted amount, a year, a delay in days, a category. It is written in a small expression language that the server checks and translates for the database — never free SQL. It belongs to the analysis and is saved with it.

---

## At a glance

---

## The editor \{#editor\}

**New calculated field**, at the bottom of the fields pane, opens the editor; the pencil of a calculated field edits it, the bin deletes it (it also leaves the shelves).

| Field | Use |
|---|---|
| **Name** | A letter, then letters, digits or `_`; unique in the analysis. |
| **Label** | The name shown in the pane and the results. |
| **Insert a field**, **Insert a function** | Insert at the cursor; a function is inserted with its arguments selected. |
| **Expression** | The formula. |
| **Test** | Compiles the expression on the server and shows its type and eight sample values. |

**Save** is enabled once the test passes. The result type decides the field's role: a **number** becomes a measure, anything else a dimension. The field then appears in a *calc* group of the pane, and can be used in the rows, the measures and the filters like any other.

---

## The language \{#language\}

A field is written by its name for the analysed entity (`AMOUNT`), or `entity.NAME` for another one (`customers.COUNTRY`). Text values go between single quotes.

| Element | Forms |
|---|---|
| Arithmetic | `+` `-` `*` `/` and brackets. A division by zero gives an empty value. |
| Comparison | `=` `!=` `<>` `<` `<=` `>` `>=` |
| Logic | `and`, `or`, `not` |
| Condition | `condition ? value_if_true : value_if_false` |
| List | `x in ('FR', 'BE')` |
| Empty | `x is empty`, `x is not empty` |
| Dates | `year(d)`, `month(d)`, `day(d)`, `days(from, to)` — the days between two dates |
| Numbers | `round(x, n)`, `abs(x)` |
| Text | `upper(s)`, `lower(s)`, `length(s)`, `concat(a, b, …)` |
| Any | `coalesce(a, b, …)` — the first non-empty value |

A yes/no result shows as `Y` / `N`. A JD Edwards EnterpriseOne Julian date is converted to a real date before a date function applies.

---

## Examples \{#examples\}

| Need | Expression | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Weighted pipeline | `STAGE = 'Negotiation' ? AMOUNT * 0.6 : AMOUNT * 0.3` | measure |
| Unit price | `AMOUNT / QTY` | measure |
| Closing year | `year(CLOSE_DATE)` | measure — a number; to group by it, prefer the *Year* grouping of the date on **Rows** |
| Days to close | `days(CREATED_ON, CLOSE_DATE)` | measure |
| Size band | `AMOUNT >= 100000 ? 'large' : 'standard'` | dimension |
| Domestic or not | `customers.COUNTRY = 'FR'` | dimension (`Y` / `N`) |

---

## Things to know

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| A type mismatch (`AMOUNT + 'x'`). | The test fails and gives the position of the error. |
| An unknown field. | The test fails and names it. |
| The two branches of `? :` have different types. | The test fails: both must be numbers, or both text, or both dates. |
| An expression over 2,000 characters. | Refused. |

## What's next

- [Analyse data](./analysis.md) — the shelves and views.
- [Saved analyses and dashboards](./saved-and-dashboards.md) — a saved analysis keeps its calculated fields.

## Liberty Next — Saved analyses and dashboards
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/explorer/saved-and-dashboards/

Keeping Data Explorer work in Liberty Next: saved analyses, private or shared, with an audience; dashboards of saved analyses with their own period and layout; Excel and PDF export; a menu entry for a shared analysis or dashboard (Add to a menu); the analyses and dashboards an app ships.

The mode bar at the top of the explorer has two modes: **Analyses**, the editor with its saved analyses, and **Dashboards**, grids of saved analyses. Each mode shows how many items the model holds; **Find**, beside them, looks in every model.

---

## At a glance

---

## Find an analysis or a dashboard \{#find\}

An analysis or a dashboard is saved under one model, and the picker of each mode lists those of the model shown. **Find**, beside *Analyses* and *Dashboards*, opens *Find an analysis or a dashboard*: every saved analysis and dashboard of the models the user may use — the shared ones and his own —, grouped under their application and model, the current one marked *the model shown*.

- Typing narrows the list on the name, the description, the audience, the owner and the model; case and accents are ignored. **All**, **Analyses** and **Dashboards** keep one kind.
- Each line gives the name, the audience and the description, *mine* on a private one, and the date it was last saved; the foot counts *N of M*.
- A click opens it — switching first to its model when it is another.

The model picker says what each model holds, in its label: *Sales orders (8 analyses, 1 dashboard)*; a model that holds nothing keeps its plain name. The list comes from `GET /api/explorer/saved`, without the definitions: opening an object reads it.

---

## Saved analyses \{#analyses\}

In **Analyses** mode, the picker lists the saved analyses of the model, grouped by audience, the user's own ones flagged *mine*. *New analysis* starts an empty one.

| Button | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Save** | Saves the current analysis — rows, measures, filters, period, view, calculated fields. |
| **Save as** | Saves a copy under a new name, always private to start with. |
| **Delete** | Shown to the owner of the analysis and to superusers. |
| **Add to a menu** | Publishes the analysis as a menu entry — see [below](#menu). |
| **Excel**, **PDF** | Export — see [below](#export). |

The save window asks for:

| Field | Use |
|---|---|
| **Name** | The name in the picker. |
| **Description** | Free text. |
| **Audience** | A group for the picker: *finance*, *sales*, *it*… |
| **Visible to everyone** | Off: private to its owner. On: **shared** — every user who has access to the model sees it. |

Saving a shared analysis changes it for everyone; the window says so. **Save as** makes a personal copy instead.

---

## Dashboards \{#dashboards\}

In **Dashboards** mode, a dashboard is a grid of **tiles**, four columns wide, each running one saved analysis in its own view — table, pivot, chart, KPI or detail.

- **The period** at the top applies to every tile whose analysis has a period field; the others keep theirs.
- **Edit layout** lays the tiles out like a dashboard's cards: a tile moves by drag and drop — its grip, a bar showing where it lands — and is sized by its corner, in whole columns (1 to 4) and the closest of the three heights (`2 × M`). The grip takes the keyboard too: arrows move, Shift + arrows size. **Add an analysis…** adds a tile.
- **The pencil** of a tile opens its analysis in the editor; a drill from a tile does the same, with the clicked values as filters.
- In view mode a tile shows its title and its pencil; in **Edit layout**, its grip, its size (`1 × S`) and a bin to remove it.
- **Save**, **Save as**, **Delete**, **Add to a menu**, **Excel** and **PDF**, in the page header, work as for analyses. A tile whose analysis was deleted says so.

---

## Add to a menu \{#menu\}

On a saved analysis or dashboard, **Add to a menu** publishes it as an entry of an application's menu. The button is shown to superusers only: the menus are configuration. The window *Add “…” to a menu* asks for:

| Field | Use |
|---|---|
| **Menu of** | The application whose menu receives the entry. |
| **Folder** | A folder of that menu; *At the top of the menu* when none is picked. |
| **Label in the menu** | The entry's label — the analysis's name to start with. |

**Add to the menu** adds the entry. One click on it opens the explorer on that analysis — its result at once, the definition one click away — or on that dashboard. The entry is shown to the users who may use the model. A private analysis cannot be published: the window asks to share it first (**Save**, *Visible to everyone*), and **Add to the menu** stays disabled until then. An entry whose analysis or dashboard was deleted, or is no longer shared, says so when it is opened.

---

## Export \{#export\}

**Excel** and **PDF** export the current analysis, or the whole dashboard (one section per tile):

| | Excel | PDF |
|---|---|---|
| Layout | One sheet per section, bold headers and subtotals, period and filters as a note. | A synthesis: a cover with the application, the period, the date, the author and the version, then the sections one after the other, in the install's PDF branding. |
| A pivot | Flattened, with its subtotals. | A table with bold group rows. |
| A chart | Its data table. | The chart drawn — bars (grouped, stacked or horizontal), line, pie or donut — in print colours, with a legend, compact axis ticks and the values on the bars. |
| KPI | A row of totals. | Cards. |
| Detail | Its rows. | A table. |

Numbers in the PDF follow the reader's language (`1 234,5` / `1,234.5`). The same document is produced when a Nomaflow job renders the analysis on a schedule — see [Steps → Report](../../nomaflow/steps.md#report). Each section holds up to 3,000 rows. The pivot view also has its own Excel button, which exports the pivot as shown. PDF branding is set in [Liberty Next → Administer → App](../build/settings-app.md).

---

## Analyses shipped with an app \{#bundled\}

An app can ship ready-made analyses and dashboards with its model. They appear as **shared** items when the app is installed, and are updated with new versions of the app — until someone saves changes to them, after which the local version is kept. A shipped item that a user deleted is not installed again.

---

## What's next

- [Analyse data](./analysis.md) — build what you save.
- [Data Explorer](./overview.md) — the whole picture.

## Liberty Next — Report templates
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/report-templates/

Liberty Next → Insight → Report templates: reports written by the operators without code — a query of a connector, parameters asked at run time and a Jinja markdown template — tested in the editor on real rows, then run from the Reports page as PDF or markdown.

A **report template** is a report written by an operator without code: a query of a connector provides the rows, parameters are asked when the report runs, and a Jinja markdown template turns the rows into the document. Once saved, the report appears on the **Reports** page (`/reports`) beside the reports the applications ship, and downloads as PDF or markdown.

Open it from **Liberty Next → Insight → Report templates** (superusers).

---

## At a glance

---

## The list \{#list\}

The page shows the file the templates are saved in and how many there are, then one card per template: its title, its id (`custom:<slug>`) and the query it reads (`<connector>.<query>`), with **Edit** and **Delete** — a deletion is confirmed first. **New template** and **Reload config** are in the page header.

A save validates every template, writes them and refreshes the list of reports at once: no restart is needed.

---

## The editor \{#editor\}

**New template**, or **Edit** on a card, opens the window *New custom report* / *Edit custom report*.

| Field | Use |
|---|---|
| **Slug (URL segment)** | The report's id, part of its address: lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`. Unique among the templates. |
| **Title** | The headline on the Reports page and on the PDF cover. |
| **Data connector**, **Named query** | Where the rows come from: a query of a connector. Both are required. |
| **Description** | Shown under the title on the Reports page. |
| **Parameters** | One line per input the report needs at run time: a name, a label, a type (`string`, `int`, `float`, `bool`) and **required**. **Add parameter** adds one. The query receives the parameters by their name. |
| **Jinja markdown template** | The body of the report, in markdown with Jinja tags. |
| **Produced as** | **PDF** and / or **Text (Markdown)** — the formats the report is offered in; one at least stays ticked. |
| **PDF settings of this report** | What this report's PDF does differently from the installation's [PDF branding](./build/settings-app.md#branding) — see [below](#pdf). |

Closing the window with changes not saved asks first: *This report holds changes that are not saved. Close it and lose them?*

### A parameter's value, help and choices \{#params\}

Under its name, label, type and **required**, each parameter has a second line:

| Field | Use |
|---|---|
| **Default value** | The value the field starts with; *none* by default. |
| **Help** | The sentence shown under the field when the report is run — *The year the report covers*. |
| **Choices** | *none: a plain field*, or a dropdown whose choices come from: *A fixed list* — **The list**, one line per choice: the value, then `=` and what is shown (`EN = English`); *The connectors* of the installation; *The schemas of a database* — **Read from** a connector, or *the connector picked in "…"* another parameter; *The rows of a query* — **Read from**, **Query**, **Column of the value**, **Column shown**. |

Incomplete choices stop the save and name the parameter: *Parameter "company": pick the query its choices are read from.* Only what the kind of choices uses is saved.

### PDF settings \{#pdf\}

**PDF settings of this report** is a list of **setting** / value lines; the setting is picked among: **Title**, **Subtitle**, **Client**, **Author**, **Date**, **Version**, **Marked confidential (true / false)**, **Line above the title**, **Name on the cover**, **Reference on the cover**, **Header, left**, **Header, right**, **Footer, left**, **Main colour**, **Light colour**. A setting left out keeps the installation's branding. The list is shown while **PDF** is ticked.

### Writing the template \{#template\}

The template reads a context, `ctx`:

| Name | Content |
|---|---|
| `ctx.data.rows` | The rows of the query, each a set of columns: `{{ row.STATUS }}`. |
| `ctx.data.columns` | The query's columns, with their name and label. |
| `ctx.params` | The values the user entered for the parameters. |

The standard Jinja filters are available (`length`, `join`, `sort`, `selectattr`…). The template runs in a closed environment: nothing outside this context is reachable. The editor completes the column names of the query as you type.

Above the editor, **Insert example** offers four starters — **Bullet list**, **Markdown table**, **Grouped sections**, **Summary + table** — each replacing the body after a confirmation. **Scaffold from query** writes a markdown table of every column the query returns; it waits for a connector and a query.

### Test render \{#test\}

Under the editor, **Test parameters** takes a value per parameter, and **Test render** runs the query with them and renders the template beside the editor — on 200 rows at most, nothing saved. The head of the preview says how many rows were rendered (*Rendered 3 of 3 rows*) or that the render failed, with the reason. When the query returns more rows, the preview says so; the real report holds every row.

---

## Running a report \{#run\}

The **Reports** page lists the reports the user may run, operator-written ones included. **Run** opens a form with the parameters and the format (PDF or markdown); **Run & download** produces the file. The PDF follows the install's branding — [Liberty Next → Administer → App → PDF branding](./build/settings-app.md#branding).

---

## Access \{#access\}

- Writing templates: superusers, in Liberty Next → Insight → Report templates.
- Running them: a role that holds `reports:custom:*:run` sees every operator-written report on the Reports page — entered as a pattern in the role editor, see [Roles and permissions](./build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md).
- The query runs under the user's data scope, as everywhere else.

---

## Tips & best practices \{#tips\}

- Write one query per report, returning exactly the columns the template prints; let the query do the sorting and the totals.
- Start from **Scaffold from query** or an example, then **Test render** with realistic parameters before saving.
- Give every required input a parameter rather than a constant in the query: the same template then serves every company or period.

---

## Liberty Next — App settings
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/settings-app/

Liberty Next → Administer → App: every setting of the install, section by section — App (name, address, sub-path, language, UI defaults, hot reload, Oracle thick mode), Server log, Sign-in, Nomaflow, Change packages, License, AI Assistant, Notifications (email), OpenID Connect (SSO), PDF branding, and the read-only Deployment values — what each field does, which secrets are encrypted, and what needs a restart.

**Liberty Next → Administer → App** holds every setting of the install: nothing needs to be edited in a file. The sections are a list on the left, in four groups that follow the order an installation is set up — **The installation** (Server, Display, External addresses, PDF branding, License), **Signing in** (Sign-in, OpenID Connect), **What is switched on** (AI Assistant, Notifications, nomaflow, Change packages), **Running it** (Server log, and the read-only Deployment). One section is open at a time, beside the list, with its fields on one grid — each label above its field, the explanation on a line under it — and the page remembers which. Each line of the list shows the section's state (*configured*, *not set — restricted mode*, *no API key*, *disabled*, *restart after a change*…). **Save** and **Discard** are in the page header, beside **Reload config**; Save validates and applies the whole page at once.

Secret fields — the licence key, the Anthropic API key, the SMTP password, the OIDC client secret and session secret — are masked inputs with an eye; they are encrypted with the master key when saved ([Encryption](../configuration/encryption-secrets.md)).

---

## At a glance

---

## Server \{#app\}

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| **App name** | The application's name. |
| **Environment** | What the installation is — `production`, `test`… It is named in the [licence usage report](./secure/license-key.md#usage-report). |
| **Public address** | The address users reach the server at: what a password-reset mail links to, and what the sign-in of a Claude client ([MCP](../mcp.md#connect)) is published on. Blank = the browser's address. Set it behind a reverse proxy. |
| **Bind host**, **Port** | Listening address and port. **Restart needed.** |
| **Sub-path behind a reverse proxy** | `/liberty` to serve the application under that path behind a reverse proxy; blank = the site root. The page, the API, the downloads, the live connection and the single sign-on callback follow it — see [Serving under a sub-path](../../installation/traefik.md#sub-path). **Restart needed.** |
| **Log level** | `debug`, `info`, `warning`, `error`, `critical`. **Restart needed.** |
| **Hot-reload config TOML files on change** | Apply configuration files as soon as they change — see [Hot reload](../configuration/hot-reload.md). |
| **Oracle thick mode (…)** | Oracle Instant Client for every Oracle pool — needed for Native Network Encryption and LOBs over a database link. Takes effect after a restart. See [Connectors](../connectors.md#oracle-thick). |

## Display \{#display\}

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Default language** | Labels when a request names no language. |
| **Default period (dashboards)** | The preset a dashboard opens on when it names none — see [Dashboards](../dashboards.md#period). |
| **Grid page size** | The grids' initial page size (10 to 10 000, default 50). A saved view's own size wins. |
| **Dashboard cache (seconds, 0 = none)** | How long a reopened dashboard reuses its widgets' results (default 60). |
| **Several tabs at once (off: one page at a time)** | On by default. Off: opening a page replaces the current one — except a page that holds unsaved changes, which keeps its tab. |
| **Close the tabs when switching application** | Off by default. On: picking another application in the switcher closes the tabs of the other applications; the tabs of the Liberty Next pages, of Monitoring and of the runs stay, and so does a tab that holds unsaved changes. |
| **Tabs at most** | 5 by default (1 to 50). When the limit is reached, opening a page closes the oldest tab that holds no unsaved changes. |
| **Drill-downs open inside the current tab (…)** | Off by default. On: a row's drill-down opens as a panel inside the current tab, with a breadcrumb and **Back**, unless the action itself decides — see [Actions](./screens/actions-and-lifecycle.md#drill). |

**Unsaved changes are never lost without a word.** A page that holds edits not yet saved — a builder or an editor window of Liberty Next, a job being edited, a data grid in bulk edit, an open record form — keeps its tab when the user moves to another page, and the tab carries an orange dot (*Changes not saved yet — kept while this tab stays open*). Closing that tab, **Close all tabs** and switching the language ask first (*Unsaved changes* — **Lose the changes** or **Stay**); the browser asks before a reload or a closed window. Nothing is asked when nothing is unsaved.

## External addresses \{#external-urls\}

The systems this install links to — the JD Edwards web client, an intranet. One line per address: a **name** in capitals (`JDE_WEB`) and its **URL** (`https://jde.example.com:8080/jde`); **Add an address** adds one. An *Open in* action or a link menu item writes `#URL.JDE_WEB#` at the start of its address instead of the address itself: the screens and menus shipped with an application then carry no customer address, and each install sets its own. A change applies at once. An address the install does not set gives no link: the action opens nothing.

When a saved change needs a restart, the page says *Saved. Restart the server to apply the new settings.*

|---|---|

| **Token issuer** | The name written in the session tokens (`liberty-next`). |
| **Session (access token) lifetime (s)** | 3600 by default: how long a session stays valid before it is renewed. |
| **Sign-in (refresh token) lifetime (s)** | 1,209,600 by default — 14 days: how long a user stays signed in. |
| **Refresh reuse grace (s)** | 60 by default: a renewal already used is still accepted for that time — two tabs renewing together; `0` = strict single use. |
| **Failed sign-ins before a pause**, **Counting window (s)** | 10 failures within 300 seconds pause the sign-ins of that account — see [Sign-in](./secure/sign-in.md#throttle). |

**Restart needed** for every field of the section.

## AI Assistant \{#ai\}

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Enabled** | The assistant answers; users need the `ai:chat` permission. |
| **Anthropic API key** | Without it, the assistant says it is not configured. |
| **Model**, **Effort**, **Max tokens**, **Adaptive thinking** | The model and how much it reasons and writes. |
| **Max tool iterations** | Tool rounds one question may use (default 15). A procedure that writes several records through its screens needs more rounds than a question. |
| **Request timeout (s)** | Default 120. |
| **System prompt** | Empty: the built-in instructions. |
| **Connector tools** | The assistant may list connectors and run their **read** queries. |
| **Rows per query, at most (the assistant's own cap, not the pool's)** | 200 by default (1 to 10,000). Beyond it, a result is marked as truncated and the assistant is told not to count or add up its rows. |
| **Data Explorer tools** | On by default: the assistant computes totals, rankings and trends on the [Data Explorer](../explorer/overview.md) models, and saves analyses and dashboards. |
| **API tool** | The assistant may call API endpoints — off by default, since an endpoint may change data. |
| **Scaffold tools** | The assistant may propose queries, dictionary entries, screens and menu items; the user applies the proposal. |
| **Write tools** | Off by default. The assistant adds, changes or deletes a record — or several on one card —, runs an action through its screen, or runs a job — for users holding `ai:write` and the screen's or the job's own permissions; applied from a card in the drawer. Over MCP they also need **Allow changes over MCP**. See [Write through a screen](../ai-assistant.md#write). |
| **Hide sensitive data from the assistant** | Off by default. The columns whose dictionary item or screen column is flagged **Sensitive** are not given to the assistant, in the drawer and over MCP. It does not cover what a user types or attaches, an unflagged free-text column, nor what an API endpoint or an application's own tool returns. See [Sensitive data](../ai-data-sent.md#sensitive). |
| **Allowed connectors** | The connectors the assistant may use; empty means all. |
| **Allowed domains**, **Max fetches per turn** | Web pages the assistant may read; no domain means no web access. |
| **Operations tools** | The assistant may read the jobs' status, the server log tail and the integrity checks — off by default, for installations whose chat users are administrators. |
| **The applications' tools** | On by default: the tools each application ships under [Liberty Next → Logic → AI](../ai-assistant.md#settings-ai). Off: none is offered. |
| **File attached to a question: megabytes at most** | 10 by default (0 to 30); `0` removes the paperclip of the drawer — see [Attach a file](../ai-assistant.md#attach). |
| **Usage record kept (days; 0 = without limit)** | 90 by default — see [AI usage](../../monitoring/ai-usage.md#retention). |
| **MCP endpoint (/mcp)** | Off by default: the same tools for an external client — Claude Desktop, claude.ai, Claude Code —, each user with a personal access token. Applied without a restart. See [Connect Claude (MCP)](../mcp.md). |
| **Allow changes over MCP** | Off by default: an external client reads only. On: a tool that saves — a record through its screen, an action, a job, a saved analysis or dashboard — is offered to it; in the drawer the user applies a card, here the only gate is the client's own approval. See [Changes over MCP](../mcp.md#changes). |
| **Personal access token: longest life (days)** | 366 by default: the longest validity of a token, and how long a sign-in from a Claude client lasts before the user allows it again. |
| **Models users may pick** | The models offered in the drawer's **Model** picker besides the one above; empty → the model above only, and no picker. |
| **Starter questions** | Questions shown on an empty conversation: everywhere (`*`), per application, or per *application/screen* — the most specific set wins. They take precedence over the questions an application ships ([Liberty Next → Logic → AI](../ai-assistant.md#settings-ai)). |

See [AI assistant](../ai-assistant.md), and [Data sent to Anthropic](../ai-data-sent.md) for what these settings let out of the installation.

## OpenID Connect (SSO) \{#section-4--openid-connect-sso\}

|---|---|

| **Attributes from claims** | One line per attribute: the user attribute ← the ID-token claim (`company` ← `org_id`). The attributes feed the roles' [data scope](./secure/roles-and-permissions.md#data-scope) and are refreshed at every sign-in; a claim missing from the token removes the attribute. |
