## Liberty Next — Packages
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/packages/

Ship configuration from one Liberty install to another with the Package page: pick screens, menu items, dashboards, Explorer models, jobs, notification rules, services or assistant material as seeds, the dependency walker pulls in everything they reach, and the package exports as a ZIP — or is promoted straight to another instance. On the target, the import is previewed entity by entity, with a field diff, before it is applied.

The **Package** page (*Liberty Next → Deploy → Package*) is Liberty's built-in deployment mechanism: an operator on the **source** install picks a few screens / menu items / dashboards as *seeds*, the framework walks every reference they reach (queries, connectors, dictionary entries, charts), and the result ships as a ZIP. On the **target** install, the same screen accepts a ZIP, previews what it would change, and applies it to the live config — followed by an automatic reload. With a target instance declared, the package can also be **promoted** straight to it, without handling the ZIP.

The page offers three views, picked from cards at the top: **Build package**, **Import package** and **Promotion**. It is reserved to superusers.

This is the standard *staging → production* path. It's also the right tool for cross-customer reuse: build a "starter" package of curated screens, hand it to a fresh install, apply with `replace_all`, done.

---

## At a glance

---

## When to use which

| Situation | Use |
|---|---|
| Promote screens / dashboards from staging to production. | Build on staging, apply on prod with `overwrite`. |
| Ship a curated set of screens to a brand-new install. | Build, apply with `replace_all`. |
| Add a few new screens to an existing customer install without touching their edits. | Build, apply with `merge`. |
| Ship a fresh release of a vendor-maintained app where the customer has local edits on a few screens. | Build, apply with `overwrite` — entities flagged `override = true` on the target are preserved automatically. |
| Promote screens to production in one step, without the ZIP. | **Promote to…** on Build — see [Promotion](#promotion). |
| Promote one Nomaflow job between environments. | Pick it as a seed under *nomaflow jobs*, or use the **Export** icon on the job's line of the Jobs page. |
| Deliver a full licensed bundle (Nomasx-1 + Nomajde plugins + config). | Not this. Use the **`liberty-apps`** wheel installer — see [Installation → Deploy prebuilt apps](../../installation/deploy-prebuilt-apps.md). |

The Package screen ships **declarative config** — TOML files. It does not ship Python code, Java JARs, plugin packages or database content. For those, the wheel installer is the canonical channel.

---

## The Build view

The left panel lists every **seed candidate** on the install — screens, menu items, dashboards. The right panel shows the **dependency closure** of whatever is ticked on the left.

### Picking seeds

The left panel groups the candidates by kind, each group with its count of ticked items (`SCREENS · 1/24`):

| Section | Drawn from |
|---|---|
| **Screens** | Every screen the install knows — grouped by app. |
| **Menu items** | Every menu item, by app. |
| **Dashboards** | Every dashboard, by scope. |
| **Explorer models** | The Data Explorer models, with their shipped analyses and dashboards. |
| **nomaflow jobs** | The jobs of `jobs.toml`. |
| **Notification rules** | The rules of Liberty Next → Logic → Notifications. |
| **Services** | The services the screens call (Logic → Services). |
| **Assistant (starters, playbooks)** | What an application ships for the AI assistant — one entry per application. |

**Filter seeds**, above the panels, filters the visible list by name / label / scope. The per-section *select all* respects the filter — narrow first (e.g. type `audit`), then tick *select all* to grab only the matching screens.

The seed picker is **bulk-friendly**: hold the filter at a customer name, tick *select all* and you've staged a per-customer slice. No need to click each screen one by one.

### What the dependency walker does

The moment you tick any seed — the **Download ZIP (n)** and **Promote to…** buttons then count what is ticked —, the right panel kicks off the walker (`POST /admin/find-dependencies` on the backend). For every seed, the walker resolves:

| Kind | What's pulled |
|---|---|
| **`screen`** | The screen's main query, all referenced sub-queries (from screen actions, nested tabs, conditional fields), every dictionary entry that backs a column, every lookup the dialog uses, every sequence and enum, the connector each query belongs to (and its pool). |
| **`menu_item`** | The screen, query, endpoint, dashboard or job the menu item targets, then the closure of *that*. |
| **`dashboard`** | Every chart on the dashboard, every query each chart reads from, the connectors. A dashboard named `<app>.<id>` is looked up in that app. |
| **`notification_rule`** | The screen or the jobs its trigger names. |

The closure is **recursive but bounded** (default depth = 50). Cycles are detected and short-circuited.

### The default-excluded kinds

The Dependencies panel pre-ticks every dep **except** three kinds:

| Kind | Why default-excluded |
|---|---|
| **Connectors** | The target install almost always already has its own connector with the right pool / credentials. Shipping the source's connector would clobber the target's secrets. |
| **Pools** | Same — pools carry DB credentials. The target's pool is the one you want. |
| **API endpoints** | Same — endpoints carry auth headers / Bearer tokens specific to the source install's wiring. An endpoint a screen reads its rows from, or saves through, is the screen's data: it is ticked like the screen's queries, and an endpoint served by a service brings that service with it. |

This makes the typical "promote screens between envs" workflow safe out of the box: nothing that carries secrets ships unless you opt in. Tick the *Connectors* group manually only when the target genuinely has none — typically a brand-new install or a per-customer staging spin-up.

The frontend remembers your per-dep ticks; the *select all* / *deselect all* toggles at the group level make it cheap to flip every connector on or off at once.

### Building the ZIP

Click **Download ZIP** and the framework runs `POST /admin/build-package`, returning a ZIP with up to six TOMLs:

| File | When present |
|---|---|
| `connectors.toml` | When at least one connector / pool / query / API endpoint is included. Connector definitions are **trimmed** — only the queries / endpoints in the closure are kept, the rest are dropped. |
| `dictionary.toml` | When the closure pulls in any dictionary entry, lookup, sequence or enum. Per-connector dictionary blocks are nested under `[connectors.<name>]`. |
| `screens.toml` | When at least one screen is in the closure. Grouped by app under `[screens.<app>]`. |
| `menus.toml` | When at least one menu item is in the closure. Grouped by app under `[menus.<app>.items]`. |
| `charts.toml` | When at least one chart is in the closure. |
| `dashboards.toml` | When at least one dashboard is in the closure. |

Plus one always-present file:

| File | What it carries |
|---|---|
| **`MANIFEST.md`** | Human-readable summary — what's in the ZIP, the seeds, per-kind counts, the env vars `${VAR}` the package references (and that the operator must set on the target), the missing references (closure couldn't resolve — usually a typo or a stale rename on the source), and the operator-facing instructions. |

The MANIFEST is the first thing to open on the target before applying — it tells you what to expect and what's still on you to wire (env vars, secrets, master key).

### What's NOT in the package

Worth knowing so you don't try to ship through this channel:

| Not included | Where it lives instead |
|---|---|
| Liberty Next → Administer → App | Per install — application settings, licence, sign-in. Never bundled. |
| `auth.toml` / DB-stored users | Per-install — carries Argon2 password hashes. Never bundled. |
| Python plugins | Shipped with the [liberty-apps wheel](../../installation/deploy-prebuilt-apps.md) or the plugin's own release channel. |
| Database content | Use a DB dump (or a [bundled preload job](../../nomaflow/bundled-jobs.md)). |

---

## The Import view

Pick the **Import package** card. The view offers three strategies — **Merge**, **Overwrite (recommended for upgrades)**, **Replace all** — and a file picker.

### The three strategies

The three columns map one-to-one to the radio cards in the UI:

| Strategy | Per-entity behaviour | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| **`merge`** | NEW entities land. EXISTING entities on the target are **kept as-is**. | Adding new things without disturbing customer edits. The package adds; it never overwrites. |
| **`overwrite`** | NEW entities land. EXISTING entities are **replaced** by the package version — EXCEPT when the target entity is flagged `override = true` (then preserved, reported separately). | The standard upgrade path. The package becomes the new truth for the entities it carries. Entities elsewhere on the target (those not in the package) are untouched. |
| **`replace_all`** | For every TOML in the ZIP, the **whole target file** is replaced by the package's version. EVERY entity not in the package is dropped from that file. Files the package doesn't touch are untouched. | Deploy-from-scratch / vendor reset / a curated baseline. |

### The `override = true` escape hatch

A customer install sometimes needs to fork a vendor entity — patch one screen's columns, swap a query — and keep that fork across vendor upgrades. Add `override = true` to the entity's TOML block:

```toml title="screens.toml on the customer install"
[screens.crm.customers]
label = "Customers (customer fork)"
override = true   # vendor `overwrite` imports will skip this entity
query = "customers_v2_custom"
# ... rest of the customer's edit
```

On the next `overwrite` import, the framework sees the flag and leaves the entity alone. The import report shows it under *preserved overrides* so the operator sees exactly which entities survived the vendor push.

Two limits worth knowing:

- `merge` already skips existing entities — the flag is redundant there.
- `replace_all` drops the entire file — overrides are NOT preserved. Use it knowingly.

### Preview, then apply \{#preview\}

As soon as a ZIP is picked — and again when the strategy changes — the page previews the import; nothing is written until **Apply**.

| Part | Content |
|---|---|
| State chips | The count per state: **New**, **Changed**, **Identical**, **Kept (override)**, **Skipped**, **Removed**, **Errors** — with *From &lt;install&gt; · &lt;version&gt;*, the package's origin. |
| Warnings | A package from a newer Liberty Next — settings this instance does not know may be rejected: upgrade it first; encrypted values this instance cannot decrypt — another master key: set them again after the import. |
| Entities | One card per file. What changes comes first; **Show identical** adds the rest. A changed entity opens on its fields: **Here now** and **After the import**. |
| **Apply N change(s)** | Writes the changes, reloads, then shows the same plan as the result with *Applied + reloaded*. When the instance already holds every entity as the package has it, there is nothing to apply. |

What travels is merged with care:

- a **connector**'s queries, tables, sequences, lookups and endpoints are imported one by one: importing a package never removes the target's other queries;
- a **job** that already exists on the target keeps its schedule, enabled flag, timezone, presets, alerts, retry, log level and timeout; a new job arrives disabled;
- the package is built from the files as written: unset values and `${VAR}` references travel as they are.

If the reload fails after a successful apply, the file changes are kept on disk; run **Reload config**, at the top of the Liberty Next pages, once the underlying issue is fixed.

---

## Promotion — straight to another instance \{#promotion\}

A **target instance** is another Liberty Next install — production, a customer's staging — reached over its API.

**Package → Promotion** lists the targets: **Name**, **Label**, **URL** (the target's root address, with its sub-path), **Account** and **Password** of a local superuser there — the password stored encrypted —, **Check the TLS certificate**, **Timeout (s)**. **Test** signs in on the target: *Signed in on prod · 7.0.64*. **Save targets** keeps them.

**Promote to…**, beside **Download ZIP** on Build, sends the selection to a target:

1. pick the **Target**, the **Strategy** and an optional **Comment**;
2. the target previews the import at once — the same plan as above, computed on the target: *Preview on prod — nothing is written until you apply*;
3. **Apply on prod** applies it there.

Connectors, pools and API endpoints stay the target's unless ticked: a connector's queries still travel, merged into the target's connector. The same **Promote to…** on *Liberty Next → Deploy → Changes* sends an approved [change package](../../nomaflow/change-packages.md#promote).

The **History** of the Promotion view lists the promotions applied from this instance — when, by whom, to which target, what, and the outcome; a row opens on the target's report.

---

## Secrets and environment variables

The package is **plaintext TOML**. Two patterns let the source's secrets travel without leaking the secret material:

| Pattern | What happens at build / apply |
|---|---|
| **Encrypted secrets** — `password = "ENC:base64=="` | The ciphertext lands verbatim in the package. The **target must have the same master key** (`LIBERTY_MASTER_KEY`) as the source — otherwise decryption fails on first use. |
| **Env var references** — `password = "${DB_PASSWORD}"` | The literal string `${DB_PASSWORD}` is in the package. The operator must set the env var **on the target** before reloading. `MANIFEST.md` lists every `${VAR}` the package references. |

Pick one pattern per install — mixing both inside a single config gets confusing. Encrypted secrets travel best across containerised deployments; env vars travel best across orchestrators (Kubernetes Secrets, Docker `--env-file`, systemd `EnvironmentFile`).

### What you should NOT ship

| Don't | Why |
|---|---|
| Move `auth.toml` between installs via the Package screen. | The screen ignores `auth.toml`. Move users via the dedicated *Users* admin (or invite them per install). |
| Expect a package to carry Liberty Next → Administer → App. | It does not — application settings, licence and sign-in stay on each install. |
| Ship a package with `replace_all` to a customer who has local edits without a heads-up. | The customer's screens / queries / dictionary entries are dropped. There is no automatic undo — keep a backup of the target's config tree first. |

---

## Inspect-without-export

The Build tab's right panel is also a **standalone dependency inspector**. Tick a single screen, look at the closure — that's exactly what the screen would carry into a package, and exactly what would break if you renamed / deleted the screen. No need to click *Download ZIP* — the inspection is the value.

Liberty also exposes a dedicated **Find dependencies** modal from any screen / menu item / dashboard list (the icon next to the rename button). Same backend (`POST /admin/find-dependencies`), simpler shape — just the closure tree for the one entity you opened it on.

---

## Common pitfalls

| Mistake | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Forgot to set a `${VAR}` listed in MANIFEST.md before reloading the target. | A connector / query fails at first use with a missing-substitution error. | Read MANIFEST.md before applying. Set the env vars in the target's environment file / systemd unit / Docker env. |
| Source and target carry different `master_key`s. | Encrypted `ENC:...` values fail to decrypt; the affected connector errors at first use. | Sync the master key (or rotate the encrypted values on the target — see [Build → Secure → Encrypted secrets](./secure/encrypted-secrets.md)). |
| Used `replace_all` to apply a small slice — wiped customer-specific screens. | Customer screens missing from the target after import. | Restore the previous TOML from your backup. Re-apply with `overwrite` next time. |
| Bundled `connectors.toml` (default-excluded) without checking pool names match the target. | Target's pools change unexpectedly; pre-existing queries error at next reload. | Leave connectors / pools default-excluded unless the target is brand-new. Or rename pools on the source before bundling. |
| Built from a source with unresolved references (broken rename / deleted query). | MANIFEST.md lists items under *Missing references*. | Fix on the source (rename / delete / restore) and rebuild. The target won't get the broken references — but it also won't get the screens / queries that referenced them. |
| A warning says the package holds values this instance cannot decrypt. | The source and the target use different master keys. | Set those values again on the target after the import, or share the master key. |
| Import landed but `Applied + reloaded` is missing — a *reload failed* warning showed. | Disk has the new config; in-memory state is stale. | Reload manually via **Reload config**, at the top of the Liberty Next pages, once the underlying issue is fixed (often a syntax error in an unrelated TOML the reload caught). |

---

## Programmatic access

The two endpoints behind the UI are usable headless — useful for CI / scripted promotion:

```bash title="Build a package"
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <superuser-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"seeds":[{"kind":"screen","name":"customers","scope":"crm"}]}' \
  https://<source>/admin/build-package \
  --output liberty-package.zip
```

```bash title="Apply a package"
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <superuser-token>" \
  -F "package=@liberty-package.zip" \
  "https://<target>/admin/import-package?strategy=overwrite"
```

`build-package` accepts an optional `include` array to filter the closure (same shape as the UI's per-dep checkbox state). `import-package` accepts `strategy` as a query param (`merge` | `overwrite` | `replace_all`) and `dry_run=true` for the preview. Both endpoints require superuser auth. `POST /admin/promotion/push` sends a package or an approved change package to a declared target.

## What's next

- [Deploy prebuilt apps](../../installation/deploy-prebuilt-apps.md) — when the package channel isn't enough (full bundle = config + Python plugins), use the `liberty-apps` wheel installer.
- [Nomaflow → Bundled jobs](../../nomaflow/bundled-jobs.md) — the ready-made jobs that ship with `liberty-apps`, including the `nomasx1-import-reference` job that loads a curated reference bundle.
- [Encrypted secrets](./secure/encrypted-secrets.md) — what `ENC:` values are, how to rotate them when promoting across installs with different master keys.

## Liberty Next — Config history & versioning
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/configuration/config-history/

Every config save is snapshotted, every screen save captures its dependency closure as a restorable bundle, version changes are logged, and the bundled release notes are readable in-app — all under Liberty Next → Deploy → History.

Liberty keeps a history of your configuration. Every time you save a config file from the Liberty Next pages, the previous state is snapshotted; every time you save a **screen**, the framework also captures that screen *with its dependencies* as a restorable bundle. You can diff any snapshot against what is live, restore it, prune the history, and see exactly when the application version last changed — all from **Liberty Next → Deploy → History**.

---

## At a glance

---

## What gets captured

| When you… | The framework snapshots… |
|---|---|
| Save any config file (connectors, dictionary, menus, pools, …) | The file's previous bytes, before the save overwrites it. |
| Save a screen in the Designer | A **bundle**: the screen *plus its dependency closure* — the queries, lookups, sequences and dictionary entries it relies on. |
| Run the assistant, a rename, a move, a clone or an import | The whole configuration, before the operation. |

Snapshots are content-addressed, so saving a file unchanged is a no-op — the history only grows when something really changed. Capturing is best-effort: it never blocks or fails a save.

---

## Liberty Next → Deploy → History

The **History** tab has three modes:

- **Files** — pick a config file on the left, with its number of versions; its versions list on the right as cards (number, date, origin of the snapshot). Expand a version to **diff it against the live file** — removed lines in red, added lines in green —; the three buttons of the card **Download**, **Restore** or **Delete** it.
- **Screens** — pick a screen (`app.screen`); each save is a bundle card. Expand it to inspect the captured dependency closure grouped by kind (connectors, queries, dictionary entries, lookups, menus, …), then **Download bundle (.zip)** or **Restore screen + dependencies**.
- **Upgrades** — the application's version history (see [below](#upgrade-history)).

### Restoring

Restore is safe and reversible — the current state is snapshotted *first*, so a restore can itself be undone:

- A **file restore** writes the chosen version back and reloads the connectors so it is live immediately.
- A **bundle restore** re-applies the screen and its captured dependencies together. Entities you have marked `override = true` on this install are **preserved**, so a local customisation survives the revert.

### Pruning

Delete removes a single snapshot (or clears one file's / one screen's whole history). The live configuration is never touched by a delete — only the history is.

---

## Retention purge job

History grows over time, so a bundled job — **`config-versions-purge`**, every night at 03:00 — trims it, file history and screen bundles alike. It keeps the most recent versions per file and drops anything older, by **two independent rules**:

- **Max versions** — keep only the N most recent versions of each file (default **20**).
- **Max age** — drop versions older than D days (default **90**).

The two rules are OR-combined, and the single newest version of each file is always kept. A rule set to `0` is disabled. Its schedule and its `max_versions` / `max_age_days` parameters are changed in the Nomaflow job editor like any other job's. [Monitoring → Retention](../../monitoring/retention.md) shows the limits in force and the number of versions, with **Preview** and **Run now**.

---

## Upgrade history

Each time the running application version changes, the framework records it under **Liberty Next → Deploy → History → Upgrades**: a row per component — **Framework** (Liberty Next) and **Apps** (Liberty Apps) — with the version it moved from and to. The first run of a component is logged as an *install*; later version changes as an *upgrade*. The list is recorded automatically at startup and is idempotent, so restarting at the same version adds nothing. Selecting a row shows that version's section of the release notes.

---

## Release notes, in-app

The **Liberty Next → Document → Release notes** page is the full changelog bundled with the build: the framework's notes and, when Liberty Apps is installed, the apps' — a switcher at the top picks one, with the version running. The versions are a panel on the left, each with its date and its number of entries; the picked version shows each entry as a card titled by the sentence it opens on. **Search every version…** finds an entry by its words across all the versions and says which version it belongs to. The text is **bilingual** — the French notes when the UI is in French, English otherwise.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Restore before you debug a bad save.** If a config change broke a screen, the fastest fix is often to restore the previous version and reload, then re-apply the change carefully.
- **Use a bundle restore to move a screen back as a whole.** Restoring the screen file alone can leave it pointing at a query you also changed; the bundle restore reverts the screen *and* its dependencies together.
- **Schedule the purge.** Without it the history grows unbounded; a nightly purge with the defaults (20 versions / 90 days) keeps it healthy.
- **Check Upgrades after a deployment.** It is the quickest confirmation that the new framework or apps version actually took effect.

---

## Liberty Next — Developer reference
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/configuration/developer-reference/

The Developer reference of Liberty Next (Liberty Next → Document): the data model of the framework and of every connector, every setting with the page that edits it and the code that reads it, every API route with the access it requires and its response, every command line with its arguments, and the impact of a change on the configuration — searchable, for superusers.

**Liberty Next → Document → Developer reference** describes the running installation from the inside: its tables, its settings, its API routes, its command lines and the links between the pieces of its configuration, read from the code and the configuration in force. It is for the people who support the install — superusers only — and changes nothing.

The page has five tabs, in its header — **Data model**, **Configuration**, **API**, **Command line**, **Impact**; it opens on **Configuration** and then on the last tab used.

---

## At a glance

---

## Data model \{#data\}

The tables of the framework, then the tables each connector declares, grouped by connector, each with its number of columns. A search finds a table, a column or a label.

A table shows its **physical table**, its **key**, the **queries** that read it and what uses it — screens, dashboards, charts, jobs, Explorer models —, its related tables, then its columns: **Column**, **Label** (from the dictionary), **Type**, **References**, **Screens**, **Description**.

---

## Configuration \{#config\}

Every setting of the install, by section, with its type, its default and its description. On the left, the sections of `app.toml` with their number of keys, under a search that runs across every section (each section then shows its matches); on the right, the shared grid — views, filters, grouping, columns, export.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Key**, **Label**, **Type**, **Default** | The setting. |
| **Edited in** | The page that edits it — *Liberty Next → Administer → App* —, or *File / environment only* with the reason, or *Not in the UI*. |
| **Read by** | The places in the code that use it. |

The header counts the settings edited in a screen, those set in the file or the environment only, and those missing from the interface; the status filter (*Any status*, *Edited in a screen*, *File / environment only*, *Not in the UI*) keeps one kind. A click on a row opens its detail, with the code that reads it.

---

## API \{#api\}

Every route of the server, by module: **Method**, **Path**, **Summary**, **Module** and **Access** — *public*, *any signed-in user*, *superuser*, a *permission* or a *role*, read from the code. A click on a route opens its parameters, its request and its response, and the place of its handler. For the main read routes — connectors, menus, screens, external addresses, the Data Explorer, Nomaflow jobs and runs — the **Response** section gives the shape of the JSON returned, with an example. The buttons in the header open the interactive API documentation of the server.

The search runs across every module and shows, per group, the number of matches.

---

## Command line \{#cli\}

Every command installed with the server — `liberty-admin`, `liberty-ops`, `liberty-connectors`, `liberty-crypto`, `liberty-license`… —, read from its argument parser. On the left, the commands with a search, folded by default, with **Expand all** / **Collapse all**.

A command shows what it does, its usage with **Copy**, the **Options of every command**, then each sub-command with its arguments: **Argument**, **Value**, **Default**, *required*, *repeatable*. Under Docker, `./liberty` wraps the installation, the upgrade, the backups and the database: see [Operations](../../installation/operations.md). The command-line section of the [technical report](./documentation-reports.md) is built from the same reading.

---

## Impact \{#impact\}

Every entity of the configuration with what it uses and what uses it, followed through: what a change to a pool, a query, a screen or a dictionary entry reaches. The links are the ones the [Package](../build/packages.md) dependency walk follows.

On the left, the entities by kind — pools, connectors, queries, API endpoints, dictionary entries, lookups, sequences, enums, screens, menu items, charts, dashboards, services, Explorer models, jobs, notification rules, AI blocks —, folded by default, with a search (`scope.name`). **Unused only** keeps the entities nothing points at — menu items, jobs, notification rules, pools, Explorer models and dictionary entries, opened or reached otherwise, are never counted as unused —, and **Referenced but not defined** lists the references to an entity that does not exist.

A picked entity shows:

| Part | Content |
|---|---|
| Header | *uses N · used by N*, and **Open in editor**, which goes to its builder. |
| **A change here reaches** | The entities reached, counted by kind: a query → its screens → the menu items opening them, the charts → their dashboards, the jobs and actions running it. |
| **Used by** | The tree of what uses it, level by level (up to 8 levels). |
| **Uses** | What it uses directly. |
| **Everything it needs** | Every entity it depends on, followed through. |

A click on an entity of the tree re-centres the view on it; **Back** returns to the previous one. A dictionary entry has no explicit reference: a column reaches its entry by name.

## Liberty Next — Documentation reports
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/configuration/documentation-reports/

Liberty Next → Document → Documentation reports: the implementation report (technical and functional documentation of the install) and the technical report (data model, configuration, API), generated as PDF or Markdown from the installation in force, sections to tick, language and date label, secrets masked.

**Liberty Next → Document → Documentation reports** writes the documentation of the installation as it stands — a deliverable for a project, a hand-over, an audit of the configuration — as a PDF or in Markdown. Superusers only.

---

## At a glance

---

## The two reports \{#reports\}

| Report | For | Sections |
|---|---|---|
| **Implementation report** — technical and functional documentation of the install | The project team, the customer. | Context, Architecture, Applications and menus, Screens, Connectors and pools, Dashboards and Explorer, Operations, Security, Reference data; on demand, the appendices *Settings* — every setting, secrets masked — and *API reference*. |
| **Technical report** — developer documentation | The people who maintain the install. | Scope, Architecture, Data model, Configuration reference, API reference, Command line, Build and packaging, Appendix: code references. |

---

## Producing one \{#run\}

1. Open the report's card.
2. Tick the sections — **All** / **None** —; the counter shows *N of M sections*. The technical report offers two options: detail every API route, and include the code snippets in the appendix — long.
3. Under **Settings**, pick the **Language** — *Français* or *English* — and, if needed, the **Date label** of the cover page; by default, today.
4. **Download the PDF**, or **Markdown** to edit it further.

Every value whose name says it is a secret — passwords, keys, tokens — is masked, and so are the connection addresses.

## Kept copies \{#copies\}

Every report produced is also kept on the server, next to the configuration — so a backup carries it. Under **Kept copies**, the report's page lists them with who built it, the language and the number of sections: **Download** fetches one again, **Delete the copy** removes the file from the server. The copies stay until they are deleted; [Retention](../../monitoring/retention.md) shows their number and size.

---

- [Developer reference](./developer-reference.md) — the same knowledge, browsable.

## Liberty Next — CLI reference
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/references/cli/

Every Liberty Next command-line tool: liberty-admin (database bootstrap, users, roles, data scope, install jobs, schema migrations), liberty-ops and ./liberty (operations), liberty-connectors (run a query without the web app), liberty-crypto (ENC: values), liberty-license (check the key).

Most administration is done in the **Liberty Next** pages. The command-line tools cover what has to work without the web application — the first start, a lost password, scripted set-up, operations.

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `liberty-next` | Starts the server. Address and port come from **Liberty Next → Administer → App**. |
| [`liberty-admin`](#liberty-admin) | Database bootstrap, users, roles and data scope, installation jobs, schema migrations. |
| `./liberty` and `liberty-ops` | Operations on a Docker or a Python install — see [Operations](../installation/operations.md). |
| [`liberty-connectors`](#liberty-connectors) | Lists the connectors and runs a query or an endpoint. |
| [`liberty-crypto`](#liberty-crypto) | Encrypts a value into an `ENC:` string. |
| [`liberty-license`](#liberty-license) | Checks a licence key. |

**Docker:** run them inside the container as the `liberty` user — `docker exec -u liberty liberty-next liberty-admin list-users`.
**Python install:** run them as the service user with its environment loaded, so that they read the same configuration and the same master key as the server.

---

## liberty-admin \{#liberty-admin\}

Two options apply to every command: `--config-app <app.toml>` and `--config-connectors <connectors.toml>`. Commands print JSON.

### Bootstrap

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `init-db [--admin-username admin] [--password P \| --password-env VAR]` | Creates the user store (the `auth.toml` file or the database tables) and the missing framework tables, then the first superuser. Without a password, a random one is generated and printed. Running it again changes nothing. |
| `set-default-pool` | Rewrites the application's default database connection from `POSTGRES_HOST`, `_PORT`, `_USER`, `_PASSWORD` and `_DB` — after the database moved. The password is stored encrypted. `./liberty db external` runs it for you. |
| `retarget-pools --from host[:port] --to host[:port] [--dry-run]` | Points every pool on one database server at another (`--from pg:5432`); `--dry-run` lists them without writing. A pool whose host is a `${VAR}` is left alone. |
| `run-install-jobs [--force]` | Runs, in order, every Nomaflow job of the licensed apps marked as an installation step (`deploy-databases`, `nomasx1-import-reference`). Jobs already completed are skipped unless `--force`. |

### Users

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `create-user <name> [--email E] [--full-name N] [--role R]… [--attribute KEY=VALUE]… [--superuser] [--password P \| --password-env VAR]` | Creates a local user. Without a password, one is generated and printed. |
| `set-password <name> [--password P \| --password-env VAR]` | Changes a password; without one, generates and prints it. |
| `set-active <name> --active \| --inactive` | Enables or disables a user. |
| `set-attributes <name> KEY=VALUE… [--replace]` | Sets the user's data-scope attributes. `company=00001,00050` gives a list; `company=` removes the key; `--replace` drops the attributes not given. |
| `list-users` | Lists the users. |

### Roles and data scope

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `create-role <name> [--permission P]… [--description D] [--scope RULE]…` | Creates a role, or updates it. |
| `set-scope <name> --rule RULE… \| --clear` | Replaces the role's data-scope rules. |
| `list-roles` | Lists the roles with their permissions and data scope. |

A `RULE` is a TOML inline table or JSON object, with the keys described on [Roles and permissions → Data scope](../framework/build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md#data-scope):

```bash
liberty-admin set-scope subsidiary --rule '{dd = "CO", source = "#USER.company#", mode = "deny"}'
liberty-admin set-scope controllers --rule '{dd = "SY", values = ["00"], exclude = true}'
liberty-admin set-attributes alice company=00001,00050
```

:::warning[Updating an existing role]
`create-role` on an existing role replaces its permissions with the `--permission` values given; without `--permission`, the role keeps its permissions. To change only the scope of a role, use `set-scope`, which needs `--rule` or `--clear`.
:::

### Schema migrations \{#migrate\}

```text
liberty-admin migrate [--app X]… [--dry-run] [--target-connector C] [--revision head]
                      [--plugins-dir D] [--stamp REV]
```

Applies the pending schema migrations of each licensed app (the `plugins/<app>/db` modules) and records each run in **Liberty Next → Deploy → History → Upgrades**.

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Lists the pending migrations. Exit code `2` when some are pending, `0` when up to date, `1` on error. |
| `--app nomasx1` | Only that app (repeatable). |
| `--target-connector C` | The connector of the database to migrate (default: the app's own). |
| `--revision R` | Stop at that revision instead of the latest. |
| `--plugins-dir D` | Where the apps' code is (default: `plugins/` next to `LIBERTY_APPS_DIR`). |
| `--stamp REV` | Repair: records `REV` as the database's current revision without running anything, then applies what is left. Needs `--app`. For a database whose recorded version is ahead of its real tables. |

`./liberty migrate` and `liberty-ops migrate` run this command.

### Upgrade reports

`record-upgrade` stores an upgrade or rollback report in the upgrade history. `./liberty upgrade`, `./liberty rollback` and `liberty-ops` call it; it is not meant to be run by hand.

---

## liberty-connectors \{#liberty-connectors\}

Runs connectors without the web application — handy to test a pool or a query from the server.

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `liberty-connectors list` | Pools and connectors. |
| `liberty-connectors describe <connector>` | One connector's definition. |
| `liberty-connectors run <connector> <query or endpoint> [-p KEY=VALUE]…` | Runs a query (SQL connector) or calls an endpoint (API connector) and prints the result. |

`--config <connectors.toml>` reads another file than the one named in `app.toml`.

---

## liberty-crypto \{#liberty-crypto\}

Encrypts values for the configuration files with the install's master key. The Liberty Next pages encrypt on their own what they save; this tool is for a value written by hand in a TOML file.

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `liberty-crypto encrypt [VALUE]` | Prints `ENC:…`. Reads the value from standard input when it is not given — better for a password. |
| `liberty-crypto is-encrypted [VALUE]` | Says whether the value starts with `ENC:`. |

The key comes from `LIBERTY_MASTER_KEY`; `--master-key` and `--config` override it.

---

## liberty-license \{#liberty-license\}

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `liberty-license status` | Checks the key configured in **Liberty Next → Administer → App → License**: validity, products covered, expiry. |
| `liberty-license verify [KEY]` | Checks a key given as argument or on standard input, before pasting it. |

`--config` names another `app.toml`. See [Licence key](../framework/build/secure/license-key.md).

---

## Liberty Next — REST API reference
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/references/rest-api/

A map of the Liberty Next REST API by domain — health, sign-in, connectors and data, screens, dashboards, menus, reports, notifications, saved views, Nomaflow jobs, change packages, access and configuration — with the access rule of each family. The exact request and response shapes are in the built-in OpenAPI pages.

This page maps the endpoints by domain. The exact request and response shapes are in the server's own OpenAPI pages: **`/docs`** (Swagger UI), **`/redoc`** and **`/openapi.json`** — generate typed clients from the latter.

---

## Conventions \{#conventions\}

- **Authentication** — `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` on every call, except `/health`, `/ready`, `/info`, `/api/theme`, `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/refresh` and the OIDC pair.
- **Access rules** — data endpoints check the permission of what they run (`sql:<connector>:<query>`, `api:<connector>:<endpoint>`), and SQL reads and writes apply the caller's [data scope](../framework/build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md#data-scope). Everything under **`/admin/`** is reserved to superusers.
- **Language** — `X-Liberty-Lang: fr` (else `Accept-Language`) chooses the language of labels in screens, dictionary and menus.
- **Pool** — `X-Liberty-Pool: <pool>` runs a multi-pool connector's queries on another pool of its set.
- **Errors** — a JSON `{"detail": …}` body with a non-2xx status. A database error gives regular users the driver's message and an `error_id`; the statement itself is never echoed to them.
- **Request id** — every response carries `X-Request-ID`; the server log lines of that request carry the same id.

---

## Health \{#health\}

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/health` | Liveness: `{"status": "ok", "version"}`. |
| `GET` | `/ready` | Readiness: `200` when the framework database answers, `503` otherwise. |
| `GET` | `/info` | Version, counts and flags; names and details for a signed-in caller. |

See [Health endpoints](../monitoring/health-endpoints.md).

---

## Sign-in and profile \{#auth\}

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/auth/login` | `{username, password}` → access and refresh tokens. `429` after too many failures. |
| `POST` | `/auth/refresh` | A refresh token → a new pair. The refresh token presented is consumed: keep the new one. |
| `GET` | `/auth/me` | The token's identity: roles, permissions, attributes, data scope — and `implied`, what the role's menu grants give, so a button a page shows or hides agrees with the server. |
| `GET` / `PATCH` | `/auth/profile` | The signed-in user's profile. |
| `POST` | `/auth/change-password` | Change one's own password (local users). |
| `POST` | `/auth/tokens` | Create a personal access token for the MCP endpoint (`{days}`, 90 by default) → `{token, expires_at, days}`. Requires `mcp:use`. |
| `GET` | `/auth/mcp/extension` | The Claude Desktop extension (a `.mcpb` file named after the instance) with the server's address filled in. Requires `mcp:use`. |
| `GET` / `POST` | `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, `/oauth/register`, `/oauth/token` | The sign-in of an MCP client: discovery, client registration, code exchange and renewal. The consent page is `/oauth/authorize`. |
| `GET` | `/oauth/grants` | The clients the caller connected by sign-in: name, connection, last use, end of the access — never a token. `?everyone=1` for a superuser. |
| `DELETE` | `/oauth/grants/{id}` | End the access of one client, refused from its next call. |
| `GET` | `/auth/oidc/login`, `/auth/oidc/callback` | OpenID Connect sign-in. |

See [Sign-in](../framework/build/secure/sign-in.md).

---

## Connectors and data \{#data\}

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/connectors`, `/api/connectors/{connector}` | The connectors and their queries / endpoints. |
| `GET` | `/api/sql/{connector}/{query}` | Run a read query; query-string parameters bind to it, with filters, paging and sorting. |
| `POST` | `/api/sql/{connector}/{query}` | Run a write query with a JSON body. |
| `GET` | `/api/sql/{connector}/_schemas`, `/_schema` | Schemas and tables of the connector's database. |
| `POST` | `/api/sql/{connector}/_import` | Import rows (the grid's Excel import). |
| `POST` | `/api/http/{connector}/{endpoint}` | Call an API connector's endpoint. |
| `GET` | `/api/actions`, `/api/actions/{action_id}` | Services (Logic → Services). |
| `GET` / `POST` | `/api/plugins/callables`, `/api/plugins/run` | Plugin functions callable from screens. |

## Screens, dashboards, menus \{#screens\}

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/screens`, `/api/screens/{app}`, `/api/screens/{app}/{screen_id}` | Screen definitions, localised. |
| `POST` | `/api/screens/{app}/{screen_id}/export` | Excel export of the screen's current view. |
| `GET` | `/api/dashboards`, `/api/dashboards/{dashboard_id}` | Dashboards and their widgets. |
| `GET` | `/api/charts`, `/api/charts/{chart_id}` | Saved charts. |
| `GET` | `/api/menus`, `/api/menus/{app}` | Menu trees, pruned to what the caller may open. |
| `GET` | `/api/theme` | Branding and UI defaults (public). |
| `GET` | `/api/pages`, `/api/pages/{app}/{page}` | The pages an application ships, and one page's module — each asks `page:<app>:<page>`. |
| `GET` / `PUT` / `DELETE` | `/api/views/{kind}` | Saved grid views. |

## Reports, notifications, licence \{#other\}

|---|---|---|

| `POST` | `/api/reports/{scope}/{report_id}/run` | Run a report (PDF or Markdown). |
| `GET` | `/api/notifications` (`?unread=1`), `/api/notifications/unread_count` | The caller's notifications. |
| `POST` | `/api/notifications/read` | Mark notifications read (`{ids}`, or all). |
| `POST` | `/api/notify/fire` | Fire an action-kind notification rule (used by the `send_notification` screen action). |
| `GET` | `/api/license` | Licence mode, customer, plan, apps, expiry. |

## AI assistant \{#ai\}

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/ai/tools` | The assistant's tool catalogue. |
| `POST` | `/ai/chat` | Send the conversation (`{messages, model?}`); the answer streams back. Requires `ai:chat`. |
| `POST` | `/ai/attachments` | A file attached to a question. |
| `POST` | `/ai/screen-write`, `/ai/screen-write-many`, `/ai/screen-action`, `/ai/job-run`, `/ai/api-run` | Apply a card of the drawer: a record written through its screen (one or several), an action, a job run, an API endpoint that changes data. Requires `ai:write` and the permission of what is run. |
| — | `/mcp` | The MCP endpoint: the assistant's tools for an external client, with `Authorization: Bearer <personal access token>`. See [Connect Claude (MCP)](../framework/mcp.md). |
| `POST` | `/mcp/files?job=<id>&filename=<name>` | A file sent by the Claude Desktop extension for a job that loads one: it lands in the job's upload area, nothing runs. Personal access token; requires `ai:write`, `job:<id>` and **Allow changes over MCP**. |
| `GET` | `/admin/ai-usage` | The assistant's usage over a period (`days`, `username`, `channel`, `failed`, `limit`). Superusers. See [AI usage](../monitoring/ai-usage.md). |

## Administration (superusers) \{#admin-config\}

| Family | Paths | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Access | `/admin/access/users`, `/admin/access/users/{username}` (+ `/password`), `/admin/access/roles`, `/admin/access/roles/{name}`, `/admin/access/menu-rules`, `/admin/access/role-templates` | Users (create, update, attributes, password), roles (permissions, data scope), what each menu entry gives in read and in read and change, and the predefined roles the applications ship. |
| Configuration | `/admin/config/{section}/parsed` (`GET` / `PUT`) for `connectors`, `dictionary`, `menus`, `screens`, `charts`, `dashboards`, `actions`, `notifications`, `theme`, `jobs`, `app`, `reports`, `explorer`; `/admin/config/pools` | Read and save a configuration file as JSON; a save is validated, then applied. |
| Configuration tools | `/admin/config/connectors/{connector}/test-sql`, `/admin/config/api/test`, `/admin/config/rename`, `/admin/config/move`, `/admin/config/clone-app`, `/admin/config/delete-app`, `/admin/config/integrity`, `/admin/config/schema` | Tests, cross-file renames and moves, integrity check, JSON schemas. |
| Studio, services, tests | `/admin/studio/overview`, `/admin/studio/map`, `/admin/studio/services`, `/admin/studio/run` and `/admin/studio/expose` (`POST`) — the [Overview and the Studio](../framework/studio.md), [Services](../framework/build/services.md). `/admin/tests` (`GET`), `/admin/tests/{suite}` (`GET` / `PUT` / `DELETE`), `/admin/tests/{suite}/run` and `/admin/tests/try` (`POST`), `/admin/test-results` — the [tests](../framework/build/tests.md), open to the holders of `tests:view` / `tests:run` / `tests:edit`. `/admin/config/api/generate` (`POST`) — [Create from…](../framework/build/api-endpoints.md#create-from); `/admin/config/pools/test` (`POST`) — **Test connection** on a pool. |
| History | `/admin/config/versions…`, `/admin/config/screen-versions…`, `/admin/upgrades`, `/admin/upgrades/{id}/report`, `/admin/release-notes` | Configuration versions, upgrade history and reports, release notes. |
| Reload | `POST /admin/reload` | Re-read every configuration file. |
| Packages | `/admin/find-dependencies`, `/admin/build-package`, `/admin/import-package`, `/admin/clone-with-deps`, `/admin/delete-with-deps` | Packages and dependency-aware clone and delete. |
| Change packages | `/admin/changesets…` | See [Change packages](../nomaflow/change-packages.md#api-contract). |
| Notifications | `POST /admin/notify/test` | Send a test through the channels. |
| Server log | `/admin/logs` (`GET`), `/admin/logs/export`, `/admin/logs/download`, `/admin/logs/levels` (`GET` / `POST`) | Search, export and download the server log; the level of each module. See [Server log](../monitoring/server-log.md). |
| Retention | `/admin/retention` (`GET`), `/admin/retention/{store}/run` (`POST`, `dry_run=true` by default) | Every store's policy and size; preview or purge one. See [Retention](../monitoring/retention.md). |

## Socket.IO \{#socketio\}

`/socket.io` carries the live updates, authenticated with the same token in the handshake: run and step state changes of Nomaflow (`job_run.state`, `step_run.state`), new notifications for the bell, record locks, and the Monitoring page's snapshots and log tail.

## Liberty Next — CRUD over an existing table
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/crud-existing-table/

Recipe — put a list / add / edit / delete interface on an existing database table from Settings: pool, queries generated by the CRUD wizard, screen, menu entry.

## The problem

A database table — `products`, `tickets`, `contracts` — and a team that needs to read and edit it, without writing a front end.

## The pattern

```
table → connector with 4 generated queries → screen → menu entry
```

## The recipe

### 1. Reach the database

**Liberty Next → Administer → Pools**: the `default` pool works when the table is in the framework's database; otherwise add a pool with the database's URL. See [Connectors](../connectors.md#pools).

### 2. Generate the queries

**Liberty Next → Data → Connectors**: create (or pick) the SQL connector, choose the **Tables** view, then **＋ Add queries → Generate from DB**. Pick the `products` table, keep the columns to show, tick **key** on `ID`, keep the four statements and save. The wizard writes:

```sql
-- products_get
SELECT ID, NAME, PRICE, STOCK FROM products

-- products_post
INSERT INTO products (ID, NAME, PRICE, STOCK) VALUES (:ID, :NAME, :PRICE, :STOCK)

-- products_put
UPDATE products SET NAME = :NAME, PRICE = :PRICE, STOCK = :STOCK WHERE ID = :ID_ORIGINAL

-- products_delete
DELETE FROM products WHERE ID = :ID
```

To stamp who changed a row and when, add the audit columns to the write queries with server tokens — the browser cannot alter them:

```sql
UPDATE products
SET NAME = :NAME, PRICE = :PRICE, STOCK = :STOCK,
    UPDATED_BY = {{LOGIN}}, UPDATED_AT = {{SYSTIMESTAMP}}
WHERE ID = :ID_ORIGINAL
```

Or give the `UPDATED_BY` / `UPDATED_AT` dictionary entries the `LOGIN` / `SYSDATE` rules. See [Parameter binding → Tokens](../build/queries/parameter-binding.md#tokens).

### 3. Build the screen

**Liberty Next → Screens → Screens**, the connector's chip (**＋ Add scope** the first time), **＋ Add screen** `products`, then in the Screen Designer, stage by stage:

| Tab | Setting |
|---|---|
| **What it is** | Label `Products`; **Editable** for in-grid editing; **uploadable** for Excel / CSV import. |
| **Data** | Read `products_get`, update `products_put`, insert `products_post`, delete `products_delete`. |
| **Grid** → **Columns** | Labels, formats, widths, filters. |
| **Record form** | Drag the columns onto the form. |

The [Screen Creation Assistant](../build/screen-assistant.md) does steps 2 and 3 in one pass.

### 4. Add the menu entry

**Liberty Next → Screens → Menus**, the connector's chip (**+ Add scope** the first time), **＋ Item**: label `Products`, type `screen`, target `products` (the screen). Save.

## Result

Clicking *Products* opens the grid: sort and filter by column, group, save views; a row opens the edit dialog, **＋ Add** an empty one, **Delete** removes the row. Each query has its own permission — `sql:<connector>:products_get`, `sql:<connector>:products_put`… — to grant through roles.

## Variations

| Need | How |
|---|---|
| **Labels and lists of values** | Dictionary entries on the columns, with an `ENUM` or `LOOKUP` rule — see [Dictionary](../dictionary.md). |
| **Read-only for some users** | Give their role only the read query's permission: writes are refused. To make the screen read-only for everyone, tick **Read-only** in the **What it is** stage. |
| **Excel export** | The screen's **Output** stage — see [Excel export](./excel-export.md). |
| **Related rows inside the dialog** | A `nested_table` tab — see [Nested tabs](../build/screens/nested-tabs.md). |
| **Bulk loading from a file** | See [Bulk import](./bulk-import.md). |

## What's next

- [Create from a database table](../build/queries/create-from-database.md) — the CRUD wizard in detail.
- [Screens](../build/screens/overview.md) — every screen setting.
- [Roles & permissions](../build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md) — who sees and edits what.

---

## Liberty Next — Excel export
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/excel-export/

Recipe — export a screen to Excel: the grid's Export menu (current view, Excel or CSV, visible or all columns), and configured workbooks from the screen's Output stage — several sheets, one file per group, built on the server.

## The problem

Users want the data of a screen in Excel — to work on it offline, to hand it to someone without access, to produce a recurring report.

## The pattern

| Level | Setting | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **The grid's export** | Nothing — every grid has it. | The current view as `.xlsx` or `.csv`. |
| **Configured workbooks** | The screen's **Output** stage. | One or several `.xlsx` files with several sheets, built on the server. |

## The grid's export

The **Export** menu above every grid offers **Excel (.xlsx)** and **CSV (.csv)**. The file holds the rows loaded in the grid, with its filters, sort and visible columns; **All columns (incl. hidden)** adds the hidden ones.

A column with a list of values gets two columns in the file: the label, and the code under `<label> (ID)` — the layout the screen's [import](./bulk-import.md) reads back.

The export covers the rows the grid has loaded: raise the screen's row cap, or narrow the filters, for a complete file.

## Configured workbooks

For a structured report — several sheets, one file per department — set the screen's **Output** stage. An **Export workbooks** button then appears above the grid; the server builds the files and the browser downloads them (a `.zip` when there are several).

| Setting | Effect |
|---|---|
| **split_by** | A column of the screen's read query: one file per distinct value. Blank: a single file. |
| **sheets** | The sheets of each file, in order. Each sheet has a **name**, a **query** (with its **connector**), and **param_binds** — `source = "split_value"` passes the file's group value to the query. |
| A sheet's **split_by** | A column of the sheet's query: one worksheet per distinct value. |
| **file_name_template** | The file name; `{{split_value}}` and `{{screen}}` are replaced. Default: `<screen>_<value>.xlsx`. |

Sheet names accept `{{split_value}}` and `{{sheet_value}}`; they are shortened to Excel's 31 characters.

### Example — one file per department

```toml
[screens.hr.employees.export]
split_by = "DEPARTMENT"
file_name_template = "staff_{{split_value}}.xlsx"

[[screens.hr.employees.export.sheets]]
name  = "Employees"
query = "employees_by_department"
param_binds = [{ param = "DEPARTMENT", source = "split_value" }]

[[screens.hr.employees.export.sheets]]
name  = "Applications"
query = "applications_by_department"
param_binds = [{ param = "DEPARTMENT", source = "split_value" }]
```

The button produces a `.zip` with one workbook per department, each with an *Employees* and an *Applications* sheet.

## Variations

| Need | How |
|---|---|
| **An aggregated export** | A query (or a database view) that aggregates, used as a sheet's query — or a screen on that view. |
| **A report sent every week** | See [Scheduled report email](./scheduled-report-email.md). |

## What's next

- [Bulk import](./bulk-import.md) — load the exported layout back.
- [Screens](../build/screens/overview.md) — the Output stage among the others.
- [REST API](../../references/rest-api.md) — `POST /api/screens/{app}/{id}/export` builds the workbooks.

## Liberty Next — Files and attachments
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/file-upload/

Recipe — what Liberty Next offers for files: screens have no attachment field, but a row can carry the address of a document stored elsewhere, a file's rows can be imported into a screen, and a Nomaflow job can load a file chosen at run time.

## The problem

A row goes with a file — the signed contract of a customer, the scan of a receipt — or a file holds rows to load into a table.

## What exists

Screens have **no attachment field**: a dialog cannot store a file in a row nor serve it back. Three mechanisms cover the usual needs:

| Need | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Reach the document of a row | An **address column**: the row stores the document's address in the document store already in place (file share, SharePoint, object storage). |
| Load the rows of an Excel / CSV file into a table, through a screen | The screen's **Import** — see [Bulk import](./bulk-import.md). |
| Load a file into a table, by job | A Nomaflow **`file_load`** step: the file is picked in the **Run with parameters** window, read from a server path, or taken from a watched folder — see [Steps → File load](../../nomaflow/steps.md#file-load). |

## Address of a document

### 1. A column for the address

```sql
ALTER TABLE contracts ADD document_url VARCHAR(500);
```

### 2. Show it

Give the `DOCUMENT_URL` dictionary entry a label and the **url** format (Liberty Next → Data → Dictionary → Entries). The grid and the dialog show the address as text, to copy into the browser — they do not turn it into a clickable link.

### 3. Fill it

Users paste the address in the dialog, or a job fills it — for example a `python` step that files the documents of a folder in the store and writes their addresses into the table (see [Plugins](../apps/plugins.md)).

Access to the document itself is governed by the document store, not by Liberty Next.

## What's next

- [Bulk import](./bulk-import.md) — load a file's rows through a screen.
- [Steps → File load](../../nomaflow/steps.md#file-load) — load a file by job.
- [Dictionary → Formats](../dictionary.md#formats) — the display formats.

## Liberty Next — Audit trail
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/audit-trail/

Recipe — record who created and last changed each row, and keep the history of every write, without trusting the browser: {{LOGIN}} / {{SYSTIMESTAMP}} tokens in the write queries, dictionary rules, and the screen's audit table.

## The problem

Who created this row, who changed it last, and what did it look like before? The answer must not depend on what the browser sends.

## The pattern

Two levels, which combine:

| Level | Mechanism | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **Last change, on the row** | Tokens `{{LOGIN}}` / `{{SYSTIMESTAMP}}` in the write queries. | `CREATED_BY`, `CREATED_AT`, `UPDATED_BY`, `UPDATED_AT` filled by the server. |
| **Every write, in a history table** | The screen's **audit_table**. | One row per insert, update or delete, with the action, the user and the date. |

## The recipe

### 1. Audit columns on the table

```sql
ALTER TABLE customers ADD created_by VARCHAR(64);
ALTER TABLE customers ADD created_at TIMESTAMP;
ALTER TABLE customers ADD updated_by VARCHAR(64);
ALTER TABLE customers ADD updated_at TIMESTAMP;
```

### 2. Stamp them in the write queries

In **Liberty Next → Data → Connectors**, edit the insert and update queries of the table:

```sql
-- customers_post
INSERT INTO customers (ID, NAME, STATUS, CREATED_BY, CREATED_AT)
VALUES (:ID, :NAME, :STATUS, {{LOGIN}}, {{SYSTIMESTAMP}})

-- customers_put
UPDATE customers
SET NAME = :NAME, STATUS = :STATUS,
    UPDATED_BY = {{LOGIN}}, UPDATED_AT = {{SYSTIMESTAMP}}
WHERE ID = :ID_ORIGINAL
```

The server replaces the tokens at execution — the signed-in user's name in upper case, the current date and time — whatever the form sends. The update query does not touch `CREATED_BY` / `CREATED_AT`, which keep their values.

:::note[Dictionary rules instead of tokens]
The `LOGIN` and `SYSDATE` [dictionary rules](../dictionary.md#rules) do the same on any write that binds the column — but `LOGIN` rewrites the column on **every** write, updates included, and `SYSDATE` only fills an **empty** value. They suit `UPDATED_BY` on a query that binds it; for creation columns, the tokens in the insert query are the safer choice.
:::

### 3. Show the columns

On the screen, give the four columns labels (dictionary entries) and a datetime format, tick **disabled** (read-only), and place them on a *History* tab of the dialog — or leave them out of the dialog and show them in the grid only.

### 4. Keep every write — `audit_table`

In the screen's **What it is** stage, set **audit_table** to `AUD_CUSTOMERS`. From then on, each insert, update or delete made through the screen also writes a row into `AUD_CUSTOMERS`:

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| The table's columns | The values sent with the write. |
| `AUD_ACTION` | `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`. |
| `AUD_USER` | The user's name. |
| `AUD_DATE` | The server's date and time. |

The table is created on the first write from the structure of the source table. Several screens can share one audit table.

## Why it is safe

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| Change the form to send `UPDATED_BY = 'someone else'`. | The token is resolved by the server; the form's value is not used. |
| Call the REST API directly with a forged body. | Same: tokens and rules are applied by the server, after the request is read. |
| Write without signing in. | The write needs an authenticated user with the query's permission. |

## Variations

| Need | How |
|---|---|
| **A version number** | `SET VERSION = VERSION + 1` in the update query. |
| **History of a whole application** | One shared audit table for its screens (`AUD_SECURITY`). |
| **Changes shipped from one environment to another** | Change tracking on the screen — see [Change packages](../../nomaflow/change-packages.md). |

## What's next

- [Parameter binding → Tokens](../build/queries/parameter-binding.md#tokens)
- [Dictionary → Rules](../dictionary.md#rules)
- [CRUD over an existing table](./crud-existing-table.md)

## Liberty Next — Bulk import
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/bulk-import/

Recipe — load many rows from an Excel or CSV file: the screen's Import dialog, which checks every row against the screen's rules and the database before saving the valid ones, and the Nomaflow file_load step for recurring loads.

## The problem

A file with hundreds of rows — customers from a trade show, products from a supplier catalogue — to load into a table, without typing them one by one.

## The pattern

| Need | Tool |
|---|---|
| A user loads a file now and then, through a screen. | The screen's **Import** dialog. |
| A file arrives regularly and must be loaded without anyone. | A Nomaflow job with a **`file_load`** step. |

## Import through a screen

### 1. Enable the import

In the Screen Designer, **What it is** stage, tick **uploadable**. The screen must have an insert query (and an update query to update existing rows). Users who may insert see an **Import** button above the grid.

### 2. Prepare the file

An `.xlsx` (first sheet) or `.csv` file with a header row. Each header is matched to a column of the screen, ignoring case:

- by the column name (`NAME`, `PRICE`) or its label (`Name`, `Price`);
- for a column with a list of values (`LOOKUP` or `ENUM`), by the code: the header `<label> (ID)` or the column name — the same layout as the screen's Excel export, so an exported file can be re-imported.

Columns not matched are ignored.

### 3. Check, then save

The **Import from Excel** dialog asks for the file and for what to do with **existing rows**: *Update or insert*, *Insert only* or *Update only*. **Check** runs two passes:

1. **Screen rules** — every value against its column: a lookup code must exist, an enum value must be allowed, a Boolean must be one of the two values.
2. **Database** — the rows that passed run the real insert or update inside a transaction that is rolled back: constraint violations, missing values and existing keys show up as in a real save.

The report lists the valid and invalid rows with the error of each. **Save N valid rows** writes only the valid rows, in batches.

The insert and update queries apply as for a dialog save: tokens, dictionary rules (`LOGIN`, `SYSDATE`, `SEQUENCE`), the screen's `audit_table` and its row hooks.

### Paste from Excel

In edit mode, rows copied from Excel can also be pasted into the grid: they are added as new rows, saved with the grid's **Save**.

## Recurring loads — `file_load`

For a file that comes back regularly, a Nomaflow job with a **`file_load`** step loads it into a table: a file chosen at run time, a server path or a watched folder; header-to-column mapping and constants; `append` or `replace_partition` (replace one period, in one transaction); a refusal query and a control total; rejected rows downloadable as CSV. See [Steps → File load](../../nomaflow/steps.md#file-load).

## Variations

| Need | How |
|---|---|
| **A key other than the table's** to decide insert or update | Mark that column as **key** on the screen. |
| **Values to compute during the import** | Put them in the queries (`{{LOGIN}}`, `{{SYSDATE}}`) or the dictionary rules. |
| **Fill related columns from a lookup** | The column's `return_binds`: on import, they fill the target column when the file leaves it empty. |

## What's next

- [CRUD over an existing table](./crud-existing-table.md) — the screen to import into.
- [Excel export](./excel-export.md) — the file layout the import reads back.
- [Steps → File load](../../nomaflow/steps.md#file-load) — loads by job.

## Liberty Next — Multi-step form / workflow
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/multi-step-form/

Recipe — an approval workflow on a status column: one guarded query per transition, row-menu actions with confirmation and a prompt for the reason, permissions per transition, fields shown or locked by status, read-only closed rows, notifications and a daily reminder job.

## The problem

An expense claim goes through *Draft → Submitted → Approved / Rejected*. Each transition belongs to a given role; some fields only matter in some states; a claim waiting too long must be chased.

## The pattern

| Need | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| A transition that only applies from the right state | One write query per transition, with `AND STATUS = '<expected>'` in its WHERE. |
| A button per transition | A row-menu action: a `chain` with confirmation, prompt and query. |
| Only managers approve | The transition query's permission, granted to the managers' role. |
| Fields by state | `visible_when`, `required_when`, `disabled_when` on the columns. |
| Frozen once decided | The screen's `editable_when`. |
| Warn the right people | Notification rules on the screen's writes. |
| Chase stalled claims | A daily Nomaflow job. |

## The recipe

### 1. Table

```sql
CREATE TABLE expense_claims (
  id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  employee      VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  amount        DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,
  description   VARCHAR(2000),
  status        VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'DRAFT',
  submitted_at  TIMESTAMP,
  decided_by    VARCHAR(64),
  decided_at    TIMESTAMP,
  reject_reason VARCHAR(500),
  reminded_at   TIMESTAMP
);
```

### 2. Status list

**Liberty Next → Data → Dictionary → Enums**: an enum `CLAIM_STATUS` with the values `DRAFT` (Draft), `SUBMITTED` (Submitted), `APPROVED` (Approved), `REJECTED` (Rejected). The `STATUS` entry gets **Kind of field** *A fixed list of values*, **List of values** `CLAIM_STATUS`: the grid shows the labels and the dialog a list.

### 3. One query per transition

In **Liberty Next → Data → Connectors → expenses → Queries**, three writable queries:

```sql
-- submit_claim
UPDATE expense_claims
SET STATUS = 'SUBMITTED', SUBMITTED_AT = {{SYSTIMESTAMP}}
WHERE ID = :ID AND STATUS = 'DRAFT' AND EMPLOYEE = {{LOGIN}}

-- approve_claim
UPDATE expense_claims
SET STATUS = 'APPROVED', DECIDED_BY = {{LOGIN}}, DECIDED_AT = {{SYSTIMESTAMP}}
WHERE ID = :ID AND STATUS = 'SUBMITTED'

-- reject_claim
UPDATE expense_claims
SET STATUS = 'REJECTED', DECIDED_BY = {{LOGIN}}, DECIDED_AT = {{SYSTIMESTAMP}},
    REJECT_REASON = :REJECT_REASON
WHERE ID = :ID AND STATUS = 'SUBMITTED'
```

The `AND STATUS = …` guard makes a transition from the wrong state change nothing; `EMPLOYEE = {{LOGIN}}` lets employees submit only their own claims (`{{LOGIN}}` is the user name in upper case, as `EMPLOYEE` must be stored).

### 4. The transition buttons

In the Screen Designer, **Actions** stage, **Row menu** section, one entry per transition:

```toml
[[screens.expenses.expense_claims.row_menu]]
type  = "chain"
id    = "reject"
label = "Reject"
prompt_title  = "Reject the claim"
prompt_fields = [{ name = "REJECT_REASON", label = "Reason", required = true }]
steps = [
  { type = "run_query", id = "do", query = "reject_claim",
    param_binds = [{ param = "ID", source = "ID" },
                   { param = "REJECT_REASON", source = "INPUT.REJECT_REASON" }] },
  { type = "refresh", id = "reload" },
]
```

*Approve* follows the same shape with a `confirm` step instead of the prompt; *Submit* with `submit_claim`. To show a clear message when the claim is not in the right state, wrap the steps in an `if` on `STATUS` (`equals` `SUBMITTED`): `then_steps` run the query, `else_steps` a `notify`. See [Actions and lifecycle](../build/screens/actions-and-lifecycle.md).

### 5. Who may do what

Each query has its own permission: `sql:expenses:submit_claim`, `sql:expenses:approve_claim`, `sql:expenses:reject_claim`. In **Liberty Next → Administer → Access → Roles**, grant the first one to employees and the other two to managers only: an employee who clicks *Approve* gets a refusal. See [Roles & permissions](../build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md).

### 6. Fields by state

On the columns (Edit and Filter tabs of the inspector):

| Column | Setting |
|---|---|
| `DESCRIPTION`, `AMOUNT` | `required_when` STATUS = `DRAFT` |
| `SUBMITTED_AT` | `visible_when` STATUS = `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`; `disabled` |
| `DECIDED_BY`, `DECIDED_AT` | `visible_when` STATUS = `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`; `disabled` |
| `REJECT_REASON` | `visible_when` STATUS = `REJECTED`; `disabled` |

And in the **What it is** stage, `editable_when` STATUS = `DRAFT`: once submitted, the claim opens read-only and only the row-menu transitions change it. See [Form conditions](../form-conditions.md).

### 7. Notifications

In **Liberty Next → Logic → Notifications**, a rule on the screen's **update** event, *Only when the written row has* `STATUS = SUBMITTED`, channel `portal` and `email`, recipients `role:managers`, subject `Claim {ID} of {EMPLOYEE} to approve`. A second rule on `STATUS = REJECTED` can warn the requester. See [Notifications](../../nomaflow/notifications.md).

### 8. Reminders

A Nomaflow job, every morning, with a `sql_query` step:

```sql
UPDATE expense_claims SET REMINDED_AT = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
WHERE STATUS = 'SUBMITTED' AND SUBMITTED_AT < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '5' DAY
```

and a notification rule on that job's `succeeded` event: `{ROWS} claims waiting for more than 5 days`, to `role:managers`.

## Variations

| Need | How |
|---|---|
| **History of every transition** | The screen's `audit_table` — see [Audit trail](./audit-trail.md). |
| **Reopen a rejected claim** | A `reopen_claim` query (`STATUS = 'DRAFT' … WHERE STATUS = 'REJECTED'`) and its row-menu entry. |
| **A long form in steps** | Dialog tabs, with `hide_on_add` / `hide_on_edit` for the tabs that only make sense in one mode. |

## What's next

- [Actions and lifecycle](../build/screens/actions-and-lifecycle.md) — chains, prompts, conditions.
- [Form conditions](../form-conditions.md) — fields by state.
- [Notifications](../../nomaflow/notifications.md) — rules and recipients.

## Liberty Next — OIDC sign-in
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/oidc-sso/

Recipe — let users sign in with the company's identity provider (Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak, Okta, Auth0…): register the application at the provider, fill Liberty Next → Administer → App → OpenID Connect (SSO), then give the new users their roles.

## The problem

Users should sign in with their company account, not with a separate password.

## The pattern

Liberty Next signs users in through any OpenID Connect provider. The local sign-in form stays available; a **Sign in with OIDC** button is added below it.

## The recipe

### 1. Register the application at the provider

At the provider (Entra ID, Keycloak, Okta…), create a web application (confidential client) with:

- **Redirect URI**: `https://<host>/auth/oidc/callback`;
- the scopes `openid email profile`;
- a **client secret**.

Note the **client ID**, the **client secret** and the **discovery URL** (`…/.well-known/openid-configuration`).

### 2. Fill the settings

**Liberty Next → Administer → App → OpenID Connect (SSO)**:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Enabled** | On. |
| **Discovery URL** | The provider's `.well-known/openid-configuration`. |
| **Client ID**, **Client secret** | As registered — the secret is encrypted when saved. |
| **Scopes** | `openid email profile`. |
| **Username claim** | `preferred_username` by default; `email` or `upn` depending on the provider. |

Save: the change applies without a restart. See [App settings → OpenID Connect](../build/settings-app.md#section-4--openid-connect-sso).

### 3. First sign-in and roles

Users appear in **Liberty Next → Administer → Access → Users** at their first sign-in, active and **without roles**: they see an empty application until a role is given to them. The usual onboarding: the person signs in once, an administrator assigns the roles. See [Users](../build/secure/users.md).

## Check

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| No OIDC button | **Enabled** is off. |
| The provider refuses the redirect | The redirect URI registered at the provider is not exactly `https://<host>/auth/oidc/callback`. |
| Signed in, empty application | Expected for a new user: assign roles. |
| Wrong user name | Change **Username claim** to the claim the provider fills. |

## What's next

- [Sign-in](../build/secure/sign-in.md) — local and OIDC sign-in in detail.
- [Roles & permissions](../build/secure/roles-and-permissions.md) — what the new users may open.
