| **Documentation** | Release Notes (`releasenotes`), Upgrade History (`upgradehistory`), Status Reference (`statusreference`), Reason Codes (`reasoncodes`), UBL Reference (`ublreference`), Business Rules (`businessrules`, which also opens Schematrons), Developer (`xref`), API Reference (`apireference`). |

A few chips carry a hint:

- **Diagnostics** is one page with five views: each view is a grant of its own, and the menu shows *Diagnostics* as soon as one of them is granted. See [Diagnostics](../../application/diagnostics/overview.md).
- **Scheduled Jobs** covers every job — polls, batch jobs, daily digests, auto-retries, lifecycle checks, retention. Running, pausing or saving a job also requires the *Run batch jobs* action (`integration.run`). See [Scheduled jobs](../../sync/scheduled-jobs/overview.md).
- **Watched Folders** grants the configuration of the folders; their schedule is on *Scheduled Jobs*.
- **Promotion** also requires the *Settings access* feature. See [Promotion](../../management/promotion.md).
- **Developer** opens the [Developer reference](../../references/developer.md): tables, configuration keys, flows, impact, API.
- **Billing overview** and **Statistics** are pages of their own, checked by the server and by the tools of the AI assistant. The upgrade gives both, once, to every role that had Operations, so nobody loses a page; removing them from a role afterwards is kept.
- **Business Rules** also opens [Schematrons](../../references/schematrons.md).
- After sign-in, the user opens on the [start page](../default-periods.md#start-page) of the instance when the role grants it, else on the Billing overview, else on the first page the role grants.

Rules:

- **All** / **None** above the cards grant or revoke every page at once.
- **Empty list = all pages allowed.** Same convention as the other lists: an unfiltered role sees everything.
- The `admin` role created at initialisation receives every page id listed above, including VAT declaration, Reports and Upgrade History.

---

## Tab — Actions

Defines **what the role can do** on the pages it can reach.

### Restrict toggle

| Toggle | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Off** *(default)* | Empty whitelist on the server — the role can perform every action allowed by its pages. |
| **On** | Only the actions checked below are allowed. Switching on **pre-fills the list with every action** so the role does not suddenly lose access — uncheck from there. |

The helper text under the toggle states *Off (default) = role can perform every action allowed by its pages. On = only the checked actions below are allowed.*

The section header above the toggle reflects the current state:

- `(every action is allowed — no whitelist set)` when the toggle is off.
- `(N actions explicitly allowed — everything else is blocked)` when the toggle is on and N actions are checked.
- `(0 actions allowed — same effect as Read-only)` when the whitelist is on but empty.
- `(Read-only mode is on under Access — every action is blocked)` when the *Read-only* feature is on — the whole tab is greyed out.

**Check all** / **Uncheck all** buttons appear under the toggle (disabled when the whitelist is off).

### Action catalog \{#action-catalog\}

Grouped by the page where the button lives — the same key can power buttons on more than one page.

| Group | Action | Key | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Invoices** | Create | `invoice.create` | The *New Invoice* button of the [E-Invoicing](../../application/invoices.md) list. |
| **Invoices** | Edit | `invoice.edit` | Update invoice fields from the detail modal / edit panel. |
| **Invoices** | Edit UBL / change type | `invoice.edit-ubl` | Change the transaction type of an invoice or edit its stored UBL as text, from the UBL tab of the [document window](../../application/edocuments.md#ubl-tab-actions). A role restricted to a list of actions does not have it until it is ticked. |
| **Invoices** | Mark reviewed | `invoice.review` | Mark invoices in error as reviewed by customer service, or clear the mark — [invoice list and window](../../application/invoices.md#mark-reviewed). The upgrade gives it to the roles that have *Edit* or *Push status (DB)*. |
| **Invoices** | Delete | `invoice.delete` | Hard-delete an invoice and all its child records. |
| **Invoices** | Delete lifecycle event | `invoice.lifecycle-delete` | Remove a single status event from an invoice history; the header realigns on the last remaining event. |
| **Invoices** | Resend to PA | `invoice.resend` | Submit / re-submit an invoice (or a bulk batch) to the PA. |
| **Invoices** | Push status (PA) | `invoice.status.pa` | Send a status event through the PA — payment received, in dispute, etc. (the *Set Status* modal's *PA* tab). |
| **Invoices** | Push status (DB) | `invoice.status.db` | Directly update a status in the database, bypassing the PA — admin break-fix path used when the PA round-trip is broken. |
| **Invoices** | Validate UBL | `invoice.validate` | Run XSD + Schematron validation against the stored UBL XML (*Validate* button in the *History* tab). |
| **Invoices** | Download UBL | `invoice.download` | Read the raw UBL XML BLOB — the *Download UBL* button and the underlying `/xml` endpoint. |
| **Invoices** | Preset actions | `invoice.preset-action` | Use the per-status preset buttons (Resend on 9904, …) in the seller actions row. |
| **Invoices** | Custom actions | `invoice.custom-action` | Use the admin-defined custom buttons in the custom actions row. |
| **Invoices** | Email PDF | `invoice.email` | Send the rendered PDF via the configured SMTP relay. |
| **Lists** | Share views | `listview.share` | Share one's [saved views](../../application/saved-views.md) with every user. Saving private views needs no grant. |
| **E-Reporting** | Generate batch | `ereporting.generate` | Build a new e-reporting batch from the *Generate* dialog. |
| **E-Reporting** | Resend batch | `ereporting.resend` | Re-submit an existing e-reporting batch to the PA. |
| **Integration ops** | Run batch jobs | `integration.run` | Trigger *Import statuses* / *Fetch received* / *Retrieve statuses* from the toolbar. |

:::info
The detail modal renders Parties, Invoice Lines, TVA recap and Notes from the UBL XML endpoint, which is **read-open** (still subject to row filters and page visibility). Only the explicit *Download UBL* button is gated by `invoice.download` — view-only roles can therefore inspect the invoice content without the right to extract the raw XML.
:::

### Invoice entry forms \{#entry-forms\}

Below the action cards, when at least one [entry form](../entry-forms.md) exists: **Invoice entry forms** *(none ticked = the complete editor)*. Tick *Complete* and the forms the role may use; with two or more, **Opens on** picks the form the invoice editor opens on. A role without any form keeps the complete editor.

## Tab — Data scope

Defines **which rows the role can see** — companies and optional row filters.

### Companies

An add-row table of company codes (`KCO`) the role is scoped to. Each row carries a free-form input and a **×** button to remove it; **+ Add company** at the bottom appends a new row.

- **Empty list = all companies.** This is the typical default — leaving the table empty grants the role access to every company in the database.
- Adding even one row restricts the role to just the listed companies.
- The placeholder hint reads *KCO code (e.g. 00001)* and the input uses a monospace font to make typos easier to spot.

### Row filters

A more granular restriction: on a field, the role can be restricted to one or more **exact values**. Typical use case — an external customer who should only see invoices issued to its own alpha key (`UHALKY`).

The **column picker** lists each field once, **by scope**:

| Group | Fields | Secures |
|---|---|---|
| **Keys — every table (doc, dct, kco)** | *Document number*, *Document type*, *Company*. | Every table that has these keys. |
| **Document (F564230) — every linked table** | The fields of the archived document: activity code, business unit, sub-type, source file, job, program, routing… | Every table linked to the document. |
| **Invoice (F564231)** | The invoice header: customer alpha key, customer name, contract… | That table. |
| **Validation findings (F564236)** | Severity, source, rule… | That table. |
| **Processing log** / **E-reporting** | Their own columns. | That table. |

Each entry reads `label · FIELD` (*— select column —* until one is picked). For the picked field, enter one or more values (*Value (exact match)*); **+ Add value (OR)** appends another value, **Remove value** and **Remove filter** drop a value or the whole filter. **+ Add row filter** combines filters on different fields.

#### Combination rules

| Pattern | Combined as |
|---|---|
| Multiple **values** on the **same field** | `OR` — the role sees rows that match **any** of the values. |
| Multiple **fields** in the filter list | `AND` — the role sees only rows that match **every** constraint. |
| **Companies** grant + row filters | `AND` — both must be satisfied. |

#### Where row filters apply

A row filter is **not** a UI hint — it is enforced everywhere a forbidden row could otherwise leak:

- **Every list that has the field**, under the name that list gives it (customer, activity code, job, UBL number, status…). A list without the field ignores the filter: a role restricted to the `FATAL` severity keeps its invoices, documents and dashboards and sees only the fatal findings.
- The **dashboards** — Billing overview, Operations, Statistics, status counts — and the **E-Documents** window, which opens under the same rules as its list.
- **Per-row endpoints** — lifecycle, lines, XML download, PDF render, status push, delete, resend, email PDF.
- The **rendered PDF byte stream** — a forbidden row cannot even be turned into a PDF.

Forbidden rows return the same **"not found"** shape the UI uses for genuinely missing data, so the response cannot be used to probe for invoices a role should not know exist.

Lists every user currently bound to the role:

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| **Username** | The user's login. |
| **Full name** | The user's display name (or `–` when not set). |
| **Status** | `Active` (green) or `Inactive` (red). |

This view is **read-only** — to add or remove a user from a role, edit the user from *Configuration → Security → Users*.

## Save / Cancel

- **Create** *(when creating)* / **Save** *(when editing)* persists the role and refreshes the list — available on every tab except *Members*.
- **Cancel** discards changes and closes the panel.
- Inline status messages appear below the panel (`Role created`, `Role updated`, `Role deleted`, error messages).

---

## How grants are stored

Every grant is one row in `F564254`. The shape:

```text
F564254
  PMROLE       — role name (FK to F564251.RLNAME)
  PMCRAPPID    — grant type: 'page' / 'company' / 'feature' / 'action'
                              / 'row-filter'
  PMCRAPPVAL   — grant value, encoded per type:
                   page             → page id          (e.g. 'invoices')
                   company          → KCO code         (e.g. '00001')
                   feature          → flag             ('settings', 'readonly', 'actions-whitelist')
                   action           → action key       (e.g. 'invoice.delete')
                   row-filter       → 'column=value'   (e.g. 'UHALKY=123456')
  PMENABL      — '1' enabled / '0' disabled (used during dialect-specific bootstrapping)
```

Row-filter grants are persisted as flat `column=value` strings — one row per `(column, value)` pair. The editor groups them by column on load and re-flattens them on save, so the operator never sees the raw shape.

Adding a future permission dimension becomes an INSERT in this same table — no DDL change required.

The bootstrap is **idempotent**: dropping `F564254` and re-running *Initialize Database* re-seeds the default `admin` and `viewer` grants without touching role rows. The init log reports the count of newly-inserted grants for visibility.

---

## Delete a role

Clicking the **🗑** icon on a role card opens a confirmation modal:

> *Delete role "X"? Users assigned to this role will lose their permissions.*

Confirming removes the role and every grant row in `F564254` keyed by it. Users previously bound to the role keep their account but lose every permission until they are reassigned to another role.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Create one role per profile, not per individual.** `operator`, `auditor`, `customer_<name>` are simpler to maintain than per-user roles.
- **Grant *Settings access* sparingly.** It opens the entire Configuration menu — limit it to a small admin group.
- **Pair *Read-only* with *Actions* off** for compliance / audit accounts — both layers reinforce each other.
- **Use the Companies table to enforce multi-tenant isolation.** Leaving it empty defeats company-level filtering for the role.
- **Row filters first, action whitelist second** when scoping an external user. The row filter hides everything the user should not see; the action whitelist controls what they can do with what they see.
- **A role sees the Operations dashboard as a whole or not at all.** To keep a team on business figures only, grant the Billing overview and Statistics without Operations.
- **Use Copy when forking a role.** Starting from an existing role with one or two grants flipped is faster than rebuilding the checklists from scratch — and the result is closer to the source role's intent.
- **Re-run *Initialize Database*** *(Database Connectors → NomaUBL)* if the default `admin` or `viewer` grants are missing — it re-seeds the rows without touching custom roles.
- **Delete a role only after re-binding its members.** Once deleted, members lose access to everything until reassigned. The Members tab is the fastest way to check who would be affected.

## NomaUBL — Status Reference
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/status-reference/

Invoice life-cycle statuses for the French e-invoicing reform — codes 200 to 501 (XP Z12-012) with actor, phase, mandatory/factoring tags and allowed actions.

# Status Reference

The screen lists every **invoice life-cycle status** defined by the French e-invoicing reform (norm **XP Z12-012**, codes 200–501). NomaUBL surfaces the same reference inside the app to help users interpret the statuses returned by the PPF and the partner platforms (PA-E / PA-R / PA-TR).

Use the **filter bar** to narrow the list by phase (transmission / processing), by mandatory transmission to the PPF, by factoring or by special codes (batch / routing). Click any card to open the full detail: who emits the status, when it applies, allowed actions per actor, and notes.

## NomaUBL — Reason Codes
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/reason-codes/

Reason codes attached to invoice life-cycle statuses for the French e-invoicing reform — refusal (B2B), PA rejection and irregularity codes from XP Z12-012 Annex A.

# Reason Codes

The screen lists every **reason code** that can be attached to an invoice life-cycle status under the French e-invoicing reform. Three families are distinguished:

- **Refusal (B2B)** — codes a buyer (or partner platform on the buyer's behalf) emits to refuse, dispute or suspend an invoice (statuses 200, 206, 207, 208, 210, 221).
- **PA Rejection** — codes a partner platform emits when an invoice fails the platform-level controls (status 213).
- **Irregularity** — codes used by the PPF when the inbound flow itself fails an integrity check before any business processing (status 213).

Filter by family, search by code or label, and read the full description plus the statuses that may carry the code. Codes flagged **mandatory in body** must be carried in the message body (not just in the envelope).

## NomaUBL — UBL Reference
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/ubl-reference/

UBL field reference for the French e-invoicing reform — 455 UBL terms from the AFNOR XP Z12-012 V1.4 matrix, each with its XPath, cardinality, profile, data type, code list, definition, usage note and the business rules that constrain it, grouped by section.

# UBL Reference

The screen lists every **UBL business term (BT)** carried by the French e-invoicing flow — **455 terms** rebuilt from the **AFNOR XP Z12-012 V1.4** matrix, covering every EXTENDED-CTC-FR block (buyer/seller agents, invoicee, invoicer, payer, line seller, line-level delivery and references, Incoterms, exchange rate, non-VAT taxes, scheme identifiers). CII-only terms are deliberately absent, and terms follow the matrix order.

Each row shows:

- the **BT identifier** and the human-readable **label**;
- the official **definition** (French and English) and the NomaUBL **usage note** as a separate line;
- the **profile** the term belongs to — `BASIC WL`, `EN 16931` or `EXTENDED` — its **data type** and its **code list** (ISO 6523, UNTDID 5305, VAT…);
- the canonical **XPath** and the **cardinality** (`1..1`, `0..1`, `0..n`, `1..n`);
- the **business rules** that constrain it — each identifier links to the [Business Rules](./business-rules.mdx) page.

Filter by section (header, supplier, customer, payee, tax representative, delivery, payment, allowances & charges, tax, totals, invoice line) or search across BT, XPath, label, definition, note, code list and rules. The table is grouped by section and colour-coded — the same scheme the application's invoice editor uses.

In the application, a **rule set** filter shows the fields of one [rule set](../ubl-tools/rule-sets.md) — EN 16931 basic, EN 16931 or France extended (CTC) — with their status in that set: required, conditional, optional.

## NomaUBL — Business Rules
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/business-rules/

The French CTC business rules of the AFNOR XP Z12-012 V1.4 matrix — twelve points of attention written from chapter 4.4 of the standard, and the full rule catalogue (BR-FR controls, consistency, flux 1/10.1 mapping, numeric formats, multi-seller, PPF) with the terms each rule constrains.

# Business Rules

Two views on the French CTC rules of the **AFNOR XP Z12-012 V1.4** matrix.

- **Points of attention** — twelve topics written from **chapter 4.4** of XP Z12-012 (June 2026) and checked against the standard: line and total calculation, rounding, gross/discount/net price, allowances and charges, VAT categories and exemption codes, non-VAT taxes and WEEE, credit notes vs negative invoices, notes and mandatory mentions, profile and invoicing framework, data types, sub-lines, and multi-seller invoices. Each topic states what the standard requires and how NomaUBL implements it, with the chapter cited.
- **Rule catalogue** — the 148 French CTC rules of the matrix (BR-FR controls, consistency, flux 1 / 10.1 mapping, numeric formats, multi-seller, PPF rules) with their full text, a family filter, search, and the [UBL terms](./ubl-reference.mdx) each rule constrains.

Each UBL term on the [UBL Reference](./ubl-reference.mdx) page links back to the rules that apply to it.

In the application, the same **rule set** filter as on the UBL reference keeps the rules that touch a field of the chosen [rule set](../ubl-tools/rule-sets.md).

## NomaUBL — Schematrons
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/schematrons/

The NomaUBL Schematrons page: read the rules of each Schematron pack the validator runs — EN 16931, CIUS-FR, extended CTC FR, Chorus Pro, NomaUBL, e-reporting, and the customer packs named by the document templates — one row per rule with severity, description and context, and the test and message of each rule.

The **Schematrons** page lists the rules of every Schematron pack the validator runs: the packs **shipped with NomaUBL** and the **customer packs** named by a document template. Each rule is a row — its identifier, severity, description and the element it applies to — and a row opens the test the rule evaluates and the message it returns. The page answers the question that follows a validation error: *what exactly does this rule check?*

Open it from **Schematrons** in the Documentation group, after [Business Rules](./business-rules.mdx).

## At a glance

## Choosing a pack

The **Choose a Schematron** picker lists the packs in two groups, each with its number of rules:

| Group | Packs |
|---|---|
| **Shipped with NomaUBL** | EN 16931, CIUS-FR, Extended CTC FR, Chorus Pro, NomaUBL, E-reporting (flux 10). The upgrade refreshes them with the release. |
| **Customer packs** | Each precompiled stylesheet named in the [Custom Schematron](../management/documents.md#ubl) field of a document template. |

Next to the picker, the page shows the file name, the version and the date of the pack, and for a customer pack the templates that use it. The last pack consulted is reopened on the next visit.

## Rules grid

One row per rule (`assert` or `report`) of the pack, sorted by identifier, 100 rows per page.

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| **Rule** | Identifier of the rule (`BR-FR-12`, `BR-CO-15`…), the one quoted in the validation errors. |
| **Severity** | `fatal`, `error`, `warning` or `info`, as a coloured pill. |
| **Description** | What the rule requires, as written in the pack. |
| **Context** | The element the rule is evaluated on (XPath). |
| **Pattern**, **Kind**, **Test** *(hidden)* | Group of rules, `assert` or `report`, and the XPath test. Shown from the column menu. |

The grid has the usual search, filters (severity, pattern), column choice and export.

### Rule window

A click on a row opens the rule: description, **Pattern**, **Context**, then the test under **Must be true** for an `assert` or **Fires when** for a `report`, and the **Message** written into the validation error.

## Access

The page follows the **Business Rules** grant of the Documentation group on the [Roles](../configuration/security/roles.md) page: a role that reads the business rules reads the Schematrons too.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Start from the error.** Copy the rule identifier from the invoice's validation errors and type it into the search box of the grid.
- **Read the test, not only the message.** The message is short; the *Must be true* expression says exactly which element and which value the rule expects.
- **Check a customer pack after an edit.** The picker shows its rule count and the templates that use it; a pack that cannot be read shows its error under the picker.
- **Keep customer rules in customer packs.** The shipped packs are replaced at each upgrade; see [Rule sets](../ubl-tools/rule-sets.md) for choosing which standard packs run.

## NomaUBL — Database Tables
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/database-tables/

NomaUBL database schema reference — every table that backs the application: invoice archive, UBL header / lines / VAT, lifecycle events, validation errors, processing log, e-reporting, notifications and authentication. Functional descriptions, primary keys and field references for Oracle and PostgreSQL.

NomaUBL persists every artefact of the e-invoicing pipeline — the original ERP source, the generated UBL document, the per-line and per-VAT-rate breakdown, the lifecycle events, the validation errors, the runtime processing log, the e-reporting submissions and the user / role / session triplet.

The schema is **identical on Oracle and PostgreSQL** — the DDL is dialect-aware (`BLOB` ↔ `BYTEA`, `NUMBER` ↔ `INTEGER`, `VARCHAR2` ↔ `VARCHAR`) but the column names, primary keys and semantics are the same. Every table name is configurable in the `db-nomaubl` system template and created by the **Initialize Database** action of the *Settings → Database Connectors* screen.

The schema applies regardless of source system — JD Edwards, SAP, NetSuite or a custom ERP. Tables follow the JDE `F564XXX` naming convention because the platform was built around JDE first; the conventions are functional, not source-specific.

A text longer than its column — a customer name, a long reference or message — is shortened to the column's size when it is written, and the UBL keeps the whole value. The size is read from the database, so a widened column is used at its real size. Codes and keys (document type, company, status) are never shortened, and the server log reports each column concerned once.

---

## Naming conventions

| Convention | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Table identifier** | `F564XXX` — JDE-style file prefix. Configurable per environment. |
| **Column prefix** | Two-letter prefix tied to the table (`FE` for archive, `UH` for UBL header, `UL` for lines, `UV` for VAT / validation, `US` for status / users, `RG`/`RH`/`RI` for e-reporting…). |
| **Dates** | JDE Julian — integer in `CYYDDD` format where `C = 1` for 2000–2099, `YY` is the last two digits of the year, `DDD` is the day of the year. Example: `125108` → 2025-04-18. Converted on the fly for the UI. |
| **Times** | Integer in `HHMMSS` format. Example: `143052` → 14:30:52. |
| **Scaled numerics** | Some amounts and rates are stored as integers scaled by a fixed factor — divide on read: `ATXA × 100` (2 decimals), `QNTY × 10000` (4 decimals), `UPRC × 10000` (4 decimals), `TXR1 × 1000` (3 decimals). |
| **XML payloads** | Stored as `BLOB` (Oracle) / `BYTEA` (Postgres) for JDE source XML, generated UBL **and e-reporting XML**. UTF-8 bytes throughout. |
| **Auto-incremented sequences** | `SEQN` columns use `COALESCE(MAX(SEQN), 0) + 1` on insert — no Oracle sequence or Postgres serial required. |

---

## Schema overview

  solid arrow — hard FK relationship
  dashed arrow — soft / cross-domain link
  highlighted card — domain anchor

## Invoice domain

The seven tables that carry an invoice through its complete life — from the raw ERP payload to its definitive lifecycle status.

### F564230 — Source archive & PA submission log

Stores the **original ERP XML** alongside the routing flags and the PA transaction UUID returned after submission. One row per source document.

- **Primary key**: `FEDOC + FEDCT + FEKCO`
- **Notable**: `FETXFT` carries the source XML payload (UTF-8 bytes); `FEUKIDSZ` holds the UUID returned by the Plateforme Agréée after successful import; `FEEV10` is the *send to PA* flag (`1` = yes, `2` = no).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `FEDOC` | Integer | Document number (PK). |
| `FEDCT` | Text(2) | Document type (PK). |
| `FEKCO` | Text(5) | Company code (PK). |
| `FEAA10` | Text(10) | Activity / routing code. |
| `FEAA20` | Text(25) | Document sub-type. |
| `FEALKY` | Text(25) | Customer alpha key. |
| `FEAEXP` | Decimal × 100 | Document amount (scaled). |
| `FEIVD` | Date (Julian) | Invoice date. |
| `FEARDU` | Date (Julian) | Due date. |
| `FEUPMJ` | Date (Julian) | Last update date. |
| `FEPID` | Text(10) | Program ID. |
| `FEVERS` | Text(5) | Version. |
| `FEUSER` | Text(10) | User who created the row. |
| `FEJOBN` | Text(10) | Job name. |
| `FEUPMT` | Time (HHMMSS) | Last update time. |
| `FEWDS1` | Text(80) | Source file name. |
| `FEEV01` | Text(25) | Routing code. |
| `FEAC04` | Text(5) | Business unit / office. |
| `FEEV10` | Integer | *Send to PA* flag — `1` = yes, `2` = no. |
| `FETXFT` | BLOB | Original ERP XML (UTF-8 bytes). |
| `FEUKIDSZ` | Text(100) | PA platform transaction UUID returned on import. |

### F564231 — UBL invoice header

The **EN 16931** view of the invoice plus the generated UBL 2.1 document. One row per invoice; same primary key as F564230.

- **Primary key**: `UHDOC + UHDCT + UHKCO`
- **Notable**: `UHTXFT` stores the generated UBL document (UTF-8 bytes); `UHK74RSCD` is the current lifecycle status code from the *statuses* reference list; `UHY56BAR` is the BAR routing code (`B2B` / `B2G` / `B2C` / `B2BINT` / `OUTOFSCOPE` / …).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `UHDOC` | Integer | Document number (PK · FK → F564230). |
| `UHDCT` | Text(2) | Document type (PK). |
| `UHKCO` | Text(5) | Company code (PK). |
| `UHODOC` / `UHODCT` / `UHOKCO` | Integer / Text(2) / Text(5) | Original (referenced) document — non-empty for credit notes pointing at a prior invoice. |
| `UHK74FLEN` | Text(25) | UBL invoice number — BT-1. |
| `UHK74XMLV` | Text(50) | Profile ID — BT-23. |
| `UHK74LDDJ` | Date (Julian) | Issue date — BT-2. |
| `UHDDJ` | Date (Julian) | Due date — BT-9. |
| `UHK74LEDT` | Text(3) | Invoice type code — BT-3. |
| `UHATXA` | Decimal × 100 | Tax-exclusive amount — BT-109. |
| `UHSTAM` | Decimal × 100 | Tax amount — BT-110. |
| `UHAG` | Decimal × 100 | Tax-inclusive amount — BT-112. |
| `UHAAP` | Decimal × 100 | Amount due — BT-115. |
| `UHCRCD` | Text(3) | Currency code — BT-5. |
| `UH55RSF` | Text(40) | Order reference — BT-13. |
| `UHY74CTID` | Integer | Contract reference — BT-12. |
| `UHAN8` | Integer | Customer AN8 (JDE address book). |
| `UHALKY` | Text(25) | Customer alpha key. |
| `UHALPH` | Text(40) | Customer name — BT-44. |
| `UHTXFT` | BLOB | Generated UBL 2.1 XML (UTF-8 bytes). |
| `UHK74RSCD` | Text(4) | Current lifecycle status code (see *Status Reference*). |
| `UHK74MSG1` | Text(500) | Status message. |
| `UHY56EPID` / `UHY56EPSC` | Text(100) / Text(25) | Customer endpoint ID + scheme — BT-49 / BT-49-1. |
| `UHY56PYIN` | Text(3) | Payment means code — BT-81. |
| `UHY56BAR` | Text(10) | BAR routing code (`B2B`, `B2G`, `B2C`, `B2BINT`, `OUTOFSCOPE`, …). |
| `UHY56RSRC` / `UHY56RSRCL` | Text(50) / Text(250) | Rejection reason code + label. |
| `UHY56ACTN` / `UHY56ACTNL` | Text(10) / Text(250) | Expected action code + label. |
| `UHY56ACTND` | Text(1000) | Status note (raw JSON returned by the PA). |
| `UHUSER` / `UHPID` / `UHJOBN` / `UHUPMJ` / `UHTDAY` | — | Audit columns — created by, program, job, last-update date and time. |

### F564233 — UBL invoice lines

One row per UBL line. Stored values for quantity, price and tax rate are **scaled** — divide on read.

- **Primary key**: `ULDOC + ULDCT + ULKCO + ULLNID`
- **Notable**: `ULLNID` is the JDE line ID × 1000 (BT-126). `ULY56QNTY` ÷ 10000, `ULUPRC` ÷ 10000, `ULATXA` ÷ 100, `ULTXR1` ÷ 1000.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ULDOC` / `ULDCT` / `ULKCO` | — | Document number / type / company (PK · FK → F564231). |
| `ULLNID` | Integer × 1000 | Line ID — BT-126. |
| `ULDSC1` | Text(40) | Item description — BT-153. |
| `ULLITM` | Text(35) | Seller item ID — BT-155. |
| `ULY56QNTY` | Decimal × 10000 | Invoiced quantity — BT-129. |
| `ULY56UM` | Text(3) | Unit of measure code — BT-130. |
| `ULUPRC` | Decimal × 10000 | Unit price — BT-146. |
| `ULATXA` | Decimal × 100 | Line extension amount — BT-131. |
| `ULREBL` | Decimal × 10000 | Allowance / charge — BT-136. |
| `ULCRCD` | Text(3) | Currency code. |
| `ULK74TVCC` | Text(2) | Tax category code — BT-151. |
| `ULTXR1` | Decimal × 1000 | Tax rate — BT-152. |
| `ULK74EXRC` | Text(100) | Tax exemption reason — BT-121. |
| `ULUSER` / `ULPID` / `ULJOBN` / `ULUPMJ` / `ULTDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

### F564234 — UBL VAT summary

One row per **(tax category, tax rate, currency)** breakdown carried by the invoice — the EN 16931 BG-23 group.

- **Primary key**: `UVDOC + UVDCT + UVKCO + UVSEQN`
- **Notable**: `UVSEQN` is auto-incremented via `COALESCE(MAX(UVSEQN), 0) + 1` on insert.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `UVDOC` / `UVDCT` / `UVKCO` | — | Document number / type / company (PK · FK → F564231). |
| `UVSEQN` | Integer | Sequence number (PK). |
| `UVK74TVCC` | Text(2) | Tax category code — BT-118. |
| `UVTXR1` | Decimal × 1000 | Tax rate — BT-119. |
| `UVATXA` | Decimal × 100 | Taxable amount — BT-116. |
| `UVSTAM` | Decimal × 100 | Tax amount — BT-117. |
| `UVCRCD` | Text(3) | Currency code. |
| `UVK74EXRC` | Text(500) | Tax exemption reason — BT-120. |
| `UVUSER` / `UVPID` / `UVJOBN` / `UVUPMJ` / `UVTDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

### F564235 — Lifecycle events

The **append-only history** of every status the invoice has been in. One row per event, in submission order. This is the source of the *History* tab in the invoice detail modal.

- **Primary key**: `USDOC + USDCT + USKCO + USSEQN`
- **Notable**: `USSEQN` is auto-incremented; events are written by `StatusTransition.apply()` together with the corresponding update of `F564231.UHK74RSCD`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `USDOC` / `USDCT` / `USKCO` | — | Document number / type / company (PK · FK → F564231). |
| `USSEQN` | Integer | Event sequence (PK). |
| `USK74RSCD` | Text(4) | Status code at this event. |
| `USK74MSG1` | Text(500) | Status message. |
| `USTRDJ` | Date (Julian) | Event date. |
| `USY56RSRC` / `USY56RSRCL` | Text(50) / Text(250) | Rejection reason code + label. |
| `USY56ACTN` / `USY56ACTNL` | Text(10) / Text(250) | Expected action code + label. |
| `USY56ACTND` | Text(1000) | Status note (raw JSON from the PA). |
| `USUSER` / `USPID` / `USJOBN` / `USUPMJ` / `USTDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

### F564236 — UBL validation errors

XSD and Schematron errors recorded for an invoice. One row per error / warning — feeds the *History → Validation errors* group of the invoice detail modal and the *Integration Errors* page when no matching `F564231` row is found.

- **Primary key**: `UVDOC + UVDCT + UVKCO + UVSEQN`
- **Notable**: `UVY56LEVEL` is `ERROR` / `WARNING` / `INFO`. `UVSRCL` flags the validator: `XSD`, `SCH` (Schematron) or `DB`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `UVDOC` / `UVDCT` / `UVKCO` | — | Document number / type / company (PK; can be orphan when no F564231 row). |
| `UVSEQN` | Integer | Error sequence (PK). |
| `UVY56LEVEL` | Text(10) | Severity — `ERROR`, `WARNING`, `INFO`. |
| `UVSRCL` | Text(25) | Source — `XSD` / `SCH` / `DB`. |
| `UVY56RULE` | Text(50) | Rule ID (e.g. `BR-01`, `PEPPOL-EN16931-R001`). |
| `UVK74MSG1` | Text(2000) | Error / warning message. |
| `UVUSER` / `UVPID` / `UVJOBN` / `UVUPMJ` / `UVTDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

### F564237 — Runtime processing log

Every event written by `RuntimeLogHandler` during XML / UBL / BIP / FTP processing — `START`, `END` and any intermediate method. Backs the *Processing Log* page (Management menu).

- **Primary key**: `FEUKID` (sequence computed via `COALESCE(MAX(FEUKID),0)+1` on insert — used as a tiebreaker for events sharing the same timestamp).
- **Notable**: `FERMK` is the processing type (`SINGLE`, `BURST`, `UBL`, `BOTH`, `UBL_VALIDATE`, `PROCESS`, `AUTO`); `FETMPL` is the template name (empty for UBL processing); `FERMK2` is `START` / `END` or the failing method name on errors.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `FEUKID` | Integer (BIGINT) | Sequence id (PK · stable insert order). |
| `FEWDS1` | Text(60) | Source file name — links to `F564230.FEWDS1`. |
| `FEUPMJ` | Date (Julian) | Event date. |
| `FEUPMT` | Time (HHMMSS) | Event time. |
| `FERMK` | Text(30) | Processing type (renamed from `FEMODE`). |
| `FETMPL` | Text(40) | Template name. |
| `FERMK2` | Text(30) | Operation — `START` / `END` / failing method name (renamed from `FEMETHOD`). |
| `FEK74MSG1` | Text(1024) | Status message or error detail (renamed from `FEMESSAGE`). |

---

## E-Reporting domain

Three tables that record the *(period, flux, company)* declarations submitted to the Plateforme Agréée — flux **10.1** (B2BINT detail) and **10.3** (B2C / OUTOFSCOPE aggregated).

### F564260 — Report log

One row per generated report. Stores the `<ReportDocument>` XML and the latest known status.

- **Primary key**: `RGUKID` (globally unique sequence — no flux / company component).
- **Notable**: `RGY56BAR` is `10.1` or `10.3`; `RGDCT` is the document type (`IN` initial, `RE` replacement, `CO` cancellation, `MO` modification); `RGTXFT` carries the generated XML as **UTF-8 bytes** (BLOB / BYTEA).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RGUKID` | Integer (BIGINT) | Report sequence id (PK). |
| `RGY56BAR` | Text(10) | Flux code — `10.1` / `10.3`. |
| `RGKCO` | Text(5) | Issuing company code. |
| `RGDCT` | Text(2) | Document type — `IN` / `RE` / `CO` / `MO`. |
| `RGEFTJ` | Date (Julian) | Period start. |
| `RGEFDJ` | Date (Julian) | Period end. |
| `RGY56EPID` | Text(125) | Issuer SIREN (scheme `0002`). |
| `RGK74RSCD` | Text(10) | Current lifecycle status code. |
| `RGK74MSG1` | Text(1024) | Last status message. |
| `RGNINV` | Integer | Number of invoices included. |
| `RGTXFT` | BLOB | Generated `<ReportDocument>` XML (UTF-8 bytes). |
| `RGUSER` / `RGPID` / `RGJOBN` / `RGUPMJ` / `RGTDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

### F564261 — Report lifecycle events

The append-only history of statuses for a given report — same shape as F564235 for invoices.

- **Primary key**: `RHUKID + RHSEQN`
- **Notable**: `RHSEQN` is auto-incremented. `RHUKID` is the FK to the parent log (`F564260.RGUKID`).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RHUKID` | Integer (BIGINT) | Report sequence id (PK · FK → F564260.RGUKID). |
| `RHY56BAR` | Text(10) | Flux code (denormalised for query convenience). |
| `RHSEQN` | Integer | Event sequence (PK). |
| `RHK74RSCD` | Text(10) | Status code at this event. |
| `RHK74MSG1` | Text(1024) | Status message. |
| `RHUSER` / `RHPID` / `RHJOBN` / `RHUPMJ` / `RHTDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

### F564262 — Report / invoice mapping

Tracks **which invoices were included in which report** — composite PK avoids re-including invoices that were already declared on a prior run.

- **Primary key**: `RIUKID + RIDOC + RIDCT + RIKCO`
- **Notable**: A secondary index on `(RIDOC, RIDCT, RIKCO, RIY56BAR)` answers "in which report was this invoice declared?" efficiently.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RIUKID` | Integer (BIGINT) | Report sequence id (PK · FK → F564260.RGUKID). |
| `RIY56BAR` | Text(10) | Flux code. |
| `RIDOC` / `RIDCT` / `RIKCO` | — | Invoice triplet (PK · FK → F564231). |
| `RIUSER` / `RIPID` / `RIJOBN` / `RIUPMJ` / `RITDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

---

## Authentication + notifications domain

Five tables for built-in user / role / session / permissions management plus the notifications inbox. The auth block is active when `authEnabled = Y` in the *global* template.

### F564250 — Users

One row per user. Passwords are stored as **PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256** hashes — never in clear text.

- **Primary key**: `USUSER`
- **Notable**: `USLDAPPSWD` format is `iterations:base64(salt):base64(hash)` (bytes). `USSECF3 = 'Y'` forces a password change on the next login (default for new accounts).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `USUSER` | Text(10) | Username (PK). |
| `USLDAPPSWD` | BLOB | PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hash — `iterations:salt:hash` (renamed from `USPASSWD`). |
| `USROLE` | Text(36) | Role name (FK → F564251.RLROLE). |
| `USFULLNAME` | Text(50) | Display name. |
| `USEMAIL` | Text(75) | Email address. |
| `USENABL` | Text(1) | `Y` = active, `N` = disabled (renamed from `USACTIVE`). |
| `USSECF3` | Text(30) | `Y` = must change password on next login (renamed from `USFORCEPASSWD`). |
| `USUPMJ` | Date (Julian) | Account creation / last update date. |
| `USTDAY` | Time (HHMMSS) | Matching time. |

### F564251 — Roles (identity only)

One row per role. This table stores **role identity only** — the grants (pages, companies, read-only, settings access) live row-by-row in `F564254`.

- **Primary key**: `RLROLE`
- **Notable**: No schema change is needed to introduce a new permission dimension — just insert rows with a new `PMCRAPPID` in `F564254`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RLROLE` | Text(36) | Role identifier (PK). |
| `RLROLEDESC` | Text(255) | Human-readable description. |
| `RLUSER` / `RLPID` / `RLJOBN` / `RLUPMJ` / `RLTDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

### F564252 — Sessions

One row per active session. Sessions are validated on every API request; expired rows are pruned by the auth handler.

- **Primary key**: `SSLSID` (UUID, renamed from `SSTOKEN`)
- **Notable**: The token is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <SSLSID>` on every API call. Two indexes on `SSUSER` and `SSETDTIM` keep lookups and cleanup efficient.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SSLSID` | Text(100) | Session token / UUID (PK). |
| `SSUSER` | Text(10) | Username (FK → F564250.USUSER). |
| `SSSTDTIM` | Timestamp | Session creation timestamp (renamed from `SSCREATED`). |
| `SSETDTIM` | Timestamp | Session expiry timestamp (renamed from `SSEXPIRES`). |

### F564253 — Notifications

One row per delivered notification. Backs the portal **inbox** and the **bell** in the utilities bar (see [Notifications](../application/notifications.md)).

- **Primary key**: `NTUKID` (globally unique sequence).
- **Notable**: `(NTDOC, NTDCT, NTKCO)` is the FK back to `F564231` when the notification relates to an invoice (nullable for system alerts). `NTUSER` is the recipient username, or `*` for a broadcast (auth-disabled mode). `NTEV01` is the read flag (`Y` = read, `N` = unread) — drives the bell badge.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NTUKID` | Integer (BIGINT) | Sequence id (PK). |
| `NTUSER` | Text(10) | Recipient username (`*` = broadcast). |
| `NTY56RULE` | Text(20) | Name of the rule that fired the dispatch. |
| `NTMSGP` | Text(40) | Short subject / title. |
| `NTK74MSG2` | Text(1024) | Full message body. |
| `NTDOC` / `NTDCT` / `NTKCO` | mixed | Invoice triplet (FK → F564231 when populated). |
| `NTK74RSCD` | Text(10) | Status code that triggered the rule. |
| `NTK74MSG1` | Text(1024) | Status message. |
| `NTY56RSRC` / `NTY56RSRCL` | Text(50) / Text(250) | PA rejection reason code + label. |
| `NTY56ACTN` / `NTY56ACTNL` | Text(10) / Text(250) | Expected action code + label. |
| `NTEV01` | Text(1) | Read flag (`Y` / `N`). |
| `NTUPMJ` / `NTTDAY` | Date / Time | Creation timestamp. |

A daily sweep driven by `global.notificationsRetentionDays` (default 90, `0` = disabled) deletes rows older than the retention window.

### F564254 — Role permission grants (row-based RBAC)

Stores role grants as typed rows. One row per `(role, permission type, value)` triplet.

- **Primary key**: `(PMROLE, PMCRAPPID, PMCRAPPVAL)`
- **Notable**: An empty result set for a given `(role, type)` means *unrestricted* on that dimension. Adding a new permission dimension is an INSERT — not a DDL change. Drop + Init Database re-seeds the default grants without touching existing role rows.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PMROLE` | Text(36) | Role identifier (PK · FK → F564251.RLROLE). |
| `PMCRAPPID` | Text(30) | Permission type — `page` / `company` / `feature`. |
| `PMCRAPPVAL` | Text(175) | Value within the type — page id, company code, or feature name (`settings`, `readonly`, …). |
| `PMENABL` | Text(1) | `Y` = grant, `N` = explicit deny. |
| `PMUSER` / `PMPID` / `PMJOBN` / `PMUPMJ` / `PMTDAY` | — | Audit columns. |

Currently used `PMCRAPPID` values:

| Type | `PMCRAPPVAL` | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `page` | page id (e.g. `dashboard`, `invoices`) | Page allowed for the role. |
| `company` | company code (`KCO`) | Company allowed for the role. |
| `feature` | `settings` | Role can access the *Configuration* menus. |
| `feature` | `readonly` | Role is restricted to read-only (no edit / delete / resend). |

### F564255 — Password reset tokens

Backs the *Forgot password* flow. One row per emailed link. The token is a UUID embedded in the `/reset?token=…` URL; it is single-use and expires after ~60 minutes.

- **Primary key**: `PRTOK`
- **Notable**: `PRUSED = 'Y'` marks a consumed token — the row stays briefly for audit before sweep. A purge deletes expired tokens and consumed tokens past their audit window.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PRTOK` | Text(100) | UUID token embedded in the `/reset?token=…` link (PK). |
| `PRUSER` | Text(10) | Target user (FK → F564250.USUSER). |
| `PRSTDTIM` | Timestamp | Token issued-at. |
| `PRETDTIM` | Timestamp | Token expires-at (~60 min after issue). |
| `PRUSED` | Text(1) | `Y` once the token has been consumed; prevents replay. |

---

## Recommended indexes

The DDL bundles a small set of indexes that every production deployment should keep — they back the most common queries from the UI:

| Index | Table | Columns | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `F564231_STATUS_IX` | F564231 | `UHK74RSCD` | Dashboard counters and *E-Invoicing* status filters. |
| `F564231_DATE_IX` | F564231 | `UHK74LDDJ` | Date-range queries on the invoice list. |
| `F564231_CUST_IX` | F564231 | `UHAN8` | Customer-scoped views. |
| `F564230_UUID_IX` | F564230 | `FEUKIDSZ` | PA UUID look-up after import. |
| `F564260_PERIOD_IX` | F564260 | `RGKCO`, `RGY56BAR`, `RGEFDJ` | E-Reporting list filters. |
| `F564262_INV_IX` | F564262 | `RIDOC`, `RIDCT`, `RIKCO`, `RIY56BAR` | "In which report is this invoice?" lookup. |
| `F564250_ROLE_IX` | F564250 | `USROLE` | User → role join. |
| `F564252_USER_IX` | F564252 | `SSUSER` | Sign-out / list-sessions per user. |
| `F564252_EXP_IX` | F564252 | `SSETDTIM` | Expired-session pruning. |
| `F564253_USR_IX` | F564253 | `NTUSER`, `NTEV01`, `NTUPMJ DESC` | Bell badge + inbox sort. |
| `F564254_ROLE_IX` | F564254 | `PMROLE`, `PMCRAPPID` | Fast per-role grant resolution. |
| `F564255_USR_IX` | F564255 | `PRUSER` | Active tokens per user (abuse protection, invalidation). |
| `F564255_EXP_IX` | F564255 | `PRETDTIM` | Expired-token sweep. |

The full DDL — including dialect-aware variants for Oracle and PostgreSQL — ships in the JAR under `sql/oracle/ddl.sql` and `sql/postgres/ddl.sql`, and is materialised on disk by **Initialize Database**.

## NomaUBL — Developer Reference
Source: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/developer/

The NomaUBL Developer page — tables and columns, configuration keys, flows, impact analysis and the API of the instance — generated at build time from the database DDL, the configuration classes, the settings editors, the Java sources and the OpenAPI document.

The **Developer** page answers the questions of whoever maintains, extends or audits NomaUBL: *what is in this table, who writes this column, where is this setting edited and who reads it, which flows a status goes through, what this API returns*. Everything on the page is **generated when the application is built**, from the database DDL, the table and column configuration, the settings editors, the Java sources and the OpenAPI document — it always matches the release that runs.

Open it from **Documentation → Developer**.

---

## At a glance

---

## Tables

The data dictionary of the sixteen NomaUBL tables, grouped by flow — *Invoice lifecycle*, *E-reporting*, *Notifications*, *Security* — with a search over table names, columns, comments and BT codes.

- **The table card** gives the purpose and notes from the DDL, the primary key and indexes, the accessor and its configuration key, the name currently configured in the [NomaUBL database settings](../configuration/database-connectors/nomaubl.md) when the table is renamed (*Renamed to*), and the flows that write and read it. The invoice tables carry a clickable strip of the lifecycle across tables, from the archive to the processing log.
- **The columns grid** — column, override, type, description (inline and `COMMENT ON` of the DDL), BT code, accessor, configuration key, screens that show it, flows, write and read counts, nullable, default. A row opens the code references, writes first, grouped by flow: processing, import poll, status poll, received invoices, e-reporting, inbound, jobs, notifications, authentication, API, screens, database, command line. The grid is the shared data table; its view is listed in the [List views](../configuration/list-views.md) editor.

The complete reference of the tables is also published in [Database tables](./database-tables.md).

---

## Configuration

Every configuration key, with **where it is edited** and **who reads it**. The templates are listed on the left, grouped like the [Settings navigation](../configuration/settings-overview.md) — Global settings, Documents, PDF templates, API and SQL connectors, E-invoicing, E-reporting, Jobs & inbound… — with their key count and their gaps. The grid shows the keys of the selected template:

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| **Key** | The configuration key. |
| **Label** | The field label in the settings editor. |
| **Edited in** | Template, tab and group of the editor field. |
| **Read by** | The flows whose code reads the key. |
| **Call sites** | Number of Java reads. A row opens the editor field and the code. |
| **State** | *editable, read* · *editable, never read* · *read, not editable*. |
| **Templates** | Templates that carry the key. |
| **Hint** | The help text of the field. |

Two check boxes isolate the gaps, one at a time: **Read but not editable** (a key the code reads that no screen offers) and **Editable but never read** (a field that has no effect). Keys built at run time — `fetchAll.N.*`, `folder.N.*`, `filter.*` — are not literal in the code and show as editable only.

---

## Flows

One short page per flow: **process a file**, **import poll**, **status poll**, **e-reporting**, **watched folders**, **reprocess**. Each gives the trigger, the command-line switch, the log module, the tables touched, the statuses written, the settings read and the steps in order. Pick a flow on the left to read it.

---

## Impact

What a change reaches. The picker goes in steps:

1. the **kind** — *Column*, *Configuration key* or *Status*;
2. the **table** or the **template**;
3. the **item**, in a wide list that shows the label first.

The result lists the **flows**, the **screens**, the **API endpoints** and the **command-line switches** the item reaches, the editor field that exposes it, then the code. Endpoints come from a scan of the server routes down to their handler class; status codes and labels come from the [status catalogue](../configuration/system/statuses.md) of the instance.

---

## API

The API of the instance, read the way the other views are read:

- **tag groups and tags** on the left with their operation counts — Invoices & documents, Processing, Platforms, Operations, Administration, Developer;
- **one row per operation** in the shared data table: method, path, summary, tag, group, access (*public*, *any signed-in user*, or the action a role must grant);
- **a window per operation** with the description, the parameters and request and response samples built from the schemas, references resolved.

**Getting started** opens the introduction of the document (session and token, rights, responses, invoice key, dates, paging, background runs). **Open the public reference (Redoc)** opens the same document in Redoc, which also serves readers outside the application — see the [API reference](/nomaubl/api-reference/) of this site.

---

## Access

Grant **Developer** in the Documentation group on the [Roles](../configuration/security/roles.md) page. The page reads the files generated at build time and, for the *Renamed to* field, the table names of the current settings; it runs no query on the invoice tables.

---

## Tips & best practices

- **Check Impact before renaming a column or retiring a setting.** The flows and endpoints listed are what to retest.
- **Review the gaps of the Configuration view after an upgrade.** A key *editable, never read* is a field to clean up; a key *read, not editable* is a setting only reachable by editing the file.
- **Send the Flows pages to a new team member** before the code: they describe each chain in a page.

---

## 2026.11.26.1 — 2026-11-26 \{#v2026-11-26-1\}

### Improvements
- **Document window: change the transaction type, edit the UBL.** On the UBL tab, two actions for administrators. Change type sets another type (B2B, B2C…) on the invoice: only the type changes, in the UBL and in the lists, with no validation, status change or send. Edit UBL opens the UBL as text; saving validates it again as the invoice window does, and an invoice already processed by the platform is refused. Both need the new right "Edit UBL / change type" (role editor, Actions): a role with an action list does not have it until it is ticked.
- **Documents: activity and type by rule.** New Rules step on a document. A rule tests the document (JDE document type, company, amount, customer number, an element of the spool; on a UBL source, the seller, the buyer, the type code, the currency or any element of the UBL) and gives an activity, a type or both. Rules are read from top to bottom; with no match the document keeps the activity and type of its Identification step. "Try on the sample" shows which rule applies. Applied when the document is processed: a save from the invoice or document window never changes them. The processing rules (treat as another type, exclude) move to the same step.
- **PDF to XML: a page in steps.** The settings are grouped in steps shown as cards with their state (Source, Invoice, Company, Lines, VAT summary, Result); the selected step's settings sit beside the rows of the PDF and the XML. One "Save to document" button, with a mark when changes are pending. Settings and results are unchanged.
- **PDF to XML: result per invoice, PDF view.** The Result step lists each invoice of a text PDF (pages, lines, VAT rates, sum of the lines against the invoice total) and marks those with no lines or whose lines do not add up; a click shows the invoice in the XML. Beside the settings, the rows read from the PDF can be swapped for the PDF itself.
- **Connectors: editor in steps.** Connection, Authentication, Endpoints, Webhooks and Test are shown as cards with their state, and an endpoint is edited in four parts (what it is, inputs, the call, the answer). Same settings as before.
- **Documents: editor in steps.** A document is edited through cards in the order of a run (Source, Identification, Enrichment, Rules, UBL, Output, Advanced), each showing its state; steps that do not apply to the source are hidden. A PDF-source document has an "Open in PDF to XML" button. Same settings as before.
- **Notification rules, watched folders, action bindings, promotion: same look.** A notification rule and a watched folder are edited through cards showing their state; an action binding shows its button followed by its calls as a chain; Promotion opens on three cards (build a package, import a package, history). Same settings as before.
- **Settings: navigation as cards, sections as steps.** The entries of the Settings navigation are cards with an icon and a line saying what each holds. E-invoicing, e-reporting, directory lookup, SQL connectors and the two databases show their sections as cards across the top, like a connector. Same settings as before.
- **Fetch status, Extract and process, File versions: same look.** Fetch status opens on two cards (retrieve statuses, checks). Extract and process follows four steps (source, processing, extraction result, processing result) with one run button. In File versions, folders are headings and files are cards.
- **Text PDF: invoices printed with their business-term codes.** A layout that prints the code of each value ("Date d'échéance (BT-9)", "Total TVA (BT-110)") is now read by its labels: fields are named by the label, text values are kept (currency, invoice type, payment means), a code in parentheses at the end of a value also comes out on its own (380, EUR, 42, the scheme of an electronic address), and values printed on several rows are joined. A block heading such as "Vendeur" or "Client" is no longer taken as the party's name, and "CITY, FR" gives the city and the country. In a table, a text left-aligned under a centred header goes to its own column; a VAT summary whose header is on two rows is read.
- **Platforms with the AFNOR flow API.** A connector can now send the e-reporting file as a flow (`{{filePath}}` and `{{reportName}}` in a multipart body), and the list of received invoices reads the `flowId` of a flow search.

### Fixes
- **Document without an RTF template run with no processing type.** It now produces its UBL instead of failing on a PDF it cannot render ("PDF creation failed").
- **Invoice window: save refused after adding a reference.** On an invoice or credit note carrying a VAT point date code without invoicing period dates, adding a preceding invoice or an order reference no longer makes the save fail on the document structure (invoicing period out of place). A document already saved that way is corrected by opening it and saving again.
- **Text PDF: name printed on two rows.** In a table read by position, a value wrapped above and below its line (a long name) no longer makes the other stacked values of the invoice be read as section titles (session number and end date lost, wrong section).
- **Text PDF: table continued on the next page.** The footer of the page and the header of the next one are no longer read as invoice lines.
- **File versions: the editor stayed on the first file.** Choosing another file while one is open in the editor now shows the other file; unsaved changes are asked about first.
- **Text PDF: fields of the header printed again on the next page.** On an invoice of several pages, the header repeated on a following page no longer produces a second set of fields (ending in _2).

## 2026.11.25.1 — 2026-11-25 \{#v2026-11-25-1\}

### Improvements
- **List filters: include, exclude, empty, not empty.** In the Advanced Filters panel and in the table's column filters, a dropdown filter has an operator button: one of the selected values (as before), none of them, no value, any value. Exclude keeps the rows with no value. Saved views keep working.
- **Explorer: "not equals" on a coded field** (status, reason, type…) now also keeps the rows where the field is empty.
- **Buyer electronic address: SIREN by default, now optional.** UBL Defaults › Scheme IDs has a box "Use the SIREN when the buyer has no electronic address", ticked by default. Unticked, an invoice whose buyer has no address is produced without one and stops at validation (address mandatory).

### Fixes
- **Validation of very large invoices.** An invoice of several thousand lines no longer stays in validation without ending: a 10,000-line invoice is now validated in about 20 seconds. The findings are the same as before. E-reporting declarations get the same correction.
- **Processing rules: "XPath on the document".** The field now accepts a path (`Facture_Entete_S4/Type_document_ID80`); until now only a bare element name worked and a rule written with a path never matched. A path that finds nothing falls back on its last element name. An attachment path's `{…}` placeholders read a path the same way.

### Upgrade
- Run the upgrade so each environment receives the new stylesheets. Nothing changes until the box is unticked.

## 2026.11.23.1 — 2026-11-23 \{#v2026-11-23-1\}

### Improvements
- **Mapping: "different from" in a condition.** In the extension fields, item properties and notes (document and line), the `=` of a condition is a button that switches to `≠`: the row is emitted when the element matches none of the listed values. An absent or empty element counts as different; `≠` with no value means "element not empty".
- **Mapping: several conditions on a row.** `+` in the condition cell adds a condition, each with its own `=` / `≠`; the row is emitted when all of them hold. Two rows for the same element cover an "either case" rule.

### Upgrade
- Run the upgrade so each environment receives the new common stylesheet. Existing mappings are unchanged.

## 2026.11.21.1 — 2026-11-21 \{#v2026-11-21-1\}

### Improvements
- **Explorer: new page layout.** View, Period, Rows, Measures and Filters are one card each; the view is picked with icon buttons; the result is a panel whose heading says what the run returned. Save, Delete, Excel and PDF are in the page header.
- **Explorer: Definition button.** It hides the fields and the shelves so the result takes the whole page. A saved analysis opens on its result, a new one on its definition; with the definition hidden, the period stays on the View line.
- **Explorer: code or label.** A row on a coded field (status, reason, type…) chooses what it shows: code and label together as before, the label, the code, or two columns. The table, the pivot, the charts, the PDF and the Excel follow, and the choice is saved with the analysis. Scheduled reports keep code and label.
- **Explorer: Excel of an analysis.** The header's Excel button exports the result as shown, the cross table for a pivot.
- **Explorer: fields list.** Expand all / collapse all next to the search, and each field shows the name used in calculated fields.
- **Explorer dashboards: layout by hand.** In Edit layout a tile is moved by dragging its grip and sized by its corner; the arrow keys do the same.

## 2026.11.20.1 — 2026-11-20 \{#v2026-11-20-1\}

### Improvements
- **UBL Defaults: invoice lines carried as a document charge or allowance.** Rules in Allowances / charges name the source lines that are not invoice lines for the standard, such as a freight line: conditions on the line's fields, charge or allowance, reason code from the list or read from a field of the line. A matching line leaves the invoice lines and is added up per reason code and VAT rate as a document-level charge or allowance; the totals follow. The source and the PDF are unchanged. General rules, overridable per document. Requires the upgrade; without a rule nothing changes.
- **UBL Defaults, companies: scheme of the electronic address (BT-34).** A company can carry its own scheme next to its electronic address, for example 9940 with the VAT number for a company in Monaco. Left on the general scheme, nothing changes. Also available in a document's company override. Code 9940 (Monaco VAT number) is added to the scheme list. Takes effect once the UBL Defaults are saved.

### Fixes
- **UBL Defaults, VAT tab: exemption code by source code.** Changes to this mapping in the general defaults were not written to the file although the page answered Saved. They are now saved; the other VAT mappings were not affected.

## 2026.11.19.1 — 2026-11-19 \{#v2026-11-19-1\}

### New
- **NomaUBL in Claude Desktop and Claude Code (MCP).** Claude can question the instance under the user's own account: invoices and their history, validation errors, e-reporting, dashboards and period figures, server log, settings, documentation. Read-only; the user's companies and data scope apply. Off by default: Settings › Global › AI › MCP server. Requires a valid licence.
- **Data Explorer and setup review from Claude.** Claude can also run any Explorer aggregation (grouping, measures, filters, period, Top N) and the saved analyses, and review the setup: configuration objects, configuration check, scheduled jobs, rule sets, licence state. The Explorer tools need the Explorer page, the setup tools the Settings access; secrets are never shown.
- **Sample files for Claude.** A customer's XML or PDF can be given to Claude to work on: added in Profile › Sample files, or sent from Claude Desktop, which reads only the samples folder chosen in the extension settings. Claude then reads the structure of an XML or converts a PDF with a document's settings, trying table anchors without saving. Samples are working copies, never processed or sent, removed after 7 days.
- **Attach a file in the assistant.** The paperclip of the AI assistant attaches an XML or a PDF to a question; the assistant reads it with the message, and can convert a PDF with a document's settings or check a document's mapping on it, as Claude Desktop does. The file is kept with the user's sample files for 7 days.
- **Mapping work from Claude.** Auto-mapping from a sample, as in the mapping editor: send an XML or a PDF of an invoice, Claude proposes the mapping (and, for a text PDF, the extraction rules), checks it and reports what is missing. Claude also reads a document's saved mapping and the variables its rule set requires, then checks a mapping on a sample and shows the UBL it gives, with other values tried on top of the saved ones. The sample follows the steps of a real run: a PDF converted as a text PDF or a JD Edwards PDF according to the document, the pre-processing stylesheet, the burst into invoices, the sign inversion. Nothing is saved: Claude gives the values to enter in the mapping editor. Requires Settings access.
- **Changes from Claude, when allowed.** A new setting, Settings › Global › AI › MCP server › Allow changes over MCP (off by default), lets Claude, when the user asks, save an Explorer analysis, save mapping values in a document's stylesheet, save a document's PDF to XML settings, and create a document (by source: XML, PDF, UBL or connector, with its own blank stylesheet, or from an existing one) or update its settings. Each source keeps its own rules: text PDF settings are refused on a JD Edwards document and the reverse, and a UBL document has no mapping. Apart from the analysis, these need Settings access; passwords, tokens and keys cannot be set this way. The previous version stays in the file or configuration history, and every change is written to the server log with the user's name.
- **AI usage.** A new view of the Diagnostics page shows what the in-app assistant, the mapping auto-map and Claude (MCP) were used for: turns, users, tokens read and written with the share served from the cache, tool calls and failures, by user, day, channel, model and tool, and each turn with its tools. Kept: who, when, the model, the counters and each tool's name and input summary; never the question, the answer or what a tool returned. Granted per role as the AI usage view; kept 90 days unless set otherwise in Settings › Global › AI.
- **Sign-in from Claude without a token.** A client given only the address of the MCP endpoint (Claude Code, a claude.ai connector when the instance is reachable from the internet) opens the browser on NomaUBL: the user signs in as usual, password or SSO, and allows the client for 30, 90 or 365 days. The access appears with the user's tokens in the profile window and is revoked there. Behind a proxy, set Settings › Global › Authentication › Public address, the address also used by password reset links. In the list of tokens, such an access shows the name of the client it was allowed for. The pasted token and the Claude Desktop extension keep working.
- **Several instances in Claude Desktop.** The extension downloaded from an instance now carries its environment and address in its name (NomaUBL – prod · host), so the extensions of several instances install side by side instead of replacing one another, each with its own token. An extension installed before under the plain name NomaUBL is to be removed and installed again.
- **Role feature "MCP access".** Only the roles that have it can connect Claude; no role has it by default.
- **Personal tokens.** Profile › Claude (MCP): create a token (30, 90 or 365 days, shown once), list and revoke them. A password change or a disabled account ends them.
- **Claude Desktop extension.** Profile › Claude (MCP) › Extension downloads a file to open in Claude Desktop: the server address is already filled in, only the token is asked. Nothing else to install.

### Improvements

- **Assistant and Claude: companies and data scope.** The invoice list, the e-reporting list and the invoice file given by the AI assistant now keep to the user's companies and data scope, as the lists of the application do. The server log, the technical dashboard and the implementation report are given only to a role that has the matching page or Settings access; PDF to XML follows the processing page.
- **Tokens ended by an administrator.** A password set by an administrator, or the deactivation of an account, removes the user's Claude tokens, as the user's own password change already did.
- **Sample files tab.** The profile window lists the user's sample files in their own tab, for every user: a file attached in the assistant is found and deleted there. Old samples are removed every day, whether the user comes back or not.
- **Settings wording.** The System Prompt help says it replaces the built-in prompt; Custom Tools says it concerns the in-app assistant only. The MCP access role feature and the Claude Desktop extension's settings are in French for a French interface.
- **Values longer than a column no longer stop a run.** A text of the invoice longer than its column in the NomaUBL tables (a customer name over 40 characters, a long reference or message) is shortened to the column's size when it is written, instead of failing the insert; the UBL keeps the whole value. The size is the table's own, read from the database, so a column that was widened is used at its real size. Codes and keys (document type, company, status) are never shortened. The server log reports each column concerned once.
- **Integrity reports: BIP jobs.** A check that integrates BI Publisher jobs has a new setting, Extract (input, output or both), so its action fetches the same files as the scheduled fetch of those jobs; until now it always took the input. The "BIP jobs not integrated" query template also lists a job whose run ended on a failed insert, since no invoice was created. Checks already saved keep their query and extract the input unless changed.

## 2026.11.18.1 — 2026-11-18 \{#v2026-11-18-1\}

### Improvements
- **JD Edwards print queue: reports running in subsystem.** A report running in subsystem keeps the same job number until it is restarted, and each trigger adds an entry to the print queue under that number. The scheduled fetch now picks up every trigger, each as its own batch, instead of the first one only. The first batch of a job number keeps its usual name (`report_version_job`); the following ones add the entry's number (`report_version_job-entry`). The "after generation" action (remove or update the JD Edwards entry) applies to the entry just processed, not to the whole job number. Fetching by job number alone (manual extraction, command line) takes every entry of that number; `job-entry` takes one. The host must be scanned by completion date, which is the case after its first scheduled batch. The command-line batch scan still goes by job number and does not see later triggers. Nothing changes for a report that does not run in subsystem.

## 2026.11.16.1 — 2026-11-16 \{#v2026-11-16-1\}

### Improvements
- **PDF to XML: tables in several sections.** A new setting of a PDF document, "Rows ignored", names the rows inside the table that are not invoice lines, such as the subtotal closing each section. The table is then read to its end, each line carrying the title of its section, with "Table end" set on the row after the last section. The setting is in the document editor (PDF extraction) and on the PDF to XML page, where it can be tried before saving. Left blank, nothing changes.
- **Processing rules: "Treat as document type" also sets the invoice's transaction type.** An invoice matched by such a rule now carries the rule's type in its UBL, instead of the type read from the source: the transaction type column of the lists, the statistics, the type and the archive-only flag given to the platform, the public-sector checks and e-reporting all follow the rule. Until now the rule only changed the send, validation and output settings applied. Invoices already processed keep their type until they are reprocessed; a rule that moves B2C or international B2B invoices to another type takes them out of the e-reporting declaration.

## 2026.11.13.1 — 2026-11-13 \{#v2026-11-13-1\}

### Improvements
- **Menu that follows the window width.** On a small laptop or a tablet (window of 1100 px or less) the menu folds to its icons by itself and its bottom button opens it over the page, which keeps its full width. On a phone-width window the menu is hidden and opens from a button at the top left; choosing a page closes it. On a wide window nothing changes.
- **Top bar that no longer overlaps.** The language, theme, notifications, account and AI buttons sit at the right of the title row: on a narrow window the title shortens and the subtitle is hidden, and the buttons no longer cover it.
- **Lists on a small screen: the grid always stays visible.** On the invoice, document, e-reporting, integration error and processing log lists, the Advanced Filters panel now scrolls inside itself when the window is short, and the page scrolls if needed, so open filters no longer push the grid out of the screen. The period and quick filters go to a second line when they do not fit.
- **Dashboards on a narrow window.** Tiles and charts of the Synthèse, Statistics, Operations and Technical dashboards go down to one column without a horizontal scroll bar, with smaller margins.
- **Lists shown as cards on a phone-width screen.** Each row of a list becomes a card with one line per visible column, its title on the left and its value on the right; no more sideways scrolling. Columns, saved views, search and filters work as before; sorting by a column header remains a wide-window gesture.
- **Windows on a phone-width screen.** The invoice, document and e-reporting windows take the whole screen, with the title on one line and values that wrap between words; the other windows take the full width.
- **AI assistant and notifications on a narrow window.** The assistant opens over the page when there is no room beside it, and the notifications panel stays inside the window.
- **Upgrade: a database error no longer stops it.** A statement the database refuses (missing rights, a rule of the DBA) is now a warning: the configuration, the files and the stylesheets are upgraded all the same and the service starts. The console, the report and the Upgrade history page list each refused statement with the database's message, and a script `upgrade-<date>-schema-pending.sql`, in `upgrade-reports`, holds the statements to run with an account that has the rights. The next upgrade tries them again and skips what is already in place. Until then, the feature these statements serve is missing.
- **Upgrade: the service is started again in every case.** When the upgrade itself fails, `nomaubl.sh upgrade` now restarts the service that was running, shows the failure and still ends with the error code.
- **Database scripts without table and column comments.** The `COMMENT ON` statements are removed from the installation script and from the 2026.11.11 migration: they brought nothing to the application and could be refused on a JD Edwards database. An upgrade that stopped on them goes through on the next run.

## 2026.11.12.1 — 2026-11-12 \{#v2026-11-12-1\}

### Improvements
- **Launch script: environments in another folder.** `ENV_HOME` in `nomaubl.conf` names the folder that holds the environments, with their PID and log files; a relative path is taken from the script's folder. Unset, they stay next to the script, as before.
- **Launch script: one master key per environment.** In `JAVA_OPTS`, `%ENV%` stands for the environment given on the command line and `%ENV_HOME%` for the environments folder, e.g. `-Dnomaubl.master.key.file=%ENV_HOME%/%ENV%/.nomaubl/master.key`. A `JAVA_OPTS` without them behaves as before.
- **Licence expiry shown and announced.** Settings › Global › License shows what the saved key gives: customer, plan, expiry date and user limit, or why the key is refused. From 30 days before the expiry, a banner reminds the users who have the Settings page.
- **User limit of the licence.** A licence may set a maximum number of enabled accounts. Once it is reached, creating a user, enabling a disabled one and the automatic creation of an account at a first SSO sign-in are refused; accounts already enabled keep working. The users list shows the enabled accounts against the limit. A licence without a limit changes nothing.
- **Licence usage report as a scheduled job.** Once a day, the server sends the licence tool the number of invoices per month (issued and received), the number of enabled accounts, the environment name and the version, with the licence key; no invoice content and no user name. The send is the "Licence usage report" job of the Scheduled jobs page (kind System): its run history shows what each send carried and the answer received, a send that fails is shown as the run's error, and "Show data sent", in the job's window, displays the exact data. Run now and Pause work as for the other jobs. Without a licence key the job is off.

## 2026.11.11.1 — 2026-11-11 \{#v2026-11-11-1\}

### Improvements
- **Saved views on every list.** A view picker in the list toolbar saves the current display under a name and brings it back in one click: visible columns and their order, grouping, sort, rows per page, column filters and, on the lists that have them, the Advanced Filters and the period (with its date basis). "Standard" remains the layout set in Settings › List views.
- **A view to open the list on.** Each user can choose one of their views as the one a list opens on.
- **Relative periods in a view.** A view saved on "This month" or "Last month" follows the calendar; only a custom range keeps its dates.
- **Views follow the user.** They are kept in the database, so the same views are available from any browser and on every server of an environment.
- **Shared views.** A user whose role has the new "Share views" action can share one of their views with every user, and stop sharing it. The others find it under "Shared views" with its owner's name and can save their own copy; only the owner changes it. A role with a restricted action list does not have the action until it is ticked in the role editor.
- **Column widths on the lists.** Drag the right border of a column header to widen or narrow it. Widths are saved with the view; "Reset widths", in the Columns menu, returns to the widths set in Settings. Once a width is changed, the list scrolls sideways when its columns are wider than the screen.
- **Entry forms for the invoice editor.** In Settings, "Add entry form" defines a simpler editor (listed under Views & UI): for each section and field, shown, read-only or hidden, with an optional default value and a "required" tick; a Preview button opens the editor on the form. A hidden field keeps its value, so a simple form never loses data from a rich invoice.
- **Warning on a form that cannot produce a valid invoice.** The form editor lists the fields the default rule set requires that the form hides or locks without giving them a value.
- **Forms per role.** In the role editor (Actions tab), tick the forms a role may use and the one the editor opens on. With several forms, a picker appears in the editor's header. A role without any form keeps the complete editor: nothing changes until a form is granted.
- **Forms move by promotion.** Entry forms are a new kind on the Promotion page.
- **Upgrade.** Views need a new table, F564256: run `nomaubl.sh upgrade <env>`. Until then the lists work as before, without the picker.

### Fixes
- **Invoice editor: "+ Price" and "+ Delivery" on a line.** The two buttons now open their block; "+ Delivery" did nothing, and "+ Price" did nothing on a line without a unit price.
- **Invoice editor: labels without field codes.** The price, preceding invoice, buyer identifier and despatch advice labels no longer carry their BT / BG code.
- **Promotion to a target with a self-signed or internal certificate.** A promotion target has a new "Check the server certificate" option (Settings › Promotion targets), ticked by default; untick it when the push fails on the certificate. The error now says so.
