## 2026.11.10.1 — 2026-11-10 \{#v2026-11-10-1\}

### Improvements
- **Buyer agent: every field.** In the XSL Editor, the buyer agent now has its legal name, SIREN, VAT number, electronic address, role code, identifiers, full address and contact. The legal name, required in this block, takes the trading name when left empty, so existing documents need no change. Other environments need `nomaubl.sh upgrade <env>`.
- **Electronic address scheme set automatically for the agent and the payer.** As for the seller and the buyer, it takes the default scheme (0225); the payer's scheme field is removed from the XSL Editor.
- **Customer contact in the PDF.** The customer box now shows the contact name, phone and email when the invoice carries them, each with its own option in the PDF template. On a self-billing invoice, this is where the issuing company's contact appears.

### Fixes
- **No resend after a failed validation.** An invoice in "Validation failed" is no longer sent to the platform: the Resend button is hidden, "Resend selected" counts only the invoices that can be sent, and an automatic retry leaves those invoices aside. Correct the invoice or reprocess it in full first.
- **Resend hidden once the platform has processed the invoice.** In the invoice window, the button no longer appears on a status the platform has returned, where the send was refused anyway.

## 2026.11.08.1 — 2026-11-08 \{#v2026-11-08-1\}

### Improvements
- **Seller legal information (BT-33) as free text.** In UBL Defaults › Suppliers, each company has a "Legal information" field written as is in the invoice (legal form, capital, RCS, registration number…). A document can set its own through a new XSL Editor variable. Without text, the capital and APE wording stays as before. Other environments need `nomaubl.sh upgrade <env>`.
- **Order line number and customer order reference shown separately.** In a PDF template's line table, each has its own option.
- **PDF template options in plain words.** Option labels no longer carry field codes.

### Fixes
- **No more "Capital Euros" without an amount.** A company with neither legal text nor capital no longer gets this mention.
- **Long contract reference.** An invoice whose contract reference exceeds 20 characters was missing from the invoice list; it is now listed, with the reference shortened in the list only (the invoice keeps it in full).
- **Text PDF: values next to another column.** A value no longer includes the text printed further right on the same line, such as an address in a second column; that address now gives its own address block.
- **Text PDF: values over several lines.** A value that wraps onto the next lines (a training title, for example) is read in full.
- **Delivery identifier labelled after its type.** In the PDF delivery block, the identifier now shows its type (SIRET, GLN…) instead of "ID".
- **Order reference taken from a line.** When only the lines carry an order reference, it no longer appears as the invoice's order reference in the PDF, the invoice window and the database.

## 2026.11.06.1 — 2026-11-06 \{#v2026-11-06-1\}

### Improvements
- **PDF to XML page (Processing menu).** Choose a text PDF and read the XML it produces, with or without a document's settings, then download it.
- **Set a PDF's table by clicking its rows.** On that page, click the first and last header rows, then the first row after the lines: the settings are worked out, tried at once and saved to the document on request.
- **Table headers printed on several rows.** A new "Header rows" setting (document, PDF extraction) merges the header per column and places cells stacked on a line in their own column. Documents that don't set it convert as before.
- **AI Auto-Map: review before applying.** Each proposal shows its path, the value it holds in the sample and your current value, checked against the file. New paths are ticked; changes to existing values and paths not in the sample are not.
- **AI Auto-Map: better proposals.** It now reads sample values and format hints, so it picks the element holding exactly the expected data, and lists required fields still empty.
- **AI Auto-Map: extraction rules for PDF sources.** For values merged or missing in the XML, it proposes rules showing what they extract; they can be saved on the document, then the PDF is converted and mapped again.
- **Document key from the PDF to XML page.** Pick the invoice number element: a number such as 36834.FU is split into number and type, and saving sets these on the document with the company and a blank burst key.
- **VAT summary of a PDF.** A second table can be read into a repeating group, one line per rate, even with another block printed beside it; set it by clicking its rows on the PDF to XML page.
- **Input PDF embedded in the invoice.** On a PDF-source document, LISIBLE and Attachment have a new "source" choice that embeds the input PDF itself, as LISIBLE or PJA, instead of a rendered one.
- **Legal notes per company.** In UBL Defaults › Notes, and in a document's override, a company can have its own set of notes in place of the general ones; a company without its own shows the general notes. Other environments need `nomaubl.sh upgrade <env>` for this to apply.
- **JD Edwards PDFs on the PDF to XML page.** A JD Edwards tagged PDF can be converted there too, with a manifest or a starter one, and its burst key, document ID, type and company saved on the document.
- **New document from the PDF to XML page.** Creates a document for the converter in use, ready to receive the settings tried on the page.
- **JD Edwards reports with other sections.** A new invoice key (document setting, or picked on the page) writes one invoice per document number with the sections as printed, for reports that don't follow the standard layout. Documents without it convert as before.
- **Find the company from the invoice.** A document can find its company by VAT number, SIRET or SIREN in the supplier companies: from an element for PDF and XML sources, from the seller or buyer for UBL. No match stops the invoice. The PDF to XML page shows the company found.
- **Several invoices in one text PDF.** A new setting gives one document per invoice number, and the embedded source PDF holds only that invoice's pages.
- **JD Edwards PDFs on Process Document.** XML-source documents accept a PDF there, converted with the document's invoice key and the watched folder's manifest.

### Fixes
- **PDF attachments on file names with spaces.** Any attachment failed when the input file name held a space; it now works.
- **Values printed together in a text PDF.** A value followed by labelled parts (SIRET - VAT - NAF) and an IBAN followed by its BIC now also give separate elements. The first element keeps only its own value.
- **Status polling no longer fetches the last event again.** With the watermark set to "Last event", the newest event came back on every run until a newer one existed. A poll with nothing new now returns nothing.
- **AI Auto-Map errors.** The real error is shown instead of "no JSON", and an answer can no longer be damaged in transit.
- **PDF totals printed larger than their label.** A value printed slightly lower than its label, such as Total TTC, is now paired with it.

## 2026.11.05.1 — 2026-11-05 \{#v2026-11-05-1\}

### Improvements
- **Import status for several invoices in one request.** A new "Import group size" setting (Settings › E-invoicing › Status) sends up to that many invoices per request, for platforms that accept a list of ids (TX2: 10, with `{{uuids}}` in the endpoint body). An invoice absent from the response stays pending. At 1, the default, nothing changes.
- **Request limits per platform.** Two new connector settings, off by default: a minimum interval between requests and an error limit over 120 seconds. They apply to everything calling that platform from the server, sends, status polls and processing runs included. After a 429, requests wait and the refused one is retried once. Suggested for TX2: 300 ms and 20, on every connector calling it.

### Fixes
- **A connector body with a syntax error no longer stops the server.** A body that is not valid JSON, such as a misplaced quote or a stray bracket in an endpoint saved from Settings, is now kept as typed and the configuration stays readable. Before, it could make whole sections of the configuration disappear and prevent the next start.
- **Brackets in configuration values.** A value containing `[`, `]`, `{` or `}` is read correctly.
- **Clear error on a damaged configuration file.** A file edited by hand with a syntax error is refused at startup and during an upgrade, with the file, line and column, instead of running on a partial configuration. An instance whose file has such an error must have it corrected to start.

## 2026.11.04.1 — 2026-11-04 \{#v2026-11-04-1\}

### Improvements
- **Document-level allowances and charges (BG-20 / BG-21).** The variable mapping of a document gains a "Document Allowances/Charges" section: repeating element, allowance or charge indicator, reason code and text, amount, base, percentage, VAT rate and category. Each occurrence becomes an allowance or a charge on the invoice, and the totals (sum of lines, total allowances, total charges) follow. Templates in place get the new fields on upgrade, empty: nothing changes until they are mapped.
- **Allowance and charge reason codes.** Two new lists: allowance reasons (UNTDID 5189) and charge reasons (UNTDID 7161), in French and English. In the UBL defaults, the default code is picked from the list and fills the reason text; a source code can be mapped to a code of the list, globally or per document. When the source gives no reason text, the label of the code is used.

### Fixes
- **UBL validation keeps the file.** Validating an XML source no longer deletes the file from the input folder, whether it was uploaded or picked from the server.
- **Process document: file picked from the input folder.** A file chosen in the template's own input folder was emptied before processing; it is now processed as is.
- **Document charges total.** A charges total mapped alone (without charge lines) is now taken into account in the sum of lines, as the EN 16931 totals rule requires.

## 2026.10.30.1 — 2026-10-30 \{#v2026-10-30-1\}

### Improvements
- **Server settings outside the control script.** `nomaubl.sh` reads an optional `nomaubl.conf` placed next to it, for the settings proper to a server (Java options such as the memory or the master key location, the default port). The script itself no longer needs to be edited, so replacing it on an update keeps these settings.

### Fixes
- **PDF templates: setting the default no longer erases the global settings.** Choosing a default PDF template (or going back to the factory default) cleared every other global setting — database connection, schema, paths, scheduled batches. Only the default template is now changed. On an instance where it happened, restore `config.properties` from its version history (snapshot taken just before the change).

## 2026.10.29.1 — 2026-10-29 \{#v2026-10-29-1\}

### Fixes
- **Invert sign: price discount kept on credit notes.** On a credit note printed with negative prices, the gross price and the price discount (BT-148, BT-147) were dropped when they had to be derived from the net price, which French validation can reject; prices are now read as absolute values and both are emitted. A gross price or discount written with a decimal comma is read as well.
- **Invert sign "All documents": discount lines on invoices.** On an invoice whose spool prints every amount negative, the normal lines were turned into document discounts and the discount lines kept as invoice lines; the sign is now read after inversion, so only the discount lines become document discounts. "Credit notes only" and "No" are unchanged.

## 2026.10.27.1 — 2026-10-27 \{#v2026-10-27-1\}

### Improvements
- **Reprocess from the command line: shorter output.** `reprocess` now prints the start, each batch and the result, plus only the errors and warnings of the processing; `--verbose` prints every line as before. The web Reprocess screen still shows the full live log. `nomaubl.sh reprocess <env>` now accepts `--full` and `--verbose`.
- **Command-line script: every command available.** `nomaubl.sh` gains `fetch-received`, `send-waiting`, `status-integrity`, `status-order-check`, `purge`, `audit`, `report`, `techreport`, `validate-ddl` and `demo`, with their options; its help lists them, and `watch-folders`. The upgrade does not replace the script: copy the new `nomaubl.sh` next to the jar.

### Fixes
- **Reprint no longer fails on a UBL that cannot be rebuilt.** A reprint delivers the readable PDF and XML and keeps the archived UBL as the reference; when the UBL can no longer be regenerated from the source, this is now a warning, the invoice counts as reprinted and gets its reprocess marker. Before, it was counted as failed and stayed eligible, so the next run delivered its PDF and XML again.
- **Processing summary reflects invoices in error.** When an invoice of a file hits an error while the file itself goes through, the end of the run says how many invoices are in error instead of "completed successfully", and the batch summary counts the file "with invoice errors" instead of OK.
- **Oracle: "character set mismatch" with Exclude reviewed errors.** On databases whose invoice columns use the national character set, the dashboards, Statistics and the invoice list failed with ORA-12704 since the previous update whenever Exclude reviewed errors was on; they load again, with the same result.
- **Readable separators in command-line output.** The run, batch and reprocess lines use plain dashes and arrows, which no longer turn into odd characters in cron mails and log viewers.

## 2026.10.25.1 — 2026-10-25 \{#v2026-10-25-1\}

### Improvements
- **Explorer PDF: readable pivots.** In a PDF, each row level of a pivot gets its own column, group rows and the total are in bold, and a single measure no longer repeats its name in every column header.
- **Explorer: build your own analyses.** A new Explorer page, next to Reports, replaces the Requêteur tab. On the left, the fields of seven entities around the invoice (invoices, archived documents, lifecycle events, validation findings, invoice lines, VAT breakdown, notifications); drag or click them onto the Rows, Measures and Filters shelves, pick a period on any date, then run the analysis as a table, a pivot with totals, or detail rows. Dates group by day, week, month, quarter or year; measures are count, distinct count, sum, average, min and max, in real units; a filter on events or lines selects the invoices that have such a row. A result row or pivot cell opens the rows behind it, and a detail row opens the invoice. Analyses are saved and shared, one file each, promotable; the saved reports of the former query tool are converted automatically. Granted per role with the new Explorer page. Works unchanged on every supported database.
- **Explorer: charts.** An analysis can now be drawn as bars (vertical or horizontal, grouped or stacked), a line or area, a pie or donut, or KPI cards. The second row field gives the series, with the ten largest and the rest grouped as Others; dates read in order, other categories by size. Hovering shows the values, clicking a bar, point or slice opens the rows behind it, and the chart downloads as PNG. Switching between table, pivot and charts does not run the query again; the chart options are saved with the analysis. The toolbar keeps the entity, the views, Top and Run on one fixed row, the options of the current view on a second row.
- **Explorer: dashboards.** The Explorer gains a Dashboards mode: saved analyses become tiles on a four-column grid, each with its width and height, its chart, table or pivot, and one period at the top applied to every tile. A tile drills like its analysis and opens it in the editor; dashboards are saved and shared like analyses. Analyses and dashboards can be promoted to another instance, a dashboard bringing its analyses, and the implementation report lists them. A daily digest can send a saved analysis: it runs over the digest's window and arrives as a spreadsheet.
- **Explorer: calculated fields, richer pivot, ready-made analyses.** An analysis can define calculated fields with a small expression language — arithmetic on amounts, the age of an invoice or the days between two dates, conditions and choices such as `age(dueDate) > 30 ? 'late' : 'on time'` — tested on a few rows before use and usable as rows, measures or filters; it runs the same on every supported database. The pivot nests its row fields with collapsible subtotals and shows each cell's share of its parent or of the total. Twelve analyses and three dashboards come ready for IT (Operations), accounting (Month end) and audit (Audit period); they are installed once and never overwritten, so they can be adapted. One of them reproduces the status statistics of the Reports page, whose tab stays as it is. Every analysis has an option to exclude reviewed errors. The cross table and a whole dashboard export to Excel, the dashboard one sheet per tile; the saved analyses and dashboards are listed by audience and name. Saving opens a window with the name in the interface's language, who can see it (everyone or only me), Save and Save as — Save as is how a provided analysis or dashboard is copied and adapted. A coded field shows the labels of the list chosen for that column in Settings › List views (Invoices, E-Documents, Integration errors), so a short list for the transaction types applies to the Explorer as well. An analysis or a dashboard exports to PDF in the audit report's layout — cover page with environment, period, date, author and version, contents for a dashboard, running headers — with each chart and all its data, filters noted. In a calculated field, the fields and the functions are picked from lists and inserted at the cursor. A daily digest can send a saved analysis or a whole dashboard, as Excel (one sheet per tile) or as a PDF in the same layout, built on the server over the digest's window; the lists show the names and audience groups of the Explorer. Picking a saved analysis runs it at once with its own period, as a dashboard tile does.
- **Settings: Custom data.** The custom lists leave Reference data for an area of their own, Custom data, right after it in the Settings navigation.
- **API connectors: platform endpoints folded.** The "Endpoints NomaUBL uses" block of an API connector is collapsed by default, with a count of the endpoints configured, since it only concerns platform connectors.
- **Invoice types: complete list, invoice or credit note.** The invoice types list now holds every UNTDID 1001 code accepted by EN 16931, each marked Invoice or Credit note in a new Type column. That type decides whether a document is produced as a CreditNote and whether it counts negatively in the e-reporting B2C totals. On upgrade, an existing list receives the missing codes and its codes get their type, labels unchanged.
- **Payment means: complete list.** The payment means list now holds every UNTDID 4461 code, with French and English labels; an existing list receives the missing codes on upgrade.
- **VAT categories: Canary Islands and Ceuta / Melilla.** The VAT categories list gains L (Canary Islands general indirect tax, IGIC) and M (IPSI, Ceuta and Melilla); an existing list receives them on upgrade.
- **Units of measure: more codes.** The units list gains 24 common UN/ECE Rec 20 codes — area, length, weight, volume, energy, time, hundred and thousand, lot and packaging (bag, bale, box, carton, drum, jerrican, pallet, package, roll); an existing list receives the missing ones on upgrade.
- **JDE SQL connector.** A ready-made `jde-sql` connector comes with prebuilt queries for the JDE database, `getUDC`, the values of a user-defined code (product code and code type) as code and labels, for example to fill a custom list, and `updateInvoiceStatus`, which puts an invoice's receivable lines on pay status H and stops their dunning letters unless already paid, for example from an invoice action, and `getCompanies`, the JDE companies with their names. Set its connection, schema and control schema once; queries write the schemas as `{{schema}}` and `{{ctlSchema}}`, so the same query runs on every JDE environment. Every SQL connector gains the control schema field and both placeholders.
- **Upgrade: new connector endpoints and queries.** On upgrade, a shipped API or SQL connector already present on the instance receives the endpoints or queries it lacks, matched by name; its connection settings and its existing endpoints and queries are kept. The upgrade report lists what was added.
- **List views: value lists by default.** On a new installation, the Invoices, E-Documents, Integration errors and E-Reporting lists show labels for document types, companies, activity codes, processing categories, review, invoice types, countries and reason codes, picked from lists in their filters, with the same column names across pages (Party Number, Party Name); E-Documents also gains the status, document type, reason, due date, UBL number and template columns, with their filters. An instance that has saved its list views keeps them.
- **Custom lists filled from NomaUBL's own tables.** A custom list's sync source can now be the NomaUBL database: Sync now adds the activity codes, sub-types, document types, companies, business units or send-to-PA flags found in the archived documents, or the levels found in the validation findings, and keeps the labels already entered. New lists come ready: sub-types (refreshed this way, like activity codes), send to PA, validation levels, validation sources and the e-reporting direction (inbound purchases, outbound sales), the E-Reporting list's former Flux column now named Direction; the company list syncs from the JDE SQL connector. Validation rules get a built-in list, kept in step with the Schematrons, that shows each rule with its description in the columns, filters and Explorer of Integration errors and Diagnostics › Failures. E-Documents, Integration errors and Failures use these lists, and the company filter of Failures becomes a list.
- **E-reporting: generate by direction and company.** The Generate dialog chooses the direction — outbound (sales), inbound (purchases) or both — instead of the 10.1 / 10.3 flux chips, which had no effect since each report carries both flows; the company is picked from the companies list, blank for all configured companies. The unused Flux setting of the e-reporting settings is removed.
- **Company pickers.** The VAT declaration, the audit report, the archive source of Extract and process and the integrity check of status retrieval choose their company, or companies for the audit report, from the companies list (code and name), like the list filters; with the list still empty, the text field remains.
- **Processing log: filter by status.** In the grouped view, the processing log filters the runs by status: OK, error, or partial (start or end missing).
- **Diagnostics: kinds and severities as lists.** Failures picks its kinds (with their counts) and the server log its severities from a multi-select list instead of a row of checkboxes; nothing selected means all.
- **Explorer: findings per day, validation or integration.** The ready-made analysis of the Operations dashboard now splits each day's findings into validation (the invoice data broke a Schematron or XSD rule, customer packs included) and integration (a technical step failed: platform, database, transformation, PDF, XML, UBL generation, validator, processing), instead of one colour per Schematron pack; a copy left untouched is updated on upgrade.
- **Billing overview (Synthèse).** A new page right after the Dashboard, for accounting, sales and the board, speaks in amounts and labels, never status codes, with a Sales / Purchases switch next to the period. It is the page NomaUBL opens on (the Operations dashboard under a restricted licence), first in the menu, on this month by default. Four headline figures, each compared with the matching earlier period — this month to date with the same days of last month, a whole month with the previous month, a quarter with the previous quarter, this year to date with the same dates last year: revenue excl. VAT, net of credit notes (invoices and credit notes shown under it), VAT, the number of invoices and credit notes, and the transmission rate — the share of the amount transmitted, with how many invoices were issued and how many not yet (acceptance rate for purchases). Below: twelve months of amount split into transmitted, in progress, to correct, and refused or disputed; "What needs a decision", all dates, in amounts incl. VAT — one line per business status (refused, disputed, suspended…), rejected by the platform, to correct before sending — each opening the invoices concerned; the split per company and per transaction type (national B2B, international B2B, B2C); and for sales, per company the last e-reporting declaration and the next period due. The period picker carries the date basis (document date by default), and "Exclude reviewed errors", on by default, also applies to what needs a decision. Visible with the Dashboard access.
- **Billing overview: PDF export.** A PDF button on the Billing overview downloads the page in the audit report's layout: cover page with the period and the direction, key figures with the previous period and the change, the twelve-month chart stacked and coloured as on screen with its table, what needs a decision, and the splits per company, per transaction type and, for sales, e-reporting. In every PDF chart, round axis steps; in PDF tables, amounts line up on the right in both languages.
- **Invoices: status by stage.** The row of status chips and its "+N more" menu give way to five stages, as on the dashboards: to correct, decision needed, processing, at the platform, completed, each with its count. A click on a stage shows all its statuses; its arrow lists them with their counts to tick one or several, across stages. The counts follow the period, the direction and Exclude reviewed errors, like the list.
- **Statistics dashboard.** A new Statistics page, the fourth dashboard after the Billing overview, Operations and IT, shows where the invoices of the period stand, sales or purchases, on this month by default. Four headline figures compared with the previous period: invoices and their amount, the share that reached the platform, the invoices to handle, those open for more than 7 days. A bar of the five stages (to correct, decision needed, processing, at the platform, completed) with their counts and change; the period day by day, week by week or month by month by stage; the open invoices by waiting time; every status with its share and change; the most frequent reasons; the split per transaction type and per activity code; and the detail by activity code, status and reason with one column per transaction type, in number of invoices or amount excl. VAT, each line compared with the previous period, with its own Excel export. Each stage, status or bar opens the invoices concerned. Excel export (one sheet per block, with the data) and PDF in the audit report's layout. Visible with the Dashboard access.
- **Status statistics move to the Statistics dashboard.** The Status statistics tab leaves Reports: its table by activity code, status and reason, per transaction type, is now on the Statistics dashboard, with the comparison to the previous period and Excel and PDF exports. Reports opens on Integrity.
- **Default periods.** Every page with a period now opens on this month, unless the user has picked another one there. Settings › Views & UI › Default periods sets the period for every view and, if needed, a different one per view (Billing overview, Operations, Statistics, Invoices, E-Documents, Diagnostics, Integration errors, Processing log, Reports). The Explorer's analyses and dashboards keep their own period.
- **List views settings grouped.** Settings › List views groups the lists by where they appear — e-invoicing, diagnostics, jobs, documentation and administration — sorted by name, and a list without an override is marked default. Opening it no longer highlights NomaUBL database in the settings menu.
- **Implementation and technical reports brought up to date.** The implementation report lists every page as it is today — Billing overview, Operations, IT dashboard, Statistics, Explorer, Schematrons — and gains a section on dashboards, lists and exports: sales or purchases, the comparison period, the five stages, Exclude reviewed errors, exports with labels, list views and the instance's default periods. The technical report describes the dashboard and analysis layer and the shared interface (lists, period picker, status stages).
- **Reports redesigned.** The Reports page opens on four cards — Integrity, Audit, Implementation, Technical — each saying what it is for. The audit, implementation and technical reports share one layout: settings on the left (the audit period with the shared period picker, last month by default, date basis inside it; direction, language and companies as switches), the contents on the right as tiles with a line on what each section holds, All / None, and a bar with PDF, Markdown, the progress and the result. Integrity lists its checks with their description, mode and connector, runs over a period and shows the outcome as a banner — no anomaly or the count, with source and target counts and duration — above the grid; the SQL folds away.
- **Diagnostics: views as cards.** The four views of Diagnostics — Integration errors, Processing log, Failures, Server log — are picked from a row of compact cards under the header, each saying what it shows, instead of the switch at the top right; only the views the role grants are shown.
- **Explorer: Analyses and Dashboards as tabs.** The switch at the top right gives way to two tabs on the first row of the Explorer, Analyses and Dashboards, each with the number saved; the picker of saved analyses or dashboards and Save sit on the same row, at the right.
- **VAT declaration redesigned.** Three headline figures open the page — VAT collected, VAT deductible and VAT due (or VAT credit), each with its base, its number of invoices and the change from the previous month or quarter. One filter bar as on the dashboards: Month / Quarter, year, month or quarter, company, the two exclusions as switches with their explanation on hover, Excel and PDF. The table reads by direction, then by country group, then by rate: Sales and Purchases carry their totals on their line, France, intra-EU and outside the EU appear once with their subtotal, each rate below them; amounts are in the normal colour and open the invoices on hover. The net VAT is no longer shown in red. The period labels are translated. In the CA3 PDF, amounts are written 125 315,78, rates 5,5 % and the period 01/09/2026 – 30/09/2026.
- **Synthèse and Statistics: permissions of their own.** The two business dashboards no longer follow the Operations dashboard permission: each has its own page in the roles (Synthèse, Statistics), also checked by the server and the AI assistant's tools. On upgrade, every role that had the Operations dashboard receives both, once, so nobody loses a page; removing them from a role afterwards is kept. A role without the Synthèse opens on the first page it grants.
- **Role row filters on document columns.** A role restricted on a column of the archived document — activity code, business unit, sub-type, source file, job, program, routing… — or on the direction saw empty dashboards, status counts and Synthèse, and could not open its own invoices from the list. These filters now apply everywhere as they do in the invoice list.
- **Role row filters across lists.** A row filter now applies to every list that has the field, under the name that list gives it (customer, activity code, job, UBL number, status…), and is ignored on a list that has no such field: a role restricted to FATAL severity keeps its invoices, documents and dashboards instead of seeing nothing. An E-Documents window opens under the same rules as its list.
- **Roles: row filters by table, dashboard cards removed.** The row-filter picker lists each field once, by scope: the keys doc, dct and kco, which secure every table that has them; the fields of the archived document (F564230), which secure every table linked to it; then the fields of each other table (invoice, validation findings, processing log, e-reporting), which secure that table. The per-card permissions of the Operations dashboard are gone: a role sees the dashboard or not; card grants already stored are ignored and dropped when the role is next saved. The "Contract" column of the integration errors is the customer's alpha key, as on the invoice list.
- **New invoice on E-Invoicing.** Creating an invoice moves to a New invoice button on the E-Invoicing list (with the invoice.create permission). The Quick actions block of the Operations dashboard is removed.
- **VAT declaration: no drill-down.** The amounts no longer open the invoice list, which could not reproduce the rate and the exclusions; each rate still unfolds into its transaction types and invoices. Amounts follow the interface language.
- **IT dashboard translated.** The title, the description and every card of the IT dashboard are translated.
- **Roles editor translated; wording aligned.** The roles editor — tabs, features, actions with their help, data scope, messages — is translated. The Explorer's switch reads "Exclude handled errors" in French like everywhere else, the English menu says IT dashboard, the VAT declaration's description no longer mentions opening the invoices, and the daily digest hides "Send even when the period has no errors" for the Synthèse and the Statistics, which are always sent.
- **Refresh on the business dashboards.** The Billing overview and the Statistics get a refresh button next to their filters, as on Operations.
- **Stylesheet errors explained.** When a UBL or post-transform stylesheet does not compile, the error recorded on the invoice now gives Saxon's reasons — file, line and message — instead of only "Errors were reported during stylesheet compilation".
- **Notifications fired again.** Since the Explorer's "Reviewed error" field, every status change logged "NOTIFY : maybeFire" and no notification rule fired; rules are evaluated again.
- **Upgrade: customised UBL defaults kept compiling.** When an instance's ubl-defaults.xsl holds its own version of a framework template (the seller party, for example), the upgrade now adds the parameters the new framework passes to it — with their shipped defaults, the template's body untouched — as it already did for the per-document stylesheets; the upgrade report still lists the template, whose customised body ignores the new values until it is updated from ubl-defaults.xsl.upstream. Until now such an instance stopped producing UBL after the upgrade ("Parameter … is not declared in the called template").
- **Daily digest: the business dashboards.** A digest can send the Synthèse or the Statistics, as PDF (the page's figures, charts and tables) or Excel, over last month, the month to date or the digest window, for sales or purchases. It can be built as a role sees it — its companies and row filters — so each recipient group receives only its scope. Any digest can be sent on one day of the month only (for example on the 1st, last month's overview); Send now ignores it.
- **Invoice types: enable or disable.** In Settings › Invoice types, each code has an Active box. An unticked code stays in the list — its labels still show on existing invoices and its invoice / credit note kind still applies — but it is no longer offered in the pickers (UBL defaults, invoice form, list and Explorer filters). A new installation offers the 16 codes of French e-invoicing (380, 381, 384, 386, 389, 393, 396, 261, 262, 471, 472, 473, 500 to 503); an upgrade leaves the existing list as it is.
- **Exclude reviewed errors: invoices without a review mark kept.** An invoice in error whose review mark was empty (an invoice written without it) disappeared from the error counts and lists as if reviewed; only an invoice marked reviewed is left out now.
- **API: form creation route removed.** POST /api/invoices answered success without creating anything; it is removed. Invoices are created with POST /api/invoices/create-ubl (a UBL document) or POST /api/process (a source file through a document's mapping).
- **Desktop app.** NomaUBL can be installed as a desktop application on Windows and macOS from Chrome or Edge (Install button in the address bar) or Safari (File › Add to Dock): its own window and icon, no browser bars, always the server's version. Each environment installs as its own app, named after it ("NomaUBL · TEST"). Requires the server to be reached over HTTPS. The application icon shows the full NomaUBL logo.
- **List views: Reset to defaults in one click.** The button now shows the shipped columns at once; saving keeps them. It used to show the customised columns again until a second click.
- **Invoices: mark errors as reviewed.** Customer service can mark invoices in error as reviewed: from the invoice list (select them, then Mark reviewed) or from the invoice window, where a "Reviewed" chip at the right of the tabs sets or clears it; each time after a confirmation. A reviewed invoice keeps its status and is left out of the error counts while "Exclude reviewed errors" is on. New permission "Mark reviewed", given on upgrade to the roles that can edit invoices or push a status in the database.
- **Invoices: Send to PA column.** The default invoice list shows whether each invoice is meant for the platform (for the platform, not for the platform, held for review before sending), with its labels and a filter on the list, instead of the status note. A list view already customised keeps its columns.
- **Navigation: auto collapse.** Settings › Navigation & lists can fold the navigation to its icons: the pages get the width, and hovering the icons opens the menu over the page; picking a page folds it back.
- **Promotion: a document's files on their own.** Each file a document uses (transform, XSL, RTF, UBL stylesheet, customer Schematron, PDF layout) is listed among the files, with the documents using it, and can be promoted alone — a stylesheet shared by several documents no longer requires promoting a document.
- **Processing log: processing and scheduled jobs apart.** A switch Processing / Scheduled jobs / All sits next to Grouped / Flat; the log opens on Processing, so the runs of the status and import polls (every few minutes) no longer bury the file processing. A job run opened from Failures lands on Scheduled jobs. Their retention is already separate: Settings › Job defaults › Retention, "Job runs (days)".
- **Start page.** Settings › Navigation & lists chooses the page shown after sign-in (Billing overview unless set): a dashboard, Invoices, E-Documents, E-reporting, VAT declaration, Diagnostics, Reports or the Explorer. A user whose role does not grant it opens the Billing overview, else the first page the role grants.
- **Dashboards: cached figures.** The Billing overview, Statistics and Operations dashboards keep the figures they loaded, so coming back to them or changing page no longer queries again; an open dashboard reloads on its own after the delay, and Refresh reloads at once. On the IT dashboard, only documents processed per day is kept, on the server for every user. Each shows when its figures were loaded; signing out or an expired session empties the cache. Delay in Settings › Navigation & lists (60 minutes unless set, 0 = always reload).
- **Reviewed errors left out by default.** The Operations dashboard and the invoice list open with "Exclude reviewed errors" on, like the Billing overview and Statistics; a link from a dashboard keeps its own choice.
- **Billing overview: transmission rate over the invoices to send.** The transmission rate, its issued / not issued split and the per-company share count only the invoices meant for the platform (sent, or held for review); invoices of document types not sent to the platform no longer lower it. The "Reached the platform" rate of the Statistics dashboard follows the same rule, and so does the daily digest.
- **Portal notifications without a recipient go to everyone.** With sign-in enabled, a rule on the portal channel with no user or role recorded nothing; it now writes one entry visible in every inbox, as without sign-in. The rule editor names this choice "Everyone".
- **Notifications from the status poll.** A scheduled status poll waits for the notifications it triggered before exiting (they were cut after two seconds), and a settings change on a running server lets the queued ones finish.
- **Lists: rows per page and rows loaded by default.** Settings › Navigation & lists sets, for every list, the rows per page (50 unless set) and the rows loaded per refresh (100 000 unless set, instead of 5 000); a list view of Settings › List views can still set its own. The E-reporting list is no longer limited to 200 declarations.
- **List filters: pick or type.** The filters on a coded column — advanced filters, column filters and the Explorer — still offer the list's values, and also accept codes typed in the search box (Enter, comma-separated for several), so a list that is incomplete or still empty (for example a custom list of document types or sub-types) still filters.
- **Mapping check: invoice type code.** A blank BT-3 mapping is no longer reported as missing: the code comes from the UBL defaults (invoice-type rules, then the default code), like the other fields filled by the defaults.
- **Diagnostics › Failures: fast with "Unresolved only".** Whether a failed file was processed successfully later is now worked out in one pass over the processing log instead of one pass per failure.
- **Statistics: fast on large archives.** The page no longer reads the whole document archive: the activity code is fetched for the invoices of the period only, so it loads quickly where the archive holds millions of documents.
- **PDF: wide tables.** Columns size to their content without crushing the text: a column never gets narrower than its header's longest word or its longest word, a number or a percentage never splits (a value with its share breaks only at the dot), and a table too wide for the page switches to a smaller font instead of breaking words.
- **PDF: euro sign in italic notes.** In the notes under a section title, the euro sign no longer runs into the following word.
- **AI assistant: new pages and two tools.** The assistant knows the Billing overview, Statistics, Explorer and the invoice stages, and reads the figures of the two business dashboards: billing_overview (revenue, VAT, credit notes, transmission rate, decisions, per company and per transaction type, compared with the previous period) and status_statistics (invoices by stage, statuses, reasons, waiting time, activity × status × reason with the previous period). Since it reads the implementation report, it also knows the default periods and the dashboard rules of the instance.
- **List exports carry the labels.** In every list, the CSV and Excel exports of a column backed by a value list (company, document type, activity code, reason…) now write the code with its label, as on screen, instead of the code alone.
- **Operations dashboard reorganised, IT dashboard reorganised.** The former Dashboard is now named Operations, opens on this month and is organised around what the team has to handle, with the same header as the other pages and the same Sales / Purchases switch as the Synthèse, which every widget follows. Under a one-line summary of the period, three work queues — in progress (followed automatically), to correct and send again (IT), a new invoice to issue (customer service) — each show their total and their breakdown by status, label first with the code as a small tag; every number opens the invoices concerned. Then one activity chart whose legend carries the period's counts (replacing the separate pipeline bar), grouped by week beyond two months and by month beyond a year; the invoices blocked the longest and the latest events side by side, in plain words; and a row with the most-failing rules, the platform delay and e-reporting. The per-company chart moves to the Synthèse. The IT dashboard is reorganised the same way: a health strip of six tiles (application, database, scheduler, disk, memory, configuration — green, orange or red, each opening its detail), the four action cards (send failures, held for review, to reprocess, to reprocess in full) in one row, their figures aligned, one card for the last 14 days with tabs — documents processed per day with those now in a technical error (a bar opens that day's invoices), errors, retries, time per document — what is running right now (processes, live events, scheduler, sessions), the recent errors, and the technical details (system, filesystem, JVM, configuration check, database tables, links) folded at the bottom; nothing is removed.
- **New period picker.** Every page's period is now one button showing the range itself ("1 – 30 Sep 2026"). It opens a panel with the presets as a list — today, yesterday, last 7 and 30 days, this month, last month, this quarter, this year, last 12 months, all — a two-month calendar to pick any range, and, where the page has one, the date it applies to (activity, document or archive date), which used to sit in separate buttons on the dashboard, invoices, e-documents and status statistics. Next to it, "Exclude reviewed errors" is the same on every page — a switch framed like the period button, lit when on — on the dashboard, invoices, status statistics and the Explorer. "Yesterday" still covers yesterday and today, so a night batch running across midnight shows whole, and "Last year" is named "Last 12 months", which is what it covers.
- **Lighter web interface.** Each page is now loaded when it is first opened instead of with the application, and the large libraries and the translations are separate files the browser keeps between releases: the first load is lighter and the build reports no warning.
- **Schematrons page.** A new Schematrons page, under Documentation after Business Rules, shows the rules of one Schematron at a time: those shipped with NomaUBL (EN 16931, CIUS-FR flux 2, extended CTC, Chorus Pro, NomaUBL, e-reporting flux 10) with their version, and the customer packs named by the document templates, with the templates using them. Each rule is a row — code, severity, description, context — that can be searched, filtered and exported, and opens on its test and message. Visible with the Business Rules access.
- **Integration errors: activity code.** The integration errors list shows and filters the activity code, with its labels.
- **Promotion: promote from the selection.** Promote to an instance moves under Export, next to the package download: pick the target and press Promote…; the selection is checked on the target and a window shows what would change there (new, changed, identical, each with its field diff), with the policy and the comment; Promote writes and the same window shows the result. The separate Promote tab is gone.
- **Shared checkboxes everywhere.** Notification rules, actions, users, enrichment, the PDF designer, file versions, status retrieval, integration errors, the buyer fix and the row selection of every table use the application's checkbox instead of the browser's.

### Fixes
- **Grouped tables: checkbox stays first.** When a table is grouped, the selection checkbox stays in the first column instead of moving after the grouped column, and a group's label and count are no longer cut by the column width.
- **Explorer: New clears the page.** Choosing New analysis or New dashboard while one is open now starts from an empty one instead of keeping the previous content.
- **Transaction types in English.** The document-types list carries only French labels; English screens, PDFs and spreadsheets showed its send flag (1, 0) instead. The French label now serves both languages.
- **E-reporting: consolidated credit notes.** A 262 credit note (consolidated credit note) now counts negatively in the B2C totals, like the other credit notes.
- **Line amount warning (BR-NOMAUBL-02) reworded.** The warning now opens with the rule itself — the line net amount must equal the unit price divided by the base quantity, times the quantity, less line allowances plus line charges — then gives the line, the declared and the computed amounts; its description in the integration errors and the Schematrons page is that rule instead of a raw piece of the Schematron.
- **Explorer charts: legend for a single series.** A chart split by a field (Series) now shows its legend even when the period holds only one value of that field, so a single bar still says what it counts.
- **Clicking outside a dropdown only closes it.** Closing the period picker or a dropdown by clicking elsewhere no longer also triggers what was clicked, such as opening the invoice of a table row.
- **Chart tooltips on one line.** A chart's tooltip keeps each label and value on one line and opens on the side of the pointer with room, instead of wrapping against the chart's edge.
- **Explorer pivot: aligned values with shares.** When a pivot shows each value with its share, the values now line up down the column whatever the width of the percentage ("6.2 %" or "100.0 %").
- **Custom lists: wider code column.** The code column of a custom list is wide enough for longer codes.
- **Dropdowns show "All".** A dropdown left on its "all" choice (All sources, All templates, All companies…) now shows it instead of an empty field.

## 2026.10.24.1 — 2026-10-24 \{#v2026-10-24-1\}

### Improvements

- **Diagnostics: one page for errors and logs.** Integration Errors, Processing Log and Server Log leave the menu and become views of a single Diagnostics page, next to a new Failures view. The switcher reads Integration errors, Processing log, Failures, Server log; each view appears only when the role grants its former page, and the dashboard links that opened the old pages land on the right view with the same filters. Integration errors opens by rule by default, and every dated view starts on yesterday. The by-rule grid no longer flickers on scroll or hover with many rules: the cards dropped their background blur and off-screen cards are skipped by the browser; the cards also stay in place while a new period loads, and the first load no longer races the period filter.
- **Failures: every failure in one list.** The Failures view lists, with one shape, the validation findings, the PA rejections, the send and import failures, the processing failures per file and the failed job runs: when, kind, source (invoice number, file or job), template, company, current status, level, rule, message. Unresolved only by default, which hides failures the invoice, file or job has moved past (status left the error statuses, a later successful run). Filters on period, kinds with their counts, template and company; the message search runs on the server across every page. A row opens the invoice window, the processing log narrowed to the file, or the scheduled jobs. Export as on every grid.
- **Every job run is recorded.** Each run of a scheduled job, fired by the schedule or by Run now, writes a start row and an end or error row in the runtime processing log, with its duration and a one-line outcome; the same for the command-line job switches. The Scheduled jobs page shows the last runs of a job behind a History action, and keeps its last-run column across restarts. The run id appears in the server log lines of that run, so the two can be joined.
- **Retention purge.** A daily job can bound the stores that nothing bounded: processing rows, step timings and job runs of the runtime log, validation errors of invoices in a terminal status, notifications. Days per store are set in Settings → Job defaults → Retention or in the job's editor; the job is off by default except the notifications, which keep their 90 days, so an upgrade deletes nothing by itself. A "Count only" button in the job editor and `nomaubl.sh purge --dry-run` report what each store would lose before anything is deleted.
- **Developer reference: configuration, flows, impact.** The Data dictionary page becomes Developer, with four views. Tables is the dictionary. Configuration lists every configuration key with where it is edited (template, tab, group, label, hint), the flows that read it and its call sites, generated by a build-time join of the settings editors' fields with every property read in the Java code, helpers and constants included; two toggles isolate the keys read but not editable and the keys editable but never read, and a row opens the editor fields and the code. Flows gives one short page per flow — process a file, import poll, status poll, e-reporting, watched folders, reprocess — with trigger, command-line switch, log module, tables, statuses, settings and steps, bundled from the docs folder. Impact takes a column, a configuration key or a status and shows the flows, screens, API endpoints and command-line switches it reaches, the editor that exposes it, then the code; endpoints come from a scan of the server routes down to their handler class, status codes and labels from the catalogue of the instance. The build also renders the three parts as one Markdown file for the docs site, next to the API reference.
- **Developer: API view and guided impact picker.** A fifth view shows the API of the instance the way the other views are read: tag groups and tags with their counts on the left, one row per operation in the shared data table (method, path, summary, tag, access), and a window with the description, the parameters and request and response samples built from the schemas with their references resolved, as Redoc shows them. A Getting started button opens the introduction; the public Redoc page stays reachable from the view and for readers outside the application. The Impact picker is now in steps — the kind (column, configuration key, status), then the table or template, then the item in a wide list that reads the label first — instead of one mixed list.
- **Promotion: move items, not files.** A new Promotion page under Management, next to File Versions, promotes configuration items between instances with the ZIP as transport only. Export: tick document templates, PDF templates and reference or custom lists in a tree by kind; a template carries the files it references (pre-processing and indexation XSL, RTF, UBL XSLT and its PDF companion, custom Schematron) and the PDF template it names, shown under it and added automatically. The package holds a manifest (items, checksums, source instance and release, author, date), one fragment per item and the files with paths relative to the environment root, so the path placeholders stay valid on the target. Passwords, secrets, tokens, API keys, the license, the environment name and colour and the watermarks never travel. Import: a preview first, one row per item and per file — new, changed, identical, skipped — with the field diff of a changed template, target against package; then apply with a policy, replace or keep the target for changed ones, and a comment. Each template is upserted by name into its own configuration file, the other templates of that file untouched; each file is written after a version snapshot; instance keys already present keep their values; the import is one entry of the versioning log with its author. The package mode of File Versions stays for raw files. Other kinds (notification rules, digests, retries, checks, integrity checks, connectors, settings) come next.
- **Developer: Configuration view reorganised.** The templates are listed on the left with their key counts and gaps, grouped like the Settings navigation; the grid shows the keys of the selected template with their label, where they are edited, who reads them and their state. The build-time scan only keeps real configuration keys, so stray words from the code no longer appear.
- **Promotion: every kind.** The Promotion page now covers notification rules, daily digests, auto-retries, lifecycle checks, connectors (API, SQL, database, FTP), the settings templates (e-invoicing, e-reporting, e-directory, watched folders, integrity checks, reports, JDE print queue) and the shared UBL defaults file, next to the document templates, PDF templates and lists. Instance keys never travel and, when already present on the target, keep their values: passwords, secrets, tokens, API keys, the license, URLs, hosts, users, the database schema, the environment name and colour, the watermarks. Promoting the e-invoicing settings from test to production thus carries the behaviour, the document types and the actions, not the platform account. Global and single sign-on never travel.
- **Roles: grants that read like the menu.** The page grants of a role are shown as cards, one per sidebar group, in the menu's order and names, with a count and an all / none link; each page is a toggle chip, its id and description in the tooltip. Diagnostics appears once with its four view grants under it, each still granted on its own, so existing roles keep working. Dashboard cards and action groups use the same cards. The server's admin page list, which seeds the admin role on a fresh install, gains VAT declaration, Reports and Upgrade history, and the sidebar shows Diagnostics to a role that holds any of its view grants.
- **Implementation report.** Reports gains an Implementation report tab that generates the technical and functional documentation of the instance from its configuration files and database, in French or English, as Markdown or PDF; a copy is kept under the environment's reports folder, and the command line has the same with `report <env>`. Sections: context, architecture (the flows enabled, polls, batches, connectors), a functional guide (what every page is for, the invoice lifecycle, the protection of deposited invoices, edit / fix / resend rules with their permissions, reprocess, status poll with the integrity and ordering checks, review and notifications, a light reference of the platform statuses and of the internal stages), the documents with their files, index fields, pre-transform and UBL sheet references and the PDF templates, the UBL transform (shared defaults, issuing companies, mapping tables and rules, validation packs with their rule counts, coverage per document, one subsection per pre-transform and per UBL sheet with the source field to BT mapping and the overrides), platform settings and document types, operations (scheduled jobs, watched folders, notification rules and invoice actions in detail, integrity checks, connectors), security (roles and users), reference data (status catalogue and every list), and optional appendices (configuration keys, API reference). Secrets and instance keys are masked; technical keys are an option. The PDF has a cover, a clickable table of contents and outline, running header and footer, placeholder chips in paths, and section links.
- **Wording.** Document templates are now called documents throughout, and the French interface and notes say « modèle » rather than « gabarit ».
- **Audit report.** Reports gains an Audit report tab: the electronic invoicing of a period, from the NomaUBL tables only, as Markdown or PDF with the same cover, contents and layout as the implementation report; the command line has `audit <env>`. Period (previous month by default), date basis (issue date or last update), companies, direction and sections are chosen on the tab; the signed-in user's company visibility applies. Sections: scope; executive summary with the previous period of the same length and the variation (processed, deposited, approved, refused, rejected, in error, pending, excluded, received, deposited amounts, first-pass validation rate, terminal share, delays from creation to deposit and from deposit to the first buyer status) followed by the findings in words; volumes per month, company, document, transaction type and VAT category; the situation at generation time by status and family with the stale pending and unreviewed errors; the errors and their handling (findings per rule and source, rejections and refusals per reason, send and import failures, resolved / reviewed / open by age, resends and reprocesses). No invoice lists, so the report stays short whatever the volume. The report runs as a background job with a progress bar naming the current step; each step's duration is written to the server log.
- **Implementation report wording.** The French text says « règles spécifiques » for the NomaUBL rule pack.
- **Audit report: lifecycle and consistency checks.** Two sections join the audit report. Lifecycle and delays: the invoices reaching each milestone per month (created, validated, failed, sent, deposited, received, approved, refused, rejected, paid) and the delays from creation to first send, first send to deposit, creation to deposit and deposit to first buyer status, as median and 90th percentile. Consistency checks: invoices in a platform status without a platform identifier, sent invoices without an archived UBL, stale pending, duplicate invoice numbers within a company, VAT total against the stored breakdown, net total against the stored lines, refusals and rejections without follow-up; an option adds the configured SQL integrity checks against JDE with their discrepancy counts. The executive summary and the status section count the invoices deposited but not transmitted (200 with reason NON_TRANSMISE) and explain that the recipient is not registered with any platform. The status table is sorted by code.
- **Audit report: operations, activity, evolution and charts.** An Operations section lists the scheduled job runs with errors and durations, the files processed per mode and document, the portal notifications per rule and the e-reporting envelopes per status. Volumes open with the evolution inside the period, per day, week or month according to its length, with the invoices deposited and in error per bucket; a table per activity gives invoices, deposits, errors and amounts per line of business; the company, document and transaction-type tables carry the previous period and the variation. The PDF draws charts: invoices per period bucket, per activity, the status family donut, the milestones per bucket and the most frequent rules. A whole calendar month, quarter or year compares to the preceding months instead of the same number of days; the tab offers a calendar-month picker next to custom dates. Rejections, refusals and error events are sorted by code; e-reporting envelopes covering a period that ends in the audit period are included.
- **Audit report: consistent, readable and complete.** The executive summary gains a breakdown of the processed invoices where every level adds up: not to send to the platform (transaction types configured not to be sent, such as B2C or international), to send, deposited, in progress, approved, rejected, not deposited and why. Deposit rates are taken over the invoices to send, in the summary, per day and per activity. Send attempts, resends (automatic retries included) and the send failure rate measure the platform's availability. Buyer-identifier fixes are reported as actions. The follow-up check covers every status awaiting an action, in two families: to fix and resend (rejected, validation failed, import failed) and answer to the buyer expected (disputed, suspended, refused). The backlog section lists the unreviewed invoices older than 30 days per status and shows net amounts; the Min invoice date setting bounds its all-periods figures. New checks: VAT lines with an amount but no rate; failed e-reporting envelopes are flagged. Per-activity tables are split in two, chart legends wrap, the per-mode table and the command-line hints are gone.
- **AI assistant: the instance, the period, offline documentation.** Two new tools: the implementation report of the instance, read by section or searched, so the assistant answers from the actual configuration (documents sent to the platform, rule packs, notification rules, roles and users, which action a status allows); and the period figures, the audit report's summary and backlog in seconds, for a monthly summary, rates, amounts or what awaits an action, within the user's company visibility. The playbooks follow the two action families (fix and resend; answer to the buyer, credit note mandatory only for a refusal) and a backlog playbook is added. The documentation index is per language: the French pages ground French answers (new URL setting, empty = English pages). The NomaUBL section of the documentation is bundled in the jar and used when the site is unreachable, with a note in the answer; the URL also accepts a local file. The starter questions become a domain picker (period, backlog, invoices, statuses and errors, configuration, documentation, technical, this invoice) with four questions each, the page choosing the starting domain; the domains stay available after an answer next to its follow-ups.
- **Technical report.** Reports gains a Technical report tab, with the API route and the command line, that generates the developer documentation of the release as Markdown or PDF from the scans bundled at build: scope, architecture, data model (every table with its columns, configuration keys, flows and call sites, and the name resolved in this instance when it differs), the flow documents each completed with the tables, statuses and keys their code touches, the configuration reference (every key with its settings field, where it is edited, flows, call sites and state, with a gaps summary), the status model (invoice and e-reporting tags with codes, labels, groups and setting flows), the impact matrix per flow with the most referenced columns and keys, the API reference with access per operation, the command line from the built-in help, the build steps with the generated artefacts and the jar layout, and an appendix of code references. Two options: detail every API operation, include the code snippets. Identical on every instance of a release.
- **Placeholder picker everywhere a token is resolved.** The insert-placeholder button now sits beside every field the server substitutes: the path constants on the Global directories and server log file, the document's UBL XSLT and custom Schematron, the E-invoicing XSLT directory, the watch-folder directory and manifest, and the image source of a PDF template block; the processing directories and the document XSLT also offer the run-time tokens of the document name and the input file name. API connector endpoints offer, per endpoint, the built-in credentials and token, the endpoint's own declared parameters and the values the callers pass; the authentication body and headers offer the authentication names; connector sources offer the single-brace tokens; SQL connector queries offer their declared parameters as :name tokens. The panel opens to whichever side has room and is no longer clipped by its row.
- **VAT declaration: refused, rejected and unsent invoices.** The declaration counted every invoice issued in the period whatever its status. Invoices refused by the buyer (210) or rejected by the platform (213) call for an internal credit note: a checkbox, on by default, leaves them all out; unchecked, only those customer service marked reviewed are left out. A second checkbox, off by default, also leaves out the invoices flagged to be sent that never reached the platform (validation, send or import failure, not yet sent). Both apply to the matrix, the drill-down, the Excel export and the PDF, whose footer states the rules applied; the API takes excludeMode and excludeUnsent.
- **Directory check: warn or block.** The E-directory settings gain a "Recipient not found" mode. Warn and send, the default, keeps today's behaviour: the miss is recorded as a warning and the invoice is sent. Block: on an invoice meant for the platform, a definitive answer from the directory (not registered, found but not reachable) or a missing EndpointID is a fatal finding; the invoice stops at validation failed and is not sent. A connector or network error only warns in both modes, and invoices configured not to be sent are never blocked. The UBL-file pipeline now records the lookup result like the JDE pipeline.
- **Demo instance: a sample corpus in one command.** A Global setting marks an instance as a demo instance; on such an instance only, the `-demo` command line fills the database with fictitious invoices: five issuing companies and thirty buyers with valid identifiers, invoices and credit notes of every type, every VAT category, document and line allowances and charges, prepayments, payees, tax representatives, deliveries, every payment means, attachments and references, spread over the last six months. Every invoice passes the French rule packs, a few are deliberately invalid, and all go through the real processing pipeline; the invoices meant for the platform are then driven through realistic paths, sent, pending, deposited, refused, rejected, disputed, suspended, approved, paid, with send and import failures, dated over the period. The same seed gives the same corpus; a reset switch removes everything the command created. The corpus also comes as JDE-like XML spools and as text PDFs, through two more demo documents that use the real XML pipeline: the spool mapping, generated from the framework template, shows nested paths, a constant, a summed VAT total, a field reached anywhere in the block and a line break in the payment terms; the PDF document shows the PDF-to-XML conversion with two address blocks, labelled rows, one table and regex fields for the document key. One run produces the three sources (60 % UBL files, 30 % spool invoices, 10 % PDF invoices); `--sources` narrows it. The demo requires the global Update DB switch at Y and writes its processing-log rows like the Process page. It also covers the platform side: supplier invoices received as UBL through a fourth demo document and driven through the buyer path (made available, under processing, approved and paid, disputed, refused); e-reporting envelopes generated by the real handler for every completed month, blank issuer and sender filled from the first demo company, then driven to deposited, import failed or rejected; a portal-only notification rule for refusals, rejections and failures, with the dispatcher started only when no rule of the instance sends e-mail. When the Demo instance flag is Y, Settings › Global shows a Demo corpus block that fills or resets the corpus as a background job with the usual progress window. The reset removes everything the demo created.
- **Promotion: promote to another instance, and a history.** Target instances are defined once in Settings › Promotion targets (name, URL, account; the password is stored encoded and used on the server for the call only, never in a package). On the Promotion page, a Promote view sends the Export selection to the chosen target: a dry run first shows the target's own preview, new, changed, identical, skipped with the field diffs, then Promote applies it with the usual policy and comment. The ZIP export stays for sites that cannot reach each other. A History view lists every package exported, import applied and promotion applied on the instance, with who, when, the counterpart, the policy, the comment and the full plan; a source keeps its promotions, a target its imports.
- **Mapping tab: rule sets.** The Variable Mapping tab of the XSL editor now reads a rule set: EN 16931 basic, EN 16931, or France extended, preselected on the one the template produces today and switchable to preview another. Every tag shows whether the set requires it, requires it under a condition (with the note and the rule ids), leaves it optional, does not know it, or gets it from the UBL defaults. Filters narrow to the required and conditional tags or to the required ones still missing; tags outside the set are hidden unless asked for, so the French extension tags appear only under the extended set. A completeness line per group counts the required fields with a source, a constant or a default. "Check mapping" lists the required fields without a source, then transforms the loaded sample with the mapping as edited and validates it; the report groups the findings by field and the tags concerned are highlighted. The rule sets are generated from the UBL reference data at build and can be overridden per environment. A document template can now name its rule set on its UBL tab: the validator then runs the packs the set lists, in every pipeline and in the invoice window's validation; blank keeps today's choice from the customization id, and the two default sets list exactly today's chain. The invoice window names the set an invoice was produced under, and the UBL reference and Business rules pages take the same set filter, with the status of each field.
- **Mapping: more tag syntaxes.** Tag values in a document mapping accept three more forms: `sum(a, b, …)` adds the amounts found at several paths, `//Field` finds a field anywhere in the spool, and `"\n"` in a concatenation inserts a line break. Existing mappings produce the same output as before. The mapping panel lists the path syntaxes above the root fields.
- **UBL defaults: VAT rate by source code.** The VAT tab gains a grid mapping the line's VAT category source (a tax zone, a tax type or a composite code built in the mapping) to a rate, with a switch: keep the source rate and let the grid fill blank rates, the default, or let a matching entry win over the printed rate. The same rate applies to the VAT breakdown rows, and a document can override the grid like the rest of the VAT family. On the category and rate grids a source ending in `*` covers every code starting with it; exact codes are tried first. An exemption reason is never emitted on the taxed and zero-rated categories, whatever the source says. Nothing changes in the produced invoices until the grid is filled; the upgrade adds the grid to each existing defaults file.
- **Post-transform: the validated UBL in another syntax.** A document's UBL tab gains a Post-transform stylesheet and an output suffix. After a validation with no blocking finding, the UBL is run through the stylesheet and the result is written next to it; a failure is recorded as a warning and the UBL keeps its course. UBL remains the pivot everywhere. The invoice and document windows gain a download of the derived file, named after the post-transform's name set on the document, computed on demand from the archived UBL. The platform connector body can send the converted file instead of the UBL with two new placeholders, derived content and derived file path, on the initial send and on resend alike; the UBL keeps the routing. Shipped stylesheet: UBL to Cross Industry Invoice (CII D16B, EN 16931 core), checked on the demo corpus against the official EN 16931 CII rules; the demo UBL document is configured with it.
- **API connectors: platform endpoints folded.** The list of endpoints NomaUBL calls on a platform is collapsed by default in the connector editor, with the configured count on its header; expand it to add one.

### Fixes

- **E-reporting envelope: credit notes and EU buyers.** The detailed block of a credit note or a corrective invoice carried no reference to the preceding invoice, which the platform's rule G1.32 requires; the preceding invoices are now read from the archived UBL's billing references and written with their date. The buyer's legal identifier was omitted when the buyer's electronic address was a national VAT number under its national scheme (German, Dutch, Italian, Spanish…), which failed rule G6.28; those schemes are now folded to the VAT identifier the envelope expects.
- **Job progress window.** It drew its own backdrop, so the page showed through it; it now uses the shared modal shell, like the resend from the IT dashboard.
- **Audit report on a large instance.** The report ran the lifecycle ordering check over the whole lifecycle table and sorted every lifecycle row in the database; both froze the generation on a large instance. The ordering check is left to the daily lifecycle check, the rows are folded in memory, the previous period computes only its summary counts, the findings query no longer sorts every message, and the error analysis reuses the rows already read. The report runs as a background job with a progress bar naming the current step, and each step's duration is written to the server log. Two checks were wrong: the platform identifier test missed blank-padded values on Oracle, and the integrity discrepancies were counted as zero.
- **Developer → API crashed.** Three request examples added with the promotion endpoints were plain text inside the OpenAPI document, which made it invalid JSON for the API view and for Redoc. They are proper JSON objects now, and the view shows a message instead of failing when the document cannot be read.
- **"Contains" filters with an underscore.** The shared filter builder treated the underscore as an explicit wildcard, so a value such as a file name fragment was sent without surrounding wildcards and had to match the whole value. Only the percent sign is a wildcard now; this fixes the file filter of the processing log and every text filter on the other grids.
- **XSD card of the by-rule view.** The card without a rule id drilled into the events with an empty filter and showed everything. It now drills on "no rule id" plus its source; the source column of the integration errors view became a server filter.
- **Audit report figures.** The first-pass validation rate counted the platform send failures as validation findings and missed the invoices fixed since; it is now taken from the lifecycle. The deposited milestone, the delays and the summary used three definitions of a deposit; all use the first platform status. Buyer-identifier fix events were counted as import failures. The status family table did not add up to the total. The approved row included plain deposits. The failures table did not say it was capped.
- **Audit report on PostgreSQL.** The send-intent filter compared the flag column to a number; the column is a string on PostgreSQL, which rejected the query. It is now compared as text on both databases.
